The Fondation Martin Bodmer is one of the world’s great repositories of rare books and manuscripts, its 160,000 treasures including a Gutenberg Bible, Shakespeare’s First Folio and a copy of Isaac Newton’s Principia Mathematica once owned by his great rival Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz.
The subject of the books came up at Sunday’s opening press conference. Gukesh said he had inspected the chairs, lighting and even the floor of the playing hall to ensure he would be comfortable during games that could last four or five hours, but admitted he had barely glanced at the books. “I don’t think I’ll be reading in between the games,” he joked.
A nugget of arcana from the Macedonian grandmaster Alex Colovic that may bode well for Gukesh. Of the four players who have deployed the Berlin defense in a world championship match, three of them (Vladimir Kramnik, Magnus Carlsen and Ding Liren) went on to win their matches. The lone exception? Vishy Anand against Carlsen.
Sindarov has expanded on the queenside and Gukesh has responded by pushing his a-pawn (14 c4 a5). The battle lines are becoming clearer: Sindarov has the more active pieces in the center, while Gukesh is looking for counterplay on the queenside to offset white’s long-term structural advantage.
“I think there were a lot of small surprises at first,” the Dutch grandmaster Anish Giri says on the Take Take Take stream. “I think on move one, maybe 1 d4 was a little more expected than 1 e4. Then from black, I think within the Spanish, maybe the Marshall was a little more expected than the Berlin.
“But then within the Berlin, I think finally the actual surprise is coming from Javokhir. I think this particular Ne4 move, we are in very rare territory. It is not something that I or many of my colleagues have studied deeply. I can imagine it’s a little bit of an obscure position.
“And yeah, a very exciting endgame ahead because there’s still a full board of pieces.”
A little diversion for those of you who, like Sindarov, have been looking forward to getting stuck into Grand Theft Auto VI. It turns out there’s a chess Easter egg buried in Rockstar Games’ sprawling recreation of Florida.
The eagle-eyed team at Chess.com have spotted a chessboard in the game which appears to reproduce a position from an actual game between the English grandmaster Daniel Gormally and Brazil’s Alexandr Fier at the 93rd Hastings Masters in 2017-18. Gormally, rated 80 points below his opponent, went on to win with the white pieces.
Something for Sindarov, who has been mulling his response to 13 ... Bd7 for more than 20 minutes, to investigate when he finally gets his hands on the game after the world championship.
The American grandmaster Maurice Ashley has joined the official Fide broadcast and admits he was hoping for something a little more combustible than a Berlin endgame to get the match under way.
“Obviously, the Berlin is one of those you see and you go, ‘Oh, OK, how’s he going to break down this wall?’ It’s obviously a big challenge when you have the white pieces, but clearly it looked like Sindarov was well prepared for this eventuality. So I’m excited to see the match get off, but it would have been nice to see something wild, crazy, queens on the board.
“I feel like [Hungarian grandmaster] Peter Leko here is excited by these kinds of positions. We were talking about endgames and his ability when he was young to play these extremely well. But I think the fans probably wanted some more sauce.”
And finally Gukesh makes his move! After a think of more than 15 minutes, the world champion has opted for 13 ... Bd7, bringing his last minor piece into play. The bishop also shields the black king from a potential check along the d-file, giving Gukesh greater flexibility in repositioning his king and coordinating his rooks. He’s more than 35 minutes behind the challenger on time, though.
Gukesh is in another deep think as Javokhir leaves the board for the nearby lounge chair inside the cramped playing hall.
“Now I understand what Javokhir was playing for,” English grandmaster David Howell says on the Chess.com broadcast. “I would have expected this opening from two older players, not maybe two 20-year-olds. But now I understand he’s trying to bait Gukesh. He’s trying to tempt him into some line where he has a deep, deep idea. Yeah, it’s very provocative.”
Gukesh has developed his dark-squared bishop and Sindarov has centralized his queenside knight (12 ... Be7 13 Ne4). The pace of play has slowed considerably as the players begin to grapple with the strategic subtleties of the Berlin. Both Stockfish and the Sesse supercomputer assess the position as dead even (0.00).
An email from the always welcome Gary Naylor, who sees parallels between the world chess championship and another of Europe’s great endurance events:
Given the location, the schedule, the fact that each leader has a team supporting him and, more than anything, the stamina required, this feels like the Tour de France. I suppose players have the ability to make stages – games – hard or easy by their strategies too.
Any sign of lycra?
No lycra to report, Gary, but there’s certainly something to the analogy. The ability to conserve energy over a three-week campaign, knowing when to attack and when to settle for a quiet day, is an underrated component of world championship matchplay.
Gukesh has been mulling his response to 12 Be3 for more than 10 minutes, after spending about eight minutes on his previous move.
“He still knows the position, but he is taking time to make sure he makes the right moves,” Russian grandmaster Peter Svidler says on the official Fide broadcast. “But Gukesh is already down almost 18 minutes on the clock. Considering he’s playing one of the most topical openings of the past 25 years, that’s some time expenditure.”
Gukesh has brought his knight to g6, putting pressure on the advanced white pawn on e5, and Sindarov has continued his development by bringing his bishop into play (11 ... Ng6 12 Be3).
Gukesh has returned his king to its original square and rerouted his knight (9 Rd1+ Ke8 10 Nc3 Ne7 11 h3). Sindarov’s last move prevents black’s light-squared bishop from coming to g4 and pinning the knight on f3, while giving his own king some breathing room.
“I think it’s important to highlight for our viewers that black is not playing for a draw,” the Hungarian grandmaster Judit Polgár says on Chess.com’s broadcast. “Black is just deciding to go into an endgame or a middlegame without queens, where it seems like only white has a slight edge. Black has doubled pawns on c6 and c7, black has the bishop pair, but basically black can go b6, develop the pieces properly.”
We’re heading straight into the famous Berlin endgame (4 O-O Nxe4 5 d4 Nd6 6 Bxc6 dxc6 7 dxe5 Nf5 8 Qxd8+ Kxd8). The queens are off the board after only eight moves, leaving white with a kingside pawn majority and black with the bishop pair but doubled c-pawns and a king that has forfeited the right to castle.
Don’t mistake the early exchange of queens for a lack of ambition. The resulting position is deceptively rich in strategic possibilities and has been the subject of decades of analysis at the highest level. Gukesh has continued with 9 Rd1+, and both players are still moving quickly.
The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.
The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.
We’re eight minutes to the scheduled first move, but American grandmaster Maurice Ashley has started with his introduction of the players to the playing hall. Gukesh enters first and takes his seat behind the black pieces. Sindarov, playing as white after Sunday’s drawing of lots, enters second.
If you’re looking for some pre-match reading, the Guardian spoke exclusively with Javokhir Sindarov on Sunday about his meteoric rise, his love of Lionel Messi, his plans to play GTA VI once the match is over and why chess’s happy warrior believes there’s more to life than the game. A taste:
“I’m the guy who can’t play games just for fun,” Sindarov tells the Guardian less than 48 hours before Tuesday’s world championship opener in Geneva, smiling at the absurdity of it. “If I play something, I always try to learn, trying to become better.”
That means poring over Counter-Strike tactics and watching YouTube tutorials before joining in with his mates. There is, it appears, no such thing as a casual game in Sindarov’s world, much less a friendly. “I always like to beat my friends,” he says. “I watch some video lessons and then come and beat them after some tournaments. I think the best thing is to beat your friends in some game.”
It is a revealing admission from a young man who has acquired a reputation for being uncommonly relaxed at the chess board. While many of the world’s elite players seem to carry the weight of every position on their shoulders – the viral clip of Sergey Karjakin agonizing for 25 minutes over a move during the 2016 world title match remains a cult classic in chess circles – Sindarov frequently gives off the impression of someone who is simply enjoying himself. The easygoing mien of the sport’s happy warrior is a quality that has caught his opponent’s attention. “One thing I learned from Sindarov is that he seems to be so happy while playing chess,” Gukesh Dommaraju, the reigning world champion, said in an interview published last week.
We’ve gone through the 140-year history of the world championship and chosen 22 of the most memorable games. You can go move by move through each of them here. It’s the perfect timesuck in the final run-up to today’s first move.
But not until Wilhelm Steinitz and Johannes Zukertort sat down in a small room at 80 Fifth Avenue in New York City on the afternoon of 11 January 1886 did a formal competition to determine the best player on the planet come to pass. Their first-to-10-wins encounter was held in three US cities over the next 78 days for a prize fund of $4,000. Since then, the world chess championship has provided the stage for countless unforgettable contests showcasing the precision, imagination and brilliance of the royal game at the highest level.
The legitimacy of the world championship, of course, remains a subject of lively debate. The absence of Magnus Carlsen continues to cast a long shadow over the sport’s showcase event. The 35-year-old Norwegian has held the world No 1 ranking for more than 15 consecutive years and was widely regarded as the game’s strongest player even before he defeated Vishy Anand for the world title in 2013. He only strengthened his claim as the greatest player of any era in 2021, when he crushed Ian Nepomniachtchi in Dubai in his fourth successful defense of the crown.
But Carlsen declined to defend his title for a fifth time in 2023, citing a lack of motivation to endure the months-long grind of preparation that championship matches demand. Only twice before had the chain of succession that stretches back to Wilhelm Steinitz in 1886 been broken: when Alexander Alekhine died as champion in 1946 and when Bobby Fischer forfeited the title in 1975.
Ding Liren went on to defeat Nepomniachtchi for the vacant title before losing it to Gukesh Dommaraju in Singapore the following year. Now Gukesh faces Sindarov in a match between two 20-year-olds ranked No 26 and No 4 in the world respectively, while the planet’s top-ranked player remains on the sidelines – at a time when his No 1 ranking is looking more vulnerable than any time in anyone’s memory. The generational stakes are undeniable, but the question that has dogged the championship since Carlsen walked away remains unresolved: can the winner truly claim to be the best chess player in the world?
For two elite players born in the same general part of the world barely six months apart, their competitive history is remarkably sparse: just three encounters in classical chess. Sindarov holds a 2½-½ advantage with two wins and one draw in their lifetime head-to-head, which dates back to their first encounter as tweens at the Moscow Open in 2018. Their most recent meeting happened in January at the prestigious Tata Steel tournament in Wijk aan Zee, where a tense positional struggle gave way to a wild, time-scrambled endgame before the pair settled for a draw after 78 moves. Sindarov also holds a 2-1 edge in their three rapid and blitz contests this year.
Gukesh’s form has largely gone off the rails since reaching the summit 23 months ago in Singapore. After making it to No 3 in the world with a peak rating of 2794, the Indian suffered a prolonged run of disappointing results, including a joint-last finish at March’s Prague Chess Festival and last-place showings at Norway Chess and the Chennai Grand Masters. He subsequently withdrew from the classical portion of the Grand Chess Tour and had tumbled to No 32 in the rankings by September, when his live rating briefly dipped below the 2700 barrier for the first time in four years, although his performances improved at that month’s Chess Olympiad.
Many of the world’s top grandmasters have expressed deep pessimism about Gukesh’s chances in Geneva due to his lengthy slump and Sindarov’s sustained upward tick. So too have the bookmakers, who have installed the Uzbek as a clear frontrunner at roughly 1-3 odds despite Gukesh being the champion. Carlsen has described Sindarov as “a pretty significant favorite”, citing the Indian’s tendency to take excessive risks. “His evaluations are way too optimistic,” the world No 1 said recently. “That makes him take way more chances than he should. I think especially now his confidence hasn’t been too high, he just tries to do a little bit too much.”
Yet one factor in Gukesh’s favor is his firsthand experience in the cauldron of a world championship match, where the intense psychological and physical rigors of facing the same opponent for weeks on end can be as punishing as the chess itself. Caruana, the world No 3 and former world title challenger who pushed Carlsen to the brink in 2018, has cautioned against writing off the champion despite his struggles. “The kind of ability he had – or has, whatever you want to say – it doesn’t disappear overnight,” Caruana said in September. “So, in my opinion, it can reverse at any moment.”
Here’s a review of the format for the world championship match. Gukesh and Sindarov will play up to 14 classical games with each player awarded one point for a win and a half-point for a draw. Whoever reaches seven and a half points first will be declared the champion (and no dead rubbers will be played).
The time control for each game is 120 minutes per side for the first 40 moves, then 30 minutes for the remainder of the game, with a 30-second increment per move starting with move 41. That means games can stretch beyond seven hours, testing both players’ concentration and endurance. Players are not permitted to agree to a draw before black’s 40th move, a rule designed to discourage short, uneventful games. A draw claim before then is only allowed in the case of threefold repetition or stalemate, subject to approval by the chief arbiter or deputy arbiter.
If the score is level after 14 games, a series of tiebreaks will be played on 12 December, starting with four rapid games at 15 minutes per player plus 10 seconds per move. If still tied, the players will contest two games at 10 minutes plus five seconds, followed if necessary by two blitz games at three minutes plus two seconds. Further single blitz games will be played until a winner emerges. Three of the past five world championship matches have been deadlocked after the classical portion and required tiebreaks: 2016, 2018 and 2023.
The complete official regulations can be found here.
Hello and welcome to Geneva for day one of the World Chess Championship. Over the next three weeks, India’s defending champion Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan will compete in a scheduled best-of-14-games match for the sport’s most prestigious title and a share of a $2.5m prize fund. The setting is the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, an affluent suburb overlooking Lake Geneva, where the two 20-year-olds will make history as the youngest pairing ever to contest a world championship match in the competition’s 140-year history.
Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world chess champion in history when he defeated China’s Ding Liren in Singapore in December 2024, aged just 18, shattering the record held by Garry Kasparov, who was 22 when he dethroned Anatoly Karpov in 1985. An aggressive player known for creating sharp, tactically complex positions aimed at unsettling opponents, the Chennai-born grandmaster has struggled badly for form since winning the crown, sliding from a career-high No 3 to No 26 in the world rankings and raising questions over his chances of retaining the title in his first defense.
Sindarov, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the most formidable talents of a new generation of Uzbek grandmasters. Born in Tashkent, he became a grandmaster at 12 years and 10 months, the second-youngest in history at the time, and secured his place in Geneva by winning the eight-man Candidates tournament earlier this year. A fearless, resourceful player in a rich vein of form, he enters his first world championship match ranked fourth in the world, up from No 25 last year and a remarkable 22 places above the reigning champion, and with a favorable head-to-head record against Gukesh in classical chess.
We’re roughly 80 minutes away from the ceremonial opening moves. Fide president Timur Turlov will do the honors for white, with five-time world champion and Fide deputy president Viswanathan Anand moving for black. Plenty more to come between now and then.

Houthis won't seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have pushed as close as 60 km to Aden, the temporary capital of the country's internationally recognised government, but they will not capture the city, Yemen's military said on Tuesday.
"I'll speak to you frankly. The situation is not where we want it to be. But it's not as dire as reported," Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, told a group of reporters via video link.
Since fighting resumed in Yemen in July in parallel with the wider Iran war, the Houthis have rapidly advanced in Yemen, seizing territory from the internationally recognised government and its allies, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.
The Saudis have carried out air strikes on Yemen in support of their allies on the ground, while the Houthis have struck Saudi oil targets, airports and office towers.
Aden, now the target of Houthi missile and drone strikes, had previously not seen major hostilities since street battles in 2015, soon after the internationally recognised government fled Houthi-run Sanaa and made the port city its base.
Reporting by Reuters

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Ceará (Alece) realiza, nesta quinta-feira (26), solenidade de entrega do Título de Cidadã Cearense à jornalista, escritora e ex-deputada federal Manuela D’Ávila. A homenagem é uma iniciativa da deputada estadual Larissa Gaspar (PT), autora do Projeto de Lei nº 961/2025, aprovado pelo plenário da Casa. A solenidade terá início a partir das 17h, no Plenário 13 de Maio.
O Título de Cidadã Cearense é concedido a personalidades que, mesmo não sendo naturais do estado, tenham prestado relevantes serviços ao Ceará e ao país. Para a deputada Larissa Gaspar, a concessão do título representa o reconhecimento de uma trajetória que inspira mulheres e fortalece a luta por um país mais justo e democrático. “Entregar o Título de Cidadã Cearense à Manuela D’Ávila é reconhecer uma mulher que tem uma trajetória marcada pela coragem, pela defesa da democracia e pela luta por uma sociedade mais justa e igualitária. Manuela representa tantas mulheres que enfrentam o machismo, a violência política e os preconceitos para ocupar os espaços de decisão. É uma honra recebê-la como nossa conterrânea”, destaca a parlamentar.
Trajetória de Manuela D’Ávila
A honraria reconhece a trajetória pública de Manuela D’Ávila, marcada pela atuação em defesa da democracia, dos direitos humanos, da justiça social e da igualdade de gênero. Jornalista formada pela Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS), Manuela também é mestre e doutora em Políticas Públicas pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).
Iniciou sua trajetória política no movimento estudantil e, em 2004, foi eleita vereadora de Porto Alegre. Exerceu dois mandatos como deputada federal (2007-2015) e um como deputada estadual do Rio Grande do Sul (2015-2019). Em 2018, foi candidata à Vice-Presidência da República na chapa encabeçada por Fernando Haddad. Neste ano, voltou a disputar uma eleição majoritária, concorrendo ao Senado Federal pelo Rio Grande do Sul.
Na Câmara dos Deputados, foi relatora do Estatuto da Juventude e presidiu a Comissão de Direitos Humanos e Minorias. Também se destaca como escritora e ativista, com livros dedicados a temas como feminismo, maternidade, democracia e enfrentamento à violência política de gênero. É fundadora do instituto “E Se Fosse Você?”, voltado ao combate à violência de gênero e ao ódio nas redes sociais.
Manuela também está à frente da construção do MEL – Mulheres em Lutas, movimento que articula mulheres de diferentes áreas e territórios, promovendo redes de apoio, formação, cuidado e fortalecimento da participação feminina nos espaços de poder e decisão.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Frieze Los Angeles reveals 102 exhibitors for 2027 edition
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Carlie Porterfield
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
The eighth edition of Frieze Los Angeles will welcome 102 exhibitors under the sprawling white tent on the grounds of the Santa Monica Airport. The exhibitor list, as in previous years, includes heavy local representation—with more than one-third of participants operating a space in Los Angeles.
The roster includes established Los Angeles galleries such as Jeffrey Deitch, Regen Projects, David Kordansky, Château Shatto, Commonwealth and Council, Anat Ebgi, Night Gallery, the Pit and Roberts Projects. Four younger Los Angeles galleries will make their debuts in the Focus section for emerging galleries: Megan Mulrooney, Rajiv Menon Contemporary, House of Seiko and Zodiac Pictures. Erin Christovale from the Hammer Museum will curate this section.
International blue-chip galleries returning to Frieze Los Angeles include Gagosian, Hauser & Wirth, David Zwirner, Pace, White Cube, Perrotin, Gladstone, Almine Rech, Thaddaeus Ropac and Sprüth Magers. First-time exhibitors include Gallery Wendi Norris from San Francisco, Franklin Parrasch in New York, G Gallery in Seoul, Newchild in Antwerp, and Yehudi Hollander-Pappi and Danielian in Brazil.
A handful of prominent galleries will not be returning after taking part in recent editions, like Berggruen Gallery from San Francisco, Ortuzar and Tina Kim Gallery in New York, Mendes Wood DM and Nara Roesler from Brazil, Southern Guild from Cape Town and Timothy Taylor from London. Turnover year-over-year remains around 28% for a second consecutive year, amid stable overall exhibitor numbers.
Visitors to the fair will be greeted at the entrance by a new work by the Los Angeles-based artist rafa esparza called Queerchana, painted across two adobe panels mounted on chrome steel, drawing on Southern California’s culture of lowrider cruising.
Amid a boom following the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic, art dealers from all over the world began setting up shop in the Los Angeles area. However, many of those outposts have since closed alongside local dealerships—most recently, the Landing on Jefferson Boulevard. Along with a global market downturn, many local businesses were hurt by the devastating 2025 wildfires that nearly saw that year’s edition of Frieze Los Angeles cancelled. A handful of galleries have closed their local spaces and shifted their attentions to New York, including Southern Guild and Pietro Alexander.
This may be one of the final years the fair will be held at the Santa Monica Airport; the facility is scheduled to close permanently to aviation at the end of 2028 for conversion into a public park.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Trump’s DoJ ‘looked into’ concerns about Jensen Huang after alleged affair with Chinese spy but no security risk found – live
Justice department and other agencies reached ‘collective consensus’ that Jensen Huang is not a national security risk, attorney general Todd Blanche says
Blanche: DoJ 'looked into' concerns about Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Chinese spy
Todd Blanche, the attorney general, defended his department’s activity related to Nvidia and Jensen Huang on Tuesday, telling reporters that they “looked into” concerns related to Huang’s alleged affair with a Chinese spy.
“What I said last week is that we were looking into it,” Blanche said during a press conference. “The FBI, law enforcement looks into things all the time. That doesn’t necessarily become a criminal investigation; it doesn’t necessarily become an indictment; it just literally is that. It’s looking into things.”
Blanche largely declined to give reporters detailed information about the Justice Department’s (DOJ) probe into Huang and Nvidia. But he insisted Nvidia is a “good corporate citizen” and that the DOJ had no information indicating Huang had committed a crime.
“To the extent that the Department of Justice had information that [Huang] was committing crimes or something like this… that’s something I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said.
But the attorney general became defensive when reporters pressed him about the Justice Department’s process for ensuring Huang had not violated any laws.
“What does that mean, ‘Had Huang been investigated?’ For what?… I don’t understand the question,” Blanche said in response to a reporter’s question.
At another point, Blanche told a reporter: “I don’t know what folks are asking about specifically… I don’t, I mean, you’re mocking me, but when you say ‘get to the bottom of what is there,’ what are you asking me about?”
DoJ and other agencies conclude Jensen Huang not a national security risk, Blanche says
Todd Blanche also indicated the DOJ reached a “collective consensus” with other agencies and departments to determine that Jensen Huang was not a national security risk.
“How we make that type of determination – there’s a whole bunch of ways. We’re using the intelligence community, the FBI, the information we know, we talk to witnesses,” Blanche said in response to a reporter’s question on Tuesday.
“I know there’s heightened focus on this situation, but that’s something that the law enforcement partners and that the leadership in this country, whether it’s Commerce, or Treasury, State Department, the attorney general – me – it’s a collective consensus that we reach all the time in all kinds of different cases, not just in this case.”

Analysis: the Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence
Robert Tait
Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view.
Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geo-strategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race.
The woman, Alice Huang – no blood relation of Jensen – was also responsible for buying $4.8bn worth of Nvidia’s highly sensitive AI chips in her capacity as head of a Singapore-based technology company, Megaspeed. The chips were then diverted to China, despite US export restrictions forbidding such sales to a country Washington regards as a key strategic adversary.
The president was inactive even after Marco Rubio, the secretary of state and national security – and one of the administration’s renowned “China hawks” – repackaged the intelligence into a classified report last May warning of the geopolitical risks posed by the relationship.
“It’s clear that the White House was warned, had adequate opportunities to take action against what was an emerging and then eventually very clear chip diversion network that was emerging under Megaspeed and other Southeast Asian offshore data farms – and it just failed to act,” said Julia Curlee, a former Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officer who specialized in the Middle East and China and also worked on the White House national security council during Trump’s first presidency. She added:
It’s the latest episode of the president ignoring or not believing the intelligence that’s being provided to him.
Despite the intelligence concerns raised by his conduct, Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s chief executive on Monday following pressure from the White House and the company’s shareholders.
Why is scandal-plagued Jensen Huang back at Nvidia? - podcast
Jensen Huang is apparently too big to fail – but what does that mean for the rest of us?
Just last week, Nvidia’s board chair told investors that the company had no intention of reinstating Huang as CEO. On Monday, they turned a full about-face. The board voted unanimously to reinstall Huang, triggering a nearly $1tn surge in the company’s stock market valuation. Donald Trump took credit, telling CNBC that he “convinced them” to bring Huang back. But questions remain about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and about whether Nvidia exploited loopholes to export chips to Chinese AI companies.
In today’s edition of our Stateside podcast, Kai Wright talks with the Guardian US’s tech editor Blake Montgomery about the many twists and turns in the Huang scandal – and why Huang embodies the “key man risk” that threatens our whole economy.
Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees. But the Nvidia board reinstated him after an intervention from the US president.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them … I made the deal.”
The US president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics indicate he might have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of 30 September, the latest available data, in news first reported by the Financial Times.
Nvidia’s shares rocketed by 31.5% on Monday, adding about $950bn to the company’s value. Huang returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, receiving a hero’s welcome, with crowds of employees chanting “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”
Trump has bought Nvidia shares worth between $23m and $86m, according to a BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the past two years. He has also sold some of his stake in the company since returning to the presidency, and gained between $3.5m and $10.2m, according to his government disclosures.
Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, on Monday weighed in on the corporate turbulence surrounding Nvidia and the chipmaker’s CEO, Jensen Huang, saying he does not think working Americans “signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of … Huang’s fidelity to his marriage.”
The mayor said Huang “had a massive impact”, with Nvidia’s share price dropping dramatically when he stepped down as the company’s CEO on 12 November after a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
But on Monday, after he was reinstated after Donald Trump intervened, the California-based company’s value bounced back by 31.5%.
Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang – who have been married since 1985 and have combined assets of about $160bn – have made no statement about their marriage in the wake of the reported affair. But at a news conference on Monday after Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO, Mamdani took the opportunity to make a point about wealth.
“We’re speaking about a divorce settlement that has been rumored to be around $81bn,” he said. “That would be the cost of providing universal childcare for every three- and four-year-old in the United States of America for an entire year.”
Alluding to Louis Brandeis, the late US supreme court justice who was at the forefront of an antitrust movement, Mamdani continued:
A lot of this just brings to mind what Justice Brandeis said quite some time ago, which is: We can have democracy. We can have great wealth concentrated in the hands of a few. We cannot have both.
Mamdani also made a point about the stock market. He said that market was “disproportionately dependent” on stocks related to the artificial intelligence boom powered by Nvidia’s chips. “It cannot help but give you a sense of concern about just how much this technology is now dominant,” he said.
“I do not think that working people across the country signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Jensen Huang’s fidelity to his marriage,” Mamdani said. “And yet, for many days, that had a massive impact.”
House Dems call for Jensen Huang to testify at public hearing
Democrat Gregory Meeks, the ranking member on the House foreign affairs committee, has called on Jensen Huang to testify at a public committee hearing following Donald Trump’s intervention to get him reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO and amid national security concerns raised by Huang’s efforts to increase and accelerate the export of high-end chips to China.
Meeks said in a statement: “Americans deserve answers to the profound questions that are continuing to emerge about NVIDIA and our national security. President Trump’s intervention to reinstate Jensen Huang as NVIDIA’s CEO raises even more concerning questions about the administration’s own role, questions the American people deserve to hear answered in public.
“For the past year, committee members have raised concerns about NVIDIA’s effort to weaken U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips sales to China, as well as widespread allegations regarding the diversion of NVIDIA chips from third countries to China. We have many questions surrounding the administration’s role in approving exports that have put America’s national security up for sale.
‘The American people deserve to hear publicly from Mr. Huang about how potentially billions of dollars’ worth of our most advanced technology wound up in the hands of our greatest competitor, and what role this administration played. A transcribed interview is critical to our oversight efforts but it should not replace a public hearing. Chairman Mast should convene one.”
Earlier we mentioned Donald Trump is participating in a Medal of Freedom ceremony in the Oval Office at 11am ET. He will be awarding the nation’s highest civilian honor to former New York mayor and Trump’s onetime personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani.
Trump said last year he would award the medal to Giuliani, two days after his longtime political ally was seriously injured in a car crash.
Giuliani was once lauded for leading New York after the September 11, 2001, attacks and later sanctioned by courts and disbarred for amplifying false claims about the 2020 US presidential election. Giuliani was also criminally charged in two states, and later pardoned by Trump, over his role in a plot to steal the 2020 election.
US preparing to raise tariffs on China and dozens of other countries – report
The US is preparing to raise tariffs on China and dozens of other countries that the Trump administration argues are harming American companies by supporting their own domestic industrial production, the Wall Street Journal reports (paywall) this morning, citing people familiar with the plans.
Per the Journal’s report: “US trade representative Jamieson Greer as soon as this week is expected to unveil the results of a monthslong tariff investigation into the industrial subsidies of China, the European Union and 14 other nations, said the people, who warned the timing could change.
“Greer has said those subsidies and other governmental supports have created excess industrial capacity in the targeted economies, allowing their firms to flood global markets with cheaper goods, undermining US producers.”
As we noted earlier, Nvidia’s freshly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang, will appear on Capitol Hill next week, where skeptical lawmakers from both parties will grill him over his ties to a woman that some in the intelligence community have said was a spy for China. Huang will also sit for transcribed interviews with the Senate banking committee and House foreign affairs committee, as well as the select committee on the Chinese Communist party and the House intelligence committee. (Here’s our Shrai Popat’s report).
Massachusetts Democrat Elizabeth Warren, the incoming Senate banking chair, has told Politico Playbook: “President Trump insisting that the company should rehire him does not get Mr. Huang or Nvidia off the hook.”
Asked whether Huang’s return changes the investigation, Warren replied without hesitation: “Yes, and not to Nvidia’s benefit.”
“All the excuses of ‘I don’t know what Nvidia is doing now because I’m not there’ will be denied to Mr. Huang,” Warren said, “and Nvidia’s ability to separate itself from a CEO that is under serious investigation over whether [he] has participated in an international scandal of monumental proportions will also have disappeared.”
Huang and Nvidia “together makes very clear the need for a serious, independent investigation”, Warren added.
Three bipartisan bills are ready to go, she outlined:
Don’t sell these chips to China. Don’t sell the equipment to make these chips to China, and every chip that leaves the United States should have a tracker on it.
Huang “will have to answer Republican and Democratic members of the Banking Committee”, Warren said, “on why he actively lobbied to send Nvidia’s chips to China and whether Nvidia’s chips have been smuggled to fuel China’s military”. She added: “I’ll be pressing for that. But I won’t be the only one.”
Iran’s chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reiterated on Tuesday that Tehran would not hold talks with the United States until Iran’s seven conditions are met.
“Our position remains what we have previously stated: There will be no actions or negotiations until Iran’s seven conditions are met,” Iran’s chief negotiator said in a report carried by the IRGC-affiliated Fars news agency.
He also warned:
Furthermore, we are prepared to respond decisively to any hostile moves by the enemy and, should the enemy commit a miscalculation, to shift the geography of the conflict.
Tehran’s conditions include sanctions relief, lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, releasing seized Iranian assets, ending hostilities on all fronts and formally declaring the war over.
It comes as the naval arm of Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said three oil tankers were struck naval mines in strait of Hormuz because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the waterway.
The Guard’s navy said in a post on Telegram on Monday that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorized routes or to disregard maritime warnings”.
It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under US aerial escort.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said on Tuesday that all three vessels continued their transits and all crew were accounted for.
Donald Trump will take part in a Medal of Freedom ceremony in the Oval Office at 11am ET this morning, it’s closed to press but we’ll let you know if it opens up. Then at 2pm he and the first lady will participate in the Thanksgiving turkey pardoning at the White House, this year featuring turkeys Freedom and Feather. The president will then do a print interview before departing for Palm Beach, where he’ll spend Thanksgiving.
Juliana Stratton, the incoming Democratic senator from Illinois, said she would support significantly reforming or abolishing the filibuster in order to allow Congress to deliver on the promises they made American voters.
The filibuster means that most successful legislation in the Senate must have 60 supporters instead of a simple majority. Eliminating that requirement is one of several reforms Democrats can act on after they won an unexpected 56-44 majority in the next US Senate, their largest majority in nearly two decades.
Stratton, currently the Illinois lieutenant governor, was a professional mediator before she entered politics. For two decades, she ran a dispute resolution firm, bringing people who did not agree together to find ways to solve problems.
The experience will serve her well in a divided government, she told the Guardian. She welcomes Republicans who want to stand up to Trump and “have a real spine” to work with and Democrats in the US Senate.
“We cannot go in kind of waffling on, ‘Well, we’ll see what we can do, it’s going to be hard.’ That’s the same kind of thing that really turned so many voters off this election cycle – people going in, telling them how hard everything is and that there’s so many hurdles,” Stratton said. “Sure, there are hurdles, but we were elected to do hard things.”
House Democrat expands investigation into Donald Trump Jr's investment firm
A top House Democrat is broadening his investigation into Donald Trump Jr’s venture capital fund 1789 Capital by demanding records from four companies that secured an investment before benefiting from lucrative federal contracts or policies, AP reports.
Representative Jamie Raskin, the ranking member of the House judiciary committee and the panel’s incoming chair, sent letters on Monday evening to the defense contractor Hadrian Automation, vape maker Juul Labs, prediction market platform Polymarket and the online firearms seller GrabAGun.
The Maryland congressman requested that each firm send him two years’ worth of communications with 1789 Capital and other select documents, saying the materials would help him investigate whether president Donald Trump’s eldest son used insider information to orchestrate or anticipate government actions that boosted the companies and his own finances.
US envoy 'not certain' military aid to Israel will end this year as Trump promised
Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, has cast doubt on whether Washington would end its $3.8bn in annual military aid to Israel by the end of this year, as promised by Donald Trump on the day of this month’s midterm elections.
In his surprise announcement as voters headed to the polls on 3 November, Trump said he had made a deal with prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu several months earlier to stop providing Israel with about $4bn in annual US funding.
Trump said Israel no longer needed US funds, and the issue had been used as a “bad talking point” by ‌his leftwing critics, Reuters reported.
The election that ‌day subsequently saw Democrats, including many who publicly oppose military funding for Israel, win control of both houses of Congress ‌from Trump’s Republicans.
Trump did not provide details or explain how the funding would be halted. The US has a longstanding agreement with Israel, known as a memorandum of understanding, to provide it with $3.8bn a year until 2028 to fund purchases of American-made military equipment.
Congress to grill Jensen Huang over ties with China and Trump’s intervention
Shrai Popat
Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s chief executive is “exhibit A” of the “political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy”, Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland Democrat vying to become the next Senate majority leader, told reporters Monday.
Van Hollen said he intends to focus on Huang’s “efforts to increase and accelerate the export of high-end chips to China, how he’s been accomplishing that, how he’s been getting his way with the administration” when the reinstalled Nvidia CEO appears before the Senate banking committee on 3 December.
It will be one of several appearances on Capitol Hill next week where skeptical lawmakers from both parties will grill Huang over his ties to a woman that some in the intelligence community have said was a spy for China. Huang will also sit for transcribed interviews with the House foreign affairs committee, as well as the select committee on the Chinese Communist party and the House intelligence committee.
“It’s completely hypocritical for the Trump administration, on the one hand, to say the reason we have to take all the brakes off AI development here at home is because China will leap ahead if we don’t,” Van Hollen said. “When in fact, it’s the Trump administration that’s helping China leap ahead.”
Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after Donald Trump intervened on the executive’s behalf, assuring company leadership that he did not pose a national security risk despite questions surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, a tech executive of no relation who has been accused of acting as a Chinese asset and routing advanced chips to Beijing via her data center company, Megaspeed.
In an interview with CNBC on Monday, the US president defended his involvement in Huang’s reinstatement, arguing it would be a “bigger threat” for Nvidia to lose Huang’s “brain power” in the AI race. Trump also confirmed that he had provided the board with assurances regarding any national security concerns.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them,” Trump said.
Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO sends a message “that the national security of this country is not as important as your relationship with president Trump”, Democratic senator Ruben Gallego said.
Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees. But the Nvidia board reinstated him after an intervention from the US president.
“We also have to figure out how corporate America doesn’t take a bad lesson from this, and thinks that somehow it’s OK for them to evade national security for the purposes of just selling more,” Gallego, an Arizona Democrat considering a White House campaign, said.
Meanwhile, California representative Ro Khanna wrote on social media that “rules should apply to everyone”, noting: “The rich + powerful, like Jensen, do not get to evade export controls or accountability just because it props up the stock price.”
Huang returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, on Monday and received a hero’s welcome, with crowds of employees chanting “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”
His return as CEO came despite Huang being subject to several government and internal investigations, shareholder lawsuits and accusations that he’s a national security threat.
Nvidia is one of the most valuable businesses in the world, worth about $4tn, and the entire AI ecosphere relies on it. The company engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power tech firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

In his surprise announcement as voters headed to the polls on 3 November, Trump said he had made a deal with prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu several months earlier to stop providing Israel with about $4bn in annual US funding.

Newsom responded by criticizing Trump for “selling” pardons and for demanding the execution of five wrongfully convicted young New Yorkers of color in 1989.

A building housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund in Riyadh has been hit for the second time in under a week.
Riyadh called Tuesday's suspected drone attack by Yemen's Houthi-aligned forces a "cowardly terrorist attack".
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence reported that 11 people were injured in the strike and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Entenda o caso do falso laudo da PF compartilhado por Nikolas Ferreira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A divulgação de um falso documento atribuído à Polícia Federal (PF) pelo deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL) voltou a ser alvo de cobranças. Após mais de dois meses sem que o caso tenha apresentado desfechos concretos, parlamentares e representantes da sociedade civil intensificam os pedidos por investigação e responsabilização do parlamentar. Uma petição pública que pede a cassação de seu mandato já ultrapassou 1,3 milhão de assinaturas.
O episódio teve início em setembro, em meio à repercussão de mensagens e áudios trocados entre Nikolas e Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, revelados pelo portal ICL Notícias. Nas conversas, o empresário mencionou ter custeado voos do deputado e demonstrou proximidade com o parlamentar. Em uma das mensagens, Vorcaro afirmou: “Esse Nikolas eu banquei todos os voos dele”.
Em outro diálogo, de março de 2025, Nikolas chama o empresário de “Dani” e pede ajuda para liberar um ativo minerário ligado a seu ex-assessor Thiago Rodrigues de Faria. Vorcaro responde demonstrando disposição para ajudá-lo: “Amém irmão estamos na guerra juntos”.
Um dos principais desdobramentos da ação envolve a Meta
Diante da repercussão das conversas, começou a circular nas redes sociais, em 3 de setembro de 2026, um suposto relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) que afirmava não haver indícios de crime nos diálogos entre os dois. O documento foi compartilhado por Nikolas em suas redes sociais, mas a corporação desmentiu sua autenticidade no dia seguinte.
Plataformas de checagem identificaram inconsistências nas datas e nas transcrições das mensagens, além de divergências em relação aos documentos oficiais da PF. O material falso indicava, por exemplo, que teria sido elaborado em 18 de novembro de 2025, enquanto o relatório verdadeiro tornado público pela corporação era datado de 27 de agosto de 2026.
À imprensa, Nikolas admitiu ter compartilhado o documento, mas alegou que não sabia que era falso. Segundo o deputado, a publicação original havia sido feita por um perfil chamado Space Liberdade, na rede X. Ele afirmou que retirou o conteúdo do ar depois que a postagem original foi apagada.
Parlamentares acionam a Justiça e cobram responsabilização
A repercussão do caso mobilizou parlamentares de diferentes estados. Entre os que passaram a cobrar providências estão Rogério Correia (PT), Túlio Gadêlha (PSD), Iza Lourença (Psol), Bella Gonçalves (PT) e Ana Elisa (PT).
A deputada Bella Gonçalves questionou a ausência de consequências para o parlamentar e afirmou que uma ação apresentada à Justiça Eleitoral, ao lado de Erika Hilton (Psol) e Ana Elisa, foi arquivada por uma questão processual, sem análise do mérito da denúncia.
“O documento falso da PF que Nikolas Ferreira divulgou não pode ficar impune. Se fosse você, cidadão comum, o que aconteceria?”, questionou a parlamentar nas redes sociais.
Bella também defendeu que o caso seja investigado e que haja responsabilização. “Lei vale pra todo mundo, inclusive pAra quem tem mandato. Seguimos cobrando investigação e responsabilização”, escreveu.
O deputado Rogério Correia também acionou o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Minas Gerais (TRE-MG), em 8 de setembro, pedindo a apuração do compartilhamento do documento falso. A ação investiga suspeitas de abuso de poder político e uso indevido dos meios de comunicação, com possibilidade de cassação do mandato caso as irregularidades sejam comprovadas.
Em manifestações públicas, Correia questionou se Nikolas teria participado apenas da divulgação ou também da produção do documento. O parlamentar ressalta que a investigação precisa esclarecer a origem do material e identificar os responsáveis por sua circulação.
“É bem possível que Nikolas tenha produzido inclusive o laudo. O fato de compartilhar já é crime. Para produzir um laudo falso seria um crime ainda maior”, afirmou.
Meta é questionada por contradições sobre dados da publicação
Um dos principais desdobramentos da ação envolve a Meta, empresa responsável pelo Instagram.
A Justiça havia determinado, em 11 de setembro, a preservação dos registros. Em 12 de setembro, a Meta informou que havia adotado as providências necessárias. Entretanto, em 9 de novembro, declarou que três dos oito conteúdos abrangidos pela decisão judicial tinham sido permanentemente eliminados, alegando impossibilidade técnica de recuperar parte dos dados.
A contradição motivou uma nova petição apresentada por Rogério Correia em 14 de novembro. O deputado pediu ao TRE-MG que rejeite a justificativa da empresa, determine explicações em até 48 horas e eleve a multa diária para R$ 50 mil, limitada a R$ 1 milhão.
Para Correia, a situação precisa ser esclarecida, especialmente porque as informações podem ajudar a identificar a origem do documento falso e os responsáveis pela página @nikolasferreirateam, que utiliza o nome do deputado.
A petição também solicita informações sobre possíveis vínculos entre os administradores dessa página e a conta oficial de Nikolas, além de dados sobre visualizações, compartilhamentos e interações com a publicação.
O parlamentar ainda apontou diferenças entre as respostas da Meta e do X. Segundo a petição, a plataforma X conseguiu fornecer informações sobre uma publicação apagada antes mesmo de receber a intimação judicial, incluindo métricas, horários e registros de acesso.
Entre os pedidos apresentados ao TRE-MG estão a identificação dos responsáveis pela exclusão dos conteúdos, a requisição de informações a provedores de internet e a avaliação do envio do caso à Procuradoria Regional Eleitoral para apuração de eventual crime de desobediência.
Parlamentar aponta possibilidade de inelegibilidade
Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, o deputado Túlio Gadelha afirmou que uma eventual condenação de Nikolas poderá resultar em inelegibilidade por oito anos e afetar outros parlamentares eleitos pela mesma chapa proporcional em Minas Gerais.
“Você não pode, Nikolas, fraudar um laudo da Polícia Federal dizendo que você não cometeu um crime”, declarou.
Gadêlha também cobrou que a Meta entregue à Justiça Eleitoral os dados relacionados à publicação. Segundo ele, a investigação precisa esclarecer a circulação do documento e as responsabilidades envolvidas.
O deputado ainda afirmou que uma eventual anulação dos votos da chapa proporcional poderia atingir outros dez parlamentares eleitos em Minas Gerais. A consequência, contudo, depende do enquadramento jurídico e de eventual decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.
Petição por cassação ultrapassa 1,3 milhão de assinaturas
Paralelamente às iniciativas parlamentares, uma mobilização nas redes sociais também ganhou força. A petição pública que pede a cassação do mandato de Nikolas Ferreira ultrapassou 1,3 milhão de assinaturas e tem como meta alcançar 2 milhões de adesões.
A campanha é conduzida pela deputada federal Sâmia Bomfim (Psol), por meio de seu site oficial.
Com o crescimento da mobilização, usuários voltaram a cobrar providências da Polícia Federal e da Justiça sobre o compartilhamento do documento falso. Na rede X, internautas questionam a demora na apresentação de resultados e cobram que o episódio não termine sem responsabilização.
Até o momento, o TRE-MG ainda precisa analisar os novos pedidos apresentados por Rogério Correia. A identificação dos responsáveis pelos perfis e a recuperação dos registros digitais são consideradas etapas importantes para esclarecer a origem, a circulação e o alcance do documento atribuído falsamente à Polícia Federal.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Morre, aos 90 anos, o jurista e professor Fábio Konder Comparato
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O jurista Fábio Konder Comparato, professor emérito da Faculdade de Direito da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) e uma das maiores referências do pensamento jurídico e da defesa dos direitos humanos no país, morreu na madrugada desta terça-feira (24), aos 90 anos, na capital paulista. A causa da morte não foi divulgada pela família.
O falecimento provocou forte comoção no meio político e acadêmico. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi uma das primeiras autoridades a prestar homenagens ao professor, destacando sua firmeza ética e intelectual. “Ao longo de décadas, Comparato dedicou o seu amplo saber jurídico à democracia, ao humanismo, à soberania nacional, aos direitos humanos e à justiça social”, disse Lula.
O presidente ressaltou ainda a presença marcante do jurista na formação e na luta popular: “Foi um mestre que formou gerações na Faculdade de Direito da USP e um intelectual comprometido com as causas do povo brasileiro, muito presente nas lutas pela redemocratização e pela efetivação dos direitos fundamentais”.
A cerimônia de despedida ocorre nesta terça, das 11h às 15h, na avenida Doutor Arnaldo, na esquina com a rua Major Natanael, na região central. O sepultamento está marcado para as 16h, no Cemitério da Consolação.
Protagonismo na Constituinte
Na mensagem nas redes sociais, o presidente Lula lembrou também a colaboração direta de Comparato na reabertura política e na elaboração da Carta Magna. “No período de formulação da Constituição de 1988, teve papel protagonista, ao atuar na proposição de um projeto constitucional e de um regimento interno completos — apresentados pelo Partido dos Trabalhadores — que ajudaram a pautar parte dos debates”, pontuou o chefe do Executivo.
Durante a ditadura militar (1964-1985), Comparato atuou diretamente na defesa jurídica de presos e perseguidos políticos. Como integrante da Comissão de Justiça e Paz da Arquidiocese de São Paulo, enfrentou os abusos do regime autoritário e criou o primeiro curso de Direitos Humanos da Faculdade de Direito da USP.
Em depoimento ao Projeto Memórias da instituição, o jurista explicou a escolha curricular: “Pude combater o regime militar doutrinariamente. Fiz questão de mostrar os crimes cometidos quase diariamente pelo regime militar”.
Mais tarde, o professor formulou teses pioneiras de revisão da Lei da Anistia de 1979, defendendo que agentes de Estado responsáveis por torturas e assassinatos fossem julgados e punidos. Em 1992, foi também um dos advogados a assinar a petição jurídica do pedido de impeachment do então presidente Fernando Collor de Mello.
O professor Vladimir Aras destacou, nas redes sociais, essa faceta combativa do jurista, relembrando que Comparato “atuou na defesa de presos políticos e perseguidos pela ditadura militar e foi referência na discussão política e acadêmica sobre direitos humanos”.
Repercussão e homenagens
Parlamentares, juristas e entidades de direitos humanos prestaram homenagens à memória do professor. O deputado federal Paulo Teixeira (PT-SP) definiu Comparato como uma “imensa referência intelectual e humanista”.
A deputada federal Sâmia Bomfim (Psol-SP) também manifestou pesar nas redes sociais: “Um intelectual da maior importância em nossa história, que tive a oportunidade de encontrar em diversas atividades dos movimentos estudantil e sindical da USP, mesmo após sua aposentadoria”.
O advogado Ariel de Castro Alves, presidente de honra do Grupo Tortura Nunca Mais de São Paulo e membro da Comissão de Direitos Humanos da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil de São Paulo (OAB-SP), comparou sua relevância à de outro ícone do direito: “Enorme perda! Junto com Dalmo Dallari, o professor Fábio Konder Comparato foi um dos maiores juristas dos Direitos Humanos da história do Brasil! Seu livro ‘A Afirmação Histórica dos Direitos Humanos’ é uma obra indispensável sobre o tema”.
Instituições do meio jurídico também emitiram comunicados oficiais. O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ministro Edson Fachin, declarou que o falecimento representa “uma perda inestimável para a comunidade jurídica e para a sociedade brasileira”, afirmando que seu patrimônio ético permanecerá vivo.
Em nota, a diretora da Faculdade de Direito da USP, professora Ana Elisa Bechara, classificou o docente emérito como “uma voz indispensável na defesa da democracia, dos direitos humanos e da justiça social em nosso país”, e destacou a coragem com que Comparato levou a ciência jurídica ao debate público em favor da dignidade humana.
Já o Conselho Federal da OAB relembrou que o professor recebeu, em 2005, a Medalha Rui Barbosa, a mais alta condecoração da advocacia brasileira, e afirmou que sua trajetória deixa “um legado de inestimável valor para a cidadania”.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: African rivals fret over Morocco’s growing football dominance
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
African rivals fret over Morocco’s growing football dominance
As Morocco enjoys success on and off the pitch, is it benefitting from preferential treatment, or setting an example?
Morocco’s growing influence in African football is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.
From reaching the semifinals of the 2022 FIFA World Cup to hosting major continental competitions and preparing to cohost the 2030 World Cup, it has arguably become Africa’s dominant footballing nation.
Morocco is also preparing to welcome FIFA’s 77th Congress in Rabat on March 18, 2027, and the country hosted the last two editions of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Awards. Three of its players – Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari – feature on the 10-person shortlist for the 2026 men’s CAF Player of the Year award.
For some, Morocco represents what sustained investment, strategic planning and football diplomacy can achieve. Others, however, question whether its growing concentration of hosting opportunities and institutional influence is creating an imbalance within African football.
Kamilla Swart, an associate professor and Director of the Master of Science in Sport and Entertainment Management programme at Hamad Bin Khalifa University in Doha, Qatar, says Morocco’s current position is the product of a strategy developed over several years.
“I think it’s a case of Morocco building its expertise over a long period of time,” she said.
“So if you even think of, you know, everybody talks about the Mohammed VI Football Academy that was inaugurated in 2010. So it’s not something that’s just happened now.”
Morocco bid unsuccessfully to host the World Cup several times before finally winning a joint bid for 2030. Swart said those bids enabled the country to assess its weaknesses and establish the infrastructure needed to compete for major international events.
However, Swart said that Morocco’s repeated hosting of CAF events has raised questions about whether other African countries are getting sufficient hosting opportunities.
“On the one hand, I can understand why all these events are going to Morocco,” Swart said.
“And on the other hand, I can see the point of view where there may be some scepticism or mixed feelings about that – potentially the rest of the continent is not benefitting from that.”
Some have also accused CAF of giving Morocco preferential treatment. These concerns intensified following the controversial 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final between Senegal and Morocco. Senegal initially won the game 1-0 after extra time, but the match was overshadowed by a late penalty awarded to Morocco, prompting Senegal’s players to temporarily leave the pitch in protest.
On March 17, 2026, CAF’s Appeal Board overturned an earlier disciplinary ruling, declared Senegal to have forfeited the final by leaving the pitch under Articles 82 and 84 of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) regulations and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of an appeal by Senegal and reinstated them as champions on Tuesday.
Speaking before that ruling, Kenyan sport lawyer and arbitrator Khayran Noor told Al Jazeera, “I think we need to distinguish between two issues: Morocco’s genuine institutional and infrastructural progress, and the responsibility of CAF to ensure that its decision-making processes are transparent and beyond reasonable suspicion.”
When it comes to awarding hosting rights, a CAF Executive Committee assesses the facilities and documentation submitted by bidding countries before making the final hosting decision.
However, Noor believes the process would benefit from greater transparency, including published evaluation criteria, independent technical assessments, disclosure of potential conflicts of interest and explanations of final decisions.
She also warned against allowing financial strength to translate into disproportionate political influence. Article 17 of the CAF Statutes provides each member association with one vote at the General Assembly, irrespective of its financial capacity.
“Morocco should be entitled to benefit from its investments, but every other African federation should have a meaningful opportunity to demonstrate its own capacity,” Noor said.
“Ultimately, institutional confidence is built not only by making the right decisions, but also by demonstrating that those decisions were reached fairly.”
Morocco’s hosting profile also has an important commercial dimension, some experts say. CAF depends heavily on broadcasting and sponsorship revenues, making the quality of its competitions and broadcasting standards central to its financial sustainability.
Gerard Akindes, a Beninese-born sports management scholar, international consultant and former professional athlete, believes the concentration of major competitions in Morocco is partly down to the uneven quality of football infrastructure and broadcasting production elsewhere on the continent.
“AFCON is what makes CAF’s revenue,” Akindes told Al Jazeera. “And they want the best product possible that they can sell to broadcasters to generate revenue that is going to sustain the organisation.”
Akindes also suggested that Morocco’s willingness to host competitions when other countries were unable or unwilling to do so had strengthened its relationship with CAF.
“Morocco managed to get a lot of influence because they saved the organisation several times by hosting events that nobody wanted to host,” he said. “When you do that, they probably get some return.”
‘It’s a conspiracy theory’
Morocco’s growing presence on the CAF Awards shortlist has also generated debate over preferential treatment.
The 2026 ceremony returns to Lagos on December 2, marking Nigeria’s first time hosting the event since 2014. However, the absence of Nigerian players from the men’s Player of the Year shortlist has attracted criticism, particularly among supporters who expected players such as Victor Osimhen, Ademola Lookman and Calvin Bassey to feature.
Morocco, meanwhile, has three nominees, including reigning winner Hakimi.
CAF-accredited journalist and Brila Media contributor Adeniyi Adebanjo believes the reaction should be considered alongside the performances of the shortlisted players and the wider dissatisfaction among African football supporters following the controversy surrounding the 2025 AFCON final, particularly CAF’s handling of the disciplinary proceedings and their decision to award Morocco a 3-0 victory.
He rejected suggestions that the rescheduling of the awards ceremony was connected to the dispute between Senegal and Morocco or intended to influence the voting process.
“I think this is a conspiracy theory,” he said. “I don’t necessarily ascribe to the idea that CAF is playing some type of game with this.”
Nigerian exercise physiologist and University of Lagos lecturer Victor Damilola Ademola – who has visited Morocco three times in the last 12 months – believes the country’s success reflects a systematic development of players at all levels of the game.
Morocco has also been effective in integrating eligible diaspora players into its national teams, strengthening its talent pool.
“They have invested significantly in training facilities, stadiums and sports science infrastructure, including facilities for youth development. The Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat is an excellent example,” he said.
“What matters is not just the facilities themselves, but how they support player development, conditioning, medical care and preparation across different age groups.”
Ademola cautioned against interpreting every Moroccan achievement as evidence of preferential treatment from CAF and argued that Morocco’s progress should also encourage other African countries to examine their own football administration, international engagement, infrastructure and player development.
“There is no established proof that CAF is deliberately favouring Morocco because of its investments or hosting contributions … [although] when similar concerns keep emerging, they deserve scrutiny rather than automatic dismissal,” he said.
“At the same time, we must not use these controversies to excuse our own shortcomings.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘O cinema continua na memória das pessoas porque ele deu sentido às vidas delas’, diz historiadora
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Cinemateca Capitólio ofereceu um programa inusitado e feito sob medida para os cinéfilos de Porto Alegre. Foi uma visita guiada gratuita pelo Circuito Cine-Afetivo de Porto Alegre. Os participantes puderam conhecer endereços onde existiram salas de exibição no Centro Histórico da capital gaúcha, além das histórias e curiosidades desses locais.
O passeio ocorreu no sábado (21), a partir das 9h, com ponto de partida na Cinemateca Capitólio (rua Demétrio Ribeiro, 1085). O circuito também pode ser percorrido de forma autônoma e gratuita.
O roteiro inclui verdadeiros “palácios de sonhos”, como o monumental Cacique, o familiar Victoria, o popular Carlos Gomes, o Imperial, o Guarani, o Capitólio, o São João, o Rex, o Palermo e o velho Marabá. Além desses espaços conhecidos e consagrados, há as salas pioneiras do início do século 20, como o Recreio Ideal (primeiro cinema da Capital), o Íris, o Smart Salão, o Avenida e o Central, entre outras.
O percurso foi orientado pela historiadora Alice Dubina Trusz (autora dos livros “Entre Lanternas Mágicas e Cinematógrafos” e “Verdes Anos”) e pelo jornalista e pesquisador Cristiano Zanella (autor da obra “The End – Cinemas de Calçada em Porto Alegre 1990/2005”). Eles foram os responsáveis pelo projeto que mapeou 20 cinemas de rua da cidade, em cujos endereços foram fixadas placas com informações sobre cada sala, além de um QR Code para acessar fotos e outros dados.
Uma iniciativa que revelou um extenso levantamento histórico desse circuito, celebrando a história, a memória e os tempos de glória que marcaram época em Porto Alegre e que, mesmo fisicamente ausentes, permanecem vivos no imaginário de muitos espectadores. O Brasil de Fato RS conversou, com exclusividade, com os dois pesquisadores.
Brasil de Fato RS: O hábito de ir ao cinema é ainda muito presente em Porto Alegre? Na comparação com outras capitais, a cidade tem muitas salas de exibição?
Cristiano Zanella: A tradição de ir ao cinema é ainda muito forte em Porto Alegre. A capital gaúcha esteve, ou ainda está, entre as que mais tiveram, ou têm, salas no país. Cada bairro tinha um cinema, não era só o Centro Histórico. Talvez esse número atingisse quase 60 salas. É claro que, hoje, estão concentrados nos shopping centers, mas ainda é uma cidade que tem uma tradição de excelência no cinema.
Alguns dos que fecharam no centro foram substituídos por centros culturais, como a Cinemateca Capitólio, o CineBancários e a Cinemateca Paulo Amorim. Tem também a Sala Redenção, da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS). Apresentam uma excelente programação e um charme especial.
Muitos cinemas de rua fecharam as portas há décadas. Por que a história desses locais continua tão presente na memória de muitos espectadores?
Alice Dubina Trusz: Bom, em primeiro lugar, cinemas abriram e fecharam em todas as décadas por diferentes motivos. Em meados dos anos 90, fecharam porque o público já não estava acompanhando esses cinemas. O público já tinha outras opções, como o videocassete. As condições da cidade também já eram diferentes. Se falava muito da insegurança.
Mas a gente vai para as redes sociais e vê que as pessoas são apaixonadas por essas salas que não existem mais. Trocam fotos dos cinemas, comentam o seu passado como espectadores e frequentadores. Se você sentar pra conversar com uma pessoa de mais idade e perguntar sobre o cinema, ela vai lembrar o primeiro filme que viu e em qual cinema, até mesmo quando era criança.
Os cinemas de calçada foram muito importantes para a formação cultural, intelectual e afetiva das pessoas. Memórias foram construídas nas experiências de se encontrar com o filme, de perceber o filme como janela para o mundo, de aprender com o cinema, de se divertir, se emocionar e também vivenciar essa experiência coletiva que o cinema proporciona. Eu mesma fiz muitos amigos em fila de cinema. O cinema continua na memória das pessoas porque ele deu sentido às vidas delas em alguma perspectiva.
Essa é, então, uma história viva?
Cristiano Zanella: Pra mim, é uma história viva. É uma pesquisa que eu já tenho há quase 35 anos. Desde o final dos anos 80, no começo dos anos 90, eu já fotografava as fachadas dos cinemas. Tentava entender por que os meus cinemas preferidos estavam todos fechando.
Talvez algumas das minhas melhores memórias e histórias da infância e juventude estejam sempre ligadas com o ato de ir ao cinema. Era também uma maneira de conhecer o Centro Histórico. Minha história está muito envolvida com isso, então é bem importante pra mim resgatar essas histórias. Acredito que pra muita gente também seja.
Como foi unir passado e futuro pra contar essas histórias? A tecnologia tornou o Circuito Cine-Afetivo ainda mais interessante, com QR Codes?
Alice Dubina Trusz: É muito bacana que as pessoas possam andar na rua e se deparar com uma placa. Entender a sua finalidade e as informações que ela traz marcando esse espaço onde houve um cinema ou vários. A gente observou, com a pesquisa, que alguns locais se consolidaram como lugares de se ver cinema. Cinco salas de cinema chegaram a se suceder num único endereço. Ele entrou no cotidiano da cidade com essa finalidade, esse território.
É muito gratificante a gente poder compartilhar esse conhecimento com o público, com quem passa pela rua. Por meio do QR Code, há a possibilidade de saber um pouco mais sobre cada cinema. Tem imagens de como eram as salas por dentro e por fora. E mais: isso pode ser feito de forma autônoma, independente e gratuita.

Riyadh's landmark 'PIF Tower' struck in aerial attack for second time in five days
A building housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund in Riyadh has been hit for the second time in under a week.
Riyadh called Tuesday's suspected drone attack by Yemen's Houthi-aligned forces a "cowardly terrorist attack".
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence reported that 11 people were injured in the strike and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).
The PIF Tower was previously hit in an attack last Thursday.
It is one of the Saudi capital's tallest buildings and is part of the King Abdullah Financial District.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Yemen's Houthis have demonstrated an ability to consistently strike prominent targets within Saudi Arabia, even as Riyadh launches its own air strikes on Yemen.
Earlier in November, a building belonging to the kingdom's oil giant Aramco was damaged in an attack in Riyadh.
In October, an attack on Riyadh's airport killed at least 14 people.
Tuesday's attack in Riyadh came as Saudi warplanes struck buses and trucks in Wadi Maabaq in Yemen’s Lahij governorate, killing as many as 25 people and wounding six, the Saba news agency reports.
Residents told Saba that badly burnt human remains were still inside one of two buses hit in the attack, hampering identification.
They said Saudi warplanes continued circling overhead, blocking ambulance crews and residents from reaching those caught in the strikes and worsening the toll.
Saudi Arabia resumed fighting in Yemen in July after years of an uneasy ceasefire. Since then Houthi forces have made significant gains, reaching Yemen's southern coastline and securing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab waterway, which connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea.
Control of the waterway means that Yemen's Houthi-led Sanaa government controls shipping traffic going up to the Suez Canal in Egypt.
Yemen's war, which started with a Houthi offensive in 2014, has claimed the lives of close to 400,000 people, according to some estimates.
A large number of Yemeni civilians have died due to Saudi-led coalition bombardment and an economic siege imposed by Riyadh on Houthi-held territory.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Bloco do MST do Rio abre ensaios para o Carnaval 2027 e convida novos integrantes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Bloco do MST do Rio de Janeiro já tem data para sair às ruas no Carnaval de 2027. O primeiro desfile será ainda no domingo que antecede os dias oficiais de folia, em 31 de janeiro, às 15h, na Praça da Harmonia. O segundo acontece já na sexta-feira (5), às 17h30, no Jardim do Méier.
Até lá, muitos ensaios vão acontecer. Eles são realizados às terças-feiras, às 19h30, no espaço Garagem Delas, na Rua da Carioca, 83. “Estamos abertos para novos tocadores, dançarinos, pessoas que querem participar. Para a bateria, é preciso ter experiência, já a ala de dança e mística é aberta para todo mundo”, contou ao Brasil de Fato Fabito Alves, dirigente do Cultura do MST e coordenador do bloco.
:: Quer receber notícias do Brasil de Fato RJ no seu WhatsApp? ::
E há mais uma novidade. Este ano, o grupo contará com estudantes de Música da Universidade Federal do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (UniRio) pelo Programa Nacional de Educação na Reforma Agrária (Pronera). Com início em dezembro, a etapa presencial segue até março e, nesse período, os estudantes também acompanham o Bloco.
Em 2026, o Bloco do MST do Rio de Janeiro realizou sua estreia no Carnaval de rua. Nesse segundo ano, a proposta é avançar nas alegorias, nas fantasias e na própria bateria.
“O Bloco do MST é um instrumento da classe trabalhadora. O MST produz alimento saudável, produz alegria, produz novas relações humanas. É uma forma de síntese e comunicação do nosso projeto da reforma agrária popular com alegria e irreverência”, completa Alves.
