https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/23/d.title: Don’t Paint ‘Look Up’ On Corners. Fix the Corners!
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/23/d.author: Bellden Mikhels
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/23/d.text:
A new City Council bill would require the Department of Transportation to paint the words “Look Up” or “Look Both Ways” at 500 or more intersections, including 200 near schools. The markings would remind pedestrians, who may be looking down, to look up at oncoming traffic.
I thought about the shortcomings of Intro 1004 after yet another completely preventable recent fatality on a known dangerous corner. On Oct. 28, Siobhan Lynch, 30, was crossing Bay Parkway at Cropsey Avenue, next to Bensonhurst Park, when a Sanitation Department truck driver turned right onto Bay Parkway and killed her.
Lynch did everything right — and the trucker did everything wrong. 
Pedestrians are the most vulnerable users of our roads, and drivers must recognize that they are responsible for the safety of people crossing the street. But the bill by Council Member Virginia Maloney (D-Upper East Side) seeks to shift that responsibility from drivers to pedestrians and, to me, raises an obvious concern: What happens if a pedestrian looks up, follows the rules, and still gets hit?
The answer to that question is embedded in the details of Lynch’s killing. As Streetsblog reported, the truck driver and Lynch had the light, but Lynch, as the pedestrian, had the right of way. Painting “Look Up” on the pavement would not have changed the outcome; such a reminder would not have made the turning trucker slow down or yield.
That’s the problem with the bill: It assumes that reminding pedestrians to pay attention will prevent crashes that are often beyond their control.
Yes, distracted walking can be an issue, and it is important for all road users to pay attention to their surroundings. But safe streets can not be solely the responsibility of pedestrians — roadways need to be designed to protect them (and that means more than designing “Look Up” stencils).
Again, the Lynch killing is illustrative: According to city data, since January 2022, there have been 76 reported crashes at that one intersection, injuring 50 people, including three cyclists and 15 pedestrians. The DOT designates Bay Parkway as a Vision Zero priority corridor, yet the department’s new Bay Parkway and Cropsey Avenue bus lane project left this intersection without the protections warranted by its crash history. The DOT says it is adding a painted curb extension to the northeast corner of the intersection. Safety advocates say that is not enough.
Clearly, distraction isn’t the only danger pedestrians face. In its plans for Bay Parkway and Cropsey Avenue, the DOT identified left-turn crashes as the leading cause of pedestrian injuries in the area, accounting for 40 percent. Its research also found that restricting left turns at certain intersections was associated with a 41-percent decrease in left-turn pedestrian and cyclist injuries. Lynch was hit by a driver turning right, not left, but the lesson is the same: when drivers turn through a crosswalk, pedestrians are exposed. 
Designing streets so that drivers slow down for turns matters far more than painting a reminder to pedestrians, who can be, and are, killed and maimed even when they follow all the rules and all the advice.
The DOT has already achieved success in its street design efforts. Its Turn Calming program uses rubber curbs, speed bumps, and flexible posts, causing drivers to execute slower, more controlled turns — and the agency says serious pedestrian injuries fell 33 percent at the intersections included in the program. Given the city’s strong evidence that these changes work, this program should be expanded.
Maloney’s bill is cost-effective — paint is cheaper than lavish curb redesigns and road diets. But turn calming is also relatively inexpensive — a couple hundred to a few thousand dollars, according to Quartz. This kind of treatment is affordable and worthwhile, especially in light of its proven, and somewhat remarkable, results.
The DOT could also daylight corners to minimize risk to pedestrians and allow drivers to better see, but the agency famously opposes removing parking spaces at every intersection, citing a 2025 report that found no statistically significant reduction in injuries from daylighting with “No parking” signs alone. But that report was flawed, the DOT had to admit: 
And the agency does support “hardened” daylighting to ensure that cars do indeed stay out of the space.
So instead of painting a slogan at every corner, the Council should require the DOT to assess each location and install improvements that address specific risks identified at each corner. Crash histories and associated risks should guide those decisions. The intersection at Cropsey Avenue and Bay Parkway would be a good place to start.
Encouraging young people to pay attention should not be abandoned, but the City Council must also take the necessary steps to ensure that one small mistake doesn’t get someone killed. When I take my driving test next year, nobody will assess whether pedestrians looked up as I drove through crosswalks. They’ll assess whether I yielded, as the law requires me to do. And if I don’t, I’ll certainly hope that the roadway is designed in a way to make me slow down.

https://taz.de/Urteil-im-Vergewaltigungs.title: Urteil im Vergewaltigungsfall Young: „Schweigen ist keine Option“
https://taz.de/Urteil-im-Vergewaltigungs.author: Carolina Schwarz
https://taz.de/Urteil-im-Vergewaltigungs.text:
Urteil im Vergewaltigungsfall Young: „Schweigen ist keine Option“
Ein weiterer Pelicot-Fall: 13 Jahre lang wurde Joanne Young von ihrem Ehemann betäubt und zum Sex angeboten. Wir dürfen uns niemals an solche Fälle gewöhnen.
Eigentlich wollte ich nach dem ersten Satz schon aufhören zu lesen. Es gibt einen neuen Pelicot-Fall. Wieder einmal. Dieses Mal kommen Täter und Opfer aus Großbritannien. Über einen Zeitraum von dreizehn Jahren hat Philip Young seine damalige Frau unter Drogen gesetzt und im bewusstlosen Zustand anderen Männern bei sich zu Hause zur Vergewaltigung angeboten. Vier dieser Männer wurden vergangene Woche wegen verschiedener Sexualdelikte, darunter auch Vergewaltigung, vom Strafgericht in Winchester schuldig gesprochen. Young, ein ehemaliger Kommunalpolitiker und Unternehmer, hat sich bereits in 56 Anklagepunkten schuldig bekannt, sein Strafmaß steht noch nicht fest.
Als ich zum ersten Mal von dem Fall höre, ist mein erster Reflex einfach weiter zu scrollen. Bloß nicht zu genau hingucken, bloß nicht im Detail nachlesen, was der Frau angetan wurde. Ich habe keine Lust mehr, von grausamen Männern zu lesen, die Frauen als ihr Eigentum betrachten und ihre Körper wie Ware behandeln. Als Frau, Freundin und Mutter möchte ich Verbrechen dieser Art nicht zu nah an mich ranlassen. Aber da ist mehr als nur meine Angst. Ich merke auch, dass trotz aller Grausamkeit langsam ein Effekt der Gewöhnung einsetzt.
Als die Verbrechen, die Gisèle Pelicot angetan wurden, vor zwei Jahren große Aufmerksamkeit bekamen, war ich wie im Schockzustand. Ich konnte mir schlicht nicht vorstellen, dass es so viele Männer auf einem Fleck gab, die eine komatöse Frau vergewaltigen wollten. Jedes Detail, das ich über den Fall lernte, machte es nur noch schlimmer. Und nicht nur ich begann mich zu fragen: Wie können wir überhaupt noch mit Männern leben?
Seitdem sind einige Fälle bekannt geworden, bei denen Frau betäubt, vergewaltigt und Videos davon ins Netz gestellt wurden. In Hannover wurde beispielsweise Anfang diesen Monats ein 39-jähriger Mann zu 12 Jahren Haft verurteilt. Der Young-Fall ist der erste dieser Art, der in Großbritannien vor Gericht landete, doch laut britischer Staatsanwaltschaft nehmen solche Gewaltfälle zu.
Unbeschreiblicher Schmerz
Am Tag der Verurteilung der vier Männer ist die betroffene Frau vor die Kamera getreten. Ihr Name ist Joanne Young, sie hat ihre Anonymität freiwillig aufgegeben, um andere Betroffene zu ermutigen. Bei Instagram sehe ich ein Video ihrer Rede. Sie sagt: „Die Person, der ich am meisten vertraut habe, hat mich auf schrecklichste Weise betrogen. Das hatte verheerende Auswirkungen auf mein Leben und das meiner Kinder.“ Im Weiteren sagt sie, dass der Schmerz, mit dem sie nun leben muss, nicht mit Worten zu beschreiben ist.
Doch die Worte, die ich höre, reichen, um mich aufzuwecken. Ich kann jetzt nicht mehr weiterscrollen. Ich muss zuhören. Und das sollten wir alle, auch wenn es schmerzhaft ist. Trotz Gewöhnung dürfen wir nicht abstumpfen. Wir dürfen nicht hinnehmen, dass das unser Normal ist. Und es ist müßig, es immer wieder zu betonen, aber wir dürfen nicht wegschauen. Denn die Verbrechen finden teilweise in der Öffentlichkeit statt – was auch bedeutet, dass eine wachsame Gesellschaft sie verhindern kann.
Die National Crime Agency war auf den Täter aufmerksam geworden, nachdem er ein brutales Bild bei der Nachrichten- und Livestream-App Kik hochgeladen hatte. Daraufhin durchsuchten sie im Juli 2024 sein Zuhause. Aber hätte die Polizei nicht schon viel früher aufmerksam werden können?
Die Orte, an denen Young den Körper seiner Frau zur Vergewaltigung freigegeben hat, waren nicht im Darknet. Es waren Seiten, die von der breiten Gesellschaft regelmäßig genutzt werden. Auf Plattformen wie Craigslist, Grindr oder Reddit postete er: „Fuck my tied and blindfolded wife – mw4m – 35 (North Swindon)“ oder „Fuck my wife – 18th September – Central Bath hotel – mw4m“.
Wie viele Tausende User haben diese Postings gesehen? Wie viele Tausende haben weitergescrollt, als sei es das Normalste der Welt, dass eine gefesselte Frau mit verbundenen Augen wie Ware angeboten wird? Auch wenn nicht zwangsläufig ein Verbrechen hinter so einem Angebot stecken muss, hätte doch irgendjemand stutzig werden und die Polizei alarmieren können.
Sie alle sollten sich die Worte von Joanne Young zu Herzen nehmen: „Schweigen ist keine Option, wenn man etwas gegen die Gewalt gegen Kinder und Frauen tun möchte.“

https://taz.de/KI-loest-heiligen-Gral-de.title: KI löst berühmtes Mathe-Rätsel: Was nützt ein Beweis, den niemand versteht?
https://taz.de/KI-loest-heiligen-Gral-de.author: Ruth Lang Fuentes
https://taz.de/KI-loest-heiligen-Gral-de.text:
KI löst berühmtes Mathe-Rätsel: Was nützt ein Beweis, den niemand versteht?
KI soll die Riemannsche Vermutung, den „heiligen Gral“ der Mathematik, gelöst haben. Doch der Wettlauf zwischen KI und menschlichem Denken ist ein Irrweg.
Es ist eingetreten, was schon lange in der Luft lag, aber von dem große Teile der Mathe-Welt gehofft hatten, dass es nicht eintreten möge: Die Riemannsche Vermutung, der „heilige Gral“ der Mathematik, scheint bewiesen – und zwar mithilfe von künstlicher Intelligenz. Der Mathematiker und Anthropic-Mitarbeiter Levent Alpöge hat mithilfe der firmeneigenen KI Claude einen mutmaßlichen Beweis vorgelegt. Und das wenige Tage nach dem Börsengang des KI-Unternehmens – was für ein Zufall.
Schlimm ist das vor allem für die vielen Mathematiker auf der ganzen Welt, die ihre bisherige Arbeit schon seit einiger Zeit bedroht sehen – spätestens nachdem im September der KI-Beweis für das Navier-Stokes-Problem publik wurde. Nun scheint das zweite der insgesamt sieben bedeutendsten mathematischen Probleme aller Zeiten durch KI gelöst.
Hunderte von Mathematikern arbeiten seit 1859 daran, die Vermutung zu lösen, die der deutsche Mathematiker Bernhard Riemann damals aufstellte. Die unter anderem deswegen von großer Bedeutung ist, weil sie etwas über die Verteilung von Primzahlen aussagt und weitere Erkenntnisse darüber liefern könnte. Und diese sind insbesondere für Verschlüsselungen extrem wichtig.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Die 250.000 Seiten des mutmaßlichen KI-Beweises, den Alpöge selbst nicht ganz versteht, aber von dessen Korrektheit ein Netzwerk an Mathematikern „fest überzeugt“ sei, freut die allermeisten Mathematiker eher wenig. Im Gegenteil: Für viele gleicht das einem Schlag in die Magengrube, Jahre an Arbeit waren völlig umsonst. Und das durch einen möglichen Beweis, den nicht einmal der Verfasser selbst versteht. Der sich wie ein persönlicher Angriff aus der KI-Welt anfühlt.
Diese könnte die Unmengen an Rechenleistung und Energie auch nutzen, um etwa konstruktiv Probleme im medizinischen Bereich zu lösen. Stattdessen versucht man mit unverständlichen vermeintlichen Lösungen die Überlegenheit von KI gegenüber menschlichem Denken zu beweisen. Doch das ist keine Mathematik. Und solange ein Beweis nicht verstanden und auf seine Korrektheit geprüft wurde, ist er auch nichts wert.

https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.author: Muriel Steinmetz
https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.text:
La romancière, essayiste et journaliste s’est éteinte lundi 23 novembre à Paris, à l’âge de 87 ans. On doit à cette fière activiste de la pensée, philosophe nourrie de psychanalyse et d’anthropologie, proche de Lacan et Lévi-Strauss, et passionnée de l’Inde, une soixantaine d’ouvrages.
Elle venait de publier son dernier roman, Sabbataï ou la doublure de Dieu (Seuil), sur ce rabbin de Smyrne qui, au XVIIe siècle, se décréta messie. Catherine Clément, fière activiste de la pensée, dont le frère cadet, Jérôme Clément, ancien président d’Arte, a annoncé la disparition, a mené de front, sans relâche, l’écriture de romans et la réflexion philosophique sur les mythes, les religions, les rapports entre le corps et l’esprit....

https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.title: Office Depot met la clé sous la porte, 185 salariés licenciés
https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.author: Scarlett Bain
https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.text:
Les derniers magasins de l’enseigne Office Depot ferme définitivement. Le tribunal de commerce de Bobigny a rendu sa décision mardi 24 novembre après qu’aucun repreneur n’a été trouvé. Les 185 salariés seront licenciés dans les prochains jours.
Dernier baissé de rideau, ce mardi 24 octobre, pour les magasins Office Depot. L’enseigne de fourniture de bureau cesse ainsi son activité en France, avec « la fermeture définitive de ses 27 magasins et de son site internet », a annoncé à l’AFP une porte-parole de la société Ankaa, qui exploite l’enseigne.
« La recherche d’un repreneur engagée dans le cadre de la procédure n’a pas permis d’aboutir à une solution de poursuite de l’activité », a précisé cette porte-parole. Ainsi, le tribunal de commerce de Bobigny, qui avait placé le 7 octobre la société Ankaa en liquidation judiciaire, avec poursuite d’activité afin de permettre la recherche d’un repreneur, a prononcé ce mardi 24 novembre 2026 « l’arrêt de (cette) poursuite temporaire d’activité », a-t-elle ajouté.
Une lente agonie
Reprise en 2021 par la société Ankaa, l’enseigne avait amorcé sa lente agonie dans la conjoncture défavorable de la pandémie du Covid 19, associée à la hausse des coûts logistiques, à la numérisation et à la baisse de la consommation.
Ce plan de reprise avait déjà acté la suppression de 1 000 postes sur les 1 500 que comptait l’entreprise. De 60 magasins qui existaient alors dans toute la France, il en reste en 2026 seulement 27, concentrés en Île-de-France. Le sort des 185 derniers employés est donc scellé, ils seront licenciés dans les jours à venir.
Le média que les milliardaires ne peuvent pas s’acheter
Nous ne sommes financés par aucun milliardaire. Et nous en sommes fiers ! Mais nous sommes confrontés à des défis financiers constants. Soutenez-nous ! Votre don sera défiscalisé : donner 5€ vous reviendra à 1.65€. Le prix d’un café.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Storms and flooding in US could disrupt Thanksgiving travel for tens of millions
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Auzzy Byrdsell
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Potent storms and flooding could disrupt the plans of tens of millions of people traveling for Thanksgiving, according to the US’s National Weather Service (NWS).
A storm system affecting the US Pacific north-west and another affecting the eastern part of the country are expected to produce periods of heavy rain and strong wind gusts, the NWS said as millions of Americans prepared to travel for Thursday’s holiday.
The NWS advised residents to check its website “for the latest forecast updates along your travel route and plan ahead”.
Both will bring the potential for periods of heavy rain and strong wind gusts.
Before Thanksgiving, parts of the US south are expected see heavy rain, including Florida, Georgia, the Carolinas, Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee, according to the Weather Channel.
Parts of the midwestern states of Missouri, Illinois and Iowa are predicted to see rain – which could become wet snow, the outlet said. And, on Thanksgiving itself, midwest airports in Chicago, St Louis, Pittsburgh, Cincinnati and Detroit could see complications.
Meanwhile, seasonal high tides up and down California’s coast are expected to trigger “major to extreme” coastal flooding, with the San Francisco Bay Area particularly being advised to prepare for travel-related delays.
Furthermore, out west on Thanksgiving, there could be mountain snow in Washington and Oregon – and possibly into Idaho and Montana, according to the Weather Channel.
Inclement weather could affect up to 81 million people expected to travel throughout the US for Thanksgiving, widely reputed to be the busiest travel period in the US. The AAA motor club anticipates more than 72 million travelers will head for their holiday destinations by car, as NBC News reported.
Beside the weather, holiday car commuters will also be grappling with gasoline prices that have been particularly high in the wake of the war in Iran that the Trump administration started alongside Israel in February. AAA data showed regular gasoline averaged $3.64 a gallon in the US on Monday – six cents above a Thanksgiving Day record set in 2022, according to the motor club.

Plusieurs îles de l’archipel des Australes sont en proie aux flammes : Rimatara, après celle de Tubuai et Rurutu. En octobre, Moorea avait déjà été touchée par un gros incendie. Partout dans le Pacifique, la sécheresse aggravée par El Nino a des conséquences dramatiques.
Même le Fenua (le pays, en tahitien, N.D.L.R.) brûle. Depuis quelques semaines, plusieurs îles de la Polynésie sont touchées par des incendies de forêt, qui, rapportés à la superficie, prennent des proportions énormes.

https://www.theguardian.com/food/2026/no.title: Nine delectable Thanksgiving sides – from a ‘perfect’ gravy to Ottolenghi’s stuffing biscuits
https://www.theguardian.com/food/2026/no.author: Danielle Renwick
https://www.theguardian.com/food/2026/no.text:
Let’s be honest, side dishes are the true workhorses of Thanksgiving dinner. From a classic green been casserole perfected by Hetty Lui McKinnon to Yotam Ottolenghi’s twist on stuffing, here are nine of our go-to trimmings for Thanksgiving dinner. Or explore more from our huge collection.
Jewelled winter salad with roast squash, butter beans and pomegranate
Rukmini Iyer’s jewelled winter salad adds a burst of color to any spread. Iyer recommends roasting the squash the day before and marinating the beans overnight.
Prep 15 min
 
Cook 30 min
 
Serves Four as a main, six as a side
1 small butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cut into 2/3 in cubes
 
5 tbsp olive oil
  
2 tsp ras el hanout
  
1 tsp sea salt flakes
  
2 small red onions (or 1 large one), peeled and each cut into eight equal wedges
 
Juice of 1 lemon, plus 3 strips of zest (use a speed peeler)
 
3 garlic cloves, peeled and finely sliced
 
20 oz canned butter beans, drained and rinsed
 
1 oz flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
 
1 oz cilantro, roughly chopped
 
1 1/2 cups feta, cut into 1/2 in cubes
 
Seeds from 1 pomegranate
 
1/2 cup pistachios, roughly chopped (if you can find the bright-green Sicilian ones, so much the better)
Heat the oven to 390F. Mix the squash, two tablespoons of olive oil, the ras el hanout and salt in a roasting tray large enough to hold everything in a single layer. In a small bowl, toss the onion wedges with half the lemon juice (this will help them keep their colour), add them to the squash tray, then roast for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, put the remaining oil, the garlic and lemon zest in a large frying pan over a low heat, and warm through for two to three minutes without letting the garlic brown. Add the butter beans, cook, stirring occasionally, for six to seven minutes, then take off the heat.
Once the squash is ready, gently stir the butter beans and herbs into the tray, then dress with the remaining lemon juice. Taste and adjust the salt as needed, then top with the feta, pomegranate and pistachios, and serve warm or at room temperature.
Kohlrabi slaw with horseradish and candied sunflower seeds
A fresh, crunchy slaw from Yotam Ottolenghi to brighten up a heavy meal. Bonus: It can be made in advance – just don’t add the dressing until you’re sitting down to eat.
Prep 10 min
 
Cook 15 min
 
Serves Four to six
2/3 oz sunflower seeds
  
1 tbsp maple syrup
  
1/3 cup olive oil
  
1 tsp nigella seeds, lightly crushed in a mortar
 
2 kohlrabi, peeled and cut into matchsticks
 
2 carrots, peeled, halved lengthways and thinly sliced
 
2/3 oz parsley, roughly chopped, plus 1 tbsp extra to serve
 
2/3 cup Greek yoghurt
 
2/3 oz fresh horseradish, peeled and finely grated (or good-quality creamed horseradish)
 
1 tbsp lemon juice
  
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Put the sunflower seeds, maple syrup and two tablespoons of oil in a small pan on a medium-high heat and cook, stirring occasionally, for two minutes, until the sunflower seeds start to brown. Take the pan off the heat, stir in the nigella seeds and a quarter-teaspoon of salt, then pour into a heatproof sieve set over a bowl. Once the solids are cool enough to handle, break up the seeds with your hands, then return them to the oil, to finish the crunchy sunflower seed topping.
Put the kohlrabi, carrots, and parsley in a large bowl and toss to combine.
In a medium bowl, mix the remaining three tablespoons oil with the yoghurt, horseradish, lemon juice, three-quarters of a teaspoon of salt and a good grind of pepper.
Just before serving, pour the dressing over the kohlrabi mixture and toss to coat. Transfer half the slaw to a wide bowl, spoon over half the sunflower seed topping, then repeat with the remaining slaw and sunflower seed topping. Scatter over the extra parsley and serve.
Green bean tahini casserole with lentils and crispy turmeric shallots
Hetty Lui McKinnon’s lighter twist on a classic, this time with shiitake mushrooms, tahini and homemade crispy turmeric shallots.
3 1/2 oz black lentils, rinsed
 
Extra-virgin olive oil
 
2 and 1/4 lbs green beans, trimmed and halved
 
3 cups fresh shiitake mushrooms, coarsely chopped or sliced
 
2 thyme sprigs, leaves picked
 
1⁄3 cup tahini
 
Juice of 1⁄2 lemon
 
1 garlic clove, very finely chopped
 
Handful of chopped chives
 
Sea salt and black pepper
Crispy turmeric shallots
2 French shallots, finely sliced into rounds
 
2 tbsp rice flour
 
1 tsp ground turmeric
 
1⁄2 cup sunflower or other high-temperature oil, plus extra if needed
 
Sea salt and black pepper
Substitute
  
Shiitake mushrooms: button or Swiss brown mushrooms
 
French shallots: small red onions
 
Rice flour: plain flour
Preheat the oven to 375F. Oil a large baking or gratin dish.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the lentils, cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, until the lentils are just tender. Drain.
Meanwhile, make the crispy turmeric shallots. Toss the shallot rounds together with the rice flour, turmeric and a pinch of salt and pepper, using your hands to break up the rings so that they are evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan until very hot (test with a wooden chopstick or wooden spoon; if it sizzles, the oil is ready). Add the shallot rings to the oil a handful at a time and fry until golden brown. When ready, place them on a paper towel to absorb excess oil and immediately sprinkle with some sea salt. Repeat until all the shallot rings are cooked. Allow to cool.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan and add the beans. Season with sea salt and black pepper and cook for 5–7 minutes, until the beans are tender and turning golden. Remove from the pan and set aside. In the same pan, add another drizzle of oil along with the mushrooms and thyme and cook until the mushrooms have turned golden. Remove from the heat.
Place the tahini in a small bowl, add the lemon juice, garlic and chives
 
and slowly whisk in cold water, one tablespoon at a time, until the mixture is the consistency of thickened cream. Season with sea salt and lots of black pepper.
Combine the beans with the mushrooms, lentils and tahini sauce. Transfer to the baking dish and bake for 10-12 minutes. Take the dish out of the oven, top with the crispy turmeric shallots and return to the oven for another five minutes. Serve immediately.
Tips
The crispy turmeric shallots can be made up to a day ahead. If you are short on time, buy ready-made crispy fried shallots from your Asian grocery store or supermarket.
The green bean casserole can be made the day ahead and topped and baked with the onions just before eating.
Thanksgiving stuffing biscuits
Ottolenghi’s stuffing-inspired biscuits infuse onion, garlic, rosemary and celery salt into a handheld treat. He suggests eating them fresh out of the oven, “though any leftovers will still be great the next day, gently warmed through, sliced open and packed with more butter, and any cold meat and cheese.”
Prep 20 min
  
Chill 20 min
 
Cook 40 min
 
Makes 9
For the onion mix
 
1/4 stick (2 1/4tbsp) unsalted butter
  
1 onion, peeled and finely chopped (150g)
 
1 garlic clove, peeled and crushed
 
1/4 oz rosemary leaves (about 1 tsp), finely chopped
 
1/3 oz sage leaves (about ¾ tsp), finely chopped
 
½ tsp celery salt
  
2 tbsp runny honey
For the biscuit dough
 
3/4 cup buttermilk
  
1 egg
  
2 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
 
2½ tsp baking powder
  
¼ tsp baking soda
  
Fine sea salt
  
1 stick (1/2 cup) fridge-cold unsalted butter, cut into 3/4 in cubes
 
3 1/2 oz onion mix (see above and method)
 
1 cup mature cheddar, coarsely grated, plus 3/4tbsp extra for sprinkling
Melt the butter for the onion mix in a medium frying pan, then stir in all the remaining onion mix ingredients apart from the honey and cook, stirring every now and then, for 10 minutes, until soft but not coloured. Take off the heat, stir in the honey and leave to cool completely.
For the biscuits, whisk the buttermilk and egg in a bowl, then put in the fridge to cool. Put the flour, baking powder, bicarb and a half teaspoon of fine salt into a food processor and pulse to combine. Add the cubed cold butter and pulse until it’s broken down into pea-sized pieces.
Set aside a tablespoon of the buttermilk-egg mix, then pour the rest into the food processor and pulse until the dough is crumbly but not quite coming together. Add the cooled onion mix and the grated cheddar, then pulse again a couple of times just to combine.
Try this recipe and many more on the new Feast app: scan or click here for your free trial.
Tip out the dough on to a lightly floured surface and, with well-floured hands, gently compress into a rough square. Fold this in half, then compress again into a square. Fold it in half again, this time the other way, then compress into a square once again: the square should by now be about 8 in wide and 1-1/4 in thick. Cut the dough into nine even squares and arrange these on a large baking tray lined with greaseproof paper. Brush the tops with the reserved tablespoon of buttermilk-egg mix, then sprinkle over the final 3-1/4tbsp cheddar. Put in the fridge for 20 minutes to cool (or cover and freeze until required).
Heat the oven to 415F. Take the biscuits out of the fridge (or freezer) and bake for 25 minutes (30 minutes if baking from frozen), rotating the tray once halfway through, until nicely browned.
Take the tray out of the oven, transfer the biscuits to a rack, leave to cool for 10 minutes, then serve at once.
Perfect vegetarian gravy
“Vegetarians tend to be sadly ill-served in the gravy department,” writes Felicity Cloake. Fortunately there’s this meat-free version – which gets its umami flavor from dried porcini mushrooms. Even better? Because it’s not reliant on the turkey, it can be made in advance.
Prep 10 min
 
Cook 40 min
 
Serves Four
2 tbsp oil
 
2 onions, peeled and roughly chopped
 
2 carrots, roughly chopped
 
2 celery sticks, roughly chopped (use the leaves, too, assuming there are any)
 
1 bay leaf
 
1 sprig fresh thyme
 
1/4 cup dried porcini
 
2 tbsp plain flour or cornflour
 
3/4 cup white wine (optional)
 
2 tsp Marmite or other yeast product (optional)
 
Port and/or madeira, sweet sherry, redcurrant jelly, cranberry sauce, etc, to taste
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over a medium-low heat, add the chopped vegetables and herbs, and fry, stirring regularly to ensure they don’t catch and burn, for about 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
Meanwhile, whiz the mushrooms to a fine powder in a food processor (or pound them in a mortar), then mix with 1/2 cup of warm water.
Once the vegetables are done, stir in the flour, cook for a minute or so longer, then, scraping the bottom of the pan as you do so, stir in the wine, 2 cups of water (or 3 cups of water if not using wine) and the mushroom paste. Bring to a simmer, stirring until thickened, then pass through a sieve and discard the vegetables and herbs.
Return the gravy to the pan, bring to a simmer, then stir in the Marmite, if using. Add the port or similar to taste; season and serve.
Whole roast cauliflower and nut pilaf
Meera Sodha’s crisp roast cauliflower and pilaf works both as a centerpiece and a “showstopping” side dish. Seasoned with chilli and fresh cilantro, most of the dish can be made ahead.
Prep 15 min
 
Cook 1 hr 20 min
 
Serves Four
For the cauliflower
 
2 tsp ground cumin
  
½ tsp kashmiri chilli powder
  
½ tsp fine sea salt
  
2 tbsp canola oil
  
1 large cauliflower (or 2 small ones), leaves removed (1-3/4 lbs)
For the pilaf
 
1 1/2 cups basmati rice
  
1/4 cup canola oil
  
2 onions, peeled and sliced
 
1 tsp fine sea salt
  
1 tsp ground cumin
  
1 tsp ground coriander
  
¼ tsp ground black pepper
 
1 3/4 oz shelled unsalted pistachios
  
1 3/4 oz whole almonds, roughly chopped in half
 
2/3 oz fresh cilantro, finely chopped
 
2/3 oz fresh parsley, finely chopped
For the tahini sauce
 
1/3 cup tahini
  
3 tbsp canola oil
  
1 lemon, juiced to get 2 tbsp
 
½ small garlic clove, peeled and grated
 
1/4 tsp fine sea salt, plus more to taste
Heat the oven to 390F. In a small bowl, mix the cumin, chilli powder, half a teaspoon of salt and two tablespoons of oil until you have a smooth paste.
Cut the base of the core off the cauliflower, so it stands flat. Rub the whole cauliflower all over with the spice paste, then put it in a high-sided or lipped baking tray. Pour 1/2 cup warm water around the cauliflower, roast for an hour, until golden on top and tender inside (check by prodding with a skewer or cake tester), then remove and set aside.
While the cauliflower is roasting, wash the rice really well in a sieve, until the water runs clear, then put in a bowl, pour over warm water to cover and leave to soak until needed.
Put 1/4 cup of oil in a large saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, turn on the heat to medium, then saute the onions with a teaspoon of salt, stirring occasionally, for 12 minutes, until soft and dark.
Add the spices, cook for a minute, then add the nuts and stir to coat. Drain the rice well, then add to the onions, give everything one more stir to distribute the nuts and onions through the rice, then add 2 cups just-boiled water and clap on the lid. Bring to a boil, cook for a couple of minutes, then turn down to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes. Take off the heat and leave to steam and settle for 10 minutes – do not lift the lid.
While the rice settles, make the tahini sauce. Put everything in a jam jar or similar, add four tablespoons of cold water, then shake like a person possessed until you have an emulsified sauce: it should be like double cream and pourable; if it is too thick, add a smidge more water; too thin, more tahini paste. Check the seasoning and adjust the salt and lemon juice as necessary.
To serve, stir the chopped herbs through the rice, then tip out on to your best platter and top with the cauliflower head. Pour the tahini sauce into a pretty jug. Stick a sharp knife in the cauliflower and encourage guests to help themselves to rice, a wedge of cauliflower and a healthy pouring of tahini sauce.
Brussels sprouts, orange and tarragon
Ottolenghi’s “sticky, salty, nutty and delicious” roasted brussels sprouts – adorned with pistachios and tarragon – are a sweet and savory dish.
Prep 10 min
 
Cook 25 min
 
Serves four to six as a side
1 1/2 lbs brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved lengthways
 
1/3 cup olive oil
  
Fine sea salt and black pepper
  
1 3/4 oz peeled pistachios, lightly crushed in a mortar
 
2 oranges, zest finely grated, to get 2 tsp, then juiced, to get 250ml
  
2 tbsp soy sauce
  
2 tbsp maple syrup
  
1/4oz tarragon leaves
Heat the oven to its highest setting – at least 475F. Toss the halved sprouts with the oil, half a teaspoon of salt and a good grind of pepper, then spread out on a large baking tray lined with greaseproof paper and roast for 10 minutes. Stir in the pistachios and roast for another 10 minutes, until the sprouts are nicely browned and the pistachios have toasted.
Meanwhile, put the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and maple syrup in a small saucepan on a medium-high heat, and leave to cook for five to eight minutes, until the sauce has reduced by three-quarters and has turned syrupy.
Once the sprouts are cooked, pour the syrup all over them, scatter over half the tarragon and toss to combine. Transfer to a platter, sprinkle over the remaining tarragon and serve.
Mac and ‘cheese’ with garlic and parsley oil
After years of experimenting with mac and cheese recipes, Sodhi came up with this creamy, vegan cashew “cheese” dish, spiked with lime and chipotle.
Prep 10 min
 
Cook 35 min
 
Serves Four
5 2/3 oz shelled cashew nuts
  
1/3 cup nutritional yeast
  
1 tsp garlic granules
  
1 tsp onion granules
  
1 tsp dijon mustard
  
1 tbsp cider vinegar
  
¼ tsp smoked paprika
  
⅓ tsp turmeric
  
Fine sea salt
  
10 1/2 oz macaroni
  
Olive oil, to drizzle on the pasta
For the garlic and parsley oil
 
2 1/3 oz parsley, woody stems removed, the rest roughly chopped
 
2 garlic cloves, peeled and chopped
 
1/2 cup olive oil
  
2 tbsp lime juice
  
½ tsp chipotle chilli flakes
  
½ tsp fine sea salt
Put the cashews and 1 cup water in a medium-sized saucepan that’s big enough to cook the pasta in later. Bring to a boil, then turn down to a simmer and cook for eight minutes. Drain the nuts and discard the water.
While the cashews are cooking, make the garlic and parsley oil: put all the ingredients in a blender and blitz until very well chopped. Transfer to a small bowl and rinse out the blender.
Put the drained cashews into the blender, then add 2/3 cup cold water, the nutritional yeast, garlic granules, onion granules, mustard, vinegar, paprika, turmeric and a half teaspoon of salt and blend until very smooth.
In the same saucepan you boiled the cashews in, bring 2 quarts of water to a boil, add two teaspoons of salt, then cook the macaroni until al dente, according to the packet instructions. Near the end of the cooking time, scoop out a mugful of the starchy cooking water, then drain the pasta, return it to the pan and drizzle with a little oil.
Put the pasta back on a medium heat, add the “cheese” sauce, then stir and toss, adding the reserved pasta water a couple of tablespoons at a time – I ended up using 3/4 cup – until the sauce turns creamy and coats the pasta.
Divide the pasta between four plates or shallow bowls, spoon over the garlic and parsley oil, then serve.
Parsnip and pecorino stuffing
Everyone likes to make stuffing their own, and this Ottolenghi version is infused with parsnips, pecorino and dried currants.
Prep 25 min
 
Cook 50 min
 
Serves Four
2 onions, peeled and thinly sliced
 
1 1/3 lbs parsnips, peeled, cut in half lengthways, then chopped into roughly 3/4 in pieces
 
3 celery sticks (200g), trimmed and chopped into roughly 1/2 in pieces (180g)
 
1/4 cup olive oil
 
1 1/2 tsp finely chopped thyme leaves
  
Fine sea salt and black pepper
 
10 1/2 oz sourdough, cut into 3/4 in-thick slices
 
3 garlic cloves, peeled and crushed
 
1 1/4 cup pecorino, grated
 
1/2 cup heavy cream
  
1 2/3 cup chicken or vegetable stock
  
2 eggs
  
1/3 cup dried currants
  
4-5 spring onions (2oz), trimmed and cut into 1cm pieces
 
2/3 oz parsley, finely chopped, plus 1 tbsp extra to finish
 
1 1/2 tsp caraway seeds, toasted
Heat the oven to 475F. Put the first five ingredients in a medium-large baking dish – ideally about 9 in by 13 in – add three-quarters of a teaspoon of salt and a good grind of pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 25-30 minutes, stirring once or twice, until golden and slightly charred, then remove from the oven and turn it down to 390F. Use a fork to smash up the parsnips.
Meanwhile, toast the bread on a low oven shelf for 10 minutes, until evenly golden and crunchy, then leave to cool and cut into roughly 1/4 in pieces.
Put the garlic, pecorino, cream, stock and eggs in a large bowl, add a half teaspoon of salt and a good grind of black pepper, and whisk to combine. Add the parsnip mixture to the cream bowl, stir in the currants, spring onions, parsley and caraway, then set aside for five minutes, so the bread absorbs most of the liquid. Tip everything back into the baking dish and roast for 20-25 minutes, until golden on top. Serve hot.

https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.title: Hexed review – Disney’s witchy caper is a wicked disappointment
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.author: Benjamin Lee
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.text:
As bleak as Disney’s overreliance on sequels might have become, it’s not quite as bleak as the crumbling state of its original output. Obviously because of the former, the latter category has become that much less populated but even when the studio has recently bothered to release something without a number in the title, it’s been hard to really see the point.
With or without Pixar, films like Elio, Strange World, Raya and the Last Dragon, Luca, Elemental, Onward and Wish have all felt as uninspired as something a rival might try to desperately cobble together in an attempt to lure kids away from Disney. Three Thanksgivings ago, Wish was a particularly poor yet extremely smug example of how rubbishy things have got, a personality-free princess tale that doubled up as a 100-year anniversary victory lap. It was Disney’s worst-reviewed animated film in almost two decades and its deserved box office failure cost about $131m. Unperturbed, its co-director Fawn Veerasunthorn (along with Moana 2 director Jason Hand) is back this holiday with another rote rip-off adventure that doesn’t deserve its place in the kingdom.
In an attempt to conjure up that long-gone magic, Hexed is a film absolutely stuffed with it, a tale of witches, spells, cauldrons and curses that is at the very least neatly timed. Interest in all things Harry Potter remains sky-high (next month’s HBO adaptation is set to be the year’s most-watched TV show) as streaming hits like Carrie and The Body and a growing YA fantasy audience have shown that witchcraft, and all similarly categorised high school powers, have started to overtake the flagging superhero genre. But then why does something like Hexed still feel so dusty?
Like Wish, it’s a film clearly crafted by people who have deep affection for the Disney back catalogue but who can’t quite turn reverence for what came before into any real idea of where to take things going forward. Again, there’s something too calculated and businesslike, with nods to previous films and regurgitated life lessons, and while Disney adventures have always emerged from a Goliath-sized mega-corporation, the best ones can make you briefly forget that. Sure Disney might have, shamefully, tried to trademark Day of the Dead before the release of Coco (!) but the film itself was charming, sweet and genuinely moving. While the company might have turned Ratatouille into everything from a theme park ride to a branded set of cheese knives, thoughts of merchandise were not in one’s head while watching a rat’s thrilling journey from gourmand to head chef. But Hexed is too soulless and synthetically corporate to distract us from its ultimate Q4 marketing aims.
It takes place in a universe where witches have been Salem trialled away to another magic-filled realm (hello new Disney World section), where they live under the tyrannical control of Queen Celeste (voiced by Jodie Foster). A powerful young witch called Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) doesn’t yet know she’s a powerful young witch after her mother (Rashida Jones) decided to keep her talents hidden via a magic-suppressing bracelet (perfect merch op) forced on her wrist at a young age, a way to keep her safe in a world that does not take kindly to people like her. But as a rebellious teen, Billie discovers her true self and after a portal opens, she travels to the world of witches to team up with a three-eyed cat called Beef Roger Crummchuk (Walton Goggins, also a stuffed toy to be) to try to save her fellow witches from their evil queen.
It’s a story of mothers and daughters and how both can try to foster empathy for the other but even a lower-tier Disney film like Brave managed to teach this same lesson with far more skill and infinitely more heart. There’s no real joy or fizz in Billie’s discovery of her powers or ingenuity to how she then uses them and the film quickly starts to resemble not just a by-the-numbers, save-the-kingdom Disney tale but also a Marvel-like superhero adventure, especially in the numbingly effects-laden showdown finale. Foster has real command as a voice actor but her villain isn’t really villainous or distinctive enough, despite attempts to paint her as a recognisably authoritarian-like ruler. Goggins is a similarly effective vocal presence but, again, his sidekick isn’t written in a way that’s all that memorable with his dialogue, together with that of another anonymously underwritten owl sidekick, depressingly devoid of any spark or inventive humour. There’s also something a little cheap and inelegant about how he’s animated and coloured, similar to some purple-eyed henchwitches, who all look like they belong in a cheap Saturday morning cartoon not a big-budget Disney epic (the choice to score a giant action sequence with Demi Lovato’s Confident also feels notably unrefined). There’s an overly hectic style to too many scenes and a lack of grace to the set-pieces, more likely to induce a headache over a sense of awe, taking us further and further away from what used to elevate the studio far above its competitors.
There would be few greater big screen pleasures at this moment than a true return to form for Disney, an original, invigorating crowd-pleaser to rival what so many of us grew up watching and loving but Hexed is another hollow and glumly disappointing also-ran. Don’t tell Mickey but it’s perhaps telling that this month’s best new animated film about a rule-breaking goth girl dealing with spells and familial strife is actually on Netflix. Forget magic, the kingdom is in need of a miracle.
- Hexed is out in US cinemas on 25 November, in Australian cinemas on 26 November and in the UK on 27 November

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: I asked AI if it was OK to use AI to write an obituary. The answer surprised me | Anna Spargo-Ryan
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Anna Spargo-Ryan
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
I know how this will sound but when my nanna died the second thought I had, after utter devastation, was: “This is a writer’s dream.” She was 101. That is so many years old. I wrote the eulogy to end all eulogies, breaking my own heart with a bottomless well of memories, anecdotes and in-jokes. It was achingly personal and exquisitely her.
The Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson’s team took a similar approach in this week’s tribute to the music legend Molly Meldrum, by which I mean they generated it with AI. I imagine the conversation went something like: we are 25 years old, who even was she? And then one of them plugged Molly’s name into Claude while the others went downstairs for $11 coffees. Job done.
AI use is now ubiquitous, including in all levels of government. Public servants use it to generate reports, sort emails and calculate how to get the most days off at Christmas. Besides the catastrophic climate impact and creative thievery, I don’t have a problem with using it to write about stuff you don’t know. Junior comms people weren’t even born the last time Molly was TV regular. It’s just another task in their day, like sending media releases about Wilson’s bus crashing into local businesses.
But there is something vulgar about using a platform that by definition cannot feel to summarise the completeness of a person’s life. My real problem, as a romantic oversharer, is the illusion of meaning.
Jess Wilson’s statement had heaps of the right words: “… he will be remembered for …” and “the enormous affection Australians held for him”, says the bot, unable to experience affection. “My deepest condolences,” it goes on, with no knowledge of what those are. The origin of the sentiments didn’t matter to the audience. That it resembled love was enough.
In the old days, you had to formulate your own ideas about what someone meant to you, reflecting on crazy nonsense like the “time you spent together” and “shared memories”. Sometimes you would include personal minutiae like how it felt to hold their hand or pick up their wet towels – the kind of specificity that can only be produced by a flawed human heart at its most spectacularly busted (ie, it loves). How could AI even come close?
I decided to go to the source for an answer, despite the minor risk of accidentally falling in love.
In the little box I typed, “Do you think it’s okay to use AI to write an obituary?”
The answer surprised me. Sort of, it said, because writing is hard enough without trying to do it when someone important has died, and it’s easy to feel overwhelmed by capturing every important detail. But on the other hand (and I’m paraphrasing here), perhaps if you can’t be arsed with it, you didn’t really love them at all?
“I think there’s a meaningful distinction,” said poet ChatGPT, “between using AI to help you express your feelings and using AI to manufacture the appearance of feelings”.
AI may be good at all sorts of things. Recipes. Gym routines. Feeding your delusions about your problematic crush. It cannot – ever – write from the torn shreds of a broken heart. But apparently we’re happy to let it try. In a world where everything is genAI, from Facebook posts to wedding vows, it has become cheap to love.
My nanna’s eulogy wasn’t perfect. I mean, obviously it was close because I am an amateur granddaughter and professional writer, but there was meaning in the flaws, too. It meant something that I couldn’t remember exactly what her perfumes smelled like because she always let me wear all of them at once. It meant something that I got a date wrong because we had so many adventures they blended into one. The imprecision of it was the point – that it wasn’t a cut-down Wikipedia entry about her life but evidence of the privilege of having known her.
I truly don’t care if the Victorian Libs can’t muster the effort to hand-type a tribute to Molly Meldrum. I would, in fact, much prefer that energy be spent on plans for public housing and accessible healthcare. But if this is the future – outsourcing the tasks that need us at our most human – I’d rather we posted nothing at all.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
The Yashar party says it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party, led by Avigdor Lieberman.
Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing opposition party in a bid to form the next Israeli government following October’s elections.
The Yashar party said on Tuesday that it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.
After no party managed to secure a 61-seat majority, Israel’s parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government.
President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, while Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister despite the October 27 election stripping Netanyahu of his majority.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.
Arab parties
The agreement between Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Lieberman, whose party won seven, was unforeseen since Lieberman has been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Netanyahu.
Lieberman had once served as foreign minister under a previous Netanyahu government but has since become a strong critic.
Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority. It now holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.
Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners, including Lieberman, hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.
The path forward
Talks are also ongoing between Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.
The left-wing Democrats party, which won eight parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot after the Yashar party leader’s talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government.
Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, said he prefers a government without Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Edward Helmore and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflicting information about how far the toxic lead dust plume could travel after the explosion.
That controlled blast has been scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.
“Inaction is no longer an option,” Army Maj Gen Eric Shirley, the commander of the operation, said at a press conference in Middletown, Iowa, on Tuesday. “It would be irresponsible for us to not take the determined, consensus-based course of action moving forward.”
Federal officials on Tuesday said mitigation measures had been put in place, including barriers around the blast zone to capture much of the dust, but warned that residents in the vicinity should be prepared to evacuate.
“We don’t believe that the public should be in a panic,” said Adam Telle, acting secretary of the army. “Our goal is to keep as much of it as we can here on our Iowa Army Ammunition plant to prevent it from traveling.”
Telle said weather conditions on Wednesday morning were expected to be “ideal to protect public health and safety across the region” and stressed that a “controlled, mitigated, detonation” was “far preferable to an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation” of the unstable material.
State officials, environmental groups and residents have sharply criticized federal authorities over what many have described as a “communication failure” about the operation.
In a statement, Iowa senator-elect Josh Turek welcomed the army’s “long-overdue press conference” about Wednesday’s operation and vowed to “continue asking questions about how we got here” when he joins the chamber in January.
“There is no excuse for such a failure of transparency and communication, especially when the health and safety of the public is involved,” said Turek, who was born with spina bifida, which he attributes to his father’s exposure to Agent Orange during the Vietnam war. “Iowans should have had a full and clear understanding of the health implications of this operation, especially as children, pregnant women, and those with chronic illness are being advised to stay away from the affected area.”
Earlier on Tuesday, the army released new maps showing the projected plume path moving south-west of the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, stretching through a south-eastern portion of the state before extending into northern Missouri.
The army sent an emergency notification to cellphones on Tuesday confirming the time of the controlled explosion – and warning that some people within 5 miles south-west of the plant may be evacuated.
The “imminent threat alert” told those up to 20 miles away to remain indoors with windows closed “to avoid airborne lead dust, noise and vibration”.
On Tuesday, the outgoing governor, Kim Reynolds, issued a proclamation of disaster emergency for Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties. Additionally, Reynolds said, she was deploying up to 100 soldiers from the Iowa national guard to support with public safety efforts.
Earlier in the day, the governor announced her support for the planned detonation after speaking with military leaders, including US defense secretary Pete Hegseth.
“I trust the army will do everything in its power to protect the people who could be affected,” she said in a statement.
The army said it had set up additional “blast barriers” around the bunkers where the lead azide will be detonated. It also said it would apply ballistic gels and foams to absorb the lead dust and douse the explosive materials with thousands of gallons of water.
The decision to proceed came after a federal appeals court cleared the way for the detonation to take place after the date had been changed three times after an outpouring of public concern. Environmentalists sued to stop the detonation, arguing that the planned explosion had not been issued permits correctly.
An attorney for the environmentalists emphasized that their legal challenge centers on the validity of the Environment Protection Agency permit – not the army’s decision to move forward with the detonation under the emergency provision.
The army said it needs to blow up the stockpile to prevent a possible chain-reaction explosion, which would be more dangerous.
The order to go ahead came after an extraordinary intervention by Donald Trump, who said on social media that in addition to the court’s go-ahead, he wanted Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, to approve the detonation.
Sand, a Democrat who does not take office until January, has said the decision is fully up to the president’s administration.
Evacuated residents will be notified by phone once they may return home, the Des Moines Register reported.
The army and the Iowa department of health and human services are recommending that those in the area take protective measures. Those include closing all windows and exterior doors; turning off or placing heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems in recirculation mode; avoiding unnecessary travel; and cleaning indoor and outdoor surfaces that may be contacted by children.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Poll finds US voters want government to end Iran war regardless of terms
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Poll finds US voters want government to end Iran war regardless of terms
New survey finds that 55 percent of voters, including 80 percent of Democrats, want the Iran war brought to an end immediately.
A new poll has found that a majority of voters in the United States want an end to the US-Israel war on Iran immediately, even if it means accepting less favourable conditions.
Overall, 55 percent of those surveyed agreed with an “end to the war now, regardless of the terms”.
That number was even higher among Democrats and independents, who agreed with the statement at a rate of 80 percent and 59 percent, respectively. About 25 percent of Republicans said the same.
A majority of Democratic voters also supported steps to pressure the administration of President Donald Trump to stop the conflict.
Fifty-three percent of party members said they would favour Congress withholding funding for military operations, and 51 percent would back an “an Iran war-funding cutoff” in upcoming budget negotiations, even if the manoeuvre risked a government shutdown.
The numbers were published on Tuesday as part of the latest Critical Issues Poll, released by the University of Maryland and the research firm Ipsos.
Shibley Telhami, the poll’s principal investigator, said he was surprised by the level of support for ending the war, regardless of the terms.
“We knew that people were strongly opposed to this war and wanted it to end,” he told Al Jazeera in a phone call. “What we were less sure of is what they would be willing to accept to achieve this.”
The survey asked 1,022 US adults about their perspectives on the war.
In one question, they were tasked with assessing with three options: whether to end the conflict immediately, escalate militarily, or continue on the current path in order to extract concessions from Iran.
Just 21 percent of all respondents favoured the current path, and 18 percent supported escalation.
“Clearly, the public mood is to end it now, whatever it takes,” said Telhami.
Questioning the rationale for war
Voters also appear sceptical about the US government’s arguments in favour of the war, which include dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme.
The Critical Issues Poll found that only 28 percent of those surveyed believed that the war had left Iran in “worse position” to develop nuclear weapons.
While the US has long voiced concerned that Iran could pursue nuclear arms, intelligence assessments have not found evidence that Tehran has authorised such a step since abandoning its nuclear weapons programme in 2003.
The Strait of Hormuz has also emerged as a key issue, with Iran closing the waterway to commercial traffic early in the war. The Trump administration has responded with a naval blockade in the strait.
Some 20 percent of the world’s oil supply passes through the maritime artery, and fuel prices have spiked as a result of the war.
About 35 percent of respondents in Tuesday’s poll said that they believe Iran is now in control of the strait, while just 12.7 percent said the US is in control.
The poll comes as the Democratic Party is debating how far it should go to end the unpopular war.
In the recent midterm elections, backlash against the war — and as well as related issues like rising fuel prices — contributed to big gains for the Democratic Party.
Trump’s Republican Party, meanwhile, suffered one of its most bruising setbacks in modern US history, losing control of both chambers of Congress.
Members of the Democratic Party’s anti-war left have pointed to the results as proof that voters want an end to the war and an end to US support for Israel.
But that position has brought them into conflict with members of the party’s more hawkish establishment wing.
While leaders such as Representative Hakeem Jeffries and Senator Chuck Schumer have both expressed support for ending the war, they have yet to commit to aggressive strategies to reach that goal.
That includes potentially cutting off funding for military operations against Iran, or using an upcoming funding battle in December to demand that the White House end the war.
“A lot of Democratic figures are dismissing the intensity of public feeling on this issue,” said Telhami. “If they don’t adapt, they will be left behind.”
He added that progressive figures such as Senator Bernie Sanders and Senator Chris Van Hollen have been among those pressing for a more assertive stance.
Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer to lead the Democratic majority in the US Senate, has used the war to portray the party’s moderate leadership as out of step with voters.
The poll found that Democratic voters prefer Van Hollen over Schumer by a ratio of nearly three to one.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120410.title: Gewalt gegen Frauen | Mehr Licht im Dunkelfeld
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120410.author: Stefan Otto
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120410.text:
- Politik
- Gewalt gegen Frauen
Mehr Licht im Dunkelfeld
Das BKA stellte Lagebilder zur Gewalt gegen Frauen vor. Immer mehr Delikte werden angezeigt. Warum das wichtig ist, erklärten zwei Ministerinnen.
Die aktuellen Lagebilder des Bundeskriminalamts zu häuslicher Gewalt und zu Straftaten gegen Frauen zeigen ein düsteres Bild. Die Zahl der Delikte ist 2025 in allen Bereichen gestiegen – obwohl die Zahl der Gewalttaten insgesamt zuletzt rückläufig war.
Im vergangenen Jahr wurden 54.675 Frauen und Mädchen als Opfer einer Sexualstraftat registriert. Das entspricht einem Anstieg von 2,3 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr. »Knapp die Hälfte war zum Tatzeitpunkt minderjährig«, sagte die zuständige Bundesfrauenministerin Karin Prien bei der Vorstellung der Lagebilder in Berlin.
Auch die Gewalt im Netz nimmt zu. Dazu zählen Nötigung, Bedrohung und Stalking. Die Zahl der weiblichen Opfer stieg um knapp 16 Prozent. Insgesamt wurden in diesem Bereich 31.221 Fälle registriert. Auch hier verwies Prien auf den hohen Anteil Minderjähriger: Etwa 30 Prozent der Betroffenen waren unter 18 Jahre alt.
Noch beklemmender sind die Statistiken zur häuslichen Gewalt. 292 Menschen starben im vergangenen Jahr an den Folgen von Gewalt in den eigenen vier Wänden. Das waren sechs Todesfälle mehr als im Vorjahr. 209 der Opfer waren Frauen und Mädchen. 130 von ihnen starben durch die Gewalt eines Partners oder Ex-Partners.
Die Zahl der polizeilich registrierten Opfer häuslicher Gewalt erreichte mit 280.129 Geschädigten einen Höchststand. Erfasst werden sowohl Gewalt in Partnerschaften als auch Gewalt innerhalb der Familie. Bei der Partnerschaftsgewalt sind fast 80 Prozent der Opfer weiblich. Bei der innerfamiliären Gewalt liegt der Anteil der betroffenen Frauen und Mädchen bei 70,6 Prozent.
»Die Zahlen der Lagebilder zeigen auf alarmierende Art und Weise, wie alltäglich Gewalt gegen Frauen in Deutschland ist«, betonte Prien. »Hinter jeder Zahl steckt unermessliches Leid der Betroffenen.« Der Ministerin ist allerdings bewusst, dass die Lagebilder nur einen Teil des tatsächlichen Ausmaßes der Gewalt abbilden.
Anfang des Jahres beleuchtete erstmals eine Untersuchung das Ausmaß des Dunkelfelds. Die Studie »Lebenssituation, Sicherheit und Belastung im Alltag« zeigte, dass weniger als zehn Prozent der Straftaten angezeigt werden. Bei sexuellen Übergriffen erstatteten lediglich drei Prozent der betroffenen Frauen Anzeige.
Angesichts des verbreiteten Schweigens dankte Prien allen Betroffenen, die sich an die Polizei wandten und über ihre Erfahrungen berichteten. Dies trage dazu bei, das Thema stärker ins öffentliche Bewusstsein zu rücken und das Tabu bei dieser Form der Gewalt aufzubrechen.
»Häusliche Gewalt und Straftaten gegen Frauen verlangen eine klare Antwort des Rechtsstaats«, erklärte Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU). Der Handlungsauftrag sei angesichts der aktuellen Lagebilder eindeutig: Betroffene müssten besser geschützt, Täter konsequent zur Verantwortung gezogen und Gewalttaten frühzeitig verhindert werden.
Bundesjustizministerin Stefanie Hubig (SPD) erwägt eine Reihe von Maßnahmen, um Frauen besser vor Gewalt zu schützen. »Familiengerichte können künftig die elektronische Fußfessel anordnen, mehr Betroffene erhalten psychosoziale Prozessbegleitung, und K.o.-Tropfen-Täter werden härter bestraft.« Letztlich sei aber ein Umdenken in der Gesellschaft unerlässlich, erläuterte die Ministerin. Nötig sei eine »Abkehr von überkommenen Männlichkeitsbildern und patriarchalen Denkmustern«.
Auch Prien will eine »Veränderung in den Köpfen der Männer« erreichen. Einen Schwerpunkt legt sie auf die Prävention. Bereits Jugendliche möchte sie für das Thema sensibilisieren. Ihr Ministerium plant derzeit Modellprojekte zur Prävention häuslicher und geschlechtsspezifischer Gewalt. Diese sollen in Schulen, im digitalen Raum und in der Täterarbeit ansetzen.
Prien und Hubig verwiesen auch auf das Gewalthilfegesetz, das im Vorjahr beschlossen wurde. Schrittweise soll ein kostenloses Hilfesystem entstehen. Ab 2032 haben Frauen dann einen individuellen Rechtsanspruch auf Schutz und Beratung.
Doch bislang reicht das Angebot an Hilfen nicht aus. Für viele Frauenhäuser ist die Finanzierung weiterhin ungeklärt. Zudem fehlen bundesweit rund 12.000 Plätze. Viele akut bedrohte Frauen erhalten daher nicht den Schutz, den sie dringend bräuchten.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
The decision follows the conclusion of the 2026 midterm elections and an effort under Trump to collect state voter rolls.
Alaska has terminated a memorandum of understanding that granted the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) access to the state’s voter rolls.
On Monday, outgoing Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom, who oversees the state’s elections, announced she had notified the Justice Department that Alaska was withdrawing from the 2025 memo, effective immediately.
In a statement, Dahlstrom said her state had entered the agreement “in good faith to cooperate with our federal law enforcement partners”. But she acknowledged a shift had taken place after the 2026 midterm elections.
“The circumstances have now changed,” Dahlstrom wrote. “The election has concluded and the agreement no longer serves a continuing purpose.”
The reversal comes after months of pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump for states to surrender their voter rolls to federal authorities.
Trump has argued that such information was necessary to root out fraud during the November 3 midterms.
But officials in certain states argued that the federal government was encroaching on their constitutional authority. Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections.
Experts have also called Trump’s claims of “rigged” elections unsubstantiated.
No voters flagged for removal
The memorandum, signed last December at the Justice Department’s behest, established terms under which federal officials could flag potentially ineligible voters on Alaska’s voter rolls.
“Since that time, the DOJ has not identiﬁed any potentially ineligible voters or raised concerns regarding Alaska’s voter registration records,” the state Division of Elections said.
“No voters were removed from Alaska’s voter rolls as a result of the agreement.”
The announcement came as the state certified its November 3 midterm election results, in which Democrats flipped a Senate seat and won the governor’s office.
Alaska was one of several surprise battlegrounds during the midterms.
Democrat Mary Peltola unseated two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in a fiercely contested Senate race marred by allegations of a spoiler candidate recruited to sabotage the senator’s re-election bid.
Meanwhile, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the state’s governorship, ending nearly three decades of Republican control in that office.
Democrats nationwide made significant gains, flipping both chambers of Congress in the midterms.
That result was largely fuelled by voter frustration under Trump, whose Republican Party suffered defeats in former strongholds like Texas.
A legal battle over voter rolls
Faced with drooping approval ratings in the lead-up to the election, Trump had falsely claimed that many non-citizens were registered to vote across the country.
His administration sued some 30 states as well as Washington, DC, after they declined to hand over their unredacted voter rolls for review.
Twenty-eight of those cases were ultimately dismissed in court, according to the Brennan Center for Justice, a public policy institute at New York University.
The Justice Department suffered a further setback last month when a federal judge struck down its nationwide voter-list maintenance programme, ruling that it lacked legal authority to collect and assess state registration lists. The administration has appealed the ruling.
Alaska was one of at least 16 states that complied with the administration’s demands for voter roll access.
But it was sued by voting rights advocates for surrendering voter information, in violation of the Alaska Constitution.
In its Monday statement, Alaska’s Division of Elections said it had directed the Justice Department to destroy Alaska’s confidential voter information in accordance with the 2025 memo — a move that could have implications for the pending lawsuit.
On Tuesday, Democratic State Senator Bill Wielechowski suggested the latest termination was timed to prevent further scrutiny from the lawsuit.
“The real reason they did this is to try to make the lawsuit over this release go away before the incoming Gov. Kreiss-Tomkins Administration could settle or produce discovery,” Wielechowski wrote on social media.
Kreiss-Tomkins is set to be sworn in as governor on December 7.
Wielechowski also noted that Alaska’s request for the Trump administration to delete the records is “likely meaningless”, since federal authorities have “undoubtedly already loaded it” onto government databases.
In its Monday statement, Alaska’s Division of Elections said its decision to end the memo did not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.
The state’s interests, it added, were “best served by terminating the agreement and continuing to rely on its established voter list-maintenance procedures”.
A Justice Department spokesperson told The Associated Press on Tuesday that the department would issue a formal response to the state.
