Publié le 25 novembre 2026
Cent jours aux commandes du pays ? Plutôt cent jours derrière les manettes d’une console, tant la gestion du président colombien d’extrême droite Abelardo de la Espriella paraît superficielle. Mais que pouvait-on attendre d’autre qu’un jeu vidéo de guerre de la part de celui qui promettait durant sa campagne de mater les « narcoterroristes » en quatre-vingt-dix jours, avec l’appui des États-Unis et d’Israël ?
Face à l’extrême droite, ne rien lâcher !
C’est pied à pied, argument contre argument qu’il faut combattre l’extrême droite. Et c’est ce que nous faisons chaque jour dans l’Humanité.
Face aux attaques incessantes des racistes et des porteurs de haine : soutenez-nous ! Ensemble, faisons entendre une autre voix dans ce débat public toujours plus nauséabond.
Je veux en savoir plus.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Miami artists’ Art Basel boycott campaign calls for alternatives to fair week’s commercial model
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Alexandra Martinez
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
As Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to return to the city, a group of local artists and organisers is asking the Miami art community to reconsider its relationship with the busy week of fairs that takes over the city every December. The grassroots collective Artists 4 Artists Miami announced plans for its “Art Basel Boycott” at a protest outside the Miami Beach Convention Center at the end of last year’s edition of the Switzerland-based fair. Now, after a year of preparation, the collective is launching its first campaign, inviting local artists, curators, gallerists, collectors and residents to reconsider their participation in Miami Art Week’s fairs while building alternatives rooted in the community.
In a city whose international cultural profile has become virtually inseparable from the Art Basel brand, the boycott poses a difficult question: can Miami’s arts economy sustain its local creative community without depending so heavily on the machinery of a global art fair? Oorganisers are not calling for a blanket rejection of Miami Art Week or even its tentpole event. Instead, organisers envision a longer-term effort to challenge the economic and political structures surrounding the fair and redirect attention toward local artists, independent galleries and experimental programming.
“We realise that in order to refuse to take part in something as intertwined and culturally impactful as Art Basel, you really have to start building an alternative,” says misael soto, an artist and founder of Artists 4 Artists Miami.
The campaign grew out of the collective’s broader efforts to connect cultural work with other grassroots struggles. After spending much of 2025 supporting campaigns led by other organisations, Artists 4 Artists Miami began considering how it could mobilise its own community. Its participation in protests organised by Jewish Voice for Peace and other groups opposing the war in Gaza helped crystallise the idea, soto says, prompting organisers to examine the connections between the art market, housing affordability, labour conditions, and the companies that benefit from the fair.
For soto, Art Basel has become a focal point for these overlapping concerns. The fair generates significant economic activity, but the group questions how much of that value reaches Miami’s working artists and residents, particularly as the city becomes increasingly expensive. The group also points to the environmental and infrastructural costs of hosting an international event, and to the political and corporate interests associated with some of its major partners and investors.
Those concerns extend to the fair’s relationship with the city itself; soto points to a recent Miami Beach Commission decision concerning Art Basel’s rental agreement for the Miami Beach Convention Center, which reduced the fair’s rent from nearly $1m to around $500,000 and committed the equivalent of an additional $300,000 in public funds toward first-responder and security costs. The group questions whether the benefits the fair brings to the community justify the public resources devoted to it.
And yet, as the Artists 4 Artists Miami organisers acknowledge, Art Basel is deeply embedded in Miami’s cultural identity and economy. For many artists and arts workers, Miami Art Week provides essential income through art handling, installation, production and other contract jobs, while offering a smaller number opportunities to exhibit their work. Local galleries rely on the annual influx of collectors, press and visitors, and cultural institutions benefit from the attention and potential donor relationships the week brings.
“Art Basel Miami Beach has been a committed partner to Miami Beach and its creative community for more than two decades, supporting local artists and organisations through cultural programming, educational initiatives and opportunities for artistic exchange,” a spokesperson for Art Basel tells The Art Newspaper. “The fair also generates significant economic activity across the region, benefiting local businesses and workers in a wide range of sectors.”
According to local officials, the 2025 edition of Art Basel Miami Beach generated nearly $60m in economic impact for the city of Miami Beach, and $570m in economic impact for Miami-Dade County. The fair has consistently included several South Florida galleries as exhibitors, and every year the city of Miami Beach acquires a work from the fair for its public art collection.
Ariel Lynch, an artist and educator who has lived in the city for four years, signed the Artists 4 Artists Miami pledge despite recognising the tensions inherent in the campaign. Lynch says the fair offers substantial economic benefits to established galleries and collectors while providing comparatively few exhibition opportunities for local artists.
“Miami deserves more than institutions like Art Basel Miami Beach,” Lynch says. She plans to spend Miami Art Week visiting local galleries, events and experimental exhibitions instead of attending the main fair, while introducing students to the city’s year-round art scene.
Still, Lynch acknowledges the difficult position facing those who depend on Art Basel for their livelihoods. For workers already struggling to make ends meet, declining paid work during Miami Art Week may not be financially feasible. That is a dilemma soto is also mindful of: the fairs have helped pay their bills and enabled them to travel internationally, but they believe the short-term benefits can obscure longer-term costs, including overwork, underappreciated labour and environmental strain.
The “Art Basel Boycott” pledge is designed to accommodate different levels of participation. Signatories must select at least one commitment: not attending Art Basel Miami Beach, not exhibiting work at the fair, not exhibiting during Miami Art Week or withholding their labour from the fair. They can also choose commitments aimed at supporting alternatives, allowing participants to assess what is realistic given their circumstances.
As of this writing, the campaign had collected 21 signatures through an online form hosted on the collective’s website. Organisers are contacting local cultural and political organisations, particularly grassroots groups, to seek endorsements and establish partnerships. One existing partner is Panamía, a local network connecting businesses, creatives and residents. Artists 4 Artists Miami is also exploring programming in conjunction with a Panamía gathering and art print fair planned for Miami Art Week.
Beyond events, the collective hopes to establish a mutual-support network that could help pledge signatories navigate the financial consequences of opting out of Miami Art Week. That would entail connecting artists and organisations with local resources, soto says, including food assistance and other forms of mutual aid.
For the boycott’s organisers and signatories, success will not necessarily be measured by a signature count or an immediate impact on the fair. Instead, they hope the campaign will encourage a gradual shift in how Miami’s cultural producers and workers understand their economic and political influence.
“If a year from now we see that much more alternative and locally focused programming happening outside of Art Week,” soto says, “that would be a huge victory.”

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Does international art sell in India? Dealers at Art Mumbai encounter deep pockets but local tastes
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Kabir Jhala
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
India’s art market rally has not yet slowed, judging by the fourth edition of Art Mumbai, held from 12-15 November. While several Indian dealers said that a clash with the Hindu festival Diwali had resulted in quieter VIP days than last year, this amounted to exhibitors rehanging around one-third of their stands, rather than 75%-100%.
The mushrooming wealth of India’s richest, who are shopping for big works to match bigger homes, appears more than capable of sustaining its small but growing domestic base of galleries and auction houses. The country’s secondary art market recorded its best year ever in 2025, at $272.1m, according to a recent report by the wealth managers 360One (a sponsor of the fair).
For India’s top galleries, success at Art Mumbai is now a foregone conclusion. “This fair is great for us, and right now I feel more inclined to invest my effort here than fairs abroad,” said Hena Kapadia, the founder of the dynamic local gallery Tarq, which sold the majority of its stand, including photographs by Ronny Sen, and rehung around 50% of it.
Notable sales in the fair’s contemporary section included a Subodh Gupta painting at the Delhi- and Mumbai-based Nature Morte, which placed to a new buyer of Indian-origin based in Europe, for €350,000. The gallery’s director Roma Patel noted that she met new collectors from south India, and diaspora collectors from Los Angeles, as well as existing clients, at the fair.
In the Modern tent, “some punchy prices” were noted by one auction executive. Works acquired at auction within the past 12 months were flipped for tidy profits, including M F Husain's 1991 Untitled (Horses & Ganesh) at Akar Prakar, bought from Bonhams in December 2025 for £179,000 (equivalent to $234,000) and resold for $600,000, although likely with a hefty discount.
Subtler gestures of confidence were also observed. Grosvenor Gallery, which counted among its sales a painting by the Sri Lankan Senaka Senanayake for a shade over $100,000, decided not to send PDFs prior to the fair. "We haven’t pre-sold anything for the past few fairs—a nice luxury afforded to us by the current market conditions, though it won’t last forever,” said the gallery’s director Charlie Moore.
With India’s place on the global stage growing, and the predominant art markets of the US, Europe and China remaining relatively muted, international players are circling. Case in point, Frieze's chief executive Simon Fox, and Art Basel’s director of fairs Vincenzo de Bellis and head of VIP Carly Murphy, all attended Art Mumbai for the first time this year. Fox said this was his first India trip for work. Meanwhile, Art Basel’s India VIP representative Shaan Shahani noted that this visit marked the first India trip by Art Basel top brass in a decade.
Also testing these waters are the 12 international galleries that showed at Art Mumbai this year, up from seven last year. Newcomers included the global dealership Perrotin, Richard Saltoun and Niru Ratnam from London, and Rizq from Abu Dhabi, while Lisson, Continua, Ben Brown and Gallery Isabelle all returned from last year. Three international galleries that took part last year did not come back: Rossi & Rossi (Hong Kong); Leila Heller (New York and Dubai) and Saskia Fernando (Colombo).
Several of these large galleries continued to play it safe, bringing presentations to suit interior design-focused sensibilities and algorithmically informed taste—plenty of reflective surfaces, legible motifs and name brands, such as Ai Weiwei and Anish Kapoor. Lisson's sales topped out at £1.2m, and included two of Kapoor’s signature concave disc sculptures. Director Ellie Harrison-Read said that she had a "good fair but closing a few more sales could make it great”.
By and large, galleries that brought subtler or nicher works, struggled. Niru Ratnam did not place a work for the first two days, having pre-sold one painting by Amal Gosh to cover stand and shipping costs, though Ratnam noted that he made some sales towards the end of the week.
One of the clearer litmus tests for this market was a painting by Robert Nava, brought by the first-time exhibitor Night gallery from Los Angeles. Nava, who is co-represented by Pace, is a US-based market star whose naive figurative style sharply divides critics. The secondary-market painting, depicting a swimming cat, was tagged at $220,000, a hefty price for a buying pool unfamiliar with his work and where contemporary art by the most established artists rarely exceeds $400,000. It did not sell by the fair’s last day, but the gallery’s director Davida Nemeroff said she had engaged in several serious enquiries, including one local buyer who went home to measure their wall following a conversation on the stand. “We went in pretty blind, and didn’t know what to expect”, she said.
The gallery did however sell a $16,000 painting installation by Dhiya Mehra embossed with words from a speech by Surya Kant, India's former chief justice, that sparked the Cockroach Janata Party protests to the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art. “We’ve learned that if you don’t bring something vaguely South Asian, or a Picasso, it won’t sell," Nemeroff said.
Speaking of Picasso, one 1930s painting by the Spanish master was brought by Ben Brown, carrying a $4.5m price tag—the most expensive work brought to the fair in its four editions. Last year, the gallery brought a smaller painting by Picasso to Art Mumbai, which did not sell. Rather than being discouraged, this only convinced director Hugo Cobb to only double down. “Our feedback was that this market is now discerning enough for quality and it doesn’t want anything second rate,” he said.
As many international visitors and exhibitors will have observed, India now has no shortage of deep pocketed buyers, but its tastes are local and largely conservative. "Collecting in India is largely informed by pride in local culture, and familiarity," says the adviser Yamini Mehta. "The market here is still not ready for super conceptual stuff."
Further factors that keep India's art market more domestically focused than other Asian art market hubs include stifling bureaucracy and high taxes to ship works in and out of this country. As Richard Saltoun director Sakshi Mahajan said, "they don't make it easy or cheap to bring in work. Even when it's worth relatively small amounts".
Meanwhile, issues of black money circulating in the Indian art market persist. As one anonymous dealer noted, "many Indians might not want to send money abroad, for fear of those transactions being registered by the RBI (Reserve Bank of India)".
India's art market growth indeed appears to be domestic success story, in contrast to its last boom in the 2000s, which was fuelled by speculative buying, often from overseas collectors with no ties to the region.
While in buzzier Asian art markets like Seoul and Hong Kong, collectors covet international names at the expense of local talent, India protects and supports its own artists and its ecosystem—representatives from a growing number of new Indian biennials were spotted at the fair, including from the Bengal Biennial and the soon-to-launch Benares Biennial, both of whose artist lists are heavily weighted towards India and the wider South Asian region.
While India might not yet be ready for an international fair or an outpost of a mega gallery, it appears to be building something more valuable: an infrastructural network supporting homegrown talent, which will help to safeguard against another crash when the market eventually enters a soberer moment.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190m at Sotheby’s following Nazi loot claims
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Carlie Porterfield
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
One of Vincent van Gogh’s last paintings, long hidden from public view, sold for $165m ($190.4m with fees) at Sotheby’s New York on Wednesday (18 November), breaking the artist’s auction record. The result helped propel two back-to-back sales to a combined $663.26m ($777.8m with fees), with additional auction records for Mary Cassatt and Aaron Douglas.
But the landmark results were high points for an evening of uneven bidding, with just more than one-third of works selling for below their pre-sale estimates. The Blaquier-Arrieta collection, billed as the most valuable collection to come to auction in New York this season, brought in $358m ($412m with fees), falling short of its roughly $450m estimate. Sotheby’s Modern Evening sale, which followed immediately afterwards, generated another $305.21m ($365.8m with fees) against a $260.2m to $378.4m overall estimate.
Van Gogh’s Blossoming Chestnut Trees (Châtaigniers en fleurs) (1890), the most valuable lot offered across New York’s auction houses this season, had attracted attention even before reaching the rostrum. One of Van Gogh’s final paintings before his death in 1890, the work had for decades been out of public view in the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, built by Argentine sugar industry heiress Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and her husband, Carlos Pedro Blaquier, who served as president of Argentina’s largest sugar producer. Just a day before the sale, Sotheby’s announced that a settlement had been reached between the Blaquier heirs and the heirs of the painting’s previous owners, Hedwig and Samuel Fischer, following questions about the work’s Nazi-era provenance.
Estimated to fetch around $180m, the painting hammered at $165m ($190.4m with fees) after nearly five minutes of bidding, eventually going to a bidder in the room—William Aquavella, the head of Acquavella Galleries. Despite the hammer price falling short of its estimate, the Sotheby’s-guaranteed work surpassed Van Gogh’s previous auction record of $117m with fees, set in 2022 when Orchard with Cypresses (1888) sold at Christie’s Paul Allen sale. The result also made it the second most valuable object ever sold at Sotheby’s, behind Gustav Klimt’s Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer (1914–16), which fetched $236.4m with fees during last November’s marquee sales, and the fourth most valuable painting ever sold at auction.
Soon afterwards, Paul Cézanne’s Arlequin (1888-90) came to the rostrum. The painting, the last of the artist’s four works from the series still in public hands, hammered at $99m ($111m with fees), falling short of its $120m estimate. It also failed to surpass Cézanne’s auction record, set during the same 2022 Paul Allen sale at Christie’s New York, when the landscape La Montagne Sainte-Victoire (1888-90) fetched $138m with fees. Nevertheless, Arlequin became the most valuable Cézanne painting from the Harlequin series to sell at auction.
Ultimately, six of the collection’s 12 lots hammered below their low estimates, while five sold within or at their estimate ranges. Just one work exceeded expectations: the final lot, Camille Pissarro’s Maison de Piette à Montfoucault, effet de neige, avec un homme portant un fagot (1875), which hammered at $1.62m ($2m with fees), against a $700,000 to $900,000 estimate.
The subsequent Modern Evening sale generated $305.21m ($365.8m with fees), although bidding was similarly patchy. Of the works sold, 14 hammered below their low estimates, 21 sold within their estimate ranges and 11 exceeded their high estimates.
The top lot was René Magritte’s L’Ami de l’ordre (1964), which hammered at $39m ($45.5m with fees), far surpassing its $25m to $35m estimate. Combining the artist’s signature bowler-hatted figure with a nighttime landscape, the painting was consigned by the estate of beauty pioneer Sydell Miller. Two years ago, 25 works from her collection brought in $215.9m with fees during a single-owner auction at Sotheby’s November marquee sales. According to Sotheby’s, only one related composition now remains in private hands. L’Ami de l’ordre is the most valuable Magritte painting featuring a bowler hat to sell at auction.
One of the evening’s most exciting results came courtesy of the Harlem Renaissance artist Aaron Douglas, whose Harriet Tubman (1931) shattered his previous auction record. The painting depicts the American abolitionist with her arms raised overhead, breaking a chain amid a leafy landscape and a smoking cannon. Estimated at $2.5m to $3.5m, it hammered at $12m ($14.48m with fees) after a seven-minute bidding battle. At one point, the competition pitted father and daughter against each other on the telephones, bidding on behalf of their respective clients: George Wachter, Sotheby’s chairman of the Americas, and Jacqueline Wachter, vice-chairman of private sales for contemporary art and head of the Los Angeles office. The result far surpassed Douglas’s previous auction record of $600,000, set at Swann in 2008. Proceeds from the sale will benefit Bennett College, one of just two historically Black women’s colleges in the US.
Mary Cassatt also established a new auction record when Summertime (1894–95) hammered at $11m ($13.3m with fees) to an online bidder, exceeding its $7m to $10m estimate. The result surpassed her previous record of $7.49m, set at Christie’s New York in 2022. The painting came from the collection of the late oil tycoon Armand Hammer, with proceeds benefiting his eponymous foundation.
Only one lot failed to sell: Remedios Varo’s El vagabundo, which passed at $1.5m. Three other works, by Henri Matisse, Cézanne and Magritte, were withdrawn during the sale. Together, the withdrawn lots carried estimates totalling between $12.5m and $18.5m.

https://gothamist.com/news/newborn-puppi.title: 1 puppy dead, another fighting for its life after dog family abandoned in NJ cold
https://gothamist.com/news/newborn-puppi.author: Catalina Gonella
https://gothamist.com/news/newborn-puppi.text:
An animal rescue group in New Jersey said it’s working to save a family of dogs found abandoned in the cold on Saturday.
The Associated Humane Societies said it received a call about two dogs tied to a fence in Orange, just west of Newark. But when animal protection officers responded Saturday morning, they also found five puppies that had apparently been born overnight. One of the puppies had died, according to a social media post by AHS.
"The remaining were freezing, alongside a frightened and protective mom and dad,” AHS said in the post. “The family was rushed to the shelter for immediate veterinary care and upon evaluation vets discovered one puppy suffering with critical injuries.”
The critically injured puppy, named Hope, suffered a large cut to the back of her head and neck and remains in critical condition, according to the organization's website.
Two of the surviving puppies are in foster care, according to AHS's social media post. The mother, whom the organization is calling Freya, and her other two puppies still need an experienced foster home, the group said.
AHS is seeking donations to help cover veterinary treatment, food and other supplies for the dogs.

https://gothamist.com/news/scattered-sho.title: Delta delays flights ahead of Thanksgiving holiday over system failure
https://gothamist.com/news/scattered-sho.author: Giulia Heyward
https://gothamist.com/news/scattered-sho.text:
A tech snafu at one of the world’s busiest airports on Sunday is delaying thousands of Delta Airlines flights headed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
An issue with Delta Airlines’ weight and balance system at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is responsible for the delay at one of the busiest airports in the country, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement posted on social media.
More than 3,550 flights traveling within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed as of Sunday afternoon, according to Flight Aware.
The governmental agency urged travelers to check in with the airline for the latest information on their flights, and said that steps have already been taken to fix the issue.
“Delta is working to resolve issues with the airline’s weight and balance automation system,” the FAA statement said. “These delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems.”
Delta said it is working limit congestion at its Atlanta hub.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” said Delta spokesperson Natalie Duggan. “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism."
The issue on Sunday comes after a communications failure grounded all flights nationwide earlier this month, leading New York Gov. Kathy Hochul to call for the removal of U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
Other recent technological malfunctions have impacted other industries, including online banking systems and Microsoft Outlook.
Delta Airlines did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Gothamist.
This is a developing story and may be updated.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: On a budget? We found 50 gifts under $50 that punch above their weight
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Lauren Gould, Nick Mokey, Danielle Renwick and Karen Yuan
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
It’s a classic holiday conundrum. You’ve set aside $50 for a gift but are left wondering: how do I find a quality present within my budget?
To answer this question, we ate a lot of chocolate, tried on many sweaters and asked actual tweens what is in this year. We ended up with 50 recommendations – including a pretty bamboo box of Japanese skincare, a neck warmer our Alaska-based writer calls her “secret weapon” for the cold and a cushy dog bed that may inspire envy among humans.
- Visit our ultimate holiday gift guide for obsessively vetted gift ideas, or get inspired by our full array of guides, including a gift guide for the person who has everything and a guide to cozy gifts.
Kitchen
A Moka pot makes espresso-like, strong coffee at a far lower price. In our global gift guide, the Filter’s Lauren Gould recommended giving one of the colored Moka pot options for a coffee maker your recipient will want to show off on their stovetop.
This handwash is “made with bread yeast enzymes to neutralize cooking odors and leaves behind sophisticated notes of bergamot and pepper that give off high-end hotel vibes”, writes veteran kitchen writer Emily Farris in our holiday gift guide. Grab this for the amateur chef who cooks with a lot of garlic.
These plastic-free deli containers have a cult following, including Farris, who called them “endlessly versatile, lightweight and durable”.
This quirky candle “can act as anything from a dinner party curio to a kitchen candle that reduces odors”, writes Filter commissioning editor Karen Yuan. Grab this for the person who could use a dash of whimsy this winter.
Home
“Have you ever seen a movie that depicts a rich person’s home or at a five-star hotel, and they have monogrammed towels? Frontgate can give you that look and feel,” writes tester Jon Chan in our guide to the best bath towels. Gift this to a new homeowner in need of a towel upgrade.
***
 
“I covet a good tea towel – though I’m often loath to use them to wipe up messes,” writes Cynthia Greenlee, the Guardian’s deputy editor for special projects. She recommends, among others, the Nasturtium towel for its “Christmas-y color scheme”.
“I once spotted Kinto’s sepia cup and saucer at a painfully cool cafe in Brooklyn, which was very validating for me, a not particularly cool person who nonetheless appreciates a nice trinket,” writes Yuan. Grab this as an artsy upgrade for a cabinet full of chipped white mugs.
Sleep
After testing a slew of pillows, this pillow was our favorite down-free option, and is especially ideal for bibliophiles. “I think bed readers will enjoy how well the Quince pillow props you up when leaning against your headboard,” writes contributor Jon Chan.
Sleep writer Richard Baguley “continued to sleep better, with fewer interruptions, especially on colder nights”, since adding this weighted blanket into his life.
You don’t need to know what a capybara is to appreciate this adorable creature. You can pop it in your microwave for warmth or your freezer if you struggle with hot flashes or someone in your house refuses to keep the thermostat below 80F.
Baguley adores this satin pillowcase for protecting his skin and hair. The quirky print adds a personal touch for the sleepy Star Wars fans.
Beauty
“When I want to air-dry my hair without dripping water on to my shoulders, I pop on one of these,” says beauty writer Maria Ricapito. These are ideal for the low-maintenance person in your life who can’t be bothered with a blow-dryer.
These sheet masks from the popular K-beauty brand Biodance have earned Filter commissioning editor Karen Yuan’s stamp of approval. “Unlike many other masks, you wear this one overnight, when it gradually turns from white to translucent as its collagen and oligo-hyaluronic acid do their work to boost skin elasticity and hydration,” she writes in our guide to the best Korean skincare brands.
“I hate the feeling of heavy mascara. After I discovered this one from Ilia in college, I never looked back,” writes Lauren Gould, the Filter’s editorial coordinator. This is the perfect stocking stuffer for the beauty obsessed person in your life.
“This Japanese skin ritual in a very giftable bamboo box aims to fix dryness and uneven texture,” writes Ricapito in this year’s comprehensive holiday gift guide. The $42 set comes with two serums, a moisturizer and cleansing oil, ideal for skincare fanatics who love testing new products.
Filter contributor Tobey Grumet Segal recommended this multi-tasker makeup product in her guide to the best beauty products for people over 50. “I’ve been known to use it all over my face for a subtle glow, dab it on my cheekbones, use it as a refreshing lip gloss, or even smooth over my eyelids,” she writes. Its many uses make it a safe gift because your recipient can use it as a highlighter, bronzer, blush and more.
Fashion
These were one of my favorite gifts last holiday season. They feel fancier than the oversized T-shirt I’d otherwise wear for bed, and I love the stretchy, soft material.
This artful hair accessory adds a unique touch to your look. It comes in a variety of colors to match your recipient’s style, including a bold cherry red and a marbled pink.
Hear us out: socks aren’t a boring gift. The UK-based brand Rock and Ruby makes cheery knit pairs your recipient can wear with their favorite sneakers or boots.
This past spring we asked stylists about the best wardrobe upgrades. One recommendation from Kelsey Ellstrom, a celebrity stylist who has dressed Zac Efron, Ben Affleck and John Krasinski, was a versatile sweater, also practical for the cold months ahead.
Food
On paper, a tin of fish may not be the obvious gift for the foodie in your life. However, Fishwife’s trendy tuna is among our favorite cans after eating our way through more than a dozen.
It doesn’t count as a gag gift if it tastes good, right? These little fish look like sardines, but are actually made of milk chocolate.
Hu Kitchen’s vegan, nut butter-filled chocolate was one of our favorites in our chocolate bar taste test. Gift the variety pack to the plant-based person with a sweet tooth.
Olipop’s prebiotic soda is a Filter team favorite – Yuan and Gould recently split an order of the limited-edition caramel apple flavor. Right now, you also get 50% off your purchase of two-plus packs (we also suggest the tart pomegranate).
after newsletter promotion
Outdoors
There is nothing worse than feeling dehydrated halfway through a hike. Owala’s FreeSip water bottle makes a great gift for your outdoorsy loved one who needs a hydration upgrade.
Anchorage-based writer Julia O’Malley calls this neckwarmer her “secret weapon” for braving the cold. At $30, this is a practical gift for city dwellers and outdoor enthusiasts alike.
Outdoor writer Paige Triola says every backpacker she knows has this handy long spoon. Grab this to toss in the stocking of your hardcore adventurer friend who brings dehydrated food on their mountainous treks.
For late-night camping adventures, gift Petzel’s lightweight headlamp. It has three brightness settings, an adjustable strap and a three-year warranty for peace of mind.
Tech
After rigorously testing 22 USB chargers, this humble option from Anker emerged as our favorite budget pick. If you know someone whose phone battery is constantly at 1%, grab the charger that tester Mark Knapp calls “minuscule, lightweight and affordable”.
Tech writer Adam Doud loves this speaker, calling it “surprisingly powerful considering its size”. Give this to your friend with great music taste who needs a lightweight, portable way to show off their newest playlist.
“A good seat cushion should ideally make you utter a small sigh of pleasure as you settle down – on whatever chair it is placed on. Look no further than the Xtreme Comfort office chair cushion,” writes Doud. Grab this under-$35 cushion for the family member who works from home, sitting on an uncomfortable office chair.
“Its approximately 100,000 soft synthetic bristles remove debris from records, turntables and audio equipment, making for a smoother listening experience,” writes Angela Serratore in our gift guide for the people who already have everything. Wrap this up for someone who refuses to listen to Spotify.
Travel
After testing every AeroPress coffee maker, food writer Joe Ray declared the AeroPress Go the best for travel. “Bad coffee is a drag on any trip for me, and whether I’m on assignment in Mexico or at a trade show in Chicago, my coffee game and my whole trip, really, gets a lot better when I bring my Go,” he writes.
Travel writer Tim Stevens has used these compression socks for five years to help prevent blood clots during flights. “They are still comfortable and look like new, perfect for the frequent-flying buy-it-for-lifer in your family circle,” he writes.
Stevens recommends AirTags for a “forgetful friend or someone whose checked bags tend to disappear”. You can grab your recipient one AirTag for under $25, so they can attach it to their most precious cargo before their next trip.
The winner of our sleep masks test is a worthwhile travel companion for your jet-setting family member. Tester Juno DeMelo appreciated the soft foam padding on the eye cups and its ability to block light.
Fitness
“Have a partner who is always begging you for a quick shoulder massage?” writes DeMelo. “This will make both of your lives better.”
These resistance bands are stocking stuffers that say, “Take care of your bones because I want you to be in my life for a while, OK?” In our guide to strength training for women over 40, a physical trainer called them “the most underrated fitness gadget”. Gritin makes her favorites: “They come in five different strengths and are cheap and easy to transport. Perfect if you are short on space and time and can do a full-body workout too.”
DeMelo calls these “the holy grail” of leggings at half the price of premium brands. They come in eight colors, including a festive-looking Big Sur Green.
Tester Tobey Grumet Segal tried these ankle weights for a week, concluding: “After an entire week of vigorous use, from walking to gym classes, I can honestly say I felt a difference in my legs.” Grab these for the sporty person who refuses to buy a gym membership.
Tweens/teens
Lego recently released sets themed after Olivia Rodrigo, the 2027 Grammy-nominated singer, that tweens, like 12-year-old Olivia, are adding to their wishlists. “I really like Legos, so I have a few Olivia Rodrigo Lego sets on my wishlist,” said 12-year-old Olivia (not Rodrigo) when we asked tweens and teens what gifts they’re asking for this year.
“I draw. I’m a big visual artist,” says 16-year-old Chelsea.
“There are fillings with beads in it, and it’s like, crunchy,” says Leo, an 11-year-old, of one of the gifts on his list this year.
“My friends have Minecraft, and I want to be creative and build houses,” says 11-year-old Mate.
Pets
In our dog enrichment guide, a trainer recommended this bacon-scented ball for teaching your pup to fetch. Gould’s nine-year-old toy poodle is also obsessed with this small toy, based on the videos her mom sends of him sprinting around the back yard with the green ball proudly clamped between his teeth.
“While it can’t stand the kind of abuse our more durable beds can, Bedsure’s Orthopedic Bolster Dog Sofa is soft, supportive and it’s available for well under $50,” writes Stevens, a dog owner and pro product teste. This was our favorite budget dog bed after testing 15, beloved by his pup Koopa for its cozy material.
Not in the market for a high-end cat bed? This grooming kit is Filter photo editor Tracy Allison’s go-to affordable gift for cat lovers. “Tux uses his whenever he’s vying for a little extra attention or looking to self-soothe,” she writes.
“A flirt pole is a crazy-good enrichment toy” for pets, according to certified dog trainer Miranda LaMorte. “Your dog can chase it and pounce on it and bite it, get a little bit of tug and get a lot of chasing, which is a super great enrichment activity.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: MPF pede mudanças na gestão de políticas para população de rua em SP
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Guilherme Jeronymo
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) e o Ministério Público de Contas do Estado de São Paulo (MPC-SP) divulgaram, na tarde desta terça-feira (24), um documento de 150 páginas no qual fazem diversas recomendações sobre políticas estaduais voltadas para a população em situação de rua.
Os órgãos apontaram problemas de acompanhamento de atuação de organizações terceirizadas e entidades assistenciais, equívocos na escolha de modelos de assistência, má gestão e falhas na transparência de atendimento e prestação de contas.
Segundo o documento, os problemas identificados incluem resultados muito abaixo das metas estipuladas, falta de transparência na aplicação de valores milionários e ausência de padrões orçamentários que permitam o acompanhamento das políticas assistenciais. As políticas públicas analisadas estão ligadas à Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Social do Estado de São Paulo (SEDS) e à Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Urbano e Habitação (SDUH).
O exame das contas revelou ainda divergências contábeis em fundos especiais vinculados à SEDS e levantou suspeitas sobre parcerias que a pasta firmou no fim de 2025. Entre 12 e 26 de dezembro do ano passado, a secretaria assinou três termos de colaboração com instituições de pesquisa que totalizaram cerca de R$ 400 milhões. Os convênios, com vigência de 32 meses, tiveram pagamento imediato de um quarto do valor previsto, sem apresentação de plano de trabalho, cronograma executivo ou demonstrativo de execução prévia de serviços que justificasse o adiantamento.
Um dos programas principais de atendimento ao público, o SuperAção SP, também chamou a atenção dos procuradores. Entendido por eles como o principal programa do governo de São Paulo para o atendimento da parcela da população em maior vulnerabilidade social, a iniciativa consumiu R$ 275 milhões em 2025, enquanto a previsão inicial aprovada era de gasto de R$ 154,2 milhões ao longo de quatro anos (de 2024 a 2027).
Apesar disso, o SuperAção SP atingiu apenas 0,23% da meta de benefícios sociais que deveriam ser concedidos a pessoas em situação de rua e não entregou nenhuma das 275 vagas de qualificação profissional previstas, de acordo com o documento divulgado.
Desses gastos, R$ 128,6 milhões foram registrados sem correspondência com indicadores definidos no Plano Plurianual 2024-2027 do estado, e são exemplo de mudanças na classificação de gastos da SEDS, apontadas pelo MPF e pelo MPC-SP como uma falha central nas contas da pasta. “A prática de criar rubricas aleatórias para declarar verbas dificulta a avaliação de resultados conforme objetivos preestabelecidos, ao mesmo tempo em que evidencia a falta de repasses para ações planejadas”, apontam os órgãos em nota conjunta.
Também é criticada a inexistência de um mapeamento sobre a capacidade de cada município do estado de atender à população em situação de rua, estimada em 150 mil pessoas pelo Observatório Brasileiro de Políticas Públicas com a População em Situação de Rua (OBPopRua).
“Sem uma visão abrangente das necessidades regionais, a distribuição de recursos acaba concentrada na região metropolitana da capital, deixando em desamparo áreas urbanas como Campinas e Santos e cidades de médio porte. Soma-se a isso a insuficiência dos recursos estaduais para financiar abrigos e repúblicas, que atualmente oferecem vagas para, no máximo, 20,5 mil pessoas”, criticam o MPF e o MPC-SP.
Os órgãos defendem, ainda, a necessidade de rever o modelo adotado na assistência social para essa população. O acolhimento provisório, em abrigos, é entendido por eles como menos eficiente, pois exige cerca de três vezes mais recursos e não favorece mudanças efetivas na situação dos atendidos. Sugerem, por sua vez, a adoção de programas de fomento à moradia, acompanhada de suporte multidisciplinar, seguindo a metodologia internacional conhecida como Moradia Primeiro (Housing First). Política semelhante foi adotada na capital, com o programa De Braços Abertos, iniciado em 2014 durante a gestão do então prefeito Fernando Haddad.
As recomendações foram encaminhadas para o Tribunal Estadual de Contas, em 19 de novembro de 2026, e para as secretarias (SEDS e SDUH), continuamente, desde 2023.
A reportagem procurou a assessoria de imprensa do governo de São Paulo e aguarda sua manifestação.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Lula não convida Milei para posse e mantém Argentina sem embaixador
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) não convidará seu homólogo argentino, Javier Milei, para a cerimônia de posse do seu quarto mandato. O governo também mantém a decisão de deixar o vizinho sem embaixador brasileiro, após reiterados ataques de autoridades do país a Lula e questionamentos sobre as eleições.
O ministro das Relações Exteriores, Mauro Vieira, havia condicionado o restabelecimento das relações entre os dois países a uma mudança de postura de Milei, que já chamou Lula de “lixo socialista”, “mentiroso”, “corrupto” e “ex-presidiário”, entre outros xingamentos.
Milei — assim como Donald Trump, dos EUA, e Benjamin Netanyahu, de Israel — não parabenizou o petista pela vitória de outubro deste ano.
O último episódio de ataques aconteceu no sábado (21), quando o chanceler argentino, Pablo Quirno, afirmou, em um programa de televisão, que “houve situações dentro do processo eleitoral [brasileiro] que colocavam em dúvida toda a situação”.
Em agosto, o Brasil rebaixou o nível das relações diplomáticas com a Argentina, ocasião em que o embaixador argentino, Daniel Raimondi, deixou o território brasileiro.
Atualmente, a embaixada brasileira em Buenos Aires é comandada pelo ministro-conselheiro Eduardo Uziel, encarregado de negócios. O embaixador Julio Bitelli está fora da Argentina desde julho, segundo o jornal Clarín.
Os ex-presidentes argentinos Mauricio Macri e Alberto Fernández, além de outras autoridades do país vizinho, como governadores, serão convidados para a cerimônia de posse de Lula.
O governo argentino define as falas de Milei como “qualificativos” e afirma que a decisão brasileira de rebaixar o nível das relações foi “unilateral”.
Nesta terça (24), Lula credenciou 14 novos diplomatas estrangeiros. Além da Argentina, os Estados Unidos também ficaram de fora.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Justiça condena Assuero Veronez a pagar R$ 200 mil por destruição de geoglifo no Acre
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação Varadouro
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Justiça Federal condenou o presidente da Federação da Agricultura e Pecuária do Acre (Faeac), Assuero Veronez, a pagar R$ 200 mil de indenização por danos morais coletivos pela destruição de estruturas de um geoglifo na Fazenda Crichá, em Capixaba, de propriedade do dirigente ruralista. Segundo o Ministério Público Federal (MPF), a área foi aterrada e nivelada em 2019 para o cultivo mecanizado de milho.
A sentença também obriga o proprietário a custear e executar a reconstituição das valetas e muretas do sítio arqueológico. A decisão é de primeira instância e cabe recurso ao Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região.
A condenação foi imposta em ação civil pública ajuizada pelo MPF em 2024, com a participação do Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan). À época, Varadouro mostrou que o órgão já pedia a recomposição do sítio e o pagamento de indenização.
O sítio era formado por cinco recintos de terra, delimitados por valetas e muretas. Imagens históricas ainda mostram os desenhos em julho de 2019. A partir de setembro daquele ano, os registros já indicam que o terreno havia sido nivelado.
Em julho de 2020, técnicos do Iphan encontraram uma área plana, com sinais de cultivo e vestígios arqueológicos dispersos na superfície. As estruturas já não eram identificáveis em campo.
A defesa e as medidas de reparação
No processo, Veronez alegou que um funcionário fez o nivelamento sem sua autorização específica e que ele não teve a intenção de causar o dano. De acordo com o relato do MPF sobre a sentença, o pecuarista havia declarado em investigação policial que sabia da existência dos geoglifos antes de comprar a fazenda. A Justiça concluiu que o nivelamento, executado por um tratorista contratado, fazia parte da atividade agrícola da propriedade.
A defesa também argumentou que o caso já havia sido objeto de um acordo de não persecução penal, com pagamento de prestação pecuniária. A Justiça manteve a obrigação de reparação civil e observou que o próprio acordo limitava seus efeitos à esfera penal.
Segundo o Iphan, é possível refazer as valetas e muretas, mas parte dos vestígios se perdeu de forma irreversível. A sentença dá ao proprietário 90 dias, contados a partir do trânsito em julgado, para apresentar um projeto de recomposição elaborado por profissionais habilitados. Se o Iphan atestar que parte da obra é tecnicamente inviável, o valor da indenização por esses danos materiais será definido posteriormente.
Veronez também deverá manter a área isolada e cercada, conforme as orientações do instituto. Intervenções que possam afetar o sítio ou sua área de proteção dependerão de autorização prévia do Iphan. Os R$ 200 mil serão destinados a ações de conservação e proteção do patrimônio arqueológico no Acre.
Em março deste ano, Assuero Veronez foi reeleito para comandar, por mais quatro anos, a federação da entidade representativa do agronegócio no Acre. Desde 2019, com a posse do então governador Gladson Cameli (PP) no Palácio Rio Branco, Assuero assumiu funções de influência dentro do Executivo acreano – sendo o principal porta-voz do grande agronegócio junto ao governo.
Influência esta que ele mantém com o governo Mailza Assis, que assumiu a titularidade da cadeira em abril, com a renúncia de Gladson para concorrer ao Senado. Ainda em fevereiro, Assuero sentou ao lado de Mailza numa reunião de membros do governo acreano com representantes da Câmara de Comércio Brasil–Rússia no Brasil.
Da Fazenda Crichá à fronteira da soja
Em Capixaba, outro geoglifo virou alvo de ação civil pública em 2025. O MPF processou a proprietária, o arrendatário e um trabalhador da Fazenda Oeste por danos ao sítio Ramal do Capatará, registrado pelo Iphan desde o início dos anos 2000.
O órgão atribuiu os danos ao preparo do terreno para o cultivo de soja. À época, o arrendatário e o trabalhador admitiram que houve intervenção com máquina na área, mas disseram que fizeram apenas a limpeza do terreno e negaram ter plantado soja no local.
Desde a retomada do Varadouro, a expansão das lavouras sobre áreas de interesse arqueológico tem sido uma das frentes da cobertura sobre o agronegócio no Acre. Em janeiro de 2024, a reportagem “Uma história soterrada” mostrou como a conversão de pastagens em lavouras de soja trouxe um risco adicional para os geoglifos.
O nivelamento do solo para a passagem das máquinas pode apagar justamente os desníveis que dão forma a esses desenhos. O pesquisador Alceu Ranzi também relatou dificuldades para entrar nas fazendas e estudar as estruturas.
Em setembro de 2026, a reportagem Geometria Histórica acompanhou esse problema na Amacro, região que abrange as divisas do Amazonas, do Acre e de Rondônia. Enquanto pesquisadores recorrem a drones e outras técnicas de sensoriamento remoto para localizar estruturas construídas por povos indígenas há séculos, a soja e a pecuária avançam sobre uma região cuja ocupação antiga ainda está sendo mapeada.
Na Fazenda Crichá, a avaliação do Iphan dá a medida do que está em jogo: é possível redesenhar os contornos no solo, mas parte do registro que ajudaria a contar a história de quem os construiu já se perdeu.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Ajuste fiscal libera R$ 1,2 trilhão para juros, enquanto coloca em risco investimentos futuros em saúde e educação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: José Eduardo Bernardes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O ajuste fiscal aprovado pela Câmara Federal na segunda-feira (23), depois de passar pelo Senado, prevê impacto de até R$ 56,1 bilhões nas contas públicas em 2027. Para o economista Paulo Kliass, porém, o problema não é só o tamanho do corte, mas onde a tesoura passa. Em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, nesta terça-feira (24), ele afirmou que o pacote aperta todas as despesas do Estado, menos a maior delas: os valores gastos com juros da dívida pública.
Kliass explica que a meta do governo é obter superávit primário, conceito que exclui da conta as despesas financeiras.
“Para o pagamento de juros não tem limite, não tem teto, não tem contingenciamento, não tem nada”, disse. Segundo ele, nos últimos 12 meses, o Brasil gastou mais de R$ 1,2 trilhão com juros, pagos basicamente a bancos e instituições financeiras que detêm títulos da dívida.
“E aí vamos cortar de quem? Vai cortar do SUS, da educação, das universidades, do saneamento, da segurança, do salário dos servidores. Por quê? Porque somos responsáveis fiscalmente. A verdadeira gastança é a conta de juros. E para isso não se mexe”, criticou.
Para o economista, a imprensa culpa aposentados, beneficiários de programas sociais, idosos e famílias de pessoas com deficiência atendidos pelo Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC) , que recebem “a fortuna de um salário mínimo”.
O pacote, na avaliação de Kliass, aprofunda o arcabouço fiscal de 2023 com a mesma lógica do teto de gastos de Michel Temer. Pela regra, as despesas só crescem 70% do ritmo das receitas, até um limite anual. Como saúde, educação e previdência têm pisos constitucionais ou estão ligadas ao salário mínimo, essas áreas acabam “esmagando” todas as outras, como ciência e assistência social.
O risco maior, segundo ele, ainda está por vir. O governo já anuncia uma segunda etapa de medidas de ajuste. Kliass teme que ela inclua a desvinculação dos benefícios previdenciários do salário mínimo ou dos pisos constitucionais de saúde e educação.
Para o economista, o governo “exagerou na dose da submissão” ao mercado e repete erros de mandatos anteriores do PT, como a dupla Antonio Palocci e Henrique Meirelles, em 2003, e Joaquim Levy, em 2015, episódios que ele chama de “austericídio”. “Ninguém está pedindo ajuste fiscal. No campo progressista, dos sindicatos, dos trabalhadores do campo, dos estudantes, dos aposentados, dos servidores, ninguém quer ajuste fiscal”, afirmou.
Kliass defende o caminho oposto. Com o crescimento econômico perto de 1% neste ano, ele avalia que este seria o momento de o Estado aumentar o investimento público, numa política anticíclica. Como a dívida brasileira é quase toda em reais, diz, o país não precisa “dar satisfação a ninguém”.
Para ele, se Lula quer marcar seu último mandato, precisa “abandonar o arcabouço fiscal e abrir espaço para o investimento”.
O economista também cobra mudanças na política de juros. Ele defende passar meta de inflação de 3% para 4,5% e critica a diretoria do Banco Central por manter a taxa Selic, que chegou a 15%, num patamar mais alto do que o registrado no governo Bolsonaro.
Na avaliação dele, baixar os juros “reduziria o gasto com a dívida e baratearia o crédito para retomar o desenvolvimento”.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Memorial da América Latina batiza espaços em homenagem a Luiz Carlos Prestes, Olga Benário e Quilombo Saracura
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Na última semana, três espaços do Memorial da América Latina receberam novas denominações como forma de resgatar a trajetória e homenagear personalidades e grupos que fizeram parte da história do Brasil.
A Praça Cívica, espaço de 12 mil m² onde está a icônica mão que sintetiza a obra de Oscar Niemeyer, passou a se chamar Praça Cívica Luiz Carlos Prestes. O parlatório, espaço externo e contínuo ao Salão dos Atos, recebeu o nome de Parlatório Olga Benário Prestes. Já a área externa próxima ao salão e à biblioteca denomina-se agora Espaço Tributo ao Quilombo Saracura.
“Preservar não é apenas impedir que alguma coisa desapareça. É impedir que permaneça diante de nós depois que já esquecemos o que significa. Talvez possamos chamar aquilo que existe nessa dimensão de patrimônio relacional. Não proponho uma nova categoria jurídica de proteção. Proponho uma maneira de olhar. Portinari é patrimônio. Prestes é memória histórica”, afirma o presidente da Fundação Memorial da América Latina, Pedro Mastrobuono, em seu despacho, acrescentando que não é uma questão de concordar com o líder comunista, mas de relembrar sua importância e trajetória. “Patrimônio não existe apenas para preservar os passados com os quais concordamos. Existe também para impedir que simplifiquemos os passados que precisamos compreender.”
Uma curiosidade é que a imagem de Tiradentes, líder da Inconfidência Mineira, que existe no Memorial, é de autoria do artista Cândido Portinari, que era amigo de Prestes e se inspirou no líder comunista para sua representação do inconfidente.
Prestes foi uma das personalidades políticas mais influentes no país durante o século 20. Líder da Coluna Prestes, o político foi perseguido e preso durante a ditadura do Estado Novo, de Getúlio Vargas, e pela ditadura militar. A outra homenagem é à companheira de Prestes, Olga Benário, morta na Alemanha nazista após ser entregue pelo regime de Vargas.
“A memória do Holocausto não pode limitar-se à memória dos mortos. Ela precisa ser também uma pedagogia dos sinais. Reconhecer o momento em que o outro começa a deixar de ser percebido como humano talvez seja uma das tarefas éticas mais urgentes de qualquer sociedade. É nesse ponto que a história de Olga ultrapassa Olga”, argumenta Mastrobuono, que é judeu.
A resistência coletiva aparece na homenagem ao Quilombo Saracura, território próximo ao córrego de mesmo nome, no local onde atualmente é o bairro do Bixiga, no centro de São Paulo. O espaço recebeu destaque após as pesquisas arqueológicas urbanas para as obras da futura estação 14 Bis–Saracura da Linha 6–Laranja.
“A iniciativa representa um importante gesto institucional de reconhecimento da presença negra na formação histórica, cultural e social de São Paulo. Ao homenagear o Quilombo Saracura, associado à região do Bixiga, o Memorial estabelece um diálogo entre territórios de resistência, ancestralidades africanas e experiências coletivas que contribuíram decisivamente para a constituição da cidade”, afirma o presidente da Fundação Memorial.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Porteira aberta: direita espanhola pode levar Vox ao poder e romper ‘cordão sanitário’ europeu
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: José Eduardo Bernardes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A cinco dias da eleição que pode levar a extrema direita ao governo da Espanha, o professor e pesquisador em Relações Internacionais Ricardo Leães afirmou em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, que a possível aliança entre o Partido Popular (PP) e o Vox, no domingo (29), reflete um movimento da direita tradicional em todo o continente.
“A gente vê que as portas estão abertas. A questão é saber se a boiada está passando. E ela está passando cada vez mais rápido. Os bois estão ficando bem animados com esses portões que foram escancarados pela direita tradicional europeia”, disse.
As pesquisas apontam nessa direção. Levantamentos publicados pelo jornal El País e pelo site El Confidencial estimam que PP e Vox conquistarão, juntos, 198 e 200 cadeiras, acima das 176 necessárias para a maioria no Parlamento de 350 deputados. Em 2023, o PP foi o partido mais votado, com 137 cadeiras, mas, mesmo com o apoio do Vox, não conseguiu assegurar a maioria.
Para Leães, cai assim o chamado “cordão sanitário”, acordo tácito entre partidos europeus para não se aliar à extrema direita, inspirado na lembrança de que os nazistas nunca venceram uma eleição na Alemanha e só chegaram ao poder com o aval da direita da época.
“Quando a situação fica dura, a direita começa a se parecer muito com a extrema direita. Começa a considerar que ela não é tão perigosa assim, que pode ser controlada e que é uma alternativa melhor do que a esquerda”, afirmou.
A eleição antecipada nasceu da crise da moradia. Pedro Sánchez, do PSOE, convocou as eleições após o Parlamento espanhol rejeitar propostas para enfrentar a crise imobiliária, depois dos protestos pelo despejo de Maricarmen Abascal, que morreu aos 87 anos, em 7 de outubro, depois de ser expulsa do imóvel onde morou por 70 anos.
Para Leães, faltou força ao governo para mudar as regras do setor e a aposta nas urnas pode ter efeito contrário: “talvez o tiro esteja saindo pela culatra”.
A provável saída de Sánchez preocupa também na política externa. O professor o aponta como a “notória exceção” entre governantes europeus, cuja maioria ignora o apoio crescente da população à causa palestina, em um momento em que uma investigação revelou como o Deutsche Bank financiou tanques que Israel utiliza contra os palestinos em Gaza. “Quando chega no ponto definitivo, que é o financeiro, os investimentos militares, nenhuma medida é tomada”, criticou.
O avanço da extrema direita também preocupa o professor na América Latina. Na Colômbia, o presidente Abelardo de la Espriella chamou de “falsa paz” o acordo com as Farc, que completa dez anos nesta semana, e autorizou a entrada de militares dos EUA no país. Para Leães, a extrema direita no poder “deu a condição para que Espriella se comporte como funcionário de Donald Trump”.
Já Cuba, diante das novas ameaças de Trump, pode virar “uma espécie de prêmio de consolação” para um presidente que acumula derrotas, segundo o professor. Ele lembra que o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, descendente de cubanos que deixaram a ilha após a revolução, vê uma mudança de governo em Havana como “triunfo pessoal”.
