Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Allegiances frequently shift and evolve: the Giants Brigade and the National Resistance Forces were each previously backed by the UAE. The leaders of both, like much of the coalition, are now bankrolled by Riyadh amid its fallout with Abu Dhabi.
With fighting spread across multiple front lines, here’s an overview of the most important military and political parties involved in the conflict.
The Presidential Leadership Council alliance
Yemen has been officially administered by the eight-member Presidential Leadership Council (PLC) since 2022, chaired by politician Rashad al-Alimi. It is recognised internationally as the government of Yemen, and backed by Saudi Arabia.
Several PLC members lead their own military units, which nominally make up Yemen’s armed forces but are ultimately accountable to their commanders and their external backers.
The Giants Brigades (Al-Amaliqa), mostly drawn from southern Salafi and tribal fighters, are estimated to number 20,000–30,000 fighters. Their leader is Abdulrahman al-Muharrami, better known as Abu Zaraa, a Salafi cleric turned military commander from Lahij governorate who sits on the PLC.
The units were originally armed, trained and funded by the UAE and were long affiliated with the STC, but have been on the Riyadh payroll since Abu Dhabi pulled back from Yemen earlier this year.
Andreas Krieg, associate professor at King's College London's School of Security Studies, told Middle East Eye that "Riyadh has been able to co-opt individuals such as Abu Zaraa, but it has not been able to absorb their entire networks. The Giants retain their southern identity and longstanding Emirati relationships."
The force is among the coalition's best-equipped: it was key to the recapture of the western coast from the Houthis in 2017 (albeit with aerial support from the UAE), and is integral to the current government's defence of Aden.
Many of the Giants’ fighters identify as southerners and are reluctant to defend territory beyond southern Yemen.
Islah (formally known as the Yemeni Congregation for Reform) is a Sunni political movement with historic ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. It also includes Salafi and tribal fighters.
Despite its ideological affiliations, it is crucial to Riyadh's political and military network in Yemen. The UAE, however, has long opposed Islah, and has lobbied abroad for it to be classified as a terrorist group.
Islah is especially influential in Taiz, where it dominates the government's security operation, including the Taiz Military Axis, which coordinates the military units defending the city against 11 years of Houthi siege.
Homeland Shield (Quwat Dira al-Watan, also known in English as the National Shield Forces) is led by commander Abdulrahman al-Lahji.
It was established in 2022 and formalised as a military unit the following year with the backing of PLC chair Rashad al-Alimi. Its estimated 30-40,000 fighters principally come from Salafi and tribal communities in the eastern Hadramaut and al-Mahrah governorates.
Homeland Shield was key to the recapture of Hadramaut from the STC-affiliated forces in January and is now fighting the Houthis along the eastern frontline. It has also been used as a police force to quell internal discontent, including in crackdowns on rallies of STC supporters.
The National Resistance Forces are led by Tareq Saleh, nephew and former aide of President Ali Abdullah Saleh, who was driven from power in 2012 and killed by the Houthis, his onetime allies, in 2018.
Many of its fighters come from the remnants of the former president's Republican Guard, who were backed by the UAE until the STC’s failed putsch in January. It has subsequently shifted allegiances - and its payroll - to Riyadh. Unlike the UAE-backed STC, it nominally supports a unified Yemen.
From its HQ in Mocha, the NRF’s estimated 50,000 fighters controlled much of the Red Sea coastline until their position collapsed dramatically amid the Houthis’ August-September offensive. Saleh fled to Riyadh on 12 September, and some NRF troops have since been redeployed to remote regions of Hadramaut.
Krieg said that the loss of Mocha meant that the NRF had lost "its principal territorial, logistical and political base," leaving the force "severely degraded. The forces retain experienced personnel, but I would no longer regard the NRF as a credible independent offensive force in the short term."
The Hadramaut Tribal Alliance (HTA) is a coalition that wants greater autonomy for the governorate, home to much of Yemen’s modest oil reserves and where there has long been resentment against Aden’s political and military control.
Founded in 2015, its leader is tribal sheikh Amr bin Habrish, who has called for greater local control over natural resources, security forces and politics. Its armed wing, the Hadramaut Protection Forces, sits outside government control but has been courted by Riyadh to counter UAE-backed southern fighters.
In December 2025, the HTA tried to take Hadramaut’s oil fields, sparking the STC’s failed putsch later that month. Bin Habrish travelled to Saudi Arabia in January amid clashes between his forces and the UAE-backed STC. In July, Saudi authorities prevented him from returning to Yemen without explanation.
The Houthis and allies
The rebel alliance is dominated by the Houthis or Ansar Allah ("helpers of God"), which emerged from the Saada governorate in northern Yemen during the 1990s.
It currently has an estimated 350,000 fighters, wants international recognition as the government of Yemen, and an end to the ongoing Saudi blockade, which has caused devastating hunger. The group is rooted in Zaydism, a minority branch of Shia Islam that is concentrated in the northern highlands.
Amid demands for northern autonomy, the Houthis repeatedly fought the Saleh government between 2004 and 2010.
The group, now led by Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, brother of founder Hussein Badreddin al-Houthi, seized Sanaa in September 2014. Six months later, Saudi Arabia led a military coalition to restore the government.
In 2022, a UN-brokered informal ceasefire left the Houthis with 30 percent of Yemen, containing 80 percent of the population.
The group has received extensive military and tactical support from Iran, including shipments that allow them to build some of Tehran’s most sophisticated missile and drone systems. It has also received support from Hezbollah. Although the Houthis claim to be Yemen's government, they are only recognised as such by Iran.
The group, whose slogan is “God is the greatest, death to America, death to Israel, curse the Jews, victory to Islam", has attacked Israel since October 2023, as well as vessels linked to Israel and Saudi Arabia that navigate the Bab el-Mandab strait. The Houthis have also repeatedly hit Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh’s airport.
Throughout its decade running northern Yemen, the Houthis have forged alliances with local tribal leaders, but have also faced discontent from local sheikhs and tribal groups that have been strong-armed by the Houthi leadership in Sanaa.
The Southern Transitional Council
The Southern Transitional Council (STC) is no longer the force it was 12 months ago but its influence is still felt. It was a political body that emerged in April 2017 amid longstanding calls for a separate southern Yemeni state, which existed between 1967 and 1990.
During the war, it had the political and financial backing of the UAE, which helped it seize Aden in 2019 and become the dominant power across much of the south. It was allied with the government against the Houthis: three STC leaders, including founder Aidarous al-Zubaidi, held seats on the PLC.
In December 2025, its Hadrami Elite Forces seized territory in Hadramaut and al-Mahra governorates, which would have given it control over almost all of the former state of South Yemen.
This sparked fury from Riyadh, which launched air strikes against the STC and backed a counteroffensive led by the Homeland Shield and others. STC forces retreated and were then forced to disband. Zubaidi fled to Abu Dhabi, was forced to leave the PLC and charged with treason. The UAE pulled all resources from Yemen, cutting military funding as well as its provision of public services, including hospitals.
The STC now lacks its previous military and political power. Many of its affiliated fighters are now allied with the pro-government bloc and paid by Saudi Arabia.
But support for the goal of an independent South Yemen remains strong in Aden and surrounding areas, where there have been pro-STC protests, prompting violent crackdowns from pro-government security forces. The group has also reopened branches across the country.
"The Saudis succeeded in dismantling much of the STC’s institutional architecture in January, but they have not dismantled the social, political and military networks on which it was built," Krieg says.
"The southern question remains unresolved, and Saudi Arabia’s inability to deliver security, economic stability and effective governance has arguably reinvigorated southern separatism."
Al-Qaeda in the Arab Peninsula
Al-Qaeda in the Arab Peninsula (AQAP) still has a presence in parts of southern Yemen, despite years of counterterror operations. It wants to establish an Islamic emirate throughout the Arabian Peninsula, and is known for its mass casualty attacks on civilians.
But the group is far weaker than it was a decade ago, when it seized and ruled the port of Mukalla for a year, as well as parts of southern and eastern Yemen. Today it has bases in mountainous outposts, from which it conducts a low-level insurgency, targeting southern government-aligned forces.
AQAP hasn't had direct clashes with the Houthis since 2022, with whom it has conducted prisoner exchanges and has been accused of coordinating smuggling operations.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Casa Enedina Marques: ocupação popular atende mulheres vítimas de violência em Curitiba
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Gustavo de Sousa
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Desde 2019, a Delegacia da Mulher de Curitiba deixou o prédio onde atendia vítimas de violência na Rua Padre Antônio, ao lado do Colégio Estadual do Paraná, na capital. O local seguiu recebendo vítimas que eram levadas ao antigo endereço pela internet, mas encontravam um terreno abandonado.
Foi assim por quase seis anos, até o Movimento Olga Benário ocupar o terreno em 25 de julho de 2025 e transformá-lo na Casa de Referência para Mulher Enedina Marques. Há mais de um ano, voluntárias e voluntários militantes se dividem em turnos para que o espaço acolha as vítimas que buscam apoio durante 24h todos os dias.
Hoje, o GPS não indica mais o endereço na Rua Padre Antônio como a Delegacia da Mulher, que passou a funcionar na Casa da Mulher Brasileira desde o abandono do prédio original. Quem busca o antigo endereço encontra uma equipe de profissionais populares, entre advogadas e psicólogas, da Casa Enedina Marques.
Em alusão ao 25 de novembro, Dia Internacional pela Eliminação da Violência contra as Mulheres, o Brasil de Fato Paraná visitou o espaço que é uma alternativa popular de luta contra a violência de gênero e de solidariedade. A data é uma bandeira dos movimentos feministas latino-americanos e foi instaurada pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) em memória de Patria, Minerva e María Teresa Mirabal, ativistas dominicanas assassinadas em 25 de novembro de 1960 pela ditadura de Rafael Trujillo.
Acolhimento pela militância
A vítima que busca atendimento na casa primeiro passa pelo acolhimento com os voluntários, em uma conversa inicial que leva ao preenchimento de uma ficha com os registros da mulher. A partir daí, quem estiver atendendo pode entender como e para onde a pessoa recebida pode prosseguir.
“Nos diferentes casos, a gente precisa pensar, então, o que vai fazer. A gente já recebeu um caso de uma moça aqui que estava com uma situação de questões de saúde mental, ela estava em um surto psicótico. Muitas mulheres hoje sofrem com transtornos mentais, ou com questões de saúde mental, justamente por essa questão da violência”, relata a psicóloga Júlia Marinha, de 22 anos.
Nesse episódio, Júlia conta que acompanhou de perto a vítima, que foi encaminhada a um Centro de Atenção Psicossocial (CAPS). A mulher estava em busca da delegacia, mas chegou à casa, onde foi acolhida pela psicóloga-militante e acompanhada ao centro psicossocial.
Após o acolhimento e direcionamento para órgãos oficiais, os militantes oferecem acompanhamento pela rede de profissionais do Olga Benário. “Tem mulheres, por exemplo, que não aceitam fazer o BO [Boletim de Ocorrência], e aí a gente respeita e faz esse encaminhamento direto para a rede, mas a gente tenta mostrar essa necessidade, inclusive do BO, da medida protetiva. Então, a gente vai acompanhando na delegacia, acompanhando o processo do IML [Instituto Médico Legal]”, conta a psicóloga.
“Às vezes, a mulher só precisa contar a história dela, ser ouvida e sentir confiança que ela vai ser acolhida”, explica Pietra Comelli. A arquiteta e urbanista de 28 anos integra a coordenação da Casa Enedina Marques em conjunto com Júlia Marinha e a estudante de Relações Internacionais Amanda Carolina, de 21 anos. As jovens contam que mais de 100 mulheres já passaram pelo espaço, que atende vítimas semanalmente.
Além do espaço em Curitiba (PR), existem outras duas casas para atendimentos de mulheres vítimas de violência, em Guaratuba (PR) e Londrina (PR). Os centros de referência levam nomes em homenagem a figuras femininas marcantes na luta contra a violência e o feminicídio: Maria Águeda e Margarida Alves.
Em Curitiba, o Movimento Olga Benário já havia tido outro centro de referência, a Casa Rose Nunes. O espaço funcionava na Rua Treze de Maio, na região central da cidade, mas sofreu reintegração de posse em 2024.
A mudança precisa ser na raiz e na política, para enfrentar o feminicídio
Em 2025, foram registradas 87 mulheres vítimas de feminicídio no Paraná, segundo o Sistema Nacional de Informações de Segurança Pública (Sinesp). Em todos os meses do ano, ao menos duas mulheres foram mortas no estado.
As coordenadoras da casa relatam casos em que receberam mulheres ensanguentadas e esfaqueadas no espaço. Pietra Comelli explica a sensação de receber essas vítimas: “A gente se sensibiliza muito, porque a gente sente que é uma violência com nós mesmas, porque a violência, ela não é um ato que vem de forma isolada.”
Para as jovens, a solução precisa ser buscada dentro dos espaços educativos e políticos, para que se enfrente o feminicídio e a violência antes que aconteçam. O combate, segundo Julia Marinha, tem que vir a favor de melhores condições de vida para a população e também no fim do sistema de exploração das mulheres que enfrentam jornadas exaustivas nos ambientes de trabalho e em casa.
“Todo esse processo que a gente vê relacionado à opressão da mulher está ligado diretamente a essa questão de manter as coisas como estão”, argumenta Marinha.
Violência de gênero aumentou no Paraná
Segundo dados do Sinesp, o Paraná é o quinto estado com mais registros de vítimas de feminicídio no Brasil, em 2026. Somente no território paranaense foram registrados 77 casos até outubro.
Os dados oficiais e levantamentos recentes mostram queda nos feminicídios no Paraná em 2025, mas alta no primeiro semestre de 2026 e volume elevado de ocorrências de violência doméstica, segundo a Secretaria de Estado da Segurança Pública (Sesp) e o Sistema Nacional de Segurança Pública.
No primeiro semestre de 2026, o estado registrou 55 feminicídios, alta de 17% frente aos 47 do mesmo período de 2025. Em janeiro de 2026, foram 6.687 ocorrências de violência doméstica contra mulheres (média de mais de 215 registros por dia). Até agosto de 2026, dados da Sesp indicaram aumento de 1,7% nos casos de violência doméstica contra mulheres. Levantamento do Monitor de Feminicídios no Brasil da Universidade Estadual de Londrina (Lesfem/UEL) identificou 355 casos somando feminicídios consumados e tentados no estado durante todo o ano de 2025.
Dificuldades estruturais na Casa Enedina Marques
Com a ocupação, a coordenação encontrou problemas estruturais no prédio que estava abandonado de 2019 a 2026. Sem abastecimento de água ou energia elétrica, o movimento conta com apoiadores que ajudam nas reformas. De julho de 2025 para cá, foram realizados diversos mutirões para limpeza e ajustes no espaço.
Para manter a casa, as militantes precisam contar com o autofinanciamento. Em um ateliê no segundo andar, camisetas e outros produtos são produzidos para venda e arrecadação de recursos que são utilizados para os reparos. Além disso, são organizados eventos culturais e de vendas, como o brechó de R$ 2,00 que acontece todos os sábados.
As fortes chuvas e tempestades que atingem o Paraná também impõem dificuldades no centro de atendimento. Goteiras surgem no telhado em períodos de vendavais intensos. Por causa da questão estrutural, a Casa Enedina Marques não abriga mulheres no prédio.
O espaço conta com um quarto com camas, mas que é utilizado apenas pelos militantes, durante os turnos de atendimento. Em um dos armários na Sala Alexandra Kollontai, onde são realizados os atendimentos com as vítimas, foram encontradas pastas deixadas para trás com registros de vítimas que buscaram apoio do Estado, no passado. Os registros incluem nomes de vítimas que buscaram atendimento e informações sensíveis das mulheres.
Quem foi Enedina Marques?
Enedina Alves Marques (1913–1981) foi a primeira mulher a se formar em engenharia no Paraná e a primeira engenheira negra do Brasil. Nascida em Curitiba, filha de agricultor e de empregada doméstica, ela começou a trabalhar ainda na infância nas tarefas do lar para custear sua educação e foi alfabetizada aos 12 anos.
Ela se formou professora normalista e lecionou no interior e na capital paranaense, conciliando o trabalho docente e doméstico com os estudos noturnos até ingressar na Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR). Em 1945, conquistou o diploma de Engenharia Civil, aos 32 anos. Ela foi a única mulher em uma turma de 33 alunos.
Após a graduação, construiu uma carreira de destaque no serviço público estadual. Atuou na Secretaria de Viação e Obras Públicas e no Departamento Estadual de Águas e Energia Elétrica. Participou de obras fundamentais para a infraestrutura do estado, como o Plano Hidrelétrico do Paraná e o projeto da Usina Capivari-Cachoeira, a atual Usina Parigot de Souza. Ela também trabalhou na construção do Colégio Estadual do Paraná (CEP) e da Casa do Estudante Universitário de Curitiba (CEU). Enedina se aposentou em 1962.
*Estagiário sob supervisão de Murilo Bernardon.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120415.title: Modell Kuba | Kaffee ohne Wifi
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120415.author: Andreas Knobloch
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120415.text:
- Kultur
- Modell Kuba
Kaffee ohne Wifi
Die kubanische Regierung hat ihr Vorgehen gegen die Nutzung des Satelliteninternetdienstes Starlink verschärft. In Havanna herrscht Unruhe.
In meinem Freundes- und Bekanntenkreis hier in Havanna herrscht seit einigen Tagen eine gewisse Unruhe. Es sind Berichte aufgetaucht, wonach die kubanische Regierung ihr Vorgehen gegen die Nutzung des Satelliteninternetdienstes Starlink verschärft hat. Die Rede ist von Durchsuchungen in Wohnvierteln in Havanna, um versteckte Antennen aufzuspüren.
Nun ist das mit dem Internet auf Kuba so eine Sache. Einen DSL-Anschluss zu Hause haben nur wenige; der Zugang über mobile Daten funktioniert zwar recht gut, aber bei den häufigen Stromausfällen stößt das Netz des staatlichen Telekommunikationsanbieters Etecsa an seine Grenzen. Viele der Funkstationen haben kein Energie-Backup und fallen aus, sobald der Strom weg ist.
Eine Alternative ist Starlink, das Satelliteninternet des US-Raumfahrtunternehmens Space X von Elon Musk. Starlink arbeitet auch bei Stromausfällen weiter, sofern Batterien oder Solarmodule zur Stromversorgung vorhanden sind. Zudem ist Starlink schnell, mit Verbindungsraten zwischen 100 und 400 Megabit in der Sekunde, während es beim Etecsa-Internet durchschnittlich drei sind. Mittlerweile gibt es in Havanna eine ganze Reihe von Cafés, die neben Kaffee und Snacks mit einem schnellen Internetzugang werben. Offen reden will darüber niemand.
Seit Jahrzehnten von den USA boykottiert, kämpft das sozialistische Kuba ums Überleben. Andreas Knobloch berichtet aus Havanna, wie sich das anfühlt. Alle Texte sind hier abrufbar.
Denn die Einfuhr und Nutzung von Starlink-Ausrüstung sind streng untersagt. Trotzdem sind die Geräte auf dem Schwarzmarkt leicht zu finden: »Starlink Mini«-Kits, die in Deutschland um die 200 Euro kosten, werden in Revolico, einer Art kubanischem Ebay, für Preise zwischen 1200 und 1650 US-Dollar angeboten. Angesichts der Preise können sich nur wenige Menschen ein solches Gerät überhaupt leisten. Einige Starlink-Besitzer verkaufen den Zugang auch an Nachbarn oder Freunde weiter.
Das Kommunikationsministerium warnte Ende vergangener Woche, dass die Einfuhr und Nutzung »nicht zertifizierter Geräte« im Land »nicht nur mit einer Geldstrafe« geahndet wird. »Die unbefugte Nutzung des Funkfrequenzspektrums sowie die illegale Einfuhr dieser Geräte können Straftatbestände nach dem kubanischen Strafgesetzbuch erfüllen. Die Sanktionen reichen von der Einziehung der Geräte bis hin zu Freiheitsstrafen in besonders schweren Fällen.« Das kubanische Außenministerium informierte einem anderen Bericht zufolge außerdem die in Havanna akkreditierten Botschaften und internationalen Organisationen, dass es ihnen untersagt sei, Starlink-Terminals einzuführen oder zu nutzen. Das für kubanische Bürger und Unternehmen geltende Verbot wird damit explizit auf Diplomaten ausgeweitet.
Das Ganze hat – wie so vieles auf Kuba – auch eine politische Dimension. Starlink funktioniert unabhängig von der Infrastruktur des staatlichen Anbieters Etecsa. Vor allem rechte Politiker in den USA fordern von Musk seit Längerem, Starlink für Kuba freizuschalten, um das Internetmonopol der kubanischen Regierung anzugreifen. Auch dürfte Kubas Regierung Befürchtungen hegen, dass die USA und andere Botschaften Starlink-Kits an dissidente Kreise verteilen. Für Havanna berührt die Nutzung von Starlink also Fragen der nationalen Sicherheit.
»Mal abwarten, ob es nicht nur Säbelrasseln ist«, sagt ein Bekannter von mir zu den Gerüchten um Starlink-Beschlagnahmungen. Eine befreundete Cafeteria-Betreiberin zeigt sich alarmierter. »Im Viertel sind wir als das ›Wifi-Café‹ bekannt«, erzählt sie. »Abends sitzen die Nachbarn zu Dutzenden auf der Straße vor unserem Lokal und verbinden sich, obwohl wir das Passwort ständig ändern.« Damit ist jetzt erst mal Schluss. »Wir werden auf unbestimmte Zeit kein WLAN haben«, sagt sie. »Das ist einfach zu heikel, ein zu großes Risiko.« Natürlich schade. Meinen Kaffee werde ich aber weiterhin dort trinken.
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Iraq denies reports of troop movements towards Kurdish region
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Iraq denies reports of troop movements towards Kurdish region
Government says there is ‘no truth’ to media reports that Iraqi army units were moving towards the Kurdistan region.
Iraq’s government has denied local media reports that army units were moving towards the Kurdistan region, as a top court backed Baghdad’s authority over the region’s border crossings and oil in a deepening dispute with Erbil.
Government spokesperson Haidar al-Aboudi told state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya on Wednesday that there was “no truth” to the media reports. He said oil smugglers were diverting “tens of billions” into “private pockets and accounts”, and that the salaries of Kurdistan’s public employees were not part of the dispute.
Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said “national sovereignty is indivisible” and that protecting Iraq’s wealth was “a battle for existence” in which the state would end all forms of smuggling.
Al-Zaidi has ordered the Border Ports Authority to take over all crossings in the Kurdistan region and to close unofficial crossings. He has also ordered federal authorities to take over oil fields in Kirkuk, Nineveh, Salahuddin and Diyala that are under Kurdish security control.
Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court has issued an interpretive ruling affirming federal powers to secure international borders and deploy armed forces across all Iraqi territory. It also affirmed Baghdad’s right to oversee border crossings, including those in Kurdistan, the production and export of oil and gas, and both oil and non-oil revenues.
Border Forces Commander Mohammed Abdul Wahab Sukkar al-Saidi told the state-run Iraqi News Agency on Thursday that the command had “begun implementing the directive of the commander-in-chief of the armed forces to close all unofficial crossings” with neighbouring countries.
He did not say how many crossings would be affected.
The Kurdistan Regional Government’s council of ministers, chaired by Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, said it rejected “any attempt to return Iraq to a centralised system”. Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani rejected addressing the region in “military language”, saying this “does not solve any problem”.
Thousands of people gathered in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdish region, on Thursday to protest against the government’s plan to take over border crossings and oil operations.
Reporting from Erbil, Al Jazeera’s Mahmoud Abdel Wahed said the protesters claim the government’s plan “touches on their sovereignty and their territorial integrity, and that this undermines the constitutional rights of the Kurdish people”.
“The question now is whether or not the government of Baghdad will be able to solve this peacefully without triggering a new chapter of conflict, a new political and economic confrontation with the Kurdish region.”
Baghdad says some 200,000 to 230,000 barrels of oil a day are being smuggled, worth about $200m a month, Al Jazeera correspondent Suhaib al-Asa said.
Salim Zakhour, a researcher in constitutional law and political systems, told Al Jazeera that the ruling, issued within 24 hours at al-Zaidi’s request, gave Baghdad a legal basis to act. “The court’s decision is final and decisive,” he said. “But the issue is not only constitutional and legal. There is a political problem.”
The country’s four presidencies have agreed to hold a national dialogue on December 1 to resolve the crisis.
The orders followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company, after which al-Zaidi dismissed eight officials, including Kirkuk’s police chief and operations commander.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).
This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.
PCATI examined 42 cases in which Palestinians filed complaints about the use of torture by Shin Bet interrogators over the last decade.
More than three-quarters said they confessed after the use of “torture or other illegal methods”, and one in 10 provided incriminating statements about other people under torture.
“When it comes to Palestinian detainees, the Israeli legal system officially sanctions torture as a tool for extracting confessions, regardless of whether the content of those confessions is true,” said Sari Bashi, the executive director of PCATI.
“Torture as a tool of interrogation is particularly egregious given initiatives to impose the death penalty in Israel for the first time since 1962.”
Over the years, in hundreds of testimonies, Palestinian detainees have consistently described interrogations employing extreme sleep deprivation, physical violence such as slapping and kicking, threats, sexual violence and being held in stress positions.
Some of this abuse is also laid out in the official records of Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security service. PCATI details the case of a Palestinian lawyer arrested in February 2019 who was subjected to extreme sleep deprivation.
During an interrogation period lasting 27.5 days, or 660 hours, he was questioned for more than 552 hours, an average of 20 hours a day, with one session lasting nearly 48 hours. Some of the remaining 108 hours were spent travelling to and attending detention hearings.
In a 1999 ruling, Israel’s supreme court explicitly prohibited sleep deprivation as a deliberate interrogation method. Despite this, the lawyer was convicted of involvement in shooting attacks based on information extracted during this period.
The state inspector for complaints about Shin Bet interrogations (Mavtan) ruled that the interrogations took place in accordance with procedures, PCATI said.
More than 1,680 torture complaints were filed between 2001 and 2024 with Mavtan. None have led to an indictment.
Other cases are indirectly documented in Israeli judicial records, although judges rarely accept testimony about torture of Palestinians, PCATI said.
In one case, a detainee’s false confession, made under torture, was used as evidence by prosecutors. The man was released after his lawyer presented proof that he was not present at the scene of the crime, PCATI said.
Sleep deprivation was the most frequently used form of torture in complaints examined by PCATI, but more than half included the use of stress positions and other forms of physical violence.
Israel is a signatory to the UN convention against torture, but its legal system has effectively codified the use of violence and abuse where it is deemed “necessary” to extract life-saving information, PCATI said.
In a “necessity interrogation” or “military interrogation”, Shin Bet officials torture detainees “after consulting with their superiors and following an internal procedure for documenting their decisions and conduct”, the report said.
“[A] supposedly narrow exception ballooned and developed into a sprawling system of legal and administrative exceptions that swallowed the so-called rule, enabling the use of violence while maintaining the appearance of prohibition,” it continued.
There is no publicly available information on the scale of “necessity interrogations” inside the Shin Bet, PCATI said. They are an urgent concern as Israel moves to end a de facto moratorium on the death penalty, which had stood since the 1962 execution of the Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann.
“The death penalty is always wrong, because it’s cruel, irreversible and negates the right to life. No one should be executed, particularly not in a system tainted by systematic violence,” Bashi said.
In March, the Knesset passed a racist law allowing the execution of Palestinians convicted of terror charges over deadly attacks, but not Jewish Israelis who commit similar crimes.
In the occupied West Bank, where Palestinians are tried in military courts, execution is now the default punishment for a defendant found guilty of deadly terror attacks.
The legislation drew fierce international criticism, including from the UN’s high commissioner for human rights, Volker Türk, who warned that it would constitute a war crime if enacted.
A separate law empowers a special tribunal to impose death sentences in cases arising from the 7 October 2023 attacks.
Even in rare cases where courts have excluded confessions obtained under torture, Israeli case law allows prosecutors to use information derived from them as evidence to secure convictions.
PCATI said that as detention conditions worsened after October 2023, rights groups documented a sharp rise in violence by Israeli prison guards and soldiers, including beatings, attacks with dogs, electric shocks, threats and rape.
At least 103 Palestinian detainees have died in Israeli custody since 7 October 2023. Of 10 postmortems reviewed by Physicians for Human Rights Israel, five showed signs of physical assault and six showed evidence of medical neglect.
The Israel Prison Service said “all prisoners are held in accordance with the law”. The Shin Bet and Israel’s justice ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

https://www.humanite.fr/sports/football/.title: Saluts nazis, cris de singe, simulation d’égorgement… Des supporters italiens accusés d’actes racistes lors du match PSG-AS Roma
https://www.humanite.fr/sports/football/.author: Éric Serres
https://www.humanite.fr/sports/football/.text:
Lors du match de Ligue des champions opposant le PSG à l’AS Roma, mercredi 25 novembre, des supporters italiens présents au Parc des Princes auraient proféré des injures racistes, imité des cris de singes et effectué des saluts nazis. Une enquête est en cours.
Décidément, les actes et injures racistes sont loin d’avoir été éradiqués des stades. Des jets de bananes sur les pelouses apparus dans les années soixante-dix en Angleterre, aux cris de singes qui descendent des tribunes dans de nombreux pays européens de nos jours (Espagne, Italie…), la parole raciste libérée ne connaît pas de limite.
Mercredi 25 novembre, lors du match opposant le PSG à l’AS Roma (2-2) au Parc des Princes, certains tifosis du club de la capitale italienne ont encore prouvé leur bêtise. Selon plusieurs rapports, ces derniers ont eu des comportements et des gestes racistes à l’égard de Parisiens, en marge du match de Ligue des champions. Des cris de singe et des insultes racistes provenant du parcage visiteur ont été entendus.
Des vérifications en cours
Ces comportements auraient été tenus notamment à l’encontre des abonnés de la tribune Boulogne, qui ont rapporté des saluts nazis. Sur une vidéo, on peut y voir des supporters italiens faire des doigts d’honneur mais surtout un homme semblant d’abord imiter un singe puis mimer un égorgement.
Face à ce déferlement de haine, la direction du club parisien dit prendre la situation « très au sérieux ». Des vérifications sont en cours afin de faire toute la lumière sur l’affaire. Le club a également porté ces éléments à la connaissance des délégués de la rencontre, chargés d’assurer que le match se déroule dans de bonnes conditions. Si ces faits étaient avérés, le club demanderait que des sanctions exemplaires soient prises à l’encontre de leurs auteurs.
Pour rappel l’exhibition de symboles ou comportements racistes dans une enceinte sportive est punie d’un an de prison et 15 000 euros d’amende. Si le geste est requalifié en injure publique à caractère racial, la peine monte jusqu’à un an et 45 000 euros d’amende.
Oui, on s’en doute : vous en avez assez
Voir ces messages d’appel au don, ça peut être pénible. Nous le savons. Et on doit bien vous avouer que nous préférerions ne pas avoir à les écrire…
Mais voilà : c’est crucial pour l’Humanité. Si ce titre existe toujours aujourd’hui, c’est grâce au financement régulier de nos lectrices et lecteurs.
- C’est grâce à votre soutien que nous pouvons exercer notre métier avec passion. Nous ne dépendons ni des intérêts d’un propriétaire milliardaire, ni de pressions politiques : personne ne nous dicte ce que nous devons dire ou taire.
- Votre engagement nous libère aussi de la course aux clics et à l’audience. Plutôt que de chercher à capter l’attention à tout prix, nous choisissons de traiter les sujets que notre rédaction juge essentiels : parce qu’ils méritent d’être lus, compris, partagés. Parce que nous estimons qu’ils vous seront utiles
À l’heure actuelle, moins d’un quart des lectrices et lecteurs qui viennent plus de 3 fois sur le site par semaine nous aident à financer notre travail, par leur abonnement ou par leurs dons. Si vous voulez protéger le journalisme indépendant, s’il vous plaît, rejoignez-les.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: STF não prorroga contrato que poderia manter R$ 394 milhões mensais em depósitos no BRB
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Kennedy Cruz
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O ministro Luiz Fux, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), não autorizou a prorrogação por mais 180 dias do contrato entre o Banco de Brasília (BRB) e o Tribunal de Justiça da Bahia (TJ-BA). O acordo, que permite ao banco administrar depósitos judiciais e recursos destinados ao pagamento de precatórios, será encerrado nesta sexta-feira (27).
Na decisão, divulgada nesta quarta-feira (25), Fux apontou que o BRB não apresentou documentos que comprovassem a continuidade das medidas exigidas pelo Supremo. Em agosto, o ministro havia autorizado uma extensão excepcional de 90 dias, condicionada à continuidade das providências assumidas pelo banco e pelo Governo do Distrito Federal (GDF) no acordo firmado na Ação Cível Originária (ACO) 3.755.
Ao justificar a prorrogação anterior, Fux alertou que a transferência dos depósitos judiciais para a Caixa Econômica Federal poderia comprometer a liquidez do BRB. Isso porque o banco deixaria de receber novos depósitos, mas continuaria responsável pelos saques das contas sob sua administração.
“Com a cessação da vigência contratual e a incontinenti migração da custódia dos valores do BRB à Caixa Econômica Federal, parece provável um impacto grave, imediato e substancial à instituição financeira sucedida, máxime no que toca à sua liquidez. […] o termo iminente do pacto acarretará a interrupção da entrada de valores substanciais sem que as saídas de valores cessem”, escreveu o ministro.
Risco de perder R$ 394 milhões mensais
Segundo informações apresentadas pelo próprio BRB ao STF em agosto, no pedido que levou à primeira prorrogação do contrato, o encerramento do acordo significaria deixar de receber cerca de R$ 394 milhões mensais em novos depósitos. Na ocasião, o banco também alegou que continuaria obrigado a processar os levantamentos das contas sob sua administração, cujo custo operacional seria de aproximadamente R$ 395 milhões.
Na nova solicitação, apresentada próximo ao fim do prazo de 90 dias, o BRB pediu mais 180 dias de prorrogação. Ao analisar o pedido, Fux destacou que o banco não comprovou a continuidade das tratativas e das providências exigidas pelo STF. O ministro também observou que a solicitação foi apresentada já na iminência do fim do prazo anterior.
“Até o presente momento, o Banco de Brasília S.A. – BRB não fez acostar aos autos nenhum elemento documental atinente à comprovação da obrigação de demonstrar a continuidade das tratativas havidas na ACO 3.755, tampouco demonstrou qualquer outra providência empreendida ou em curso para o desiderato em tela”, registrou o ministro.
O contrato também abrange a administração de R$ 2 bilhões de uma operação de crédito do governo da Bahia, com garantia da União, destinada ao pagamento de precatórios.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Highway explosion in Giza: How deadly are Egypt’s roads and railways?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Highway explosion in Giza: How deadly are Egypt’s roads and railways?
Egypt has suffered another tragedy as a deadly road explosion kills 31 and injures dozens.
An explosion rocked a highway in Cairo when a fuel truck overturned and caught fire, killing at least 31 people on Wednesday.
Egypt’s public prosecutor has announced an investigation into the crash, and the Ministry of Health said it will continue to monitor the situation.
But Egypt is no stranger to deadly accidents on its roads, despite spending billions of dollars on its transportation systems.
So what exactly caused the explosion and how unsafe are Egypt’s roads?
Here is what we know.
What happened?
On Wednesday evening, a fuel tanker travelling on a busy ring road in Giza’s Imbabah district, a highly populated, working-class part of the Greater Cairo area, crashed and exploded, causing a fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others.
Local media have reported that the explosion happened after the truck driver swerved to avoid a high-voltage cable which fell in front of the vehicle.
Twenty-seven vehicles were caught up and burned in the accident, according to Egypt’s judicial office.
Thirty-nine ambulances were dispatched to the scene, taking the injured to nearby hospitals for treatment, the Health Ministry said.
Egypt’s public prosecutor announced that there will be an investigation into the crash and ordered DNA samples from victims.
How unsafe are Egypt’s roads?
Egypt, which has a population of around 120m, is known for its dangerous roads. It clocked up a total of 44,940 road deaths and 476,126 injuries between 2019 and 2025, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).
Last year, more than 5,800 road deaths and 84,000 road injuries were recorded by the agency, with pedestrians making up more than one-third of those killed.
Children under the age of 15 made up 1,580 of the deaths and 29,101 of the injured.
A World Bank report in 2020 found that the incidents occur because 97 percent of Cairo’s streets lack traffic lights and 78 percent of them have no clear pedestrian footpaths.
What is Egypt’s train system like?
In 2025, there were 170 train incidents recorded, resulting in the deaths of 44 people and injuries to 215.
Earlier this month, at least seven people were killed and more than 125 others injured when a train backed into another, also in Giza, triggering calls for political accountability.
Egypt’s Ministry of Transport said that approximately $37bn was spent on transport investment between 2014 and 2024, but recurring incidents have raised questions about the effectiveness of this project.
The leader of the centrist Reform and Development Party’s parliamentary bloc, Irene Saeed, called for full financial transparency on how the Ministry of Transport spent its funding and loans in 2016.
A member of the Egyptian Parliament and leader of the Justice Party, Abdel Moneim Imam, told Al Jazeera earlier this month that the continued “turning of a blind eye to the shortcomings and the recurrence of accidents without genuine accountability leads to the continuation of the crisis”.

https://www.humanite.fr/environnement/es.title: Vers une marée noire ? Ce que l’on sait du naufrage au large d’Ibiza d’un navire chargé de milliers de tonnes de diesel
https://www.humanite.fr/environnement/es.author: La rédaction avec AFP
https://www.humanite.fr/environnement/es.text:
Un navire transportant jusqu’à 7 000 tonnes de diesel a coulé, jeudi 26 novembre, au large de l’île espagnole d’Ibiza, en Méditerranée, faisant un mort parmi les membres de l’équipage, ont annoncé les services de secours. Si « aucun débris du navire, aucun objet flottant ni aucun signe de pollution » n’a été pour l’heure signalé, le plan national d’urgence contre la pollution maritime a été activé au niveau 2.
C’est un drame humain qui pourrait se doubler d’une catastrophe environnementale. Un navire transportant jusqu’à 7 000 tonnes de diesel a coulé jeudi 26 novembre au large de l’île espagnole d’Ibiza, en Méditerranée, faisant un mort parmi les membres de l’équipage.
Le Med Emre, un pétrolier transportant des produits chimiques (plus de 8 millions de litres de diesel et 1,2 million de litres de pétrole, selon les médias espagnols) et battant pavillon maltais, a fait naufrage à quelque 25 milles nautiques (46,3 km) au nord-est de l’île touristique, située dans l’archipel des Baléares, ont indiqué les services de secours dans un communiqué.
Le plan national d’urgence contre la pollution maritime activé
Le navire était parti du port d’Algésiras, dans le sud de l’Espagne, et se dirigeait vers Barcelone, au nord. L’équipage de 17 membres a été secouru mais l’un d’entre eux a ensuite été déclaré mort à l’hôpital, à Ibiza, selon les secours. Six autres souffrent de « blessures légères », notamment d’hypothermie.
Les éventuels dommages environnementaux sont en cours d’évaluation, au moyen d’un navire spécialisé, le « Clara Campoamor », et d’un avion appartenant au service espagnol de sauvetage maritime « Salvamento Maritimo », ont ajouté les secours.
Pour l’heure les autorités se veulent rassurantes : « aucun débris du navire, aucun objet flottant ni aucun signe de pollution » n’a été signalé dans le dernier rapport daté de 7h37, selon des sources gouvernementales citées par la RTVE. Le plan national d’urgence contre la pollution maritime a toutefois été activé au niveau 2, le deuxième plus élevé.
« Nous suivons de près les conséquences environnementales potentielles de cet accident. De fait, le Plan national d’intervention en cas de pollution marine a été activé au niveau deux afin de mener à bien toute surveillance nécessaire et de réagir à toute situation qui pourrait en résulter », assure le directeur général des situations d’urgence du gouvernement des Baléares.
La Terre de nos batailles
La justice climatique, c’est notre bataille. Celle qui relie luttes environnementales et sociales pour contrer un système capitaliste faisant ventre de tout. Du vivant, de la planète, de notre humanité.
Il n’y a pas de fatalité.
- Nous démasquons les manipulations des lobbies.
- Nous battons en brèche les dénis climatiques mortifères.
- Nous mettons en valeur les initiatives visant à réduire les inégalités environnementales et les fractures sociales.
Soutenez-nous.
Je veux en savoir plus

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Governo de Minas terá de explicar indícios de corrupção em contrato de R$ 142 milhões
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
“R$ 72 milhões já foram pagos. Mas as recentes denúncias que recebi dão conta de que, desde setembro de 2025, as atividades do Instituto foram paralisadas, mas os consultores permaneceram contratados e remunerados somente para habilitar a emissão de notas fiscais, pois assim se comprovaria que o contrato está ok”, afirmou a deputada estadual Beatriz Cerqueira (PT), durante audiência pública realizada nesta terça-feira (24), na Assembleia Legislativa de Minas Gerais (ALMG).
A declaração expõe a gravidade das suspeitas envolvendo o contrato de R$ 142 milhões firmado pelo governo de Minas Gerais, por meio da Secretaria de Estado de Educação (SEE), com o Instituto Hortense, organização fundada pelo cantor sertanejo Leo Chaves, da dupla Victor & Leo. O acordo foi celebrado sem licitação para a compra de materiais didáticos e a oferta de serviços de formação em educação socioemocional.
O governo estadual terá de esclarecer por que o contrato foi ampliado em mais de 570%, quais critérios justificaram a dispensa de concorrência e por que, segundo as denúncias apresentadas, pagamentos teriam continuado mesmo após a suspensão das atividades e diante da falta de entrega dos materiais previstos.
O caso foi debatido pela Comissão de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia da ALMG, em audiência requerida por Beatriz Cerqueira, que preside o colegiado. Participaram o subsecretário de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica, Paulo Leandro de Carvalho, e a auditora do Tribunal de Contas do Estado (TCE-MG), Paula Fernanda Martins.
As denúncias se somam ao escândalo envolvendo o programa Aprender Já, que apontou desvio de R$ 348,4 milhões na Secretaria de Estado de Educação para a compra de livros escolares que, segundo as informações apresentadas, sequer chegaram a ser utilizados. O caso levou à demissão do ex-secretário Rossieli Soares, durante o governo de Romeu Zema (Novo).
Contrato ampliado em 570% sem estudo prévio
O primeiro contrato com o Instituto Hortense foi assinado em 19 de novembro de 2024, no valor de R$ 21 milhões. A proposta previa atender 100 mil estudantes dos anos finais do ensino fundamental e formar 2 mil profissionais da educação.
Menos de um mês depois, o acordo foi tornado sem efeito. Em fevereiro de 2025, a secretaria efetivou uma nova contratação, desta vez no valor de R$ 142 milhões, para atender 670 mil estudantes e formar quase 10 mil profissionais.
Durante a audiência, Beatriz Cerqueira questionou a ampliação do valor e do escopo do contrato e cobrou a apresentação de estudos técnicos que justificassem a mudança. Segundo o subsecretário Paulo Leandro, não houve estudo prévio para embasar a ampliação. A alteração teria ocorrido por decisão de gestão, estendendo o atendimento aos estudantes do 6º ao 9º ano da rede estadual.
A contratação foi realizada por dispensa de licitação, sob a justificativa de que a metodologia de educação socioemocional oferecida pelo instituto seria específica e não encontraria concorrência equivalente no mercado.
Para Cerqueira, a justificativa não se sustenta. A parlamentar criticou a ausência de disputa entre instituições que poderiam prestar o serviço e questionou por que universidades públicas mineiras não foram consideradas para a execução do projeto.
“Um governo que começou com o partido Novo e terminou com um PSD, mas que no seu conteúdo ideológico dizia sempre do direito do mercado concorrer. E olha a contradição: é uma deputada do PT que faz audiências para lembrar que deveria ter tido licitação. O mercado teria que ter tido oportunidade de concorrer”, afirmou.
A deputada também citou instituições como UEMG, Unimontes, UFMG, UFVJM, Universidade Federal de Viçosa e Universidade Federal de Lavras como alternativas para a formação dos profissionais e o desenvolvimento de ações na área.
Pagamentos continuaram após suspensão
Um dos principais pontos levantados na audiência diz respeito à execução financeira do contrato. De acordo com Beatriz Cerqueira, o acordo previa 23 parcelas de aproximadamente R$ 4,3 milhões, e cerca de R$ 72,9 milhões já haviam sido pagos antes da suspensão.
A parlamentar afirmou que recebeu denúncias de que as atividades do instituto estariam paralisadas desde setembro de 2025, mas os pagamentos continuaram sendo realizados.
Segundo relatos apresentados por ela, consultores contratados para atuar nas Superintendências Regionais de Ensino teriam permanecido conectados à plataforma do instituto por quase 12 horas diárias, mesmo sem a realização efetiva das atividades previstas, para comprovar a execução dos serviços e permitir a emissão de notas fiscais.
O número de consultores, conforme os dados apresentados na audiência, passou de 20 para 46 mesmo após a suspensão das atividades. Cerqueira questionou a destinação dos recursos, considerando que cada consultor receberia cerca de R$ 6 mil brutos por mês.
A deputada também denunciou relatos de pressão excessiva, assédio e demissões em massa de profissionais nos meses de julho e agosto de 2026.
Materiais não entregues e investigação
O subsecretário Paulo Leandro informou que a fiscalização da secretaria identificou, em janeiro de 2026, que os materiais didáticos previstos no contrato não estavam sendo entregues. A previsão era fornecer livros para aproximadamente 600 mil estudantes.
Segundo informações apresentadas pela deputada, em 2025 haviam sido entregues apenas 34 mil livros, enquanto, em 2026, cerca de 600 mil exemplares deixaram de ser disponibilizados aos estudantes.
O representante da SEE também afirmou que a equipe técnica da própria secretaria concluiu que a contratação não era vantajosa para a administração pública. A execução financeira teria sido superior à contrapartida efetivamente entregue.
A contratação foi assinada em novembro de 2024, durante a gestão do então secretário Igor de Alvarenga. A ex-subsecretária de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica Kellen Silva Senra foi apontada como uma das responsáveis pela gestão do contrato e assinou o acordo de 2025.
A denúncia apresentada por Beatriz Cerqueira já está no Tribunal de Contas do Estado. De acordo com a auditora Paula Fernanda Martins, a representação está em análise pela equipe técnica. Após essa etapa, o processo retornará ao conselheiro relator e será encaminhado ao Ministério Público de Contas para emissão de parecer. Os responsáveis terão direito à defesa antes do julgamento.
A deputada afirmou que, caso sejam identificados indícios de uso de recursos federais na execução do contrato, também acionará a Polícia Federal (PF).
Governo se posiciona
Em audiência pública, o subsecretário de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica, Paulo Leandro de Carvalho, afirmou que o contrato com o Instituto Hortense está suspenso e que o governo de Minas Gerais estuda a possibilidade de encerramento definitivo.
Segundo ele, o ex-secretário de Educação Gustavo Braga, que esteve à frente da pasta entre abril e agosto de 2026, determinou a suspensão cautelar do acordo para revisão. Uma apuração preliminar realizada pela controladoria interna da secretaria foi encaminhada à Controladoria-Geral do Estado (CGE), que conduz a investigação.
O subsecretário informou ainda que a equipe técnica da SEE não identificou vantagem na manutenção da contratação. A partir dessa avaliação, o setor jurídico passou a analisar alternativas para a extinção do contrato, seja por acordo entre as partes ou de forma unilateral, com possibilidade de devolução de valores aos cofres públicos.
Carvalho também afirmou que não ocupava o cargo no momento da assinatura do contrato e que a equipe técnica está avaliando as medidas cabíveis diante das irregularidades identificadas.
Até o momento, o governo aguarda a conclusão da investigação da CGE. O contrato permanece suspenso.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: ‘Proscribing free speech’: Why a Jewish group is challenging UK’s Hamas ban
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
‘Proscribing free speech’: Why a Jewish group is challenging UK’s Hamas ban
The Jewish Network for Palestine says the complete ban on Hamas was being used to stifle free speech and to target its members.
London, United Kingdom – The Jewish Network for Palestine (JNP) has filed an application to reverse the proscription of Hamas under Britain’s Terrorism Act, arguing that the ban is being used against its members and is hampering freedom of speech in the United Kingdom.
The JNP filed a formal de-proscription application on Thursday under Section 4 of the Terrorism Act, which oversees applications to remove a group from the UK’s list of banned organisations.
This follows the arrest of the 80-year-old son of Auschwitz survivors and the prosecution of a 72-year-old Jewish writer – both members of the JNP’s Steering Group – for pro-Palestinian and anti-Zionist speech.
The JNP was founded in 2018 by British members of the United States organisation Jewish Voice for Peace, a group which aims to bring together Jews and non-Jews who support Palestine. It is one of 11 Jewish and Jewish-led organisations that form the UK’s Jewish bloc for Palestine, which is frequently present at protests against Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and pogroms in the West Bank.
According to the chair of the JNP, David Cannon, proscription of Hamas has made it near-impossible to openly discuss the events of October 7, 2023, when Hamas led an attack on villages and army outposts in southern Israel. In particular, the JNP says, it has been unable to talk publicly about false narratives that followed for fear of contravening the act.
“Now, all of these things needed to be discussed, but the UK government’s proscription of the political wing of Hamas has made referring to such evidence [of false reporting] risk the accusation of supporting Hamas, which is not what we’re saying. We’re saying that we want to discuss these issues,” he said.
In the days following October 7, when more than 1,000 people were killed, many stories about babies being killed by Hamas fighters and mass rapes were circulated in international media. There has been no evidence of these.
Cannon added that one of the group’s active members had resigned, fearing that what she could say would affect her immigration status if found to violate the act.
According to the application, the JNP has about 600 members and supporters.
‘Disproportionate interference’
The JNP’s application was filed five years to the day after the British government proscribed the whole of Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
Hamas’s armed wing had been banned in 2001, but in 2021 the then-Home Secretary Priti Patel extended the ban to cover the whole political group, describing the organisation as “fundamentally and rabidly anti-Semitic” and arguing that the proscription was required to protect the Jewish community.
The government did not, however, explain how the proscription of Hamas would protect the Jewish community in the UK. Instead, the JNP argues that the designation has now been used against the Jewish community it was supposed to protect.
The group also argues that the continued proscription of Hamas in its entirety was a “disproportionate interference with the rights of JNP and its members” under the European Convention on Human Rights Articles 9, 10 and 11 on freedom of thought, expression and assembly, with the burden of the proscription falling on people in Britain.
Finally, they argue, Hamas has “no presence in the UK and has not been shown to pose a specific threat to it”.
“The less intrusive position that applied before November 2021 shows that proscription of the whole organisation is not necessary. On a proper application of the policy, and with the impact on JNP weighed, continued proscription is not justified,” the application stated.
Following the JNP’s application, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmoud has 90 days to consider it beginning the day after it is received. If it is refused, the group can appeal the decision.
‘Chilling free speech’
Tony Greenstein, 72, an anti-Zionist writer and blogger and prominent member of the JNP, was prosecuted for publishing a blog on October 7, 2023, titled “Full Support for the Gaza Ghetto Uprising”, in which he evoked the Jewish Warsaw Ghetto Uprising in 1943.
While his post only mentioned Hamas in passing, in November 2024 Greenstein was charged under section 12 of the British Terrorism Act with inviting support for Hamas on the basis of one sentence in that blog and for writing “please share” on social media, promoting the piece.
After nearly three years and appearances in different courts, Greenstein was acquitted in August this year.
“If you can’t actually say what you think about an organisation without watching over your shoulder in case you’re contravening some law, then that’s chilling free speech, and that is the real issue,” Greenstein told Al Jazeera.
“That’s been made time and time again about the Terrorism Act. It’s really about clamping down on free speech,” he added.
During the criminal proceedings against him, five banks and building societies closed his accounts.
In Greenstein’s view, arresting Jews is not the best way to protect the Jewish community in the UK.
“It’s a very good way of protecting Zionism and the Zionists, and that is the difference,” he said. “The way they dress up their foreign policy choices is by saying they’re protecting a particular community. The reality is, of course, banning or proscribing Hamas has nothing at all to do with racist attacks against Jews, they’re completely separate phenomena.”
He added: “Hamas doesn’t operate in Britain. It never has operated in Britain …So how can we be at risk of being attacked by a group that doesn’t even exist here? It was about stopping people expressing an opinion on what’s happening in Gaza and in the occupied territories. That’s a very different thing.”
The right to oppose a genocide
One of the founders of the JNP is Haim Bresheeth-Zabner, an 80-year-old Jewish-Israeli anti-Zionist filmmaker and film studies professor at the School of African and Oriental Studies (SOAS).
He was arrested and held for 13 hours in November 2024 immediately after he made a speech at a protest in Swiss Cottage, north London. It was part of wider protests held weekly by the International Jewish Anti-Zionist Network with the JNP’s involvement against the Israeli ambassador and the actions of the Israeli government in Gaza. In his speech, Bresheeth-Zabner said that the Israeli army “cannot fight the resistance” and “cannot win against Hamas … against Hezbollah …[or] against the Houthis”.
“They [the police] refused to discuss with me what I said that is considered applicable under the Terrorism Act. It took many hours of waiting in a very cold car park … I’m 80 … I have heart failure and cancer. So I wasn’t feeling all that well, but that didn’t make a difference. I also told them that I need to take my medications in the early evening, and they disregarded that,” Bresheeth-Zabner told Al Jazeera.
While he was not charged following his arrest, he said the ban has been used against people who want to speak up against the genocide in Gaza, making it impossible to criticise the Israeli army.
“This is a really odd situation where Britain, as a society, as a politicised society, as a country, as a regime, if you want, is not acting to uphold international law, and is proscribing our ability to speak against the genocide, to speak against Zionism, to speak against Israel. When we do that, we are arrested. We are charged,” he said.
“We’re [the JNP] supporting human rights, and human rights include the right to oppose a genocide, not just our right to oppose a genocide, but of course the rights of the victims of the genocide to resist it.”

https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.title: ‘I was very aggressive. They threw me out of every school’ … Julie Delpy on acting, anger and predatory directors
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.author: Emine Saner
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.text:
To listen to Julie Delpy talk about her workload is to feel the need for a nap coming on. She is writing six screenplays at the moment that range from dark comedies to thrillers. “I don’t do monoculture,” she says. If her producer hadn’t reined her in, she would be working on five horror film scripts too.
The actor, writer and director says she doesn’t sleep well – she can sit at her desk for up to 18 hours, writing “until I run out of steam. I know you could think I’m exaggerating. I’m not. If you look at my computer, you will see how bad it is.”
We’re on a video call, Delpy from her home in Los Angeles. She is charming – intense and funny in big black-framed glasses. “I look so weird with this angle on my hair,” she says, of the ceiling light behind her. “Like an angry bald man!”
Now 56, she has been working in film since she was a teenager, in a career that has spanned European arthouse (such as Krzysztof Kieślowski’s Three Colours: White, from 1994), romance (Richard Linklater’s Before trilogy, which began in 1995) and indies (Jim Jarmusch’s Broken Flowers, 2005). In 2015, she was even in Avengers: Age of Ultron.
As a writer and director, Delpy has made eight feature films, including 2 Days in Paris and its follow-up, 2 Days in New York. She is, by any measure, a Hollywood success, and yet she still has the feel of an outsider. She has been, she will say a little later, “broken many times” by the industry.
Now the comedy she directed and co-wrote, Meet the Barbarians, about a French village that takes in what local people believe will be a Ukrainian refugee family, only to find out they are Syrian, is being released in the US. The idea for the film came out of the 2015 refugee crisis, in which 1.4 million people arrived in Europe via the Mediterranean after fleeing the Middle East. She interviewed refugees and organisations that worked with them – many of whom spoke about Europe’s reluctance to make long-term plans for the people arriving on its shores. Since Russia invaded Ukraine, more than 4 million Ukrainian refugees have been granted temporary protection status to stay in the EU. She found the difference in approach to these two groups of people startling. “So many people I know [in Europe] were welcoming Ukrainian refugees, which is great. But I was like, wow, I’ve just interviewed hundreds of people that have been treated like shit, and no one would open their doors to them.”
She is an immigrant herself, she says, having moved from her native France to the US in 1990, but, she points out: “I’m an immigrant who is blond with blue eyes.” She is lucky, she says, even if her husband, the production manager Dimitris Birbilis, who is Greek, has experienced more overt xenophobia: “I can feel that there are looks sometimes.” (She has a 17-year-old son with her previous partner, composer Marc Streitenfeld.) “We have legal papers, I’m an American, but you feel the tension.” Trump, she says, “has brought so much darkness to this country. He’s made people confident to say the most horrible things – racist, misogynist, homophobic things without feeling affected. It’s very disturbing.”
Politicians around the world, she believes, are “pushing their agenda of fear and fearmongering to get elected. Refugees don’t steal jobs. They don’t destroy the economy. All that is bullshit.” France is facing the possibility of a far-right president in Marine Le Pen next year. Delpy is off now, switching from lambasting the demonisation of “wokeism” to the distortion of “reality and truth, so much that it’s difficult to even talk about history or facts with some people”. She feels it’s a scary time. “The most unqualified people are in power around the world, and I’m terrified of that.”
Delpy’s parents were actors and have appeared in her films (her mother, Marie Pillet, died in 2009). Her father, Albert Delpy, played her fictional father in 2 Days in Paris and is also in Meet the Barbarians. Is he good at taking direction from her? “No. It’s like directing King Kong.” She laughs. “As he’s getting older, he’s getting sweeter. We used to have major fights, but now he’s such a good guy.” She describes a bohemian Parisian childhood. She didn’t like school. “I was very aggressive, so they threw me out of every school until I got out completely and became an actor,” she says.
She recently went back through some of her diaries and stories from working as a child actor, “just cleaning up, going through shit. It explained a lot for me. I realised how sensitive I was and how much I was putting on an armour to survive.” She found things she had written as a child actor, she says, “about this business and how creepy it was in France with directors”.
At 13, at an audition, she says she was alone with a director in his apartment when he asked her to take her clothes off. “I took the script and threw it in his face,” says Delpy. She told her parents. “I said: ‘I don’t want to be an actress if that’s what it means.’ And they were like: ‘Well, look at us. We didn’t do that.’”
Other early experiences were better. Delpy’s first film role was in Jean-Luc Godard’s Detective. “It was great to work with him, and he was such a nice guy,” she says. “I mean, he was not a nice guy” – the influential French director was notoriously volatile and difficult – “but with me he was incredibly nice and respectful, and protective.”
But sexual harassment as a young woman in Hollywood was unavoidable. “I remember this guy, who’s still around, a very powerful guy. He tried to break into the bathroom where I was at a party.” She has spoken before about turning down a director’s sexual advances around the same time, when she was in her early 20s, and that he had spread word in the business that she was “difficult”. “The minute you say no to people …” She pauses. “And also the way I was expressing myself, I was very straightforward.”
When Harvey Weinstein’s company Miramax was involved in releasing the second part of the Three Colours trilogy, White, in which Delpy starred, she says she chose to stay in a different hotel from him because of the rumours she had heard. “I was not naive because I was coming from France, where it was like, you were dodging the paedophiles basically,” she says with a grim laugh. “I had the luck to not be a young girl from the midwest who has no idea what’s going on.”
Making Before Sunrise (1995), in which she plays Céline, a beautiful young free spirit who spends a night in Vienna with Jesse (Ethan Hawke), Delpy says she contributed many lines and ideas to the script and was frustrated that this wasn’t recognised with a writing credit. “I went through a really rough time in my late 20s but it took me reading my journal to actually know that. I was like: ‘Oh, that sounds like a breakdown.’” On the surface, she says, most people wouldn’t have known anything was wrong. “I wouldn’t cry and stay alone.” Instead, she felt a lot of anger. “I was doing quite a lot of drinking.”
She was, however, along with Hawke, recognised as a writer on the sequel, Before Sunset, which was nominated for a best adapted screenplay Oscar. When Before Sunrise was released, she says, it wasn’t a big success. “It grew with the second film. Even when I was writing the second one, my agent fired me, saying I was wasting my time writing a sequel to a little indie film that no one gave a shit about, and I should be going on auditions instead of writing.”
Delpy doesn’t come across as bitter, but she is evidently still angry. “People have hurt me in this business,” she says. When I ask her to elaborate, she talks vaguely, mentioning people “telling me I was stupid. Trying to break my confidence.” Just a few years ago, she says, a financier pulled out of her sci-fi drama My Zoe at the last minute, put off, she believes, by someone briefing against her. “There’s still a system that’s trying to keep people where they want them to be,” she says.
Delpy always wanted to write and direct, and she made her first film, Blah Blah Blah, a short that was shown at Sundance, in 1995. She never wanted to be typecast as the ingenue. “I was able to get out of that pretty quickly,” she says. It became even more important to create her own work as she got older in an industry where good parts for middle-aged actors are still scarce. Twenty years ago, it was even worse. “Yeah, I didn’t love some of the stuff, so I started writing.” She created and starred in the 2021 Netflix series On the Verge, about the lives of four women in their late 40s, but it lasted for only one season. “I don’t know what happened,” she says, but “the algorithm doesn’t love women in that age group apparently”.
Next year Delpy is in a Ruben Östlund comedy with Keanu Reeves, The Entertainment System Is Down, and in actor Sonoya Mizuno’s directorial debut, Stages, about a young dancer at an elite ballet school. She is regularly asked about a fourth Before film but says 2013’s Before Midnight is the last one. “Richard approached us at one point, but the idea didn’t really go very far.” Reportedly, her character, Céline, was going to die. “I wasn’t into it. Ethan was not really into it, and Richard was not really into it. Nobody liked it.” She laughs. “Now we’ve passed the time that we were supposed to do it. It’s a trilogy. We’ll never know what happens to them.”
Does she feel – as I do when I watch those films – sad and wistful for the feeling of time passing, and what might have been? No, says Delpy, “I’m really excited about the future.” She says it was good to revisit the journals of her childhood and youth, “but now I’ve done it, I’m focusing on stuff I’m writing”. Those six (and counting) screenplays are calling and she’s energised because she thinks they are among her best work. It’s all she can do not to become completely consumed by them.
She says she has to make an effort to see people, “because I’m so happy in my world. You create a world and you live in it. I know it’s a film, but it’s also like jumping into a parallel universe. It’s the most fun thing in the world. I love making films because what was only in your head becomes something tangible.” She pauses. “I’m not saying all of this is great. A lot of it might end up turning shit, right? But, you know, I’m doing it anyway.”

https://www.humanite.fr/politique/essais.title: Le gouvernement veut torpiller la loi sur l’indemnisation des victimes des essais nucléaires en Polynésie
https://www.humanite.fr/politique/essais.author: Benjamin König
https://www.humanite.fr/politique/essais.text:
Patiemment élaboré, notamment par la députée de Polynésie Mereana Reid-arbelot, le texte de loi qui vise à améliorer l’indemnisation des victimes des essais nucléaires est l’objet d’une tentative de sabotage par le gouvernement. Mais les députés peuvent résister, en votant la loi ce 1er décembre.
Des années de travaux, une commission d’enquête, des dizaines de réunion, d’auditions des associations de victimes, puis la construction d’une proposition de loi adoptée à l’unanimité par l’Assemblée et le Sénat : tout ce travail pourrait être balayé d’un revers de main par le gouvernement. C’est le danger qui pèse sur un texte ô combien important : celui visant « à reconnaître les victimes des essais nucléaires français et à améliorer leur indemnisation ».
La loi doit être examinée en seconde lecture par l’Assemblée ce 1er décembre, pour une adoption définitive. Elle prévoit notamment la suppression du seuil d’exposition arbitraire fixé à un millisievert. C’est sans compter sur l’intervention de dernière minute du gouvernement, qui a pourtant participé à l’élaboration du texte et veut maintenant le modifier, repoussant d’autant la fin de son parcours législatif que permettrait un ultime vote conforme.
« Un changement de posture incompréhensible, choquant et méprisant »
Mereana Reid-Arbelot, la députée de Polynésie issue du parti de gauche indépendantiste Tavini Huira’atira (Servir le peuple, en tahitien), co-rapporteuse du texte, s’inquiète de ce que « le gouvernement, par la voix de la ministre des Armées, Catherine Vautrin, a changé de cap, affichant clairement sa volonté de faire obstacle à une adoption conforme du texte ».
Moetai Brotherson, le président de la Polynésie, a également réagi, en dénonçant « un changement de posture incompréhensible, choquant et méprisant tant pour les Polynésiens que pour les vétérans ». Ce revirement illustre à quel point la question des essais nucléaires et de leur réparation demeure un sujet tabou pour l’État français, qui s’enfonce dans le déni et le mensonge dès qu’il s’agit « d’avancer et de réparer les erreurs du passé », pointe Mereana Reid-Arbelot.

Kushner: 'The good thing about the war is that Gaza does need to be built. So why build it into what it was?'
US special envoy Jared Kushner framed the destruction of Gaza as an opportunity to rebuild differently rather than restoring it to how it was before Israel’s genocide.
"The good thing about the war is that Gaza does need to be built. So why build it into what it was?" he said during an interview on Mathias Dopfner’s MD Meets podcast..
Kushner outlined a vision for Gaza’s future focused on reconstruction, economic development, and regional cooperation. He suggested that if Gaza can be “solved”, there would be opportunities for joint projects with Egypt, including developing data centres and energy projects in the Sinai Peninsula.
Since October 2023, Israel has killed at least 74,700 Palestinians, leaving much of the territory in ruins and forcing 2.1 million people to live in tents and makeshift shelters. Meanwhile, the Israeli military says it currently controls 60 percent of the land.
