Eisenkot navigates tricky waters as he tests power-sharing with Netanyahu
Some of his allies are calling for such an arrangement, but it would represent a betrayal of his pre-election promise.
The 2026 Israeli elections were termed the most consequential in recent decades for the country – for multiple reasons.
For Benjamin Netanyahu, the caretaker prime minister, and his right-wing coalition, the elections were about keeping the far-right in power to protect the formative changes they enacted in state policies and institutions. For the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot – or the “change bloc”, as it is referred to – the promise was to replace the failed October 7 government as they termed it, rehabilitate Israel’s international standing, and end internal divisions.
Once the results were announced, things changed. Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with forming Israel’s next government. But his bloc does not have enough seats in the Knesset to win a vote of confidence on its own. The United Arab List and the Joint List, parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, have 19 seats and are willing to back Eisenkot in his efforts to replace Netanyahu as Israel’s premier. But some in the change bloc, such as Avigdor Lieberman, promised not to support any government coalition that includes an Arab-led party or one that depended on votes from Palestinian citizens of Israel.
This, despite the fact that Lieberman himself became chair of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee thanks to those same votes. That contradiction was pointed out by Mohamed Majadli, the chief editor of AlNas Radio in Israel and an analyst on the country’s Channel 12.
In such a limited space for political manoeuvres, Eisenkot embarked on forming a coalition, holding talks with his partners, while also trying to open channels of communication with ultra-Orthodox parties, particularly the United Torah Judaism party. At the same time, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led efforts to form a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party and succeeded in convincing Eisenkot’s Yashar party to open formal talks with Likud.
The prospect of reneging on the change bloc’s central promise to oust Netanyahu looms large over these talks. Bennett and others are advocating for that outcome in light of the lack of a clear Zionist majority against Israel’s longest-serving prime minister.
Meanwhile, leader of the Democrats group, Yair Golan, has publicly opposed any unity formula with Netanyahu and has called out Bennett for his efforts to reach it. The Yashar-Likud talks are complex and overshadowed by, among other issues, accusations between the two sides.
Netanyahu accuses the change bloc of working to undermine Israel by working with Arab-led parties, which he has referred to as “the enemy”. Eisenkot has gone on the record saying that Netanyahu endangers the security of Israel and is willing to ignite war for his personal gain.
From Likud’s perspective, a unity government would require a rotation agreement on the premiership. That means that rather than getting rid of Netanyahu, Eisenkot would have to agree to Netanyahu staying on as prime minister for two years, or agreeing to serve second in the rotation.
This scenario gained traction after judges presiding over Netanyahu corruption trials recommended dropping the most serious charge of bribery, as well as reconsidering the charges or reaching a plea bargain in the others. This development has strengthened Netanyahu’s negotiating position and prompted him to call for an end to the political boycott against him.
Against this backdrop, Eisenkot is manoeuvring through dangerous political waters. If he fails to form a government, voters may be forced to return to the polls again while Netanyahu remains at the helm. This scenario could translate into a loss of support for the change bloc and hand Netanyahu a renewed mandate, while simultaneously ending the political careers of some leaders such as Eisenkot.
If Eisenkot chooses unity with Netanyahu over the promises he made to his voters, he will lose credibility among supporters. Additionally, Eisenkot could be outmanoeuvred by Netanyahu.
Many point to the coalition agreement between Benjamin Netanyahu and Benny Gantz in 2020, which included a rotating premiership. The government collapsed before Benny Gantz assumed his position and his political career never recovered.
In political terms, forming a unity government with Netanyahu would represent a reversal of election promises on fundamental issues such as transparency, judicial reform, and the influence of religion on the state, because unlike the change bloc, Netanyahu’s allies are already embedded in the state bureaucracy and able to entrench these policies.
More strategically, it reflects the knee-jerk reaction of Israel’s body politic to Palestinian citizens of Israel. This is what leading sociologist and researcher Honaida Ghanem calls Israel’s structural problem: its inability to reconcile that part of Israel’s political and leadership crisis is that in today’s Israel, anti-Arab sentiment is one of the few policies most Jewish Israelis can agree on, while they no longer agree on the nature of the state, the influence of religion over the state, or many other fundamental issues of identity and governance.
The prospect of a unity government with Eisenkot and Netanyahu remains possible, though not likely, primarily because of the personal and political risks such an unholy political marriage would entail for the change bloc leaders.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/wa.title: Was Andy Burnham right to accept his award from the Muslim-baiting Spectator?
https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/wa.author: Peter Oborne
https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/wa.text:
Was Andy Burnham right to accept his award from the Muslim-baiting Spectator?
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) finally ruled last week that the Myanmar government carried out a genocide when its army slaughtered thousands of Rohingya Muslims in an orgy of planned killing and mass rape.
This is the second time that the ICJ has found that genocide was committed against a Muslim population. Twenty years ago, it reached that verdict in the wake of the systematic execution of more than 8,000 Bosnian Muslims in Srebrenica.
That could become three times if the ICJ ultimately resolves that Israel’s ongoing slaughter of Palestinians in Gaza - where more than 74,000 have been confirmed dead so far, almost all of them Muslim - amounts to a genocide.
The world has become an intolerably dangerous place if you are Muslim.
French writer Renaud Camus once warned that Muslim immigration would wipe out white Europeans. “The great replacement is very simple,” he said in 2012. “You have one people, and in the space of a generation you have a different people.”
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Meanwhile, China has held hundreds of thousands of Muslims in secretive detention camps in recent years, while the Muslim community in India has been denounced as a “virus” by the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh.
This view that Islam is a danger to humanity is impossible to substantiate. When Muslims travel to other countries, they normally arrive as victims of oppression, war or civil conflict, not as aggressors.
Yet across much of the globe, Muslims are portrayed as the enemy - and that includes in Britain.
Islamophobic tropes
Pick up a newspaper. Read a book on current affairs. Consult a think tank. Listen to a politician. Go down to the pub. You will hear the same story: Islam is on the march, hell-bent on destroying the West.
Muslims are presented as invaders, enemies of civilisation, parasites, unpatriotic - uncomfortably similar to the tropes deployed before the Srebrenica and Myanmar genocides.
According to the British Muslim Trust, there were 78 verified attacks involving mosques over the 12 months to July 2026. In recent decades, several Muslims have been murdered simply for being Muslim, while others get abused, targeted or beaten up. They fear going out at night.
This past April, a man was jailed for 13 years after raping a Sikh woman because he believed she was Muslim.
It is easy to understand why some openly racist politicians dash along to Spectator events - and equally easy to understand why others failed to show
Yet the systematic demonisation of Muslims has become a central part of the narrative of the British political and media classes in the 21st century. As I set out in my book The Fate of Abraham, this rhetoric has strong historical roots. But it is now so much a part of normal discussion that almost nobody notices.
At Westminster in particular, there is an adamantine reluctance to challenge the demonisation of a relatively small section of the British population. Politicians are rightly wide awake to the problem of antisemitism, a poisonous virus that has been deeply embedded in western Christian DNA for a millennium of British history.
But the majority of British MPs and newspapers flatly refuse to acknowledge that Islamophobia has become a problem in contemporary Britain.
Wednesday night provided a powerful and very telling example. Politicians from the main political parties gathered in central London to celebrate the Spectator Parliamentarian of the Year awards.
The most senior politicians in Britain were singled out for awards, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch. Former foreign secretary David Lammy and Michael Gove, the former Tory cabinet minister who now edits the Spectator, presented the awards.
On the face of things, this was an admirable cross-party event, when journalists and politicians resolved for an evening to overcome their differences and celebrate the fact that we British have the good fortune to live in a parliamentary democracy. (The revered Spectator political columnist Henry Fairlie once memorably recorded that he slept more soundly in his bed when Parliament was sitting).
Troubling message
But let’s pause a moment and reflect on how all this good cheer and cross-bench jollification looks and feels if you are a British Muslim. This past summer, the Centre for Media Monitoring produced a report on the Spectator’s coverage of Islam.
It found that the magazine’s extensive (one might even say obsessive) output on Islam portrays Muslims as invaders who don’t belong in this country, don’t share British values, and threaten our public spaces.
The report also documents how Spectator writers substantiate this thesis through misrepresentations, fabrications, vulgar abuse, and conspiracy theories. Some of the examples are horrifying.
Many observers would regard such coverage as Islamophobic. Not the Spectator, which refuses to frame Islamophobia in its accepted sense as an irrational fear, hatred or prejudice directed at Muslims for being Muslim.
Instead, it turns the concept on its head, arguing that the term is a cynical attempt to exempt Muslims from criticism, and to import a blasphemy law through the back door.
The magazine ran the headline: “There’s not enough Islamophobia in the Conservative Party.” After an outcry the Spectator changed the headline.
But one only has to imagine the career-ending consequences - not just for the writer, but also the editor, and indeed the magazine itself - that would (rightly) follow if a Labour magazine asserted “there’s not enough antisemitism in Labour”.
Lammy might be interested to learn that the magazine recently ran two articles calling for the rehabilitation of the racist 20th-century Tory politician Enoch Powell.
Defenders of the Spectator are entitled to point out that Britain is a free country, and any magazine or newspaper is permitted to propagate whatever views it likes, no matter how bigoted or divisive, so long as they stay within the law.
But that is not the case with political parties. When senior politicians accept awards, they do not send out a message that they agree with the organisers’ beliefs and objectives, and it would be absurd to claim that they do. Yet they are signalling that they regard the Spectator’s commentary on Muslims as within the boundaries of acceptable discourse.
It is easy to understand why some openly racist politicians dash along to Spectator events - and equally easy to understand why others, like Zack Polanski’s Green Party, failed to show.
When Burnham accepted his well-deserved award as politician of the year (last year’s recipient was Reform UK leader Nigel Farage), he was not endorsing the Spectator’s compulsive hostility to Muslims. But he certainly was sending the message that the Spectator operates within the acceptable boundaries of public discourse when it demonises Muslims.
That is a troubling message to send out at any time - all the more so as Islamophobia Awareness Month reaches its climax.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Exposição Território Vivo – Uma Terra Onde Corre Leite e Mel: 20 anos depois
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Leonardo Melgarejo
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Esta semana acontece a Feira do Cooperativismo da Reforma Agrária Popular, e um dos muitos pontos de destaque em sua programação é a conexão entre arte, cultura e reforma agrária popular. É nesse encontro que o Programa PACRA – Arte e Cultura na Reforma Agrária apresenta a exposição “Território Vivo – Uma Terra Onde Corre Leite e Mel: 20 anos depois”, fruto de duas décadas de registro e valorização das manifestações artísticas e culturais dos assentamentos rurais cearenses.
A seguir, compartilhamos o texto de apresentação da exposição e algumas das fotografias selecionadas para esta atividade. O convite é para olhar essas imagens como testemunhos de história de vida, de resistência criativa e de bem viver nos territórios da reforma agrária.
Confira fotos neste link: https://claude.ai/artifact/Da835JNiMwXioMCDkLttvy
Há duas décadas, percorremos estradas e caminhos de terra batida no Ceará. Com um olhar atento e acolhedor, foi realizada a primeira documentação visual dos assentamentos rurais cearenses, com foco nas suas manifestações artísticas e culturais e nos seus territórios de vida, trabalho e resistência. Foram dois mil quilômetros de poeira, sol, mar e esperança, atravessando os sertões dos Inhamuns, Canindé, Crateús, Sobral até o Vale do Curu-Aracatiaçu.
Dessa longa caminhada nasceu a exposição “Uma Terra Onde Corre Leite e Mel”. Mais do que imagens, o acervo procurou capturar a alma da reforma agrária na sua diversidade humana e cultural, em um tempo em que reter a luz em uma fotografia era raro no meio rural.
Em 2025, com o apoio da Divisão de Arte e Cultura do INCRA, retornamos aos sertões de Canindé e ao Vale do Curu-Aracatiaçu, ampliando o alcance das nossas lentes para mais dois Pontos de Cultura.
Esta seleção reduzida de um acervo de dois mil registros reúne imagens atuais. Testemunhas de sentimentos e belezas compartilhadas por crianças e idosos, elas reverenciam mestres da cultura que já não existem, mas que ainda assim ali estão presentes, compartilhando um futuro de bem viver.
Trata-se da captura de momentos de partilha e construção solidária, reveladores de uma cultura que resiste e se renova, sustentada principalmente pelas mulheres e nutrida na relação intergeracional. São quintais produtivos, brincadeiras populares do reisado, grupos de dança que valorizam suas raízes da terra, brotando semente e luz, carrapichinhos reinventados na nova geração e a comida farta do povo sertanejo.
No mar de Caetanos, a dança do coco mira estranhas torres eólicas, que giram capturando energia do vento leste, alterando paisagens milenares e ameaçando a paz de modos de existência tradicionais. Nos territórios fruto da luta camponesa emergem resistências criativas, apoiadas nas Escolas de Educação do Campo e nos Equipamentos Culturais.
O convite é para que estas imagens sejam interpretadas considerando o que significam em termos de história de vida. Trata-se de relembrar a importância das ações culturais de valorização, registro e memória como elementos de autonomia coletiva, que se opõem a mecanismos de dominação que, para roubar nossas riquezas, precisam capturar e erodir a alma de nossos povos e territórios. A defesa do que somos e do que poderemos vir a ser exige compreensão e valorização da arte e da cultura popular que nos definem e que são essenciais para conter os grupos que operam em favor de interesses que nos ameaçam.
PACRA – Arte e Cultura na Reforma Agrária
O Projeto Arte e Cultura na Reforma Agrária (PACRA) nasceu em 2003 como uma iniciativa pioneira da Superintendência Regional do INCRA/CE. O projeto rompeu com a visão reducionista do acesso à terra para entender a reforma agrária também como um direito pleno à memória, à identidade e às políticas culturais. O que começou como uma ação institucional e inovadora amadureceu e expandiu suas fronteiras ao longo das décadas. Hoje, consolidada de forma autônoma como Rede PACRA, a iniciativa segue atuando.
Ao longo de mais de duas décadas, essa trajetória transformou as paisagens sociais e artísticas do campo cearense.

Tiracanga/Canindé (CE)

Concepção e Curadoria – Silma Magalhães
Ano do Registro Fotográfico – novembro de 2025

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Famine expect to rise due to global conflict, El Nino, warns UN
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Famine expect to rise due to global conflict, El Nino, warns UN
El Nino is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots, mainly in different parts of Africa.
Hunger ‌is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six months, mainly due to armed conflict and extreme climate events, two United Nations agencies said in a new report.
The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday that Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen faced the gravest threats of famine, driven by violence, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather, including the El Nino phenomenon.
Listings in the report, released twice a year through the Global Network Against Food Crises, have risen from 13 hotspots in June, with Chad, Uganda and parts of both Southern Africa and Central America added, while Lebanon was removed.
Armed conflict and violence were driving hunger in 12 of the 16 hotspots, the report said, as soaring food, energy and transport costs were eroding people’s ability to feed themselves.
El Nino, which is set to intensify to exceptional levels in the coming months according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots: Southern Africa, the Central American Dry Corridor and northeastern Uganda.
Covering December 2026 to May 2027, the agencies warned that shrinking humanitarian funding was affecting efforts to avert catastrophe.
In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1bn to $2bn.
“While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote the FAO and WFP.
While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks – including risk of famine – re-emerged within a few years.”
In Sudan, famine remains a risk in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January 2027, as fighting disrupts food production, markets and aid deliveries.
The agencies also identified famine risks in parts of Somalia and South ‌Sudan, where escalating violence has compounded an already desperate humanitarian situation.
Afghanistan, Haiti, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Gaza were also classified as areas of very great concern.
Gaza was ‌downgraded ‌from the highest level of concern after small improvements in food security following the October 2025 “ceasefire”. But agencies warned that conditions remained fragile in Gaza, while in the occupied West Bank, acute food insecurity is expected to worsen.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israe.author: Imran Mulla
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israe.text:
Israeli group promoting illegal settlements touring UK reported to police over 'threat'
An Israeli non-profit organisation promoting illegal settlements in occupied Palestinian territory that is touring Britain has been reported to the police over an alleged threat to the Palestinian rector of Glasgow University, Dr Ghassan Abu-Sittah.
Abu-Sittah, a British Palestinian surgeon who operated in Gaza during Israel's genocide and the rector of Glasgow University, had last week criticised Shivat Zion and the "failure of the British government to move against these companies, that are basically facilitating the commission of crimes".
In a statement to the National newspaper earlier this week Shraga Evers, a senior Shivat Zion official, responded by saying: "Honestly, I don’t care what Sheikh Ghassan Abu-Sittah says; he is a Hamas supporter - it’s like asking me about a statement by a staunch Adolf Hitler fan about Jews.
"I would like to send him our regards in his own language: كُلّ كَلْب بِيجِي يُومُه [every dog has its day]. Nazi and Hamas ideology isn’t distant from each other with regards to Jews."
The Arabic phrase "every dog has its day" was used by Israeli officials in relation to Yahya Sinwar, the Hamas leader in Gaza whom Israel killed in 2024. Shivat Zion works with the Israeli Ministry of Aliyah and Integration, and says on its website: "We’re here to help with your Aliyah and Integration into Israeli life!"
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Last week MEE reported that a page on Shivat Zion's website promotes a kibbutz in Gush Etzion, a collection of settlements in the illegally occupied West Bank, while other pages promoted events and teacher training in illegal Israeli settlements.
Shivat Zion's two-week tour began last Sunday with an event in Glasgow and is continuing in cities across Britain.
MEE has approached Shivat Zion for comment.
'Incitement to violence'
Abu-Sittah responded by calling Evers' remarks "incitement to violence", adding: "If this was a country with a functioning police force, that didn't spend its time arresting thousands of pensioners because they held up a placard, then this man would be arrested."
Evers has said he lives in Efrat, an illegal West Bank settlement. He is currently touring the UK with Shivat Zion.
MEE understands that Jewish Anti-Zionist Action (Jaza), a British activist group, has reported Shivat Zion and Evers to Police Scotland.
Talia Woodin, a spokesperson for Jaza, said: "Shivat Zion is so confident sending a racist, violent diatribe to a newspaper because of the impunity it feels, bolstered by the Israeli state’s support for pro-settlement groups."
Woodin added: "Making a death threat against a heroic British Palestinian doctor and elected university official is utterly deplorable and must now be the last straw. This extremist group must be sanctioned and banned from operating in the UK."
Labour MP Abtisam Mohamed asked Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband "what specific action can be taken against" Shivat Zion during a parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee hearing earlier this week.
Miliband said he would not comment on Shivat Zion specifically, but added: "We do not want to see advertising of settlement property. We do not want to see advertising of those sorts of opportunities."
Pressed on whether action would be taken against Shivat Zion, he responded: "We will ensure we have a comprehensive [sanctions] regime."
In September, the UK government recognised Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory as illegal and announced comprehensive sanctions on Israeli settlements.
Implementing the full sanctions could take up to nine months, according to government sources.
Sara Husseini, the director of the British Palestinian Committee, said Shivat Zion spokesperson Evers "has exposed the prejudice and disdain in which they hold Palestinians, underscoring the intent to ethnically cleanse the Palestinian people from our homeland with the full backing and involvement of the Israeli state".
Husseini added: "The UK, particularly in light of its recent announcements on sanctions, should take swift action to ban such organisations from promoting unlawful activities."
MEE has contacted Police Scotland for comment.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Os desafios das nossas vidas
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Selvino Heck
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Há momentos na vida e na História que são especiais. O Brasil está vivendo um deles. Depois da eleição das nossas vidas, é hora de enfrentar os desafios das nossas vidas.
A democracia no Brasil, ao longo da história, nunca esteve consolidada por muito tempo. Depois de séculos de escravidão e de um longo Império, o século 20 foi marcado por muita instabilidade política e por tempos de ditadura. Basta lembrar o suicídio de um presidente, Getúlio Vargas, nos anos 1950. Ou ainda a Campanha da Legalidade no Rio Grande do Sul para garantir a posse de um vice-presidente eleito, João Goulart, com o governador Leonel Brizola à frente, nos anos 1960. Mesmo assim, houve o golpe e instaurou-se uma ditadura militar de 21 anos.
Houve muita resistência, até chegarem as grandes mobilizações pelas Diretas Já e por uma Constituinte livre e soberana nos anos 1980. Parecia que a democracia finalmente tinha se consolidado, depois dos governos democrático-populares de Lula e Dilma, mas não. Outro golpe é dado, com o impeachment da presidenta Dilma Rousseff, já nos anos 2010, em pleno século 21.
Toda vez que o povo brasileiro começa a ter vez e voz, a ultradireita fascista liquida as conquistas, ameaça os direitos das trabalhadoras e dos trabalhadores, especialmente os dos mais pobres entre os pobres. E a desigualdade social e econômica, historicamente uma das maiores do mundo, em vez de diminuir, volta a aumentar, como aconteceu recentemente com a volta do Brasil ao Mapa da Fome, de onde novamente saiu no governo Lula 3.
Quem garante que, depois da vitória histórica de Lula, a democracia não estará novamente ameaçada logo ali adiante, ainda mais num contexto internacional altamente problemático? Basta ver o resultado final da COP31, há poucos dias, em tempos de crise climática profunda, que terminou sem acordo, enquanto os desastres ambientais ocorrem diariamente, não apenas no Rio Grande do Sul, mas em todo o país e no mundo inteiro.
Estamos, pois, em 2027 e nos anos seguintes, diante dos desafios das nossas vidas. O que fazer?
É preciso construir um programa estratégico de Nação, que garanta soberania, produza igualdade social e econômica e dignidade, com vez e voz para o povo.
É hora, depois da brilhante e emocionante campanha de segundo turno, de haver novamente mais movimento e menos instituição, inclusive no governo: manter um pé fora, para ampliar a democracia, e um pé dentro, com visão, programas e práticas democráticas e inclusivas.
Nos próximos anos, será decisiva a mais ampla participação social e popular, envolvendo jovens, mulheres, população negra e indígena, sonhadoras e sonhadores da utopia de “um outro mundo possível”, mais que nunca urgente e necessária nesta quadra da história.
A Formação na Ação no cotidiano, à luz de Paulo Freire, ação-reflexão-ação, prática-teoria-prática, com muito trabalho de base, especialmente nas periferias, deve envolver educadoras e educadores populares, movimentos populares, pastorais sociais, movimento sindical, escolas e universidades, ONGs e partidos políticos na construção da soberania, da democracia e da justiça social e econômica.
Sem ampla unidade popular, de todas e todos que acreditam na transformação social e política, de todas e todos que constroem a utopia com generosidade, amorosidade, solidariedade, amor à natureza e cuidado com a Casa Comum, não será possível dar conta dos desafios das nossas vidas.
Os desafios estão colocados. É hora de ninguém soltar a mão de ninguém, companheiras e companheiros. Na boa luta, com fé e coragem, ESPERANÇAR.
* Este é um artigo de opinião e não necessariamente representa a linha editorial do Brasil de Fato.

D’autres sont optionnels mais contribuent à faciliter votre expérience de lecteur ou de lectrice et d’une certaine façon à soutenir Mediapart. Vous pouvez les refuser ou les accepter ci-dessous, selon leurs finalités. 
Acceptez-vous que Mediapart utilise des cookies ou technologies similaires pour les finalités suivantes ?

                                Nécessaires au fonctionnement
du site ou de l’application
                            Connexion des abonné·es, mesure d’audience anonymisée, envoi des notifications push, suivi des pannes, mise en avant de nos services : ces outils sont nécessaires au suivi de l’activité de nos services et à leur bon fonctionnement.
                                    Voici les différents cookies et technologies similaires compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Cookies d’authentification : connexion des abonné·es.

- Datadog (uniquement sur le site web) : indicateurs techniques et équilibrage de charge.

- Nonli (uniquement sur le site web) : permet à notre équipe des réseaux sociaux de publier les contenus Mediapart sur les réseaux sociaux.

                            Il n’y a pas de publicité sur Mediapart. Mais nous faisons la promotion de nos contenus et services sur d’autres sites et réseaux sociaux. Pour cela, nous utilisons les technologies mises à disposition par certains acteurs publicitaires.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :

                                Gestion de l’accès aux contenus
                            Nous utilisons le service Qiota d’Opper Marketing Suite pour configurer l’activation d’un datawall sur certains de nos contenus (uniquement sur le site web). Ce dispositif destiné aux utilisateur·ices non abonné·es requiert la saisie d’une adresse email pour accéder aux contenus concernés. https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120417.title: Humanitarian Pilots Initiative | Zivile Seenotretter fliegen jetzt auch über dem Atlantik
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120417.author: Matthias Monroy
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120417.text:
- Politik
- Humanitarian Pilots Initiative
Zivile Seenotretter fliegen jetzt auch über dem Atlantik
Die Humanitarian Pilots Initiative sucht zwischen Westafrika und den Kanaren Boote mit Migranten in Seenot. Diese Route ist wieder besonders tödlich.
Wer von Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Senegal oder Mauretanien auf der Suche nach Schutz oder einem besseren Leben in Booten zu den Kanarischen Inseln aufbricht, geht ein hohes Risiko ein. Die spanisch als Cayucos bezeichneten offenen Pirogen sind oft wochenlang auf offener See, meist überladen und haben für die Reise zu wenig Proviant an Bord.
Deshalb schickt die Schweizer Humanitarian Pilots Initiative (HPI) nun ein Flugzeug der zivilen Seenotrettung über den Atlantik. Die Besatzung der »Seabird« meldete bei ihrem Erstflug am Montag auch sofort fünf Sichtungen. Nach ihrer Schätzung saßen jeweils zwischen 28 und 80 Personen im Boot, teils dicht gedrängt, auf manchen standen fast alle Insassen. Ob die Boote die Kanaren erreichten, ist unklar.
Auf dem Atlantik gibt es kaum systematische Seenotrettung – diese Lücke will HPI füllen. »Die Atlantikroute ist extrem gefährlich. Uns erreichen immer wieder Berichte von Booten, die vom Kurs abkommen und wochenlang auf dem Atlantik treiben. Viele Menschen sterben während dieser Zeit an Dehydrierung oder Unterkühlung. Andere Boote verschwinden, ohne dass je geklärt werden kann, was mit den Menschen an Bord geschehen ist«, sagt Omar El Manfalouty, Stiftungsratspräsident von HPI.
Besonders viele Ankünfte jedes Jahr im November
Angesichts des nahenden Winters und stärkeren Seegangs kommen jedes Jahr im November besonders viele Boote mit Migrant*innen auf den Kanaren an. Zurzeit ist El Hierro davon am meisten betroffen. Am Dienstag zählten die Behörden 2121 Menschen, so viele wie noch nie an einem Tag. Allein 14 Boote wurden in den Hafen des Fischerdorfes La Restinga geleitet.
Der vorherige Höchstwert war erst zehn Tage alt: Am 14. November hatten 1580 Menschen innerhalb von 24 Stunden die Kanaren erreicht. Das spanische Innenministerium zählte in der ersten Novemberhälfte insgesamt 11.037 Ankünfte auf den Kanaren.
Vor Westafrika ist aber derzeit auch die von der EU unterstützte senegalesische Marine sehr aktiv. In den vergangenen Wochen haben ihre Kriegsschiffe Tausende Menschen in Pirogen abgefangen und in das Land zurückgeholt.
Viele Tote und Vermisste auf der Route
Die Crew der »Seabird« war erst am Sonntag auf den Kanaren gelandet. Weil für den nächsten Tag eine Schlechtwetterfront angekündigt war, was besondere Gefahren für die Cayucos bedeutet, startete das Flugzeug gleich am Montagmorgen. Auf die Spur der Boote brachte sie ein Segelschiff, das Positionsdaten per Funk durchgab. Auf zwei der Boote sah die Besatzung der »Seabird« keine einzige Rettungsweste, auf einem schöpften Insassen weit draußen auf dem offenen Meer Wasser. HPI gab daraufhin Position und Zustand der Boote an die zuständige spanische Seenotrettungsleitstelle weiter.
Das Flüchtlingshilfswerk der Vereinten Nationen (UNHCR) schätzt, dass in diesem Jahr fast 600 Menschen auf der Atlantikroute starben oder verschwanden. Die spanische Organisation Caminando Fronteras zählte allein bis Ende Mai 635 Tote.
Auch in den vergangenen Wochen forderte die Überfahrt viele Menschenleben. Ende Oktober wurde südlich von El Hierro eine Piroge aus Gambia mit 115 Menschen geborgen, von denen vier gestorben waren, darunter ein Baby. Zwei weitere Tote hatten die Überlebenden unterwegs über Bord werfen müssen.
Anfang November starben mindestens sieben Menschen auf einer Überfahrt zu den Kanaren; Überlebende berichteten, fünf weitere ins Wasser geworfen zu haben. Am 9. November kenterte zwischen Dakar und Saint-Louis ein Boot, mindestens 34 Menschen kamen ums Leben. Bei einem Unglück vor Senegal starben schließlich vergangene Woche mindestens vier Menschen, Dutzende werden vermisst.
Flüge auch im Mittelmeer
Im Mittelmeer sind Flugzeuge von HPI und den französischen Pilotes Volontaires schon länger unterwegs. Sie fliegen zusammen mit Sea-Watch. Deren »Airborne«-Abteilung hat zuletzt für Januar bis Juni 2026 eine Bilanz vorgelegt. In diesem Zeitraum absolvierten die Flugzeuge 76 Einsätze und dokumentierten 44 Boote in Seenot mit mehr als 2027 Menschen.
Wie in internationalen Konventionen vorgeschrieben, werden über die Sichtungen alle Anrainerstaaten des zentralen Mittelmeeres, aber auch Schiffe der zivilen Seenotrettung informiert. Mindestens 758 Menschen wurden von den dortigen Küstenwachen nach Libyen und Tunesien zurückgeholt, mindestens 102 Menschen starben oder gelten als vermisst.
Zivile Organisationen retteten 657 Menschen auf 13 Booten, italienische Behörden 449 Menschen auf neun Booten, Handelsschiffe 58 Menschen auf zwei Booten. Sea-Watch betont, dass die Zahlen nur Fälle erfassen, die die eigenen Flugzeuge direkt beobachteten.
Seit einem Jahr fliegt Frontex im Atlantik
Auch für die Dokumentation derartiger Fälle sind die Flüge auf der sogenannten Kanarenroute wichtig. »Was wir derzeit auf dem Atlantik sehen, zeigt einmal mehr, wie dringend sichere und legale Migrations- und Fluchtwege gebraucht werden. Es ist beschämend, dass Menschen gezwungen sind, auf solchen Booten tagelange und lebensgefährliche Überfahrten auf sich zu nehmen«, sagt HPI-Präsident El Manfalouty.
Seit einem Jahr fliegt auch Frontex zur Überwachung im Atlantik. Dazu hat die EU-Grenzagentur ein Flugzeug in Praia auf den Kapverden stationiert. Einsätze erfolgen aber vor allem nördlich des Inselstaats und nur selten vor Westafrika. Es sei möglich, dass Frontex auch mutmaßlichen Drogenschmuggel aus Lateinamerika nach Europa oder illegale Fischerei verfolgt, sagt die in London lebende Goldsmith-Doktorandin Sasha Milonova, die Frontex-Flüge im Mittelmeer und im Atlantik auswertet, »nd«. Frontex bezahle Trackingdienste wie FlightRadar24 dafür, ihr Flugzeug nicht öffentlich sichtbar zu machen.
»Das macht zivilgesellschaftliche Beobachtungsmissionen wie jene von HPI unverzichtbar: sowohl zum Schutz der Sicherheit von Menschen auf der Flucht als auch zur Stärkung von Transparenz und Rechenschaftspflicht in Europa und Afrika«, so die Forscherin.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israe.title: Israel kills Gaza deputy education minister and wife in fresh attack on Gaza
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israe.author: MEE staff
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israe.text:
Israel kills Gaza deputy education minister and wife in fresh attack on Gaza
A senior Palestinian education official and his wife have become the latest victims of a string of Israeli attacks targeting Hamas officials this week, medical sources report.
Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Gaza's Ministry of Education, and his wife were killed in an Israeli attack on a residential block in central Gaza's Deir el-Balah, according to medics at Al-Aqsa Hospital. They added that another six people were wounded, some of them critically.
Abu Nada was a member of Hamas's political bureau, and also served as deputy education minister.
Al Jazeera reported that Israeli Apache helicopters "without warning" fired "two missiles directly and in succession" at Abu Nada's apartment, adding that the attack took place during dawn prayers, and that the surrounding area was crowded with tents where displaced families were sheltering.
Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed Abu Nada's killing, claiming that he was “a Hamas figure responsible for the group’s economy and education portfolios”.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
They added that his death forms part of a "targeted operation” waged against “operatives and senior officials” belonging to Hamas, claiming that they had killed around 80 of the group’s members in the last month.
The Israeli officials did not make any suggestion of Abu Nada having a military role in Hamas.
Abu Nada’s assassination follows a string of other attacks on Hamas officials in recent days.
Early on Wednesday, Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, internal security chief for northern Gaza, was killed alongside his wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15. Naim Abu Nahl, Gaza’s internal security director, was killed the day before.
Gaza's Ministry of Interior said that the assassinations are an attempt by Israel to sow chaos in the territory.
“What stands out is the direct targeting by Israeli forces through the assassination of security and police commanders," the ministry's spokesperson, Abu Amra said.
The Jerusalem Post reported that Abu Nada’s killing marks a “turning point in Israel’s targeted assassination policy in Gaza” with the aim of collapsing Hamas’s "control over the enclave”.
Hamas condemned Abu Nada’s killing as “a new crime added to the occupation's long record of targeting civilians, educational personnel, residential apartments and neighbourhoods in the Strip".
A 'systematic targeting of all pillars of life'
Meanwhile, Israeli attacks killed another seven Palestinians on Thursday.
Wafa news agency reported that at least three people were killed and others wounded when Israeli forces fired a drone at a group of people in northern Gaza’s al-Shati camp, west of Gaza City.
According to Al Jazeera, Israeli forces shot dead a 62-year-old man in Bureij refugee camp, in central Gaza.
A Gaza health ministry spokesperson described the surge in attacks in recent months as “a systematic targeting of all the pillars of life in the Gaza Strip”.
Hamas chief Khalil Al-Hayya - who narrowly escaped assassination himself - said on Thursday that the group was not prepared to withstand continued Israeli attacks.
He said the movement would discuss with other Palestinian factions how to respond to "Israeli violations and the policy of daily killing”.
"The equation of killing and blockade cannot be accepted under the (ceasefire) agreement," he added.
Gaza’s health ministry reported that Israel has killed at least 1,600 Palestinians, including 130 this month, since the so-called “ceasefire” was imposed last October.
It added that at least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since October 2023.
UN human rights chief Volker Turk warned on Wednesday of a growing risk of further atrocity crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, urging all states to take immediate action to prevent them.
Turk cited inflammatory statements by senior Israeli officials advocating annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment, alongside increasingly widespread and systematic violations against Palestinians.
“Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes - war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide - has been appalling,” he said in a statement.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.title: ‘Cupim do mercado editorial’: editor defende lei para frear Amazon e salvar livrarias
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.author: BdF Entrevista
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.text:
Todo fim de ano, a mesma cena se repete nas livrarias de São Paulo (SP): leitores folheiam livros, anotam títulos e vão embora sem comprar. Eles estão montando a lista para a Festa do Livro da USP, que acontece de 25 a 29 de novembro na Cidade Universitária e chega à 28ª edição neste ano, com recorde de 245 editoras e desconto mínimo de 50%. “As livrarias viram uma espécie de showroom das editoras”, resume o livreiro e editor João Varella, sócio da editora Lote 42 e da Banca Tatuí, em entrevista ao BdF Entrevista, do Brasil de Fato.
A feira é sucesso de público, mas incomoda o comércio. O presidente da Associação Nacional de Livrarias (ANL), Alexandre Martins Fontes, criticou o evento. Varella explica o problema: “Quando a editora vende diretamente para o público final, você está queimando uma etapa, atravessando um negócio, e está acostumando leitores a comprar com desconto. Muita gente deixa de adquirir um livro ao longo do ano para esperar essas datas”.
O impacto vem no pior momento para as livrarias, que dependem do Natal para fazer caixa antes de janeiro e fevereiro, meses fracos de vendas. Para tentar equilibrar o jogo, a Lote 42 criou o Lote 21: durante a feira, reduziu pela metade o preço de capa de seus livros em livrarias parceiras. “Vender livro com desconto é bom para o leitor, que bom. Melhor ainda se for na livraria, para preservar o ecossistema. É um teste, isso aqui é um laboratório”, diz.
‘Terra sem lei’
Para Varella, o caso da USP é sintoma de um mercado sem regras. “É um bangue-bangue, uma espécie de terra sem lei que é o mercado editorial brasileiro. Aqui, por não ter uma regulamentação, todo mundo é um pouco tudo. Eu sou livreiro, editor, autor, produtor cultural. É um monte de crachá que a gente precisa ter para conseguir sobreviver”, afirma.
Ele vê com bons olhos a Lei Cortez, que estabelece que, nos 12 meses posteriores ao lançamento de uma obra ou nova edição, o desconto máximo permitido para venda ao público será de 10%. O projeto foi aprovado no Senado e enviado à Câmara. “Eu enxergo como um bom primeiro passo. Não é uma panaceia”, avalia. Na Argentina, compara, a lei exige respeito ao preço de capa de todos os livros, e não só dos lançamentos.
O livreiro critica as grandes editoras, que demoraram a apoiar a regulação. “Eles não viram que a Amazon ia chegar. Esse cupim do mercado editorial chamado Amazon já atacou outros países, e a gente viu o que aconteceu. Eles leram, eles sabiam. Depois que a Amazon se instalou, disseram: ‘Vale a pena defender uma lei’. Só que foi tarde demais.”
Amazon encarece o livro
Segundo Varella, metade das vendas das editoras vai hoje para as livrarias online, como Amazon, Mercado Livre e Shopee. Ele também aponta as “dark bookstores“: “Livrarias que só trabalham para a Amazon, de porta fechada, que não existem na rua”. O resultado, diz, é o contrário do que o consumidor imagina: “As editoras precisam compensar essas taxas, esse desconto muito forte, subindo o preço de capa. E aí, no final das contas, o livro fica mais caro”.
A defesa da regulação, no entanto, esbarra nas redes sociais. “Você tem frase de efeito, lacração, radicalismo e ideias curtas. Qualquer aceno em prol de uma regulamentação, você é imediatamente taxado de elitista. Mas eu quero o livro mais barato, porque a regulamentação vai deixar o livro mais barato”, afirma.
‘Anticorpo mental’
Contrariando o senso comum, Varella diz que o livro brasileiro não é caro. “Comparado a outros países, o livro no Brasil é baratíssimo. Eu desconheço país onde o preço médio seja tão barato. O que o Brasil não tem é a valorização do livro.” Ele lembra que a pesquisa “Retratos da Leitura” não aponta o preço como barreira: os não leitores alegam falta de tempo ou de interesse.
Para o editor, essa valorização tem também um sentido político. “A gente teve agora uma eleição em que o Brasil passou raspando de eleger uma figura tétrica, tenebrosa. Se a gente tivesse um pouco mais de leitura, eu acho que a gente não teria passado esse risco. A leitura serve como uma espécie de anticorpo mental, te dá repertório, te faz duvidar de certos influenciadores”, diz.
Por isso, ele cobra políticas públicas para estimular livrarias, sobretudo fora dos grandes centros. “Uma livraria hoje exerce um papel de centro cultural, um lugar de convivência. Na maioria dessas 3 mil e tantas cidades sem livraria, tendo uma boa livraria, a vida dessas cidades ia mudar, com certeza”, afirma Varella, que cresceu numa cidade sem livraria.
O modelo, para ele, está ao lado. Na Argentina, editoras enviam livros ao exterior com frete subsidiado e bibliotecários recebem vale-livro do governo na Feira de Buenos Aires. “Eles pensam de um jeito muito holístico: biblioteca, livraria, editoras, está tudo conectado. O Brasil fica olhando muito para os Estados Unidos. Esqueça o Trump, vamos olhar para os nossos vizinhos. Eles são gente como a gente”, conclui.
Para ouvir e assistir
O BdF Entrevista vai ao ar de segunda a sexta-feira, sempre às 16h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: England’s Overton takes 5-12 as Australia bowled out for record low in T20
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
England’s Overton takes 5-12 as Australia bowled out for record low in T20
Australia are bowled out for 108 as Jamie Overton claims career-best figures in England’s seven-wicket win in Brisbane.
Jamie Overton took a career-best 5-12 as England thrashed Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 international in Brisbane on Friday.
Overton’s figures were the best by an Englishman against Australia in T20s as the home side were bundled out for 108, their lowest score on Australian soil.
“I thought Jamie Overton was outstanding tonight,” England captain Harry Brook said.
“He’s worked hard and put in some extra graft at training.
“He simplified his game and reaped the rewards tonight – he had it on a string and it felt like we could change the field and make them make a mistake.”
Brook won the toss and sent Australia in to bat, and off-spinner Liam Dawson struck early when he had Australian skipper Mitch Marsh caught at mid-on.
Jake Fraser-McGurk and Sam Harper attacked during the powerplay, taking the score to 55 after five overs.
Harper raced to 26 off 14 balls before Dawson grabbed his second when the Australian wicketkeeper got a top edge to Overton at mid-on.
Overton then swung into action with the ball, claiming the next five wickets as Australia slumped from 65-2 to 92-7 and then collapsed to 108 all out when Sam Curran clean-bowled Billy Stanlake.
Aneurin Donald, who smashed 85 off 32 on the Gold Coast on Tuesday, got the run chase off to a spectacular start, belting 31 from just 11 balls.
But a rain delay seemed to help the Australians, as Brook holed out for nine after play resumed, before Donald fell for 32, leaving England 49-3.
Another rain break threatened to stop England’s momentum again, but Jordan Cox blasted 33 in quick time to give the visitors an easy win and go ahead in the five-game series 2-1.
Marsh conceded that Australia were outplayed by a better team.
“No excuses, we’ve got to be better,” he said.
“We’ve all played Big Bash games here (at the Gabba).
“You have to give yourself the chance to cash in at the back end (of the innings), but we didn’t get near that tonight.”
The two teams head to Sydney for the fourth game on Sunday night.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: A disputa contra o rentismo: orçamento participativo e bancos públicos como saída
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Cristóvão Feil
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Keynes, se vivo fosse e examinasse a macroeconomia hegemônica do Brasil — o rentismo parasitário —, diria, já desanimado: “O neoliberalismo conquistou o Brasil tão completamente quanto a Santa Inquisição conquistou a Espanha”.
O sério e conceituado economista liberal André Lara Resende afirmou, semanas atrás, que as taxas de juros no Brasil são o maior obstáculo ao desenvolvimento produtivo do país. Vou repetir: Lara Resende é liberal.
O texto de Lara destaca que “reduzir os juros é a única saída”, já que juros altos travam o investimento privado e pressionam a dívida pública.
Muito bem: é raro, mas acontece — um liberal nem sempre é aquele que critica a política do rentismo, e Lara Resende o faz com grande coragem e argumentação inatacável.
Ocorre que o rentismo não vive só de juros altos. No Brasil, mesmo com juros baixos e menos agressivos, havia permanente ameaça ao desenvolvimento produtivo, uma vez que os bancos aplicavam outra modalidade de rentismo: o rentismo do spread, na modalidade do crédito.
Está provado que o rentismo no Brasil é estrutural e adaptativo. Combatê-lo exige políticas que enfrentem o poder de mercado dos bancos e a lógica de acumulação financeira, e não apenas a gestão da taxa básica de juros — o bicho-papão chamado Selic.
Há um artigo do economista Bruno Mader, publicado em 2023 na Brazilian Journal of Political Economy (BJPE). Mader oferece uma contribuição empírica e teórica relevante ao debate sobre a financeirização e o rentismo no Brasil.
A hipótese tradicional associava o lucro fácil dos bancos brasileiros à remuneração de títulos públicos em períodos de Selic elevada. A partir de 2020, com a Selic real em regime negativo, a expectativa natural seria de achatamento desses ganhos. Mas isso não ocorreu; ao contrário.
O artigo de Mader é leitura essencial para quem estuda a economia política brasileira. Ele desloca o foco do debate do “rentismo da Selic” para o “rentismo do spread” (o crédito), demonstrando que a financeirização no Brasil encontrou uma rota de fuga para manter a extração de renda mesmo em um ambiente de juros baixos.
O artigo trata os bancos em geral como um bloco relativamente homogêneo. Contudo, a capacidade de elevar spread e a composição de receitas variam significativamente entre bancos públicos, bancos privados de varejo e bancos de investimento.
Nesse caso, é fácil identificar que há uma contradição — quase antagônica — entre os bancos. Uma oportunidade para o Lula 4. Esse é o ponto que vamos tratar.
É, pois, explorando essa contradição que o governo Lula 4 pode promover políticas públicas habilitadas a fazer a disputa com o capital financeiro privado.
Trata-se, portanto, de fazer a disputa financeiro-interbancária (públicos versus privados) e a disputa política pela hegemonia.
Quem ganha e quem perde?
Os números ajudam a dimensionar a transferência de renda.
Quem ganha: o rentista parasitário, o detentor de títulos públicos. Estima-se que a Selic no nível atual coloque entre R230bilho~eseR 340 bilhões por ano no bolso dos rentistas, valor que excede o que os fundamentos macroeconômicos justificariam.
O valor pago aos rentistas representa cerca de 8% do PIB no Brasil, contra 2% na média da OCDE (Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico), organização econômica intergovernamental com 38 países membros, fundada em 1961 para estimular o progresso econômico e o comércio mundial.
O setor financeiro também ganha com o spread elevado e com a gestão da dívida pública.
Quem perde: o trabalhador e a pequena e média empresa. O crédito caro encarece o consumo dos assalariados, dificulta o investimento produtivo e pressiona a geração de empregos. Sindicalistas descrevem a política como “extorsão financeira” e “nefasta para o setor produtivo e para o próprio sistema capitalista”. O crescimento de 2,3% em 2025 veio com perda de força do consumo e do investimento.
Em resumo, é uma transferência de renda do conjunto da sociedade para os credores da dívida pública, quer dizer, para alguns milhares de brasileiros que apostam no capitalismo financeiro improdutivo e parasitário.
Lula 4 exige ações políticas como disputa distributiva, não como participação genérica
A narrativa dominante, endossada por 100% da mídia, apresenta o orçamento como questão técnica e o rentismo como responsabilidade fiscal.
A adoção do Orçamento Participativo (OP) pode constituir-se como instrumento de massa para enfrentar o rentismo minoritário e altamente ideologizado.
O OP deve ser enquadrado como o que é: quem paga a dívida e quem recebe os juros versus quem depende do investimento público.
Cada plenária deve explicitar que uma parte enorme do orçamento está comprometida com o serviço da dívida e que o OP disputa o orçamento livre — e que esse espaço pode ser ampliado com mudanças na indexação da dívida e no regime de metas.
A ofensiva midiática do rentismo não é acidental. A imprensa hegemônica atua como “aparelho privado de hegemonia” (no sentido gramsciano), e há registro documentado de manipulação na cobertura do OP para fazê-lo parecer um fracasso.
Combater isso exige uma contraofensiva comunicativa articulada ao próprio novo projeto de OP.
Exige usar os canais que as classes populares efetivamente acessam. Rádios comunitárias, WhatsApp (com listas de transmissão e grupos por bairro), carros de som e mídia alternativa e comunitária são mais eficazes do que plataformas digitais complexas ou publicidade oficial em veículos hegemônicos.
Eis uma tarefa estratégica desafiadora para o vitorioso exército do Lula, do midiático “general” Janones.
Já a experiência internacional mostra que o rádio é o meio de maior abrangência em contextos de baixa conectividade (locais remotos), e que o WhatsApp é o canal dominante nas periferias. O OP deve ter agentes de mobilização territorial — pessoas treinadas para visitar bairros, explicar o processo e convocar reuniões, como já foi proposto em experiências municipais de sucesso.
Exige-se formação popular como parte do processo, não como pré-requisito. A educação orçamentária não pode ser um “curso técnico” que exclui quem não tem tempo ou escolaridade.
Deve ser uma formação política dialógica, nos moldes da educação popular freiriana, contratada junto a institutos federais e movimentos sociais, para que delegados e conselheiros entendam o orçamento como linguagem de poder.
Porto Alegre chegou a contratar o Instituto Paulo Freire para treinar delegados do OP em todos os níveis territoriais e setoriais. Um OP nacional deve fazer o mesmo em escala ampliada.
O objetivo é garantir caráter deliberativo sobre uma fatia real e visível do orçamento.
Participação sem poder decisório real desmobiliza. O OP precisa incidir sobre um montante significativo e não “carimbado”, com regras claras de vinculação entre a votação popular e a execução efetiva.
Se a população decide, mas o dinheiro é posteriormente redirecionado por emendas ou contingenciamento, a versão rentista — sempre falsa — vence pelo desencanto. E a massa perde o estímulo, quase sem retorno.
Exige-se transformar a transparência em contranarrativa permanente. O OP deve produzir e divulgar resultados verificáveis: obras entregues, valores executados, comparação entre o decidido e o realizado.
Cada entrega deve ser comunicada como prova de que a participação popular funciona melhor do que a velha mediação parlamentar clientelista para levar recursos a quem precisa.
É fundamental articular o OP a uma coalizão de movimentos populares, sindicatos, coletivos periféricos, clubes de mães etc.
O OP não mobiliza no vazio. Ele precisa ser convocado e disputado por sujeitos coletivos organizados e mobilizados.
A experiência petista mostra que o OP nasceu de uma interação pedagógica entre poder público e movimento popular, não de um decreto de gabinete.
O governo pode criar o canal, mas são os movimentos que garantem que ele não seja capturado por setores já organizados ou por demandas corporativas — como ocorreu no PPA, em que as propostas mais votadas foram pautas de servidores públicos.
Uma coalizão popular ampla é o antídoto contra a reprodução das desigualdades de representação ilegítima.
O que o OP já provou: em suas origens, foi um instrumento de “politização do orçamento” e de “inversão de prioridades”, quebrando padrões de espoliação urbana ao delegar poder decisório às classes populares organizadas.
Cidadãos historicamente excluídos passaram a se articular, eleger delegados e acompanhar a execução de obras, inibindo superfaturamento e corrupção. Esse é o fundamento para acreditar que um OP nacional pode reconstruir a conexão entre a população e o destino dos recursos públicos.
O que o esvaziou: o próprio PT, ao buscar governabilidade no plano federal, permitiu que as emendas parlamentares se tornassem o principal canal de alocação de recursos. Isso transferiu o poder de decisão sobre “o que, quando e para onde” destinar verbas das mãos da população para as mãos de parlamentares com base eleitoral local.
O resultado foi a diminuição da democratização do orçamento e a perda de força e legitimidade do OP. Em 2026, as emendas parlamentares somam R$ 50 bilhões, cerca de 20% de tudo o que a União gasta com investimentos e manutenção.
Qualquer OP nacional que não dispute esse montante de recursos tende a ser uma consulta simbólica sobre migalhas.
Para tanto, devemos instituir um OP híbrido, com versão presencial de massa e versão digital — agora com registro via gov.br (nas modalidades prata e ouro).
O risco da versão digital: a experiência do PPA Participativo (2024–2027) mostrou alcance inédito — 1,4 milhão de participantes e 8.254 propostas —, mas também revelou limites: a plataforma digital funcionou mais como agregação de preferências do que como deliberação popular.
Não havia interação discursiva entre cidadãos, e as plenárias presenciais tenderam a validar propostas já registradas, em vez de promover debate real.
No Piauí, por exemplo, o WhatsApp concentrou a maioria das interações, enquanto plataformas mais complexas tiveram baixo engajamento, evidenciando barreiras de acesso e escasso letramento digital. É que ambos exigem estratégias híbridas com apoio presencial e unidades móveis.
Um OP nacional puramente digital reproduziria a exclusão que deveria combater. É preciso, pois, encontrar a fórmula híbrida, para combinar o OP presencial com a opção digital. São modos complementares visando o mesmo objetivo: politizar o tema orçamentário — às vezes opaco e tecnicista em demasia —, de forma a esclarecer e mobilizar as populações de todas as regiões do País.
Governo como coordenador, não como sinalizador
O Lula 4 precisa de uma instância permanente de coordenação antirrentismo, com mandato claro e poder orientador sobre CMN, BC, Fazenda, bancos públicos e reguladores.
Não basta o GT do spread do governo Lula 3, que foi útil para diagnóstico, mas conviveu com bancos à mesa e sem poder de decisão. A presença direta da Febraban — inclusive sediando a instalação do grupo — e de executivos dos maiores bancos privados (como Itaú e Bradesco) ao lado de fintechs e centrais sindicais gerou uma relação ambígua e de mútua anulação. Soma zero.
Em resumo, o GT foi pródigo em esforço inútil de enxugar gelo. Cumpriu o papel de construir consenso técnico sobre os gargalos do crédito, mas, sem caneta executiva e negociando com os próprios regulados dentro da sala, acabou limitado a avanços incrementais e dependentes de articulação política posterior.
No próximo quadriênio de Lula, os bancos públicos devem servir de benchmark de preço, não como exceção. Benchmark significa “ponto de referência” ou padrão usado para avaliar e comparar desempenho.
No Brasil, temos cinco grandes bancos federais: Banco do Brasil, Caixa Econômica Federal, BNDES, Banco do Nordeste e Banco da Amazônia.
Temos quatro bancos públicos estaduais: Banrisul, BRB, Banestes e Banpará.
Temos quatro bancos públicos de desenvolvimento: BRDE, BDMG, [BanDES — conferir sigla: provavelmente Badesc ou Desenvolve SP] e Badesul.
Vamos falar concretamente: consignado, crédito para PMEs e crédito popular ofertados pelos bancos públicos no piso do teto regulatório, obrigando os bancos privados a competir por preço. Pix-garantia e centrais de garantias públicas para reduzir prêmio de risco e assimetria de informação. Cooperativas de crédito e fintechs reguladas como contrapeso à concentração — com metas de expansão e regulação proporcional.
Setores industriais que o OP pode fomentar
Aqui reconheço que estamos antecipando etapas, mas quero demonstrar que o OP — como estratégia política de massas e instrumento de disputa do orçamento público — pode favorecer setores para bem além dos protagonistas diretos do OP híbrido, mas sobretudo o desenvolvimento produtivo por meio da retomada decisiva da industrialização no Brasil.
A reindustrialização significa estímulo direto ao crescimento do emprego e da renda. Com vantagens político-ideológicas adicionais, que legitimam o OP, em face da disputa com o Legislativo conservador, e fortalecem a conquista da hegemonia junto aos diversos setores do capital produtivo nacional.
Para impulsionar a reindustrialização com ênfase no encadeamento produtivo rápido (capacidade de arrastar outros setores) e na geração de empregos em larga escala, o Brasil conta com vantagens competitivas únicas.
Diferentemente de indústrias que precisariam ser construídas do zero, existem setores em que o país já possui demanda interna garantida, recursos naturais ou base científica instalada.
Os quatro setores com maior potencial imediato para canalizar recursos públicos e orientar um eventual Orçamento Participativo nacional são:
1. Complexo Econômico-Industrial da Saúde (CEIS)
O Brasil possui o maior sistema público de saúde universal do mundo (SUS).
2. Transição Energética e Bioeconomia Industrial
Com uma das matrizes elétricas mais limpas do mundo e liderança em biocombustíveis, o Brasil tem condições imediatas de liderar a chamada “neoindustrialização verde”.
3. Agroindústria de Alto Valor Agregado e Máquinas Agrícolas
Em vez de exportar apenas commodities brutas (soja em grão, milho, minério), o adensamento da cadeia agroindustrial permite processar alimentos no país e fabricar internamente os insumos e as máquinas que o campo consome.
4. Infraestrutura Urbana, Saneamento e Mobilidade Elétrica
Tem alto potencial de encadeamento, já que puxa imediatamente a indústria da construção civil, a siderurgia, a petroquímica (tubos e conexões), a indústria naval (cabotagem e embarcações fluviais) e a cadeia automotiva voltada para ônibus elétricos e veículos híbridos a etanol.
Mas isso é matéria para o próximo artigo.

Trump embraced Xi, then slapped new tariffs on China: What’s his game plan?
US president’s new tariff regime targets China hardest, just weeks before Trump and Xi meet again at the G20 in Miami.
In February 2025, US President Donald Trump marked his return to office by kick-starting a trade war with China.
New tariffs, amid accusations that China was failing to prevent the flow of drugs into the United States, set the stage for an escalating economic confrontation between the world’s two largest economies, which stands to reshape global trade.
While Trump’s new trade tariffs regime hit allies and rivals alike, China took the fight head-on.
Washington first put a 10 percent duty on Chinese goods, citing fentanyl and immigration concerns, and Beijing responded by curbing exports of five rare earth metals key to defence, clean energy and tech products.
Then it came to a showdown with Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April, including 34 percent for Chinese products. A tit-for-tat exercise ensued as headline US tariffs on China climbed to 145 percent, while US goods entering China were slapped with tariffs of 125 percent, alongside restrictions on rare earth exports.
The tariff war seesawed for much of that year before the two leaders sat at a table in October, on the sidelines of the 2025 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in South Korea, to call a truce.
The limited-time pause in hostilities paved the way for a diplomatic thaw.
Trump then travelled to Beijing last May for talks with Xi, who then visited Washington in September for the first time in more than a decade. Trump embraced the Chinese president when he arrived in Shenzhen, China’s technology hub, earlier this month for this year’s APEC summit.
But then Trump returned to Washington and, in less than a week, his administration had announced a new tariff regime – its second attempt at reshaping its trade war after the Supreme Court declared his Liberation Day tariffs of April last year illegal.
“The practical purpose is simple: rebuild [the] tariff leverage the Supreme Court stripped away and force Beijing to the table before the next summit,” said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, the chief economist for Asia Pacific at investment bank Natixis.
‘Purpose changed somewhat’
This time, the Trump administration has announced plans to impose new tariffs on 14 of its major trading partners, including China, the European Union and India, accusing them of flooding world markets with cheap goods through unfair government subsidies, policies and suppressed wages.
China is subject to the highest rates – a new 20 percent levy that is still within the bounds of the trade truce that is set to expire in January. Washington has, however, threatened a 40 percent levy if trade talks break down.
Instead of the emergency powers it used the first time – and which the Supreme Court struck down – the Trump administration is using Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, alleging that targeted countries are making use of “structural excess capacity”. It has identified these 14 specific economies during an investigation it launched in March, but views China as the biggest offender, particularly in its steel, aluminium, electric cars, household appliances and solar panels industries.
Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation, a trade policy think tank in Singapore, said the “original intention” of the investigation “was to provide a more durable way to get back to the tariff levels” announced on Liberation Day.
“Over that time, I think the purpose changed somewhat,” she told Al Jazeera.
“Originally a means to apply tariffs, it seems clear that the White House wants a more sweeping use of Section 301, which allows a broad range of activities to be subject to possible negotiations and future punishment like tariffs,” she added.
Elms argued that Trump’s announcement coming in “now is rather interesting”, given he is due to meet with Xi next month, in Miami, at the G20 Leaders’ Summit. “This announcement adds another layer of possible tensions,” she said.
‘Right to retaliate’
Just before Trump landed in Shenzhen, where he was greeted by Xi on the tarmac, earlier this month, the Chinese leader had opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”.
Xi also portrayed Beijing as a stable trade partner in contrast with the US, where Trump’s tariff war had already rattled global economic equations.
Responding to the latest round of tariffs this week, Beijing warned that it “reserves the right” to retaliate with steeper tariffs.
“China urges the US to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” a Ministry of Commerce spokesperson said, adding that Beijing “will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests”.
Referring to the eight-month investigation into “structural excess capacity” practices undertaken by Jamieson Greer, Trump’s trade representative, China said it was “a typical act of unilateralism that severely disrupts the international economic order and seriously violates WTO rules”.
Under the latest measures, Washington is seeking to take its economic confrontation with Beijing beyond bilateral trade, targeting the industrial policies of countries emerging as alternative manufacturing hubs but whose supply chains remain closely intertwined with China’s.
Hinrich Foundation’s Elms told Al Jazeera that while Beijing “is probably ok with a 20 percent tariff, they are undoubtedly less comfortable with the attempt to hold all other trade partners accountable to the US for engagement with China”.
‘China can blunt this’
Investment bank Natixis’s Herrero said that Trump’s latest tariffs “are less a grand strategy than a familiar negotiating ploy: keep the pressure on after a friendly photo-op”, referring to the meeting in Shenzhen.
“The stated rationale is Chinese overcapacity,” she said, adding that, however, the aim is to “rebuild tariff leverage” and “force Beijing to the table before the next summit”.
Chen Bo, a senior research fellow at the National University of Singapore (NUS), said the new measures are a substitute for the struck-down reciprocal tariffs, with “the same kind of inherent reasons or motivations”.
Bo argued that the US government “needs to raise money to keep its many activities going, including the war on Iran”. Furthermore, “it cannot rely on the bond market due to high interest rates – and consumer inflation already hit them hard in midterm election results”.
“Tariff money is one of the easiest ways to finance itself, rather than asking for more from Congress,” Bo told Al Jazeera.
Despite nearly a decade of the ongoing trade tensions between the US and China, Beijing’s global goods trade surplus reached a record $1.19 trillion last year, underscoring the scale of its export dominance. By comparison, the US ran a $1.24 trillion goods trade deficit over the same period.
“Nothing has changed substantially over the years,” he said, adding that “no new tariff will be effective to reduce the Chinese overcapacity at all, or in a significant way.”
Bo said he believes both China and the US are “working hard on the trade negotiations to de-escalate or mitigate” before the two leaders meet again next month, where they want to discuss issues like AI, nuclear weapons and the wars in Iran and Ukraine. “That’s a much bigger picture for them than a trade relationship,” Bo said.
For Beijing’s part, Herrero said that “China can still blunt” these new measures by the US.
“Rare earths remain its sharpest tool,” she added.
“The risk for Trump is the same as always: higher prices land on American consumers, and the wider trade system frays further,” Herrero said. “Whether that counts as a feature or a bug depends on how much pain Washington is willing to absorb.”

In Israel, calls for 'unity' are a code for Jewish tribal supremacy
The saying “when fascism comes to America, it will be wrapped in a flag and carrying a cross” is commonly attributed to American novelist and playwright Sinclair Lewis.
German writer Thomas Mann, himself a Nobel laureate in literature, had a slightly different version: “If ever fascism should come to America, it will come in the name of freedom.”
Former Republican President Ronald Reagan, meanwhile, offered his own version: “If fascism ever comes to America, it will come in the name of liberalism.”
Whatever form fascism may take when it arrives in the US, one thing can be said with certainty: in Israel, it arrived in the name of unity.
It is hard to think of a word in the Hebrew language that has been more shamelessly abused than “unity” by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s inciting, divisive gang.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Take, for example, Elisha Madan, the newly elected Likud MK who has set up a “Unity Tent” outside the Knesset. “I intend to sit in the tent day and night, in the cold and rain, to give voice to the many people who keep reaching out to me, yearning for unity,” he declared poetically.
This great champion of unity, it is worth recalling, helped establish the settlement of Avigail. He was also filmed hurling vile slurs at the late human rights activist Ezra Nawi, who had come to the area to protect Palestinian residents from settler violence.
Common ground
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the man who warned before the election that a left-wing government would pose an existential threat to the state of Israel, suddenly remembered after the vote to reach out to his “Jewish brothers” with a call for unity.
Amir Ohana - the former Knesset speaker who boycotted the swearing-in ceremony of Supreme Court president Yitzhak Amit, and who refused to allow bereaved families into the Knesset gallery during a Netanyahu speech about the 7 October attacks, instead having them forcibly removed - also professes to see unity as a cherished goal, with the 26th Knesset holding the means to achieve it.
The use of the term 'the people of Israel' is no accident. It is a code word, an effective shortcut for establishing a shared sense of tribal belonging
And this week, comedian Guy Hochman shoved a camera rudely into MK Ahmad Tibi’s face, shouting at him: “Ahmad, unity? Unity?” This knight of unity is the same man who found the genocide in Gaza particularly amusing, and a fitting backdrop for a stand-up performance intended to boost the morale of the forces of destruction and annihilation.
He is also the same comedian who attended a left-wing demonstration and declared that its participants were "scarier than Qatar". Now, he too wants unity.
It is easy to dismiss the unity tantrum gripping Netanyahu’s camp as a cynical ploy, designed to neutralise the meaning of its electoral defeat and spare its members the prospect of being banished to the opposition benches.
But the truth is that it rests on something much deeper, rooted in the anomaly of Israeli politics: a political landscape divided not primarily along ideological lines, but above all, over the question of support for Netanyahu.
Remove Netanyahu himself from the equation, and the common ground between the two blocs is far greater than it might appear; on many issues, their areas of agreement actually outweigh their differences.
A call for unity between two blocs that stood firmly together around the most defining event in Israel’s history since its founding - the perpetration of genocide against a besieged and defenceless Palestinian population - is not entirely baseless.
But the foundation of this call for unity runs even deeper than a consensus on any particular policy. It concerns the most instinctive sense of belonging shared by members of both blocs: who they mean when they say “we”.
Dangerous distinction
The Israeli right long ago replaced the concept of “Israeli citizens” with the tribal notion of “the people of Israel” - a term that clearly refers exclusively to the Jewish collective. This dangerous substitution is no longer confined to the right.
“The people of Israel cannot trust Netanyahu when he claims his motives are not political … We must not allow him to exploit Israel’s security to disrupt the elections,” Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats, tweeted about a month before the election.
The distinction between “the people of Israel” and “Israeli citizens” is anything but semantic. It reflects two fundamentally different conceptions of the Israeli collective, only one of which includes Palestinian citizens of Israel.
Why did Golan choose to invoke “the people of Israel” rather than “Israeli citizens”? Are Arab citizens of Israel not equally affected by security concerns? Do they not flee to bomb shelters - when such shelters are available to them - during wartime?
The use of the term “the people of Israel” is no accident. It is a code word, an effective shortcut for establishing a shared sense of tribal belonging and manufacturing intimacy.
When Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot tells a former Likud voter, disillusioned with Netanyahu, during an election campaign that “as far as I’m concerned, there is no way the people of Israel will not prevail,” he knows exactly what he is doing: building a sense of tribal intimacy whose boundaries are perfectly clear to both men.
It is within those boundaries that the right is now calling on him to gather under its unity campaign - boundaries that necessarily leave Arabs on the outside.
It is hardly surprising, then, that the Arab parties are the only ones presenting a civic discourse as a substantive alternative to the Jewish tribal discourse embodied in the phrase “the people of Israel”.
Here lies one of the great paradoxes of the Zionist state. Since its founding, Israel has relentlessly sought to sever the connection between Arab citizens and their Palestinian national identity, subjecting them to a process of forced “Israelisation”.
Yet the moment Arab citizens seek to give real substance to the citizenship imposed upon them after the Nakba, “the people of Israel” are quick to reclassify them as Palestinians and push them back beyond the boundaries of the Israeli collective. This is the declared position of at least two of the four parties that make up the so-called change bloc.
The choice now facing Eisenkot is not merely between two different governing coalitions. It is a choice between two fundamentally different conceptions of the boundaries of Israeli citizenship: between “the people of Israel” and the citizens of Israel. If he chooses the former, he will become, under cover of the “unity” discourse, a pale appendage of a fully fledged Jewish-supremacist coalition.
If he chooses the latter, he will have to accept Arab citizens as full partners in Israeli citizenship, with an equal and legitimate stake in shaping the country’s character - rather than as people whose struggle is limited to securing whatever crumbs the state is willing to throw their way.
