https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Bolsonaristas pagam anúncios para pressionar senadores do PL a romper com Alcolumbre
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Cleber Lourenço
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A disputa pela presidência do Senado em 2027 ganhou uma frente de atuação nas redes sociais. Bolsonaristas passaram a investir em anúncios pagos para pressionar integrantes do próprio PL com publicações que defendem até a expulsão de senadores da legenda caso votem pela permanência de Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) no comando da Casa.
Registros da Biblioteca de Anúncios da Meta analisados pelo ICL Notícias mostram que o deputado federal Bibo Nunes (PL-RS) impulsionou uma publicação na qual defende a expulsão dos correligionários que votarem em Alcolumbre. O conteúdo registrou entre 300 mil e 350 mil impressões nas plataformas da empresa, proprietária do Facebook e do Instagram.
Ao defender a expulsão dos senadores, Bibo transforma uma eventual aliança com Alcolumbre em uma questão de fidelidade partidária. A publicação patrocinada leva ao público uma disputa que envolve diretamente as negociações políticas do PL para a próxima legislatura.
O deputado também investiu entre R$ 500 e R$ 599 para impulsionar outra publicação contra o presidente do Senado, na qual responsabiliza Alcolumbre pela falta de ajuda ao município de Tupanciretã, no Rio Grande do Sul. O anúncio registrou entre 300 mil e 350 mil impressões.
Somente essas duas publicações contra Alcolumbre acumularam entre 600 mil e 700 mil impressões. O indicador contabiliza o número de vezes que os anúncios foram exibidos, incluindo eventuais visualizações repetidas por um mesmo usuário.
Pressão sobre senadores do próprio PL
A cobrança pública sobre integrantes da legenda de Jair Bolsonaro não se restringe à disputa pela presidência do Senado. Outros anúncios patrocinados procuram pressionar parlamentares do partido a assumir compromissos com pautas defendidas pelo bolsonarismo, especialmente aquelas relacionadas ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).
O perfil Chico Raiz, por exemplo, investiu entre R$ 1 mil e R$ 1,5 mil para impulsionar uma publicação que questiona se o senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) apoiará o impeachment de um ministro do Supremo. O anúncio registrou entre 250 mil e 300 mil impressões.
Os três anúncios foram identificados em um levantamento que analisou 708 publicações patrocinadas sobre política, eleições e temas sociais nas plataformas da Meta entre 18 e 24 de novembro.
Juntos, os conteúdos registraram entre 850 mil e 1 milhão de impressões. Embora tratem de questões distintas, têm em comum a utilização de publicidade paga para ampliar cobranças sobre integrantes do Congresso, inclusive parlamentares do próprio PL.
STF e comando do Congresso mobilizam bolsonaristas
O levantamento, que também analisou publicações no X, no Instagram e no YouTube, identificou que os conteúdos relacionados a Bolsonaro e ao STF estão entre aqueles que mais geram engajamento entre perfis da oposição.
Enquanto as críticas econômicas, especialmente aquelas relacionadas ao ajuste fiscal e aos impostos, são direcionadas principalmente ao governo Lula, as publicações sobre o Judiciário e a situação de Bolsonaro têm como alvos também os presidentes das duas Casas do Congresso.
A diferença ajuda a explicar por que parte da publicidade política identificada nas plataformas da Meta é direcionada a parlamentares da própria direita, e não exclusivamente a adversários eleitorais.
No Senado, a pressão envolve tanto a composição da futura Mesa Diretora quanto a posição dos parlamentares sobre medidas contra ministros do Supremo. Cabe à Casa processar e julgar ministros do STF por crimes de responsabilidade, atribuição que coloca sua presidência em uma posição central nessas discussões.
Os registros analisados não permitem afirmar que exista uma atuação coordenada entre os anunciantes. Também não foi possível determinar se os recursos empregados nos impulsionamentos são particulares, partidários ou provenientes de verbas parlamentares.

https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.title: Avengers: Doomsday has brought with it more ‘Marvel homework’ than ever. That’s just as it should be
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.author: Ben Child
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.text:
The cinema release of Avengers: Doomsday is now roughly three weeks away and, judging by the final trailer, we’re living in the one timeline where every loose end Marvel has left dangling for years is now worth tugging on. Even the ones we thought the studio had tied up rather nicely. Ever since it became apparent that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers would be returning in the new film, along with next year’s sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, fans have been asking themselves: where exactly has he been all this time? Now, thanks to the latest footage, we’re beginning to get an idea, and we might also be starting to pick up clues as to why Doctor Doom would take an interest in his new postcode.
One of the most startling aspects of the new trailer is the arrival of the Fantastic Four, led by Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, on Rogers’ front lawn. We’ve known since the finale of Avengers: Endgame that Steve used Tony Stark’s newly discovered time-travelling tech to go back to the 1940s and live out his life with Peggy Carter during the events of that film – but until recently it seemed most likely that happened in good old Earth-616, the main Marvel Cinematic Universe continuity.
Then there was the new final scene in Endgame: Encore, in which Loki turned up to offer the happy couple some kind of nebulous “help”. Fans have been theorising for a while that because the god of mischief is now holding the multiverse together (thanks to the events of season two of Loki) he might be offering them the chance to shift into an alternative reality, for reasons unknown. That idea looks a little more plausible now that Richards and co have turned up at the lovers’ house. Did Steve and Peggy somehow make it to Earth-828, the retro-futurist reality introduced in last year’s The Fantastic Four: First Steps? And is this one of the reasons why Doom is so angry with them?
Stay with me here. We already know, thanks to a mid-credits scene in Encore, that the multiverse is collapsing due to a series of incursions between different universes across thousands of worlds. Might moving Steve and Peggy into another reality have helped trigger one on Earth-828? Doomsday co-director Joe Russo has spoken about how this new version of Doom is suffering from the loss of a child, which might explain his anger towards the universe (or multiverse) in general. Have Steve’s reality-shifting antics, his decision to try to find himself a life away from heroism, created the circumstances that have led others to suffer? “All of you have lived stolen lives,” says Doom in the new footage. “But now you must give them back.” The trailer then cuts to Thor and Scott Lang (Ant-Man) with their daughters.
Thor’s adoptive daughter, Love, is an intriguing choice for the trailer to focus on. At the end of Thor: Love and Thunder, Christian Bale’s Gorr uses his one wish to bring her back from the dead, and Thor takes her in. Now here’s another father who’s lost a child, telling the Avengers they have to give back the lives he says they stole. And then there’s the child Doom has already paid a visit. In a First Steps credits scene, Sue Storm goes to fetch her son Franklin a book and comes back to find a certain sinister supervillain kneeling in front of him in the living room. We know the boy has godlike powers, having brought his mother back from the dead. It’s worth asking what a man in Doom’s position might want from him, especially when he’s lost a child of his own.
One of the biggest criticisms of Marvel over the past few years has been the sheer amount of required viewing everyone has to get through – from Disney+ shows to post-credits teasers and new footage tucked into rereleases – just to be able to work out what’s going on. And yet here we are, three weeks from Doomsday, checking the custody arrangements at the end of a four-year-old Thor film, combing the multiversal electoral roll for Captain America, and desperately trying to remind ourselves why the ruler of Latveria turned up in full armour for story time. Which of course is exactly what should be happening this close to the release of a new Avengers movie: Marvel reminding us that sometimes, the right kind of homework is actually worth completing.

European football violence causes concern with far-right claim in UEFA game
Claims of Nazi salutes at UEFA Europa League game in Marseille headline night of further violence in European football.
Violent clashes at two European football matches have stoked concerns about fan violence and prompted the leaders of France and Bulgaria to condemn behaviour that had “no place in civilized Europe”.
Images showed masked and bloodied fans wielding improvised weapons and metal pipes during a brawl at a UEFA Europa League match on Wednesday evening between Marseille and Levski Sofia, which the Bulgarian club said began when their fans were attacked by supporters of the French side.
A photographer working for the Reuters news agency said the clashes at the Stade Velodrome in Marseille had started after a supporter from the visitors’ stand made a Nazi salute.
Clashes also broke out at a Europa League match in the Georgian city of Batumi between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva, forcing the referee to suspend the match for 30 minutes.
European football’s governing body UEFA told Reuters its disciplinary body “would assess the match reports before considering any potential ‌next steps”.
What was the reaction to the Marseille and Levski Sofia game?
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke by phone and condemned the violence at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match, in which Marseille police said 11 Bulgarian fans were hurt, five of whom were taken to hospital.
“We share the position that aggression and violence have no place in civilized Europe,” Radev said on Facebook.
“I thank President Macron for his personal commitment to this case, for the medical care provided to the injured by the French authorities, for the measures taken to ensure the safety of Bulgarian citizens, and for the perpetrators to be held accountable.”
Macron said he had condemned “with the utmost force” acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans, which he said had “no place in sport or in public space”, and told Radev they would not go unpunished.
A protest was planned in front of the French embassy in Sofia later on Friday.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said: “Violence, racial hatred and provocation have no place in our stadiums.”
Manuel Bompard, a French lawmaker for the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party in the Marseille department, commented on a video on social media appearing to show a Levski fan performing a Nazi salute.
“Congrats to the Marseille fans who responded with an antifascist chant,” Bompard wrote on X. “The far-right has no place in our stadiums!”
Batons fly, flares lit in Marseille and Levski Sofia clash
Levski Sofia, which lost the match 1-0, said masked fans had attacked its supporters with batons and flares. Some had let off flares and tried to get through the barrier as security staff tried to hold them back.
Images showed fans attacking each other through a netted fence separating sections of the stadium.
Before Thursday’s match, French authorities had introduced a sevenfold reduction of ticket sales to Levski supporters and imposed additional restrictions on their movement to and around the stadium, aiming to curb risks of violence.
The Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it would request a thorough investigation. Marseille said it would conduct its own analysis and was working closely with law enforcement.
What happened in the Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva match?
The match between Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva had been moved from Istanbul for what UEFA said were safety and security reasons.
Clashes in the stands led referee Morten Krogh to suspend the match in the 26th minute, and it resumed after a 30-minute delay. Georgian police entered the stands, and television footage showed one ‌fan being carried out on a stretcher.
Turkish outlet NTV reported that police used pepper spray. Besiktas condemned what it called “disproportionate force” by security staff and said a number of fans had been denied entry. Besiktas went on to win 2-1.
Turkish Football Federation chair Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu defended the ‌decision ‌to keep Israeli clubs out of Turkiye following Israel’s invasion of Gaza in 2023 after the deadly Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/gazas.title: Gaza’s children caught in the grip of a meningitis outbreak
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/gazas.author: Hani Abu Rezeq
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/gazas.text:
Gaza’s children caught in the grip of a meningitis outbreak
For 10 days, two-month-old Mostafa Hallawin has been bedridden at Al-Rantisi Children’s Hospital in Gaza City.
After suffering a persistent high fever, reaching 39C, and recurring abdominal swelling, the Palestinian infant was diagnosed with meningitis.
“It started with a skin rash and a high fever, with his temperature reaching 39C,” his mother, Amal, told Middle East Eye.
“Every day, doctors perform medical scans and laboratory tests,” she added, saying his condition has shown little improvement, largely because of shortages of essential medicines.
Hallawin is one of the most recent children to develop meningitis amid a spike in cases across the war-torn enclave, where Israel has all but destroyed the healthcare system and continues to ban essential medicines.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) reported 413 suspected meningitis cases in Gaza between 27 September and 31 October, including 294 viral and 119 bacterial cases. The report said 68 percent were recorded in Gaza City.
On Tuesday, the Palestinian Health Ministry declared an "epidemic alert" across Gaza, citing a sharp rise in meningitis cases and deaths.
The ministry said 1,790 people had been diagnosed with meningitis since the beginning of the year, with 15 deaths recorded. In October alone, at least 272 infections were confirmed.
The risk of infectious diseases has increased amid overcrowded displacement shelters, unsafe drinking water, damaged sanitation systems and the collapse of essential healthcare services across Gaza.
In September, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said microbiological contamination in tested water samples rose from less than six percent in January to nearly 20 percent in August.
At Al-Rantisi Children's Hospital, which was heavily damaged in Israeli attacks during the war, beds are filled with children suffering from infectious diseases, including meningitis.
The growing number of cases threatens to create conditions in which infections can spread easily between children. Amal believes her child’s condition deteriorated during his hospital stay because of overcrowding and inadequate isolation facilities.
“There is little access to basic hygiene facilities, clean food and safe drinking water,” she said.
“I appeal for medicines and essential medical equipment to be allowed into Gaza for our children.
"We have lost our homes and our lives in this war. We don’t want to lose our babies too.”
Contaminated water
For Reham Wahdan, the health crisis became personal when her nine-month-old son, Mohammed, developed a high fever.
Wahdan and her family have been living alongside other displaced families in a room in the partly destroyed Islamic University building, after their home in Shujaiya, east of Gaza City, was destroyed by an Israeli attack during the war.
She said Mohammed's health began to deteriorate a day after they visited relatives staying in a makeshift tent near their displacement shelter.
'I appeal for medicines and essential medical equipment to be allowed into Gaza for our children'
- Amal Hallawin, Palestinian mother
She believes he got the infection from a child with meningitis whom they'd visited.
“He had suffered from a high fever for nearly a month, despite repeated attempts to give him medication to bring his temperature down,” she said.
Wahdan took Mohammed to several medical tents and treatment points, where he was given medication to reduce his fever. His temperature would fall briefly, only to rise again.
“Doctors at Al-Rantisi Hospital performed a lumbar puncture to collect a cerebrospinal fluid sample, and the test results confirmed that he had meningitis,” she said.
Wahdan also said her family had no access to safe drinking water where they were displaced.
“We drink contaminated water, and we rely entirely on distributed food,” she said.
Deteriorating conditions
Dr Nidal Ghunaim, the deputy director-general of primary health care for public health at the Ministry of Health, said both bacterial and viral meningitis cases had increased significantly compared with previous years.
He attributed much of the rise to enterovirus, which he said was closely linked to deteriorating environmental conditions across the Gaza Strip.
The contamination of drinking water with sewage had further worsened the situation, contributing to the increase in reported infections, he said.
The situation has become even more concerning following recent heavy rainfall in Gaza.
“Many areas were flooded with rainwater, and sewage mixed with drinking water. The destruction of infrastructure has made the situation worse, and we expect that any further wave of flooding could make things much more difficult,” he told MEE.
“There are also significant shortages of laboratory supplies, medical treatments and isolation facilities in hospitals,” Ghunaim added.
He called on the international community to intervene urgently and support a comprehensive, long-term response to Gaza's environmental and water crises.
“The extensive destruction of water infrastructure has severely affected access to safe and clean water. Restoring and rehabilitating the water network must be an essential priority,” he said.
Back at Al-Rantisi Hospital, Reem Hamada has spent the past 10 days at the bedside of her five-year-old grandson, Mohammed, after he developed a high fever.
“One day, he came back from kindergarten with a high fever. We applied cool compresses to his forehead, neck and armpits to try to bring his temperature down, but it did not improve,” she said.
Throughout the interview, Mohammed lay beside her, his eyes closed, a cool compress resting on his forehead as the fever persisted.
“He is my only grandchild. What has he done to deserve this suffering?” she said.
“We are no longer living; we are as good as dead.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Itamaraty diz que Macron, presidente da França, ‘dissemina desinformação’ ao chamar carne brasileira de ‘dopada’
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O governo brasileiro acusou o presidente da França, Emmanuel Macron, de espalhar desinformação ao se referir à carne produzida no Brasil como “dopada”. Em nota divulgada na noite de quinta-feira (26), o Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) lamentou a fala e rebateu o líder francês. “Tais declarações disseminam desinformação e contrariam as evidências técnicas e científicas amplamente disponíveis sobre a produção de proteína animal no Brasil”, afirmou a pasta.
Macron fez a declaração na quarta-feira (25), durante reunião com representantes do setor agrícola francês no Palácio do Eliseu, ao comemorar a suspensão das importações de produtos de origem animal do Brasil pela União Europeia (UE), em vigor desde 3 de setembro.
Na nota, o Itamaraty lembra que o Brasil é, há décadas, fornecedor seguro de proteína animal para o bloco europeu e exporta carnes para 177 mercados. Segundo o ministério, o rigor do sistema brasileiro de controle sanitário foi confirmado pelas conclusões favoráveis da recente auditoria europeia nas cadeias de aves e de mel.
O texto destaca ainda que a produção nacional segue exigências ambientais muitas vezes mais rígidas que as europeias, como a obrigação legal de preservar vegetação nativa em até 80% da área das propriedades rurais, além de contar com uma matriz energética predominantemente renovável.
“Preocupa ao governo brasileiro a clara natureza política das restrições sanitárias atualmente impostas pela União Europeia ao Brasil”, declarou a chancelaria. Para o Itamaraty, o uso dessas medidas com fins protecionistas viola as regras da Organização Mundial do Comércio (OMC) e o espírito do acordo entre o Mercosul e a UE, criando um desequilíbrio evidente nas concessões negociadas entre os blocos.
O governo brasileiro reafirma a importância da parceria estratégica com a França, mas pede que o governo francês reveja sua posição com base nas evidências científicas e lembra que a relação bilateral deve ser pautada pelo respeito mútuo e pela reciprocidade. “O governo brasileiro reserva-se o direito de recorrer aos instrumentos de que dispõe para defender os interesses legítimos de seus produtores e exportadores”, advertiu o ministério.
Macron celebrou veto à carne ‘dopada’
No encontro com agricultores franceses, Macron associou o bloqueio aos produtos brasileiros à pressão política da França contra o acordo comercial entre a UE e o Mercosul, em vigor provisoriamente desde maio. “Tínhamos ainda mais razão porque, com o Mercosul assinado, aquilo que denunciávamos se confirmou, já que finalmente os serviços da Comissão perceberam que o que nós dizíamos a eles era verdade. E a carne dopada, por assim dizer, em todo caso a carne do Mercosul, em especial a brasileira, que chegava aos nossos portos e, portanto, aos nossos mercados, e que não respeitava as nossas regras, acabou sendo proibida”, disse o presidente francês.
A UE suspendeu as compras por considerar que o Brasil não cumpre as regras europeias sobre o uso de antimicrobianos, substâncias usadas para tratar infecções em animais. O bloco proíbe o uso desses produtos para estimular o crescimento dos rebanhos e restringe, na pecuária, a aplicação de antibióticos considerados essenciais para o tratamento de seres humanos. A decisão, no entanto, não foi motivada por irregularidades encontradas na carne brasileira, mas pela avaliação de que os controles adotados no país eram insuficientes.
A suspensão começou poucos dias depois da entrada em vigor do acordo com o Mercosul, que enfrentou forte resistência de agricultores europeus, temerosos da concorrência de produtos sul-americanos mais baratos. O Brasil, principal exportador agrícola do bloco sul-americano para a Europa, é o único país do Mercosul atingido pela restrição. Argentina, Paraguai e Uruguai seguem autorizados a vender produtos de origem animal ao mercado europeu.
Exportadores falam em ‘inverdades’
A fala de Macron também provocou reação do setor. A Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA), que representa a indústria de frango, considerou grave e inaceitável que um chefe de Estado recorra a inverdades, sem fundamento técnico, para questionar os alimentos de um parceiro que contribui há mais de 40 anos para a segurança alimentar europeia. Segundo a entidade, a própria ministra da Agricultura da França, Annie Genevard, reconheceu o rigor da auditoria e o cumprimento das normas europeias pelo Brasil.
A Associação Brasileira das Indústrias Exportadoras de Carnes (Abiec) avaliou que a postura do presidente francês escancara o caráter político e protecionista do veto. “Não foi apresentada justificativa técnica ou científica para a exclusão do Brasil da lista de países autorizados, tampouco para a interrupção do fluxo comercial durante o período de adequação ao protocolo”, afirmou a associação. A entidade lembra que a UE responde por cerca de 5% das exportações brasileiras de carne bovina. “Após mais de duas décadas de negociações, é inadmissível que os benefícios do acordo sejam unilaterais”, cobrou a Abiec.
A declaração de Macron ocorre a menos de duas semanas da reunião da UE marcada para 7 e 8 de dezembro, que deve discutir a volta do Brasil à lista de países autorizados a exportar carne de frango e mel ao bloco. O tema seria analisado em 17 de novembro, mas foi adiado. Em nota ao g1, a Comissão Europeia informou que vários países-membros pediram esclarecimentos adicionais sobre o sistema de controle brasileiro. A missão técnica europeia esteve no Brasil entre 24 de agosto e 4 de setembro e, em 28 de setembro, a Comissão Europeia divulgou relatório segundo o qual o país atendia às exigências do bloco para exportar esses produtos.
*Com informações do g1.

Les cookies et technologies similaires que nous utilisons sur Mediapart sont de différentes natures et nous permettent de poursuivre différentes finalités. 
Certains sont nécessaires au fonctionnement du site et de l’application mobile (vous ne pouvez pas les refuser). D’autres sont optionnels mais contribuent à faciliter votre expérience de lecteur ou de lectrice et d’une certaine façon à soutenir Mediapart. Vous pouvez les refuser ou les accepter ci-dessous, selon leurs finalités. 
Acceptez-vous que Mediapart utilise des cookies ou technologies similaires pour les finalités suivantes ?

                                Nécessaires au fonctionnement
du site ou de l’application
                            Connexion des abonné·es, mesure d’audience anonymisée, envoi des notifications push, suivi des pannes, mise en avant de nos services : ces outils sont nécessaires au suivi de l’activité de nos services et à leur bon fonctionnement.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Saudi strike kills ’11 civilians’ in Yemen’s Taiz: Houthi media
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Saudi strike kills ’11 civilians’ in Yemen’s Taiz: Houthi media
Hostilities between Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed coalition continue to push Yemen into a humanitarian crisis.
Saudi air strikes have killed 11 civilians in Yemen’s Taiz governorate, according to news media affiliated with the Houthi armed group.
The attack reported on Friday hit the city of al-Turbah, located south of the provincial capital, Taiz.
The alleged strike comes as hostilities in Yemen continue between the Iran-backed rebel Houthi group and government forces backed by Saudi Arabia.
A local source said that a residential building was struck and that “most” of the victims were children, according to the media report.
Rescue teams retrieved eight bodies from the site, the report said. Three people remain missing beneath the rubble.
Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports. The Saudi Arabia-led coalition supporting the internationally-recognised Yemen government did not immediately comment.
The coalition said later on Friday that it had destroyed a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region.
Humanitarian crisis
Yemen has been racked by violence since the Iran-backed Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and other parts of the country in 2014, prompting Saudi Arabia to lead a military coalition in support of the internationally recognised government in March 2015.
Fighting between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, as the United States’ war on Iran escalated hostilities and the collapse of a 2022 ceasefire.
Some 13,343 people have been killed or injured since August, according to the World Health Organization, while the country is sliding into a humanitarian crisis.
The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme said on Friday that Yemen is among conflict hotspots that face severe food insecurity.
The Norwegian Refugee Council warned this week that the renewed fighting has displaced thousands and piled pressure onto dangerously underfunded aid efforts.
Aid from the US, Germany and others has shrunk considerably in recent years, the nongovernmental organisation noted, saying it has received only 12 percent of funding for emergency shelter support in Yemen so far this year.
“Fighting has again displaced entire communities, while disrupted supply routes have driven up food and fuel prices,” NRC Secretary-General Jan Egeland said, warning that families across Yemen are being pushed deeper into need.
“All parties to the conflict bear responsibility for the vast scale of harm here,” Egeland stated.
Calling for better humanitarian access and civilian protection, he demanded that “the powerful countries backing the armed actors must commit to making this a reality”.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Guardiãs da cura: mapeamento inédito revela a força das benzedeiras e raizeiras em BH
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Lucas Wilker
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Para lançar luz sobre um patrimônio imaterial vivo, a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte (PBH), por meio da Diretoria de Políticas de Reparação e Promoção da Igualdade Racial (DPIR), realizou em 2026 o primeiro mapeamento sistemático de benzedeiras, raizeiras, erveiras e curadoras populares.
O estudo combinou um formulário digital participativo, com momentos de escuta presencial, a exemplo da “Mostra com Prosa de Saberes Tradicionais: 8 anos”, idealizada pela psicóloga e benzedeira Ana Maria Soares (Mãe Ana).
O levantamento registrou inicialmente 107 inscrições e validou a atuação de 100 guardiãs e guardiões de saberes tradicionais, constituindo uma radiografia estatística e humana na história social de Minas Gerais. Os resultados comprovam que a prática da cura popular na capital mineira é uma tecnologia social de resistência e cuidado comunitário profundamente estruturada.
Sagrado feminino
A pesquisa confirmou que o ofício do cuidado comunitário em Belo Horizonte é exercido majoritariamente por mulheres. Entre os 100 registros validados, 77% identificam-se como mulheres cisgênero, enquanto homens cisgênero somam 12%, pessoas não-binárias correspondem a 4% e homens transgênero representam 1%. Outros 6% preferiram não responder.
Esse protagonismo feminino encontra eco nos estudos acadêmicos sobre a cultura mineira. Conforme destaca a pesquisadora Celina Gontijo Cunha em sua tese de doutorado defendida em 2023, e citada pelo documento, a mulher ocupa uma posição de liderança de primeira ordem na tradição da cura pela palavra. Ao ser iniciada nesse universo mágico-religioso, a benzedeira converte-se em uma agente social garantidora da própria identidade cultural e comunitária do seu povo, em patamar de relevância equivalente aos mestres do Congado, da Folia de Reis e da Marujada.
Matriz étnico-racial negra
A composição racial das praticantes atesta a profunda conexão entre a benzeção, a medicina de ervas e as matrizes africanas e afro-brasileiras. O levantamento estatístico apontou que 53% das praticantes declaram-se pretas, 24% brancas, 22% pardas e 1% indígena.
Somadas as categorias preta e parda — que compõem a população negra segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) —, atinge-se o índice de 75% de negras entre as guardiãs mapeadas. Contudo, os analistas do mapeamento ressaltam a necessidade de interpretar a categoria ‘parda’ com cautela analítica, dado que ela frequentemente abriga trajetórias complexas de miscigenação que envolvem ascendências indígenas e negras nem sempre capturadas pelas métricas censitárias tradicionais.
Como pontuou a liderança Mãe Ana durante o Encontro do Programa Vozes Raízes da PBH, o reconhecimento oficial dessas mulheres é uma pauta direta de reparação histórica e equidade racial:
“A gente sabe o tanto que nós raizeiras e benzedeiras interferimos e diminuímos dados de sobrevida e sobre saúde, e isso precisa ser reconhecido, isso precisa avançar”, afirmou.
Sabedoria geracional e territorial
Outro dado diz respeito ao envelhecimento das praticantes: 73% das benzedeiras e raizeiras de Belo Horizonte possuem 45 anos ou mais. A distribuição detalhada por faixas etárias demonstra que a experiência acumulada é o solo onde esses saberes florescem.
A distribuição territorial do cuidado tradicional em Belo Horizonte revela uma geografia marcada pelas periferias e por bairros populares de ocupação histórica. O mapeamento comprovou a presença de benzedeiras e raizeiras em todas as nove regionais administrativas do município.
As regionais Nordeste (21,4%), Leste (14,3%) e Noroeste (13,3%) concentram juntas quase metade (49%) de todas as benzedeiras e raizeiras registradas na capital. Bairros tradicionais da Zona Nordeste, como o Concórdia, destacam-se pelo elevado adensamento de rezadeiras e ervanários comunitários ativos.
Um aspecto metodológico e social apontado pela equipe de pesquisadores do mapeamento foi a identificação de diversos Códigos de Endereçamento Postal (CEPs) fornecidos pelas praticantes que não constavam nas bases de dados cartográficas formais do município. Esse detalhe evidencia a existência da “cidade real”, composta por vilas, aglomerados e becos, cuja dinâmica social e comunitária transcende os limites dos mapas oficiais do planejamento urbano.
Pedagogia comunitária
Os dados do documento demonstram que a aprendizagem não decorre de manuais ou cursos formais, mas sim da experiência vivida, da observação atenta e da mediunidade. A orientação espiritual (36%) e a herança familiar direta, somando avós, mães, pais e parentes, constituem os pilares fundamentais dessa tradição.
Em relato registrado no relatório da PBH, a benzedeira Maria Ephigênia descreve o despertar espontâneo aos 38 anos.
“Eu comecei a rezar e nem sabia que sabia rezar. Fui na Umbanda, cheguei lá e uma senhora velha, de quase 100 anos, disse que minha mediunidade estava avançada e que eu precisava prestar caridade. Ela me mandou sentar na corrente dos Pretos Velhos. Quando cheguei em casa, uma vizinha bateu à porta trazendo o filho para eu benzer, dizendo que a entidade tinha mandado”, contou.
Tempo de prática
Cerca de 30% das praticantes exercem a benzeção ou o preparo de remédios há mais de 20 anos, 22% atuam entre 10 e 20 anos, 18% trabalham de 5 a 10 anos, 18% aprenderam e praticam desde a infância e apenas 12% possuem menos de 5 anos de atuação.
Ao menos 88% das mapeadas declaram compartilhar ativamente seus conhecimentos com aprendizes, familiares, filhos de santo ou moradores do bairro. Ao todo, 31 praticantes ensinam diretamente as pessoas da comunidade e 16 mantêm aprendizes formais.
O mapeamento revelou que o uso de recursos vegetais é praticamente universal entre as guardiãs de Belo Horizonte: 96% das praticantes utilizam ervas medicinais em suas atividades cotidianas, enquanto apenas 4% dedicam-se exclusivamente a rezas sem o suporte de plantas.

https://cartoonmovement.substack.com/p/c.title: Cartoons from the frontlines
https://cartoonmovement.substack.com/p/c.author: Cartoon Movement
https://cartoonmovement.substack.com/p/c.text:
Ruslan Pikhota is a Ukrainian frontline cartoonist and an active-duty officer in the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Before the full-scale invasion, he spent 15 years working in children’s publishing in Kharkiv. He volunteered in February 2022, served as an infantryman on the Donetsk and Kharkiv fronts, and was wounded near Bakhmut. He now serves with an unmanned systems unit.
Since the spring of 2022, he has created more than 550 drawings in trenches, dugouts, ruined buildings, and between military duties. His work documents frontline life, drone warfare, fear, loss, brotherhood, absurdity, and the black humour soldiers use to endure war. His English-language book, Smile under the Roar of Cannon Fire, was published in 2025, and his drawings have been shown in Prishtina, Geneva, and Grenoble. He is now developing this archive into a three-volume visual diary of the war.
We are delighted to welcome Ruslan to Cartoon Movement! As an introduction, we asked him to select what he considers to be his ten most telling drawings made at the front lines.
Drawing No. 519 — FOUR IN THE MORNING
At the front, you constantly feel Death nearby, until it begins to seem like another member of the unit. I imagined the beginning of their day at four in the morning: the soldier starts with coffee, while Death takes a strange pet for a walk.
Drawing No. 393 — WHEN YOU’RE IN A TRENCH
A soldier sitting in a trench always wants more behind him — more artillery, more armour, more aircraft. I drew a very simple infantry feeling: you are one small person in a hole in the ground, and suddenly no amount of support seems excessive.
Drawing No. 533 — WHEN THE SKY FILLS WITH MACHINES
When I first went to war, the sky was mostly empty. A few years later, it had become crowded with reconnaissance drones, FPVs, bomber drones and interceptors. The soldier remained, but the war around him changed.
Drawing No. 564 — WHEN MACHINES BECOME PREDATORS
When two FPV drones suddenly rise in front of a soldier, they stop looking like machines. In that instant, the mind reads them as something alive — predators preparing to strike.
Drawing No. 527 — WHEN DRONES CHANGE THE FOREST
Through drone cameras, I have seen entire battlefields wrapped in fibre-optic cable, birds’ nests made from it, and our own drones caught in cables left by others. The moose is invented, but the new web spreading across the landscape is real.
Drawing No. 541 — THE SEASONS OF WAR: AUTUMN
This drawing is rooted in what happened to my platoon near Kurdiumivka in December 2022. Under fire, we dug shallow shelters in the frozen ground and covered them with plastic, but when the temperature rose to 1°C and rain began, they filled with water while shelling and assaults continued. We remained there for 19 days; when we were finally pulled back to rest, only five of the original twenty-four men were still with the platoon.
Drawing No. 419 — BOTH RIFLES JAMMED
During an assault, Amigo, a soldier of Ukraine’s 3rd Assault Brigade, found his rifle jammed just as the Russian soldier facing him discovered the same thing. Rapira, another soldier from the brigade, intervened and saved Amigo. I later turned the real incident into a short comic: the black humour is invented, but the absurdity that produced it was not.
Drawing No. 562 — PILA: A MODULAR PROBLEM-SOLVING SYSTEM
Pila, a soldier of Ukraine’s 3rd Assault Brigade, lost an arm in the war. I did not want to portray him as a victim, so I imagined his prosthesis as a modular system — a weapon, a bottle, a flower or a fork, whatever the situation requires. Dark humour does not erase trauma; sometimes it gives a person control over it again.
Drawing No. 362 — MOTHER OF GOD: OKHMATDYT
After Russia’s missile strike on the Okhmatdyt Children’s Hospital in Kyiv on 8 July 2024, I saw a photograph of a woman comforting a young patient. I redrew the photograph and transformed it into an icon of the Mother of God and Child. Some events leave no room for satire; they can only be witnessed and remembered.
Drawing No. 396 — THE FIRST DAY AFTER THE WAR
I imagined the first day after the war at the Swallow’s Nest in Crimea. Russia’s war against Ukraine began in Crimea, and it will end there; the soldier has put down his weapon, but learning to live after the war will be another long journey.

As some of you might know, Cartoon Movement is a consortium partner in Horizon Europe project DELIAH (Democratic Literacy and Humour). In addition to researching humour, part of DELIAH’s mission is to raise awareness about the role of humour in our democracies. We try to do this in various ways: by writing about it, by giving workshops and now also by making a comic about it.
Over the last few months, we have worked with the renowned cartoonist Pedro X. Molina to create a four-page comic that explains what we currently know about how humour works in a democracy.
Depending on your device, you can choose to read the mobile version (just below) or the desktop version (below the mobile version).

Hi!
We did not have a newsletter last month (we were on summer break), so it’s about time for an update! Below you’ll find our latest news, cartoon collections, and the most popular cartoons of the month. Enjoy! And no newsletter is complete without promoting our other newsletter, our daily editor’s choice.
Cartoon Movement at the Dutch Journalism Festival
The Dutch Journalism Festival (Nederlands Journalistiek Festival) is taking place on September 18 and 19 in Deventer, the Netherlands. The two-day festival features panels, workshops, movie screenings and live journalism. Cartoon Movement is also present with the workshop we delevoped for DELIAH: The Importance of Humour for Democracy: Good Humour versus Bad Humour
Unfortunately, the workshop is already fully booked. If you are interested, we did a similar workshop at the International Journalism Festival in Perugia in April, which was recorded:
Also, if you are planning to visit the festival, several Dutch cartoonists will be drawing live on Saturday to see who can make the best cartoon.
The state of democracy, in cartoons
The Kettering Foundation has published a collection of international cartoons with different perspectives on democracy. The collection, with cartoons from 19 renowned cartoonists, was put together by Tjeerd Royaards (cartoonist and editor-in-chief at Cartoon Movement), Terry Anderson (executive director at Cartoonists Rights), and Patrick Gathara (2026 CFK Global Fellow).
Satire translates complex political realities into stories, images, and jokes that ordinary people can engage with. In doing so, it lowers the barriers to political participation while creating space for critique that is often less threatening to audiences than overt political argument.
Patrick Gathara

https://theintercept.com/2026/11/18/greg.title: Greg Abbott Tried to Destroy Muslim Group By Calling Them Terrorists. Texas Voters Balked.
https://theintercept.com/2026/11/18/greg.author: Sanya Mansoor
https://theintercept.com/2026/11/18/greg.text:
As Texas Republicans pursued their crusade against the Council on American-Islamic Relations, they ran into an unexpected obstacle: voters.
Republicans Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton had carried out their crackdown on the largest Muslim civil rights group in the U.S., hoping to ban CAIR’s operations in the state and label it a terrorist organization. That agenda suffered a crippling blow in the midterm elections, when Democratic candidates beat Abbott and Paxton in stunning upsets — with both their current offices set to be led by Democrats.
Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa promised to reverse Abbott’s designation of CAIR as a foreign terrorist organization. She told the Washington Post last week, “We have to use public safety measures for public safety” — decrying Abbott’s designation as “nonsense.” Paxton, who lost a bid for an open U.S. Senate seat, dropped a lawsuit, filed in February, that would have banned CAIR from operating in Texas.
“Don’t underestimate the power of the vote to create the administration that creates and enforces these laws,” said Chelsea Glover, a lawyer with the Muslim Legal Fund of America, who is representing CAIR Texas in litigation challenging Abbott’s designation. “Lots of times we don’t think it’s possible but, as Texas has shown, anything is possible.”
The Muslim Legal Fund of America said the lawsuit is ongoing and will be until Abbott’s terror designation is formally withdrawn by Hinojosa.
CAIR’s suit was necessary, said Glover, but acknowledged that the ballot box can be a faster way to shut down bigotry than drawn out court cases.
CAIR welcomed Hinojosa’s promise to walk back Abbott’s proclamation, which CAIR called a “baseless, unconstitutional order.”
The proclamation classified CAIR and its Texas chapter, as well as the Muslim Brotherhood, as foreign terrorist groups; it also banned designated groups from buying or acquiring land in the state.
“When you get the right person in power, who is going to follow the Constitution, it’s like — poof, the designation is gone almost overnight,” said Imran Ghani, director of digital communications for CAIR Texas and operations director for the Houston branch.
Ghani said CAIR Texas noticed a chilling effect after Abbott’s proclamation last November. Some donors stopped giving money, and a few mosques became hesitant to platform CAIR. He said the organization quickly rebuilt trust and also won over new supporters who were invigorated by the state’s targeting of CAIR and wanted to help.
“I tend to look at it rather positively,” Ghani said. “The designation gave CAIR more publicity than we have ever received.”
CAIR Texas officials pointed out that Republican candidates leaned heavily into fabricated fears about Muslims taking over Texas and enforcing sharia law.
“We had to send a strong message,” said Shaimaa Zayan, Austin director for CAIR Texas. “If we allow them to say all of that and stay home that would be a green light for them to continue harassing our community.”
CAIR Texas says the organization scaled up its engagement around the elections this year by showing up weekly to dozens of mosques in Houston, Austin, and Dallas, from August until early October, during Friday prayers, to encourage voter registration.
CAIR Action, the group’s political wing, reported historic turnout for Texas Muslims voting early in a general election—marking a 78.6 percent increase since 2018.
State-Level Bigotry
Republican candidates’ anti-Muslim rhetoric came alongside the state education board approving an anti-Islamic rewrite of Texas social studies lessons and exclusions on a voucher program for K-12 Islamic schools.
Islamophobia has also led to violence against Texas’s Muslim population in recent years. In 2024, the Justice Department sentenced a Dallas man to 37 years in prison after he killed one person and tried to kill four others during a mass shooting at a Muslim-owned business; the FBI said he intentionally targeted Muslims.
While designating terrorist organizations is normally a power reserved for the federal government, Texas and Florida have taken unprecedented actions to allow state officials to apply those labels.
CAIR and its Florida chapter suspended operations in Florida earlier this month after Gov. Ron DeSantis and four state officials designated the groups as domestic terror organizations under a new, unprecedented administrative process approved by the legislature this summer.
The American Civil Liberties Union and CAIR sued DeSantis, alleging free speech and due process violations. The civil rights groups also argued that the debilitating penalties associated with the designations effectively force targeted groups to shut down.
On Monday, DeSantis commented on X about news of Hinojosa’s promised reversal and said, “This would be a huge contrast with Florida, where CAIR has disbanded.”
“Elections have consequences,” said Shirin Sinnar, a law professor at Stanford University.
She pointed out that the different outcomes in Florida and Texas “show the power of electoral consequences on the same issue.”
“A Loaded Gun”
Sinnar cautioned that the federal government may have plans of its own to crack down on nonprofits.
The Wall Street Journal reported on November 6 that the Trump administration is considering an executive order that would list some nonprofits as being tied to terrorists, effectively shutting down their operations.
Sinnar said that while Texas may be backing off from the executive order and lawsuit against CAIR, there’s more work to be done at the state level.
“It’s a good moment for civil rights advocates and communities to push the legislature to repeal the laws that enabled these designations,” she said. “Otherwise, they’re a loaded gun available to be used in the future against CAIR or another disfavored target.”
Those laws include measures that created the category of Texas foreign terrorist organizations and authorized state and local officials, as well as private residents, the ability to bring civil suits against them without having to prove any personal injury.
Youssef Chouhoud, a research scientist for the Texas-based nonprofit Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research, which focuses on issues related to Muslims, said Republicans in the state will likely continue engaging in Islamophobic rhetoric and policies. Attacking the Muslim community was “very much a winning strategy” in the Republican primaries, he said.
Though 95 percent of Republican primary voters said they supported a ballot proposition asking if “Texas should prohibit sharia law,” critics pointed out that the state’s anti-Muslim hysteria has led to an overblown focus on Muslim religious law.
Ghani, in Houston, had left a corporate job for more meaningful work and joined CAIR only about two months before Abbott’s terror designation. He took solace in his five daily prayers and hoped the past would become precedent.
“History has shown this is the path of many civil rights groups,” Ghani said of the persecution — and perseverance — of other civil rights groups like the NAACP in the 1950s and 60s, and the ACLU itself during the McCarthy era.
“It’s a badge of honor,” Ghani said, “to be targeted by extremists in the government.”
IT’S EVEN WORSE THAN WE THOUGHT.
What we’re seeing right now from Donald Trump is a full-on authoritarian takeover of the U.S. government.
This is not hyperbole.
Court orders are being ignored. MAGA loyalists have been put in charge of the military and federal law enforcement agencies. The Department of Government Efficiency has stripped Congress of its power of the purse. News outlets that challenge Trump have been banished or put under investigation.
Yet far too many are still covering Trump’s assault on democracy like politics as usual, with flattering headlines describing Trump as “unconventional,” “testing the boundaries,” and “aggressively flexing power.”
The Intercept has long covered authoritarian governments, billionaire oligarchs, and backsliding democracies around the world. We understand the challenge we face in Trump and the vital importance of press freedom in defending democracy.
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?
IT’S BEEN A DEVASTATING year for journalism — the worst in modern U.S. history.
We have a president with utter contempt for truth aggressively using the government’s full powers to dismantle the free press. Corporate news outlets have cowered, becoming accessories in Trump’s project to create a post-truth America. Right-wing billionaires have pounced, buying up media organizations and rebuilding the information environment to their liking.
In this most perilous moment for democracy, The Intercept is fighting back. But to do so effectively, we need to grow.
That’s where you come in. Will you help us expand our reporting capacity in time to hit the ground running in 2026?
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?
