https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.title: Straßenbahn im Berliner Norden | Pankow soll eine neue Straßen­bahn­strecke bekommen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.author: Nicolas Šustr
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.text:
- Berlin
- Straßenbahn im Berliner Norden
Pankow soll eine neue Straßenbahnstrecke bekommen
Für die Erschließung des Neubaugebiets »Alte Schäferei« ist ein Abzweig von der Linie 50 geplant. Nun wurden die Pläne der Bevölkerung vorgestellt.
Derzeit liegt der nördlichste Punkt des Berliner Straßenbahnnetzes an jener Stelle, wo die Linie 50 an der Kirche in Französisch Buchholz nach Westen abknickt. Untersucht wird nun jedoch der Neubau einer Strecke, der die Tram ein ganzes Stück weiter in den Berliner Norden bringen würde.
»Straßenbahnneubauvorhaben im Buchholzer Norden« nennt die Senatsmobilitätsverwaltung das Projekt, das bei einem Infomarkt am Mittwochabend in den Räumen der freikirchlichen Gemeinde »Treffpunkt Familienkirche« in Französisch Buchholz vorgestellt wird. Je nach Variante rund zwei bis etwas über vier Kilometer lang wäre die neue Strecke, die im Bereich der Kirche in Französisch Buchholz von der Linie 50 abzweigen würde. Hauptzweck wäre die Erschließung des geplanten neuen Wohngebiets »Alte Schäferei«.
Bis zu 2500 Wohnungen will die landeseigene Gewobag in Zusammenarbeit mit dem privaten Projektentwickler Treucon bis 2035 auf derzeit landwirtschaftlich genutzten Flächen bauen. Weitere rund 2000 Wohnungen sollen bis voraussichtlich 2040 in mehreren kleineren Projekten östlich der Schönerlinder Straße entstehen. Dereinst könnten hier zusammengenommen 9000 Menschen leben.
Doch die Straßenbahn könnte noch weiter nach Norden führen – entweder bis zum geplanten neuen S-Bahnhof Schönerlinder Straße, wo derzeit die Züge der S8 durchrauschen, oder in der Maximalvariante noch darüber hinaus, um das geplante Gewerbegebiet Buchholz Nord zu erschließen. Der Senat hat diese Flächen auch für die Ausrichtung einer möglichen Weltausstellung Expo 2035 ins Auge gefasst.
Bereits vor Beginn der Veranstaltung um 18 Uhr ist der Raum gut gefüllt. Dutzende Anwohnerinnen und Anwohner studieren die Plandarstellungen mit teils verwirrend vielen bunten Linien und diskutieren mit den zahlreichen Beschäftigten des Planungsbüros über das Projekt.
Mélanie Jachtner von der Senatsverkehrsverwaltung weist in ihrer kurzen Begrüßung auf die sehr frühe Phase hin, in der sich das Projekt befindet. »Das sind die ersten Infos für uns, sind Überlegungen, sind Anregungen, sind Ideen, aber auch Fragen, die wir Ihnen beantworten können, wo wir Sie vielleicht abholen können. Es ist aber noch kein förmlich-rechtliches Verfahren«, unterstreicht sie.
Abgeschlossen ist derzeit nur die Bewertung des geeignetsten Verkehrsmittels – die Tram hat sich hier in der Reihenfolge vor einer möglichen U-Bahn, dem Bus, einer Seilbahn und der S-Bahn durchgesetzt. Außerdem wurden die ungünstigsten Trassenoptionen für eine Straßenbahn aussortiert.
Für die Maximalvariante bis ins Gewerbegebiet sind so insgesamt vier Optionen übrig geblieben. Entweder würde die Strecke an der Hauptstraße oder an der Triftstraße von der Linie 50 abzweigen, schließlich der Schönerlinder Straße folgen, dann entweder einen Schlenker durch das neue Stadtquartier »Alte Schäferei« machen oder direkt weiter der Schönerlinder Straße folgen. Nach der Kreuzung der Eisenbahnstrecke würde die Linie im Gewerbegebiet Richtung Osten abknicken und entweder an einer Wendeschleife enden oder das Gebiet großflächiger mit einer Blockumfahrung erschließen.
Abgeschlossen werden sollen die Untersuchungen bis Ende 2027. Dann soll eine Vorzugstrasse festgelegt und auch die Wirtschaftlichkeit untersucht sein. Tatsächlich könnte es passieren, dass sich das Projekt als unwirtschaftlich erweist und nicht weiterverfolgt wird. Sollte eine Realisierung empfohlen werden, könnten die ersten Straßenbahnen im Jahr 2035 rollen.
Anwohnerinnen und Anwohner sorgen sich beispielsweise um die Bausubstanz der Kirche; sie wollen wissen, was mit den Gebeinen auf dem Kirchhof geschieht, sollte die Trasse dort entlangführen. Auch wird die Triftstraße von manchen als zu schmal für eine Tram angesehen. Die CDU-Abgeordneten Johannes Kraft und Lars Bocian sind anwesend. Beide waren in der vergangenen Legislaturperiode im Mobilitätsausschuss des Parlaments aktiv.
»Ich finde es gut, dass es eine so frühzeitige Beteiligung für die geplante Straßenbahn gibt«, sagt Lars Bocian zu »nd«. Allerdings sei die geplante Bebauung der Alten Schäferei und auch des nahe gelegenen Stadtquartiers Elisabeth-Aue zu massiv und dauere deswegen sehr lange. »Wir brauchen schnell Wohnungen, ortsüblich und ortsverträglich«, meint Bocian. »Zu den rund 22.000 Bewohnern von Buchholz würden bei bisheriger Planung rund 15.000 oder mehr hinzukommen«, rechnet er vor. »Das würde den historisch gewachsenen Charakter des Ortsteils am Stadtrand massiv verändern.« Er halte es für legitim, wenn die Bewohner sich gegen 17 oder 40 Geschosse am Stadtrand aussprechen.
Bocian artikuliert damit durchaus die Haltung, die bei vielen Besucherinnen und Besuchern des Infomarktes zu spüren ist. Kritisiert werden eher die Wohnungsbaupläne als das Straßenbahn-Vorhaben. Der ebenfalls anwesende Stadtplanungsexperte Matthias Grünzig lobt hingegen gegenüber »nd« sowohl die Entwürfe für die Elisabeth-Aue als auch für die Alte Gärtnerei als gelungen und zukunftsweisend. Auch die Erschließung beider Quartiere mit der Straßenbahn ist für ihn der richtige Ansatz.
Lars Bocian fordert, ganz dem CDU-Mantra folgend, den Bau einer U-Bahn für so große Neubaugebiete, um den entstehenden Bedarf zu decken. »Die Straßenbahnlinie 50 ist jetzt schon überlastet, und nur eine Verlängerung der Strecke beseitigt nicht das Problem der ungenügenden ÖPNV-Anbindung«, glaubt er.
Tatsächlich ist die Linie teilweise sehr gut ausgelastet. Allerdings ließe sich der derzeitige Zehn-Minuten-Takt recht problemlos auf eine Bahn alle fünf Minuten verdoppeln, wie es im bisherigen Nahverkehrsplan auch vorgesehen war. Eine weitere Option könnte sein, die Verlängerung der Linie M2 in den Blankenburger Süden, wie ursprünglich vorgesehen, bis zum S-Bahnhof Blankenburg zu führen und weiter über die Blankenburger Bahnhofstraße an die Trasse der Linie 50 anzuschließen. Die M2 könnte dann die Bedienung des Astes in den Buchholzer Norden übernehmen.
Denn tatsächlich dürfte die geplante Verlängerung der Linie 50 in die Elisabeth-Aue die Fahrgastzahlen weiter steigen lassen. Allerdings soll zusätzlich auch die Tram M1 dorthin führen. Weil sie die schnellere Verbindung Richtung Pankower Zentrum böte, würde sie vermutlich die Hauptlast der Passagiere tragen.
Die frühzeitige Bürgerbeteiligung läuft noch bis 9. Dezember auf dem Beteiligungsportal mein.berlin.de. Dieser Link führt auf die Projektseite.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
Power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of heavy wind, rain and snow.
Heavy rain and flooding have begun to ease along the US East Coast as power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of holiday storms.
The storms disrupted travel and downed trees and power lines, leading to water rescues in multiple states, from New York to Virginia.
In New York City, preparations were under way for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.
The parade, an annual spectacle usually held on Thanksgiving Day, sees brightly coloured balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan. The festivities also kick off the holiday shopping season for the US.
The same balloons and floats, and most of the original celebrities, are still set to take part, organisers said.
Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.
While conditions are expected to improve across the entire eastern US, the National Weather Service warned that “this huge system will take some time to weaken”.
The low-pressure system that brought the storm to the East Coast, the service added, would continue to slowly exit to the northeast, “bringing lingering showers and isolated freezing precipitation through Saturday”.
Coastal flood warnings were also issued in several states from New Jersey to Virginia.
Power restored, travel disruptions ease
The number of power outages, which peaked on Thursday at more than 900,000, fell to 264,000 by Friday evening as crews worked to restore electricity, according to poweroutage.us.
Pennsylvania had the most, followed by Missouri.
Some flight disruptions also lingered on Friday, with about 1,600 delays and more than 500 cancellations, according to the tracking service FlightAware.
In the southern US, part of Tennessee was under a winter storm warning for up to 2.5cm (one inch) of snow on Friday, after rain turned into light snow on Thanksgiving.
In the Midwest, conditions were calmer than they were the previous day, when as much as 38cm (15 inches) of snow fell in eastern Missouri.
The weather service said heavy snow was still expected in parts of Montana and Wyoming, however.
Along the Pacific coast, waves driven by high tides caused flooding and continued to affect train services. Record tides along the California coast prompted evacuations from Humboldt County in the far north to Ventura County near Los Angeles.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.title: Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.author: Hilal Saki
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has rejected a new request from military chief of staff Eyal Zamir to authorise administrative detention orders against Israeli settlers involved in attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, Kan reported.
Zamir told Katz at a security consultation on Thursday that further steps were needed amid rising settler violence, and called for administrative detention and restraining orders against perpetrators, the report said.
Administrative detention allows suspects to be held indefinitely without charge or trial. It is widely used against Palestinians, including children, but Katz halted its use against Jewish Israelis in November 2024. He has, in fact, repeatedly boasted of doing so, while expanding its use against Palestinians.
Dozens of restraining orders, which bar individuals from parts of the West Bank, are awaiting Shin Bet approval, according to Kan. Channel 12 reported that 70 people suspected of involvement in such attacks were arrested in recent weeks, but Israeli courts released all of them without indictments.
Shin Bet chief David Zini, who belongs to the Orthodox nationalist Hardal camp, has consistently objected to movement bans. He has been accused of undermining the agency's unit tasked with tackling settler violence.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Despejo de idosos, aluguel e imigração: o que move eleição deste domingo na Espanha
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Larissa Bohrer
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Maricarmen tinha 87 anos e morava há décadas no mesmo apartamento em Madri quando foi despejada, em setembro. “Ofereceram pagar o aluguel por ela e a empresa não aceitou. Então nunca foi sobre dinheiro, realmente”, conta a comunicadora digital Camila Alvarenga, que vive na capital espanhola. Em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, ela afirmou que o caso ajuda a explicar a eleição deste domingo (29).
O despejo levou milhares de pessoas às ruas e centenas de manifestantes acamparam na Puerta del Sol ao fim da marcha pela moradia, para exigir a aprovação do chamado ‘decreto Maricarmen’. “Era uma forma de dizer: até aqui, basta já”, resume Alvarenga. Para ela, o tema chega às urnas como um dos principais fatores na decisão do voto.
O possível resultado segue em aberto. PP e PSOE aparecem separados por menos de um ponto percentual, mas o bloco com a extrema direita projeta conquistar 187 cadeiras, conseguindo maioria absoluta no Parlamento. Como os espanhóis votam em listas de deputados e não diretamente no chefe de governo, Pedro Sánchez, do PSOE, só fica no cargo “se conseguir formar governo com alguma outra sigla de esquerda”, explica a comunicadora.
Essa possibilidade ganhou fôlego no último debate, que reuniu Sánchez, Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP), Santiago Abascal (Vox) e Ada Colau (Frente Amplio). Segundo Alvarenga, Sánchez e Colau “souberam atuar como aliados” contra Abascal, enquanto Feijóo fugiu das perguntas importantes. “Eu acho que isso é uma boa notícia para a esquerda.”
Do outro lado há um possível cenário inédito: a chegada do Vox ao governo nacional. Para a comunicadora, isso põe em risco direitos recentes. O partido “já disse abertamente” que quer devolver imigrantes aos países de origem e rejeita as medidas de proteção às mulheres, por enxergar nelas “um tipo de perseguição contra os homens”.
“As coisas que a gente foi conquistando ao longo dos últimos anos estão em risco”, alerta. Segundo ela, isso vale também para a população LGBT.
A aproximação com o Vox também mudou o PP. “Durante muito tempo o PP não quis formar governo com o Vox. Agora eles já estão abertos a essa possibilidade e, para isso, tiveram que ir mais para a direita”, afirma Alvarenga.
A imigração é justamente onde a disputa fica mais acirrada. Em abril, o governo espanhol aprovou uma regularização extraordinária para conceder autorizações de residência e trabalho a cerca de meio milhão de migrantes em situação irregular. Alvarenga considera a medida uma conquista, mas diz que ela “não foi vista assim por uma camada importante da população”.
“A gente está tendo uma geração de pessoas muito jovens indo para a direita, que relacionam a chegada dos imigrantes com a violência no país, sendo que não tem a ver”, destaca.
Por trás desse discurso, segundo ela, está o mesmo medo que levou multidões à Puerta del Sol. “Apesar da economia estar crescendo, os dados de emprego estarem melhorando, existe essa sensação de insegurança: ‘beleza, estou ganhando mais, mas a qualquer momento uma empresa gigante compra meu prédio e eu não vou poder pagar o meu aluguel’. Esse medo atravessa a sociedade espanhola”, afirma.
É nesse ambiente que Alvarenga vê peso na passagem de Lula, que se reuniu com Sánchez no Palácio da Moncloa, em Madri, no dia 16 de novembro. “A imagem do Sánchez está muito desgastada, infelizmente”, reconhece. Ela acredita que um apoio com a credibilidade de Lula pode mobilizar eleitores de esquerda, que pensavam em não votar por não se sentirem representados por um socialista de centro-esquerda.
“Ver Lula falar ‘eu apoio’ talvez seja uma motivação de votar agora”, conclui.
Para assistir e ouvir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Men dominate this Japanese game. One woman broke a 100-year-old barrier to rise to the top
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Encouragement was in short supply when, in the 1960s, Akiko Takojima set her sights on becoming an elite shogi player. Women were too “stupid” to excel at the Japanese board game, a male instructor told her, before suggesting she find something else to occupy her time.
Decades after Takojima and five others became the first female professionals, a 100-year-old barrier in the game is about to be broken. From April, Tomoka Nishiyama will turn shogi’s gender bias on its head when she becomes the first woman to compete against men at the highest level of the game.
“Senior women players have always been kind to me,” Nishiyama, 31, told reporters after announcing she would become a kishi, a gender-neutral classification that, nonetheless, has featured only male players since the Japan Shogi Association was formed in 1924. “They have also taught me about the difficulties of being a woman in shogi.”
A Yomiuri Shimbun editorial hailed her promotion as “a new era” in the world of shogi, but with the exception of Nishiyama, women are still marginalised in professional shogi and among the ranks of amateurs.
“Even today, there are far fewer girls playing than boys,” says Saori Shimai, a professional shogi player in the women’s game, who began learning shogi at the age of six after watching her grandfather play.
“When I was learning shogi there were hardly any girls playing at all,” says Shimai, who is also executive director of the Ladies professional shogi players’ association of Japan.
Often referred to as Japanese chess, shogi is thought to have originated in India before spreading to China and other parts of Asia. Playing on a rectangular board comprising 81 grids, each player manoeuvres their 20 pentagonal pieces as they aim to checkmate their opponent’s king and win the game.
About 5 million Japanese play regularly, according to a 2025 government white paper, but only about 20% are women.
When the shogi association relaxed the promotion criteria last year to allow women to become kishi based solely on their results in all-female tournaments, several male professionals raised objections, while Nishiyama was subjected to abuse on social media. Some attempted to dismiss her advancement as “affirmative action”, prompting the shogi association to intervene in her defence.
The notion that male players are naturally superior persists, right down to commentary arrangements, in which the resident expert is invariably male. Last year, the Japan shogi association prohibited pregnant players from playing in title matches for 14 weeks around their expected due dates but was quickly forced to scrap the rule.
“There need to be other big changes to how shogi is organised so that they reflect how women live their lives,” says Karolina Fortin, the first foreign player to turn professional, who fell in love with the game as a puzzle-obsessed child. “Long overdue things, like maternity leave and childcare.”
Fortin says she was delighted, but “anxious”, about Nishiyama’s achievement. “There’s no doubt that she’s made history … But the road ahead will be difficult. She will be surrounded by male players so will need to keep proving herself.”
The introduction of women’s professional shogi in 1974 was a reminder of how far the game has come. “The boys I had played against as an apprentice had agreed that if they lost to me they would have to pay a fine or shave their heads,” Takojima said in a 2019 interview with Shukan Bunshun magazine, referring to a traditional display of contrition in Japanese culture.
The upper echelons of the elite game have long struggled to reflect growing interest among women. As of October, there were 174 active players with the kishi rank, all of them men. That will change when Nishiyama takes up her new status next year. The number of female professionals, who compete against each other, has risen from the original six to more than 80, but they are still outnumbered by men.
Shimai, who turned professional when she was 15, says she had always believed it was “only a matter of time” before a woman started competing in the same professional category as men.
“The number of female professionals has increased, and the standard of play has dramatically improved,” she says. “Attitudes are gradually changing. Women were often assumed to be weaker players, but the perception gap is narrowing. But we want to do more to create an environment in which women can enjoy shogi.”
Itsuko Hayashi, a shogi instructor, believes those involved in the game are beginning to accept players on merit, irrespective of their gender. “I think the shogi world respects strength,” says Hayashi, a member of the women’s association, which arranges events to promote the game among women and girls. “Male players have no problem recognising shogi ability among women.”
As she prepares to make shogi history next spring by competing against men in title matches, Nishiyama says she has been inspired by a desire to take on stronger opponents, and by the women who had come before her.
“I recognise that I’m someone who can help create a new milestone in the history [of shogi]. I’m very aware that the history built up by those players is what allowed me to get to where I am today.”

https://taz.de/Aktion-im-Bundestag/!6233.title: Aktion im Bundestag: Was will die Linke sein?
https://taz.de/Aktion-im-Bundestag/!6233.author: Kersten Augustin
https://taz.de/Aktion-im-Bundestag/!6233.text:
Aktion im Bundestag : Was will die Linke sein?
Linke Abgeordnete stören eine Veranstaltung eines grünen Parlamentskollegen. Das bricht ein Tabu – und zerstört das Vertrauen in Rot-Grün-Rot.
G erade erst hat die Linke in Berlin beschlossen, Vanessa Emde aus ihrer Fraktion auszuschließen – und damit endlich den Weg freigemacht für ein rot-grün-rotes Bündnis in der Hauptstadt. Wer aber dachte, dass die internen Probleme der Partei damit erledigt seien, wurde am Mittwoch im Bundestag eines Besseren belehrt. Dort trafen sich sechs AktivistInnen, die in ihrem Nebenberuf als Bundestagsabgeordnete bisher kaum in Erscheinung getreten sind, um eine Veranstaltung im Parlament zu stören.
Eingeladen war David Barnea, der ehemalige Chef des israelischen Geheimdienst Mossad, die Schirmherrschaft der Veranstaltung hatte der Grüne Konstantin von Notz. Doch bevor es losgehen konnte, blockierten einige der sechs Abgeordneten zeitweise die Eingänge zu dem Raum. Später störte ein weiterer Aktivist den Ablauf der Veranstaltung. Wie er in den Bundestag kam, ist unklar. Es liegt aber nahe, dass er von den linken Abgeordneten eingeladen wurde. Eine Anfrage der taz dazu blieb unbeantwortet. Die beteiligten Abgeordneten nannten die Aktion im Nachhinein „legitim“.
David Barnea ist verantwortlich für den Pagerangriff auf die Hisbollah im Libanon, bei dem auch ZivilistInnen schwer verletzt wurden. Er ist mutmaßlich an israelischen Kriegsverbrechen beteiligt. Einen Haftbefehl oder eine Anklage gegen ihn gibt es bisher nicht. Von Notz wurde auch aus der eigenen Partei für die Einladung kritisiert. Diese Kritik ist legitim. Ein parlamentarisches Frühstück ist womöglich der falsche Rahmen für die Einladung eines derart umstrittenen Mannes.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Aber das rechtfertigt nicht die Wahl der Mittel. Es sollte ein absolutes Tabu für demokratische Abgeordnete sein, die Veranstaltung anderer demokratischer Abgeordneter im Bundestag zu stören und zu blockieren.
Der Bundestag als Ort der parlamentarischen Demokratie steht zu Recht unter einem besonderen Schutz. Blockaden wie die der linken Abgeordneten dürfen auf keinen Fall Schule machen. Was passiert, wenn Abgeordnete anderer Parteien anfangen, Veranstaltungen der Linken zu stören und zu blockieren? Treffen sich dann Abgeordnete zur Saalschlacht?
Politische Konflikte sollten im Parlament nicht durch Stören und Blockieren ausgetragen werden; Abgeordnete dürfen andere nicht an ihrer Arbeit hindern. Es ist deshalb richtig, dass Bundestagspräsidentin Julia Klöckner die Beteiligten der Linken nun sanktionieren will.
Zudem beschädigen solche Aktionen das Vertrauen zwischen linken und anderen demokratischen Abgeordneten. Wenn der Aufstieg der Rechtsextremen gestoppt werden soll, braucht es auch auf Bundesebene eine glaubhafte politische Alternative. Wenn Linke aber lieber die Grünen an ihrer Arbeit hindern, statt nach Möglichkeiten der Zusammenarbeit zu suchen, wird das nichts mit Rot-Grün-Rot.
Die Störaktion im Bundestag zeigt: Vanessa Emde ist nicht allein. Es gibt einige in der Partei, die lieber kompromisslose Aktivisten sein wollen als eine linke parlamentarische Kraft. Die Partei muss sich entscheiden, was sie sein will.

https://www.humanite.fr/sports/rugby/rug.title: Rugby : six matchs en trois jours, la pelouse de Twickenham sous le labourage intensif du Championnat des nations
https://www.humanite.fr/sports/rugby/rug.author: Éric Serres
https://www.humanite.fr/sports/rugby/rug.text:
Six matchs en trois jours pour les finales du Championnat des Nations à Twickenham, c’est du jamais-vu. Devant ce défi, le gazon de l’antre du rugby anglais a été chouchouté comme jamais.
À 17 h 40, ce vendredi 27 novembre, les finales du Championnat des nations débutent par le match Italie-Fidji. Ce grand raout rugbystique permettra aux supporters, fans de ballon ovale, de suivre six matchs en à peine plus de 72 heures. Six rencontres sur trois jours, et donc des dizaines de mêlées, de rucks, de touches, de cadrages débordements, de placages, de rush défenses…
La situation est inédite dans ce sport où aucun stade n’a jamais accueilli sur un laps de temps aussi court autant...

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.title: Wassermangel | Brandenburg kann von Afrika lernen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.author: Andreas Fritsche
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120418.text:
- Berlin
- Wassermangel
Brandenburg kann von Afrika lernen
Die heimische Landwirtschaft muss sich auf Wassermangel einstellen. In Simbabwe hat sie das bereits getan.
»Es startet alles mit der richtigen Einstellung«, sagt Kudzaiische Ndawana. Sie ist in ihrer Heimat Simbabwe Direktorin der christlichen Entwicklungs- und Hilfsorganisation Medra. Nach Brandenburg gekommen ist sie als Gast der evangelischen Spendenaktion »Brot für die Welt«.
In Rambanepasi, einem Dorf in einer heißen und trockenen Gegend, mussten die Frauen früher zwei Kilometer zu Fuß laufen, um Wasser aus einem Fluss herbeizuschaffen, oder endlos an einem Brunnen anstehen, der von Hand betrieben wurde. Doch Medra hat dafür gesorgt, dass es in Rambanepasi und in fünf umliegenden Dörfern nun mit Solarstrom betriebene Brunnen gibt. In Rambanepasi wurde außerdem ein Gemeinschaftsgarten angelegt. Hier erlernen Dorfbewohner klimafreundliche Anbaumethoden. Das Projekt dient auch dem friedlichen Zusammenleben. Wegen der besseren Lebensbedingungen gibt es weniger häusliche Gewalt.
Kudzaiische Ndawana spricht beim Besuch in Potsdam von der Aufgabe, Ressourcen zu teilen, Frieden zu finden und Vorbilder zu schaffen. Dazu sagt sie diesen Satz: »Es startet alles mit der richtigen Einstellung.« Seit 2004 ist Medra aktiv, seit 2009 offiziell als Hilfsorganisation anerkannt.
Der Landtagsabgeordnete Johannes Funke (SPD) war schon einmal in Simbabwe, auch wenn es lange her ist. Er freut sich, Ndawana im Parlament zu treffen. Warum gibt es Hunger in der Welt ausgerechnet vor allem in ländlichen Regionen, wundert sich der Politiker – weiß aber, dass es an Kriegen und Korruption liegt, am Wassermangel und an der Eigentumsfrage. Was nützt es Bauern, wenn sie Felder bestellen könnten, aber keine besitzen und auch nicht pachten dürfen?
Funke warnt vor dem Irrglauben, dass Brandenburg auf immer von Hunger verschont bleiben muss. Kriege anderswo in der Welt haben schon Auswirkungen auf die Versorgung in Deutschland. Die Energiepreise machen den Landwirten zu schaffen. »Ein rentabler Ackerbau ist in Brandenburg im Jahr 2027 nicht möglich, wenn die Rahmenbedingungen bleiben, wie sie im Moment sind«, sagt Funke.
Auch die zunehmende Hitze spielt für den Abgeordneten eine Rolle. »Die letzten 50 Jahre ist es bei uns 1,5 Grad wärmer geworden, und wenn der Klimawandel so weitergeht, müssen wir damit rechnen, dass in den nächsten 50 Jahren noch einmal 1,5 Grad dazukommen«, sagt Funke. »Die Fakten sprechen dafür.«
Brandenburgs Bauern müssen lernen, damit klarzukommen. Deshalb sei der Austausch mit Südeuropa wichtig, mit Spanien, Italien und Griechenland, die schon immer mit anderen klimatischen Bedingungen leben, als Brandenburg sie bisher kannte. Aber auch von Afrika könne Brandenburg lernen, insbesondere was Strategien zur Bewässerung betreffe. Brandenburgs Landwirte werden ihren Acker in Zukunft mehr bewässern müssen, ist Funke überzeugt. Aber der Wassermangel werde zunehmen. Behandeltes Abwasser in die Flüsse abzuleiten, die in die Ostsee oder in die Nordsee münden, das werde man sich künftig wohl nicht mehr leisten können.
Aufbereitetes Abwasser auf die Felder zu leiten und Wasserspeicher zu bauen – auch das beginnt vielleicht mit der richtigen Einstellung.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.

Yemeni forces claim 121 Houthi fighters killed in 726 attacks
28 November 2026 02:26 GMT
Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili, spokesman for Yemen’s government forces, claimed as many as 726 attacks had been carried against Houthi positions over the past 24 hours.
Al-Nuzaili said the operations, conducted as part of the “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, included 23 air strikes, 642 artillery attacks, 35 drone operations and 26 rocket strikes. They resulted in the killing or wounding 121 fighters and commanders, according to the state-run Saba news agency.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Da pilhagem à prosperidade compartilhada? Brics+, África e a luta contra as trocas desiguais
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Clube Valdai
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Já se passaram vinte anos desde que os ministros das Relações Exteriores do Brasil, da Rússia, da Índia e da China discutiram pela primeira vez trabalhar em conjunto, à margem da 61ª Sessão Ordinária da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova York, em 2006, e cerca de 17 anos desde que a primeira Cúpula do Bric foi realizada na Rússia, em 2009. As duas últimas décadas assistiram a mudanças significativas na divisão internacional do trabalho e nas relações geopolíticas que sustentam os sistemas-mundo, escreve abaixo Rasigan Maharajh, especialmente para a 4ª conferência africana do Clube de Discussão Valdai [realizada no Cairo, novembro de 2026].
Embora a atual encarnação dos Brics+ ainda não ocupe o centro do palco das relações internacionais, a simples existência dessa associação voluntária serviu como importante força de contrapeso à hegemonia do Ocidente combinado depois da Segunda Guerra Mundial e, mais particularmente, desde o fim da primeira Guerra Fria, com a dissolução da União das Repúblicas Socialistas Soviéticas ao final de 1991. A importância crescente dos Brics+ encontra eco no reconhecimento feito pelo Council on Foreign Relations dos Estados Unidos, cuja missão declarada é “informar o engajamento dos Estados Unidos com o mundo” e que sustentou que “o grupo Brics se tornou uma grande força política nas duas últimas décadas, a partir de seu desejo de criar um contrapeso à influência ocidental nas instituições globais”.
Tal reconhecimento por parte do líder do Ocidente combinado, no entanto, é pouco em comparação com o interesse demonstrado pelos países da maioria mundial (o Sul global e o não-Ocidente global) em trabalhar com os Brics+ e até em aderir a eles. Segundo a presidência do ciclo de cúpulas de 2026, os Brics+ reúnem atualmente 11 países membros plenos e 10 países parceiros. Em reportagem, Geeta Mohan sugeriu que “há uma fila de mais de 30 nações ainda tentando entrar — com mais de 50 manifestando interesse no total”.
A África do Sul foi o primeiro país africano a integrar os Brics+, em 2010, seguida pelo Egito e pela Etiópia, que ingressaram em 2024. A Nigéria e a Uganda se tornaram países parceiros em 2025, e o governo de Gana decidiu apresentar pedido formal de adesão em 6 de outubro de 2026.
Com base nas projeções demográficas de meados de 2026 das Nações Unidas, os cinco países africanos hoje associados aos Brics+ abrigam cerca de 412,9 milhões de pessoas, pouco mais de um quarto da população total do continente, de 1,59 bilhão. Essa envergadura quantitativa, porém, encobre discrepâncias qualitativas significativas na qualidade de vida experimentada no continente. Cada um dos países africanos associados aos Brics+ conquistou a libertação nacional da captura colonial e da subjugação imperial em momentos muito distintos, com exceção da Etiópia, que nunca foi colonizada.
O Egito obteve independência nominal em 1922; Gana, em 1957; a Nigéria, em 1960; e Uganda, em 1962, enquanto a África do Sul só realizou suas primeiras eleições nacionais com sufrágio pleno em 1994. Cada um dos seis territórios lançou-se a iniciativas de desenvolvimento variadas, e alguns chegaram a experimentar caminhos não capitalistas. O resultado líquido é que a renda per capita varia consideravelmente, enquanto as desigualdades continuam a afetar a distribuição efetiva.
O Fundo Monetário Internacional publicou estimativas de renda per capita a preços correntes para a Etiópia (1.130 dólares), o Egito (4.020 dólares), Gana (3.600 dólares), a Nigéria (1.590 dólares), Uganda (1.450 dólares) e a África do Sul (7.660 dólares). O Banco Mundial mediu a desigualdade de renda nesses países pelo índice de Gini: a Etiópia marcou 0,311 (2021); o Egito ficou em 0,285 (2021); Gana está em 0,435 (2016); a Nigéria, em 0,339 (2022); e Uganda, em 0,382 (2023). A África do Sul segue sendo o país mais desigual do mundo, com 0,541 em 2022.
Segundo a Organização Mundial da Saúde, a Etiópia tem expectativa de vida ao nascer de 68,7 anos e expectativa de vida saudável ao nascer de 59,6 anos; o Egito tem expectativa de vida ao nascer de 71,9 anos e expectativa de vida saudável ao nascer de 61,6 anos; Gana tem expectativa de vida ao nascer de 67,7 anos e expectativa de vida saudável de 58,7 anos; Uganda tem expectativa de vida de 66,0 anos e expectativa de vida saudável de 57,2 anos; a Nigéria tem expectativa de vida ao nascer de 62,9 anos e expectativa de vida saudável de 54,1 anos; já os sul-africanos podem esperar viver 66,0 anos, com expectativa de vida saudável de 56,2. A expectativa de vida saudável (Hale) ao nascer é um indicador que a OMS usa para medir “quantos anos uma pessoa pode esperar viver em plena saúde”.
Como observa o recente pedido de adesão de Gana aos Brics+, a associação é vista como oportunidade de “diversificar as parcerias internacionais do país e criar oportunidades adicionais de comércio, investimento e cooperação econômica”. Aspirações desse tipo valem para todos os associados africanos dos Brics+. A África do Sul, o Egito e a Etiópia, como membros, e tanto a Nigéria como Uganda, na condição de parceiros, de fato se valeram de sua posição nos Brics+ para ampliar suas relações econômicas e políticas com o resto do mundo. As oportunidades que foram e vêm sendo exploradas muitas vezes procuram responder a desafios definidos nacionalmente, ao mesmo tempo que se aventuram além de relações internacionais historicamente configuradas, que serviram com frequência para manter e assegurar a continuidade das trocas desiguais nos períodos pós-colonial e neocolonial.
Os países da África representam, em conjunto, o grosso do subdesenvolvimento; o continente abriga o maior número de países menos desenvolvidos (PMDs) e o núcleo das periferias nos sistemas-mundo. Ainda assim, e a despeito de uma economia política intransigente, a África transborda da população mais jovem do planeta e, segundo o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Meio Ambiente, “abriga cerca de 30% das reservas minerais do mundo, 8% do gás natural e 12% das reservas de petróleo do mundo. O continente tem 40% do ouro do mundo e até 90% de seu cromo e de sua platina. As maiores reservas de cobalto, diamantes, platina e urânio do mundo estão na África. Detém 65% das terras aráveis do mundo e 10% das fontes internas de água doce renovável do planeta”.
Séculos de expropriação, extração e exploração coloniais e imperialistas, no entanto, não se converteram efetivamente em ganhos de qualidade de vida para a maioria dos africanos. Os benefícios decorrentes do fluxo da riqueza biofísica da África foram, em larga medida, capturados por elites transnacionais e pelas elites compradoras locais*, de modo que a maioria do continente convive com desemprego, pobreza e desigualdade endêmicos. A dimensão africana dos Brics+ precisa, portanto, garantir que suas iniciativas se distingam explicitamente dos comportamentos pós e neocoloniais abomináveis que, no conjunto, serviram à pilhagem em vez de construir prosperidade compartilhada para todos.
A Rússia e todos os parceiros com histórico de solidariedade, cooperação e colaboração deveriam acionar seus potenciais progressistas e garantir que os aspectos negativos da África sejam corrigidos. Isso exige integridade e honestidade nos diversos contatos de povo a povo, de governo a governo e de Estado a Estado, com a multipolaridade incorporada como mecanismo central de salvaguarda. Embora tais aspectos da multipolaridade demandem atenção cuidadosa, eles deveriam constituir uma característica duradoura das iniciativas de desenvolvimento dos Brics+.
As contradições que caracterizam a economia política dos Estados Unidos informam também as posições políticas que o país professa e defende. A atitude do regime que ocupa a autoridade executiva dos Estados Unidos, porém, exala belicosidade na tentativa de manter a hegemonia. Com a base material de seu poder psicológico se erodindo e sua legitimidade se esvaindo, o racismo brutal e a arrogância passam ao primeiro plano. Os Estados membros e parceiros dos Brics+ têm muito a ganhar com a solidariedade que sua associação voluntária oferece e poderiam usar os potenciais positivos emergentes para realizar as aspirações nacionais de cada um sem que os outros perdessem.
Mais trabalho substantivo de pesquisa e de apoio a políticas entre os Estados membros e parceiros dos Brics+ deveria ser dedicado ao monitoramento do progresso — sobretudo diante da inflação real na extensão das declarações de cúpula — e deveria incluir tanto a avaliação dos resultados como o compartilhamento do aprendizado que deles decorre. Para assegurar a consolidação, pode fazer sentido conter o crescimento quantitativo e aumentar os avanços qualitativos que seriam sentidos pelas respectivas populações domésticas e, coletivamente, pelo agrupamento como um todo.
Os conflitos também exigem atenção, e a experiência mostrou que as soluções dirigidas às causas profundas dos problemas são as mais promissoras para entregar uma paz sustentável. O uso de redes por todo o continente, bem como entre todos os países dos Brics+, também ajuda a construir confiança e permite contestar de modo mais robusto as antigas potências coloniais e seus regimes neocoloniais de patrimonialismo.
A persistência do genocídio na Palestina, a guerra ilegal contra o Irã e os conflitos em curso na República Democrática do Congo e no Sudão compartilham muitos aspectos, características e protagonistas. A associação Brics+ não deveria permitir a normalização de tais crimes contra a humanidade, e é preciso fazer mais para interromper as atrocidades atuais e anular a possibilidade de novas erupções adiante.
Ter herdado muitos problemas sem necessariamente ter contribuído para a origem deles configura os Brics+ como potencial solucionador de problemas globais. Para cumprir à altura uma responsabilidade tão elevada, é preciso que Brics [em Nova Délhi, Índia] se organizou em torno do tema “Construir para a resiliência, a inovação, a cooperação e a sustentabilidade”.
*N.E.: No vocabulário da economia política, «comprador» designa o intermediário nativo que opera a serviço do capital estrangeiro — a camada que lucra com a intermediação, e não com a produção.
**As opiniões expressas são de responsabilidade individual dos membros e colaboradores, e não do Clube, salvo indicação explícita em contrário.
***Rasigan Maharajh é professor titular de Assuntos Públicos na Faculdade de Humanidades da Tshwane University of Technology, na África do Sul, e membro da Academia de Ciências da África do Sul.
****Este é um artigo de opinião e não necessariamente representa a linha editorial do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.title: Princess of Wales documentary Heal charts ‘pilgrimage’ after cancer treatment
https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.author: Caroline Davies
https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text:
On the day the Princess of Wales undertook the Three Peaks challenge, there was rain, hill fog and, finally, watery June sunshine.
It is hard to not see it as a meteorological metaphor for Catherine’s journey – from cancer diagnosis through treatment and to remission – as she treks first Ben Nevis, then Scafell Pike and Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) within 24 hours, the camera capturing her physical challenge for a new documentary.
Titled simply Heal and premiering on the BBC from Sunday, this is far from usual royal fare. – It is powerful emotional excavation as Catherine undertakes her “pilgrimage” to search for what life is, or can be, after cancer treatment, physically and spiritually.
“I think when you’re on your hospital bed and it is so clinical around you, you haven’t got fresh air, no greenery around you, it’s very stark and alien and stripped back,” she says.
“The darkness was a really scary, disorientating experience. I think I was sort of in and out of consciousness. It was a really dark time. But also, somewhere through that, too, I became aware of someone holding my hand.
“They weren’t talking to me. They weren’t trying to fix anything. They were just there. And the presence of someone that stood by me in that time, I’ll for ever be grateful for.”
Who that hand belonged to – doctor, nurse, husband – is left unsaid. But it is implied that she is speaking not just of the physical but also of a spiritual presence.
Catherine was diagnosed with an undisclosed type of cancer in March 2024, underwent chemotherapy, and announced she was in remission in January 2025.
But what then? “It’s very hard to go back to the person you were before,” she says in the 30-minute programme.
This challenge, through which she is raising money for the Royal Marsden hospital in London where she was treated, is her “then”.
The journey “is a chance to explore what life looks like, what healing looks like beyond diagnosis, beyond treatment,” she says. There is no end goal, it is simply “what comes along the way”.
It is her ringing of the bell, which patients customarily do when hospital treatment ends but which she “weirdly didn’t realise was a thing” and so never got to do.
The main voice throughout is hers. We see her walking alone and with her brother, James Middleton, occasionally chatting with other fundraising trekkers en route, or meeting people undergoing treatment in hospitals, at pub support groups and art therapy.
We see her talking directly to the camera, shot in closeup profile, gazing occasionally into the distance as she articulates the inner turmoil, describing how with cancer you “in a way lose yourself”. She is “having to learn again to live life fully”.
We see her smiling brightly, mostly, but also in tears. At the top of Scafell Pike, James whips out his phone and plays voice notes sent by Prince William and recorded by their children Prince George, 13, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight.
Louis’s little-boy enthusiasm serves as poignant reminder that throughout all this she is a mother of still young children, and of the ripple effect of the disease on loved ones.
“Hello, Mummy. I really love you and I hope you do well going up the mountain,” Louis says. “Remember, I’m always in your heart with you, and I love you very much. And I’ll be following behind your back with you, and I’ll always be with you. And remember, I love you really lots and lots, and I give you lots and lots of love.”
George says he is tracking her on Flightradar up the mountains “and you look really, really strong. Keep going and we’re right behind you.” Charlotte is “so proud of you doing your walk and your challenges”.
Catherine wipes away tears. “They gave me the reason to get out of hospital. They’re going to give me the reason to finish this challenge,” she says, placing a stone on a rock. “This is for the kiddies.”
Speaking at a private screening this week, Catherine said cancer “profoundly affects every aspect of life”. She added: “I know this personally and that the journey through and beyond treatment requires more than medicine alone.”
She set out on the challenge to explore life after diagnosis “as a solitary experience – in a way, as a pilgrimage. But what I quickly realised is that our vulnerability is not something that we simply have to overcome or that separates us from others. It is an essential part of being human. It could be the very thing that connects us.”
Her hope is that the film will encourage compassion and show “the real value in standing alongside one another in the hardest of times”.
She sees every day as a day “given back to me”. Catherine says she hopes to remind people that whatever road they face, whatever challenge ahead, they are not alone.
Nature has helped her healing. “Even when I physically couldn’t get into nature, I imagined nature from my hospital bed. And now that I’m well enough, I feel a deep longing for all those spaces, for the ocean, for the trees, for the mountains,” she says in the film.
As for her pilgrimage, it has become “so much more than a personal or solitary experience but really a collective one”.
There is light. Just being alongside someone is enough, she says. “So often you think you need to fix something or say something or do something, and you don’t. You just need to be there. And that’s what love looks like.
“That’s what I think the light is that we can often find out of the darkest of times. In the midst of the fog and everything, it’s just so special. That’s a moment of consolation.”

Debattenkultur im Deutschen Bundestag : Die gespielte Ohnmacht
Politiker*innen machen im Bundestag keine Politik, sondern PR. Warum sind sie dort nicht ideenreicher?
A b und an kann es gute Unterhaltung sein, die Sitzungen des Deutschen Bundestags live zu verfolgen. Auch im Wissen darum, dass dort Politik nicht gemacht, aber der Öffentlichkeit verkauft wird. Das war schon so, bevor Abgeordnete damit begannen, Ausschnitte ihrer Redebeiträge auf Social Media zu teilen – damals ging es eben darum, mit ein oder zwei Sätzen in die „Tagesschau“ zu kommen.
Gerade Haushaltsdebatten wie in dieser Woche zeigen auf: Es ist eine grundlegende Neuordnung gesellschaftlicher, wirtschaftlicher, geopolitischer und ökologischer Realitäten im Gange – und all dem läuft der politische Diskurs hinterher. Wer den Kanzler Friedrich Merz von der Union bei der Generaldebatte am Mittwoch gesehen hat, hat einen Redner erlebt, der um Verständnis fleht, als wolle er für seine Politik wenigstens noch das Urteil erbetteln, er habe sich stets bemüht.
Ganz anders ist das bei der Opposition. Breitbeinig und mit dem Nimbus, ihm gehöre die Zukunft, tritt AfD-Chef Tino Chrupalla auf. Inhaltlich wahrhaftiger und rhetorisch deutlich gewandter, aber mit nicht minder vernichtender Regierungskritik Britta Haßelmann von Bündnis90/Die Grünen und mit plattestmöglichem Kapitalismusbashing in sprachlicher Doubletime schließlich Heidi Reichinnek von der Linkspartei. Zwischendurch erklärt SPD-Fraktionschef Mathias Miersch, wie schwer doch das Regieren sei. Oh weh.
Die extreme Rechte schürt immer erfolgreicher das Gefühl, Demokratie – „der Altparteienstaat“ – sei zur Lösung der Gegenwartsaufgaben nicht in der Lage. Wenn verhindert werden soll, dass die sozioökonomische Transformation in einen Sturz des politischen Systems mündet – dann sollten die Debatten im Bundestag doch schnellstmöglich ideenreicher werden. Und wenigstens den Eindruck erwecken, Politik könne wirklich etwas gestalten und hätte auch noch eine Vorstellung davon, wie.

Sachsen-Anhalt: Gewaltschutz für Frauen vor dem Aus
Vor einer möglichen AfD-Regierung will der Paritätische die Finanzierung der zentralen Hilfsstruktur einstellen – vorauseilender Gehorsam?
Gut einen Monat vor Ende des Jahres verkündet der Paritätische Wohlfahrtsverband Sachsen-Anhalt in einer Mail an seine Netzwerkpartner und Mitarbeiter*innen, die Trägerschaft der Landeskoordinierungsstelle (Liko) zum Jahreswechsel zu beenden. Die Liko ist seit knapp 20 Jahren die zentrale Koordinationsstruktur des Hilfesystems für Frauen in Sachsen-Anhalt. Zum Netzwerk zählen 19 Frauenhäuser, dazu kommt eine Vielzahl an Beratungsstellen und weiteren Hilfsangeboten. Nun steht diese Struktur vor dem Aus – wegen fehlender Gelder, so der Landesverband.
»Das ist das falsche Signal zur falschen Zeit«, sagt Annett Kannenberg-Bode, Vorsitzende des Landesfrauenrates Sachsen-Anhalt. Die Liko sei das »Rückgrat« des gesamten Gewaltschutzes in dem Bundesland. In einer ohnehin schon politisch und finanziell angespannten Situation würden mit ihr eine zentrale Koordinierungsstelle, jahrelang gewachsene Kooperationen und fachliche Kontinuität wegfallen.
»Die Beendigung der Trägerschaft so kurzfristig anzukündigen, ist grob fahrlässig und richtet potenziell einen Riesenschaden an«, meint auch Heinz-Jürgen Voß, Professor am Fachbereich Soziale Arbeit an der Hochschule Merseburg. Er ist durch seine Forschung im Bereich der sexuellen Bildung eng verbunden mit dem Netzwerk. Mit dem Wegbrechen der Liko würde hilfesuchenden Personen der Zugang zu Unterstützung und Fachkräften die Übersicht erschwert, so Voß: »Das gesamte Hilfesystem wird nun vor vollendete Tatsachen gesetzt, ohne nach Lösungen zu suchen.« Es sei kaum möglich, in so kurzer Zeit einen anderen Träger zu finden.
Der Paritätische Wohlfahrtsverband begründet die Entscheidung mit zu hohen Kosten durch die Eigenbeteiligung von 37.000 Euro, die demnach für den Verband anfallen. Angeführt werden vor allem die »tarifbedingt gestiegenen Personalkosten«. Voß hält das für vorgeschoben. »Eine Eigenbeteiligung für den Träger ist nichts Neues und war für den Paritätischen planbar. Und auch abseits davon: Es hätten solidarische Wege gefunden werden können, das Geld einzuwerben.« Die Solidarität mit Sachsen-Anhalt sei derzeit aufgrund der politischen Situation groß, die Gelder hätten problemlos durch ein Crowdfunding oder auf anderen Wegen aufgetrieben werden können, ist der Wissenschaftler überzeugt. Es vermutet ein strategisches Interesse hinter der Entscheidung: »Es liegt nahe, dass sich der Verband, bevor eine rechtsextreme Partei an die Macht kommen könnte, im Vorhinein aus der Auseinandersetzung herausstiehlt.«
Dass er sich in Anbetracht einer möglichen AfD-Landesregierung in vorauseilendem Gehorsam unliebsamer Strukturen entledigen und sich Türen offenhalten möchte, dementiert der Landesverband. Dass es zu dieser Entscheidung gekommen sei, habe »rein wirtschaftliche Gründe«, so Jesko Döring, beim Paritätischen Sachsen-Anhalt für Öffentlichkeitsarbeit zuständig, im Gespräch mit »nd«. Man habe sich jahrelang um Lösungen für die Finanzierung der Eigenbeteiligung bemüht, aber es »nicht an die große Glocke« gehängt.
Ausblick auf stürmische Jahre
Auch der Landesfrauenrat kritisiert die steigende Eigenbeteiligung bei Hilfestrukturen, die vor allem für kleinere Einrichtungen zunehmend schwer zu stemmen sei – eine Struktur wie die Liko sei aber alternativlos. »Was dort an Vertrauen, Fachwissen und gemeinsamen Arbeitsstrukturen entstanden ist, lässt sich nicht kurzfristig ersetzen oder zusätzlich von den ohnehin stark beanspruchten Einrichtungen auffangen«, betont Kannenberg-Bode. Der Ball liege nun beim Paritätischen Verband.
Auch ohne eine AfD-Regierung stünden die Hilfestrukturen in Sachsen-Anhalt unter Druck. »Die Kommunen stehen vor finanziellen Problemen, weshalb Projekte gestrichen und Stellen gekürzt werden«, sagt Voß. Zum anderen müsse eine Struktur wie der Paritätische Verband in sich stabil sein. Das heiße: Sei ein Landesverband in Not, werde vertraulich nach Lösungen gesucht und geschaut, wie die Zusammenarbeit gemeinsam gestemmt wird. Mit Hinblick auf die politische Lage sei es besonders wichtig, auf solidarische Strukturen innerhalb eines Netzwerks zurückgreifen zu können. Diese Struktur sei aber zurzeit durch das Agieren des Paritätischen gefährdet.
Der Landesfrauenrat blickt angesichts der politischen Situation zwar besorgt auf die kommenden Jahre, sieht zugleich aber derzeit ein großes Bemühen von Stiftungen und anderen Akteuren um den Erhalt bestehender Gewalthilfestrukturen. Für den Frauenrat ist klar: »Egal welche Landesregierung – Gewaltschutz für Frauen bleibt unabdingbar.«
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.

Hunted beyond borders: Allegations of Tanzanian repression in Kenya
The case of a missing activist raises fears for the safety of Tanzanian dissidents.
Nairobi, Kenya – On October 25, 2026, Tanzanian opposition activist Twaha Salim Mwaipaya was travelling in a taxi to visit friends in Kamulu, in Kenya’s Machakos County, when three vehicles intercepted it.
According to the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR), unidentified individuals forcibly removed him from the taxi and took him away. His whereabouts remain unknown.
Amnesty International reported that the vehicles included a Toyota Land Cruiser Hardtop. The organisation called on Kenyan authorities to establish Mwaipaya’s whereabouts, guarantee his safety and investigate the circumstances of his disappearance.
The International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT) subsequently described the incident as an enforced disappearance and called for an independent investigation, including into possible cross-border involvement.
The identities of those responsible have not been established, and it remains unclear who ordered the abduction.
Mwaipaya, a former youth organiser of Tanzania’s opposition party Chadema, had fled to Kenya in 2025, citing threats to his safety.
On November 3, Kenya’s inspector general of police, Douglas Kanja, appeared before the High Court to explain the activist’s whereabouts. He denied that Kenyan police had arrested or detained Mwaipaya.
“We do not have him in our custody,” Kanja told the court, adding that investigations were ongoing. He acknowledged that Mwaipaya’s relatives had reported him missing at a police station in the Ruai area.
Kanja also said he had consulted other security agencies but had received no information confirming that Mwaipaya had been transferred to Tanzania.
The case returned to the High Court on November 23. Judge Alexander Muteti summoned Mohamed Amin, head of the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), to provide an update on the investigation into Mwaipaya’s disappearance.
The judge said Amin’s appearance was necessary because the inspector general had placed the investigation within the DCI’s mandate. The court declined to summon Deputy Inspector General of Police Eliud Lagat, ruling that his testimony would not add significant value to the proceedings. Amin was ordered to appear on a date to be determined by the court.
Tanzania’s high commissioner to Kenya, Bernard Kibesse, told news outlet The Citizen on October 26 that the embassy was following up on the disappearance but had not received an official report.
Mwaipaya’s disappearance recalls the January 2025 abduction of Tanzanian activist and government critic Maria Sarungi Tsehai in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi. Unidentified men forced her into a vehicle before releasing her several hours later following public pressure and intervention by human rights defenders, according to reports at the time by Amnesty International Kenya and other organisations.
Sarungi believes her abductors intended to take her across the border into Tanzania.
“In 60-90 minutes, they would have reached the border and crossed with me, and I would have disappeared for good like hundreds of Tanzanians who have disappeared in such manner in Tanzania under Samia Suluhu,” she told Al Jazeera.
She said some of the men appeared to be Kenyan, while another appeared Tanzanian based on his Kiswahili. She alleged that a Tanzanian national directed the operation. The identities of her abductors and who organised the operation have not been independently established.
The incidents have renewed concerns about the safety of Tanzanian dissidents in Kenya and allegations of transnational repression.
In May 2026, President Samia Suluhu Hassan made remarks about dealing with antigovernment protesters that drew criticism.
Speaking alongside Kenyan President William Ruto at State House in Dar es Salaam on May 4, Hassan said protesters should be flogged with canes if they crossed into either country, The Standard reported.
The leaders were attending a joint press briefing following the signing of eight bilateral agreements.
“I have told President William Ruto we must stand firm against those who lack discipline. We should not choose between Tanzanians or Kenyans. If they come to me, I flog them with canes; if they come to you, you flog them with canes, so that they behave,” Hassan said, according to The Standard’s May 5 report.
Former Kenyan Chief Justice David Maraga condemned the comments, describing them as abhorrent. No evidence has emerged linking the remarks to either abduction.
History of repression
Political repression in Tanzania predates Hassan’s presidency. Under her predecessor, John Magufuli, human rights organisations documented restrictions on political freedoms, intimidation of opposition figures and attacks on government critics.
In September 2017, opposition leader Tundu Lissu survived an assassination attempt in Dodoma, the capital of Tanzania, during which he was shot 16 times by unidentified men. He received treatment in Nairobi before continuing his recovery in Belgium. The attack remains unresolved.
Hassan initially raised hopes of political reform after taking office in 2021, easing restrictions on political rallies and allowing some politicians who had fled the country to return.
However, human rights organisations subsequently documented renewed restrictions on opposition activity, arbitrary arrests and intimidation of critics. The African Union’s 2025 election observation mission also noted that the political opening following her accession had been short-lived.
Lissu was arrested in April 2025 and charged with treason. On November 6, 2026, a Tanzanian court acquitted him of treason but convicted him of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison.
The Reuters news agency reported that the charges arose from remarks prosecutors said urged supporters to disrupt the election. Lissu denied wrongdoing.
The treatment of critics has also affected activists from neighbouring countries.
In May 2025, Kenyan activist Boniface Mwangi and Ugandan human rights defender Agather Atuhaire travelled to Dar-es-Salaam to observe Lissu’s treason proceedings. They were arrested on May 19 and subsequently deported.
Both later described being held incommunicado and subjected to abuse. Amnesty International reported allegations of torture and ill-treatment, including sexual violence, while United Nations human rights experts issued a communication to the Tanzanian government detailing allegations of enforced disappearance, torture and other abuses. These were allegations documented by the organisations and UN experts, not judicial findings.
The aftermath of the 2025 elections
Tanzania’s political crisis intensified following the October 29, 2025 general election, which was marked by restrictions on opposition participation and deadly post-election violence.
The African Union Election Observation Mission concluded that the elections did not comply with AU democratic principles and international standards. It cited restrictions on political competition, shortcomings in the electoral framework and an internet shutdown that disrupted observation.
The disputed vote triggered protests, arrests and a security crackdown. Human Rights Watch reported that police and people in civilian clothing killed hundreds of protesters and bystanders.
A year later, the organisation said authorities had yet to make arrests for human rights violations committed before and during the election.
A presidential Commission of Inquiry reported that 518 people died from unnatural causes during the unrest. Its chairman, retired Chief Justice Mohamed Chande Othman, said the figure might not be conclusive.
The commission also recorded allegations that security officers shot people in their homes and shops. Human Rights Watch criticised the inquiry for failing to meaningfully scrutinise the conduct of security forces.
The figures remain contested. Chadema and other sources have reported higher death tolls, although these estimates have not been independently established.
A CNN investigation published on November 20, 2025, analysed geolocated videos, audio evidence and witness accounts showing police and armed men shooting at protesters, including some who appeared unarmed.
It also documented evidence supporting witness accounts of overflowing morgues and possible mass graves. The Tanzanian government disputed aspects of the reporting.
Kenya’s responsibility
Mwaipaya’s disappearance raises questions about Kenya’s responsibility to protect foreign nationals within its territory, particularly those fleeing political persecution.
Kenya has long provided refuge to activists and opposition figures escaping repression elsewhere in the region. However, the cases of Mwaipaya and Sarungi have raised concerns about whether that protection can be guaranteed when critics of neighbouring governments are allegedly targeted on Kenyan soil.
The Kenyan authorities must establish Mwaipaya’s whereabouts, investigate the circumstances of his disappearance and identify those responsible. Tanzania, meanwhile, must address allegations that its critics are being pursued beyond its borders.
For Tanzanian human rights lawyer Tito Magoti, the disappearances are part of a wider human rights crisis facing the country.
“Tanzanians are not free. Abduction is one side of the coin. There are plenty of other atrocities committed against Tanzanians and they run hand in hand with the abductions. It starts there. You abduct, you torture, you extrajudicially kill, persecute through judicial forums, sexual assault and more, so the state of political freedom is in limbo,” he said.
