https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.
During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.
There were also many happy admissions of historical ignorance. Since taking on the Ukraine brief a year ago, Kushner said, he had to learn “the algorithm of Europe and how complicated that is”, and he had to get abreast of “the local issues with Ukraine”.
As a businessman he brought a special expertise, he claimed. “Look at what’s happening in the Middle East with sanctions, with Russia, with Iran. I think that you have to understand economics in order to understand geopolitics because the two go together very, very closely,” he said.
But the main revelation was how much he believes the Ukraine conflict is not a case of an aggressor and a victim – but is simply a series of misunderstandings and miscommunication.
Indeed, he treated Vladimir Putin as if he were a masterful corporate executive quite willing to close the deal if he were only given the right economic incentives – instead of a man ready to sacrifice hundreds of thousands of Russians to reclaim part of a historical empire.
In the process, Kushner revealed – often inadvertently – that he had largely bought into the Russian narrative of a string of postwar missteps by Europe and the US coming to a head in Nato’s expansion eastwards after 9/11.
That, in turn, has led him to adopt Moscow’s central demand to reshape the European security order to allow Russia, without opprobrium, to retain land it has gained by force. Shining through his answers was a naive bias towards the aggressor, presented as a mediator’s desire to understand both parties.
Praise veering on awe for the Russian leader flowed. “Putin – people can like what he has done, they can not like what he has done – [but] he is a grand master of politics. He is a historic figure,” he said. Any sense that Putin may have blundered escaped him.
As to the rights and wrongs of invading another country, Kushner was blasé. “After all, most lines in Europe have changed over time and they are decided through war or peace, or concessions. It’s not about fairness or who is right or wrong. It’s about ending the killing,” he said.
He understood, too, why Putin could not offer a ceasefire: “He has very little confidence that if he stops the war, that he [will] be able to get to a postwar settlement that leads to not having a future war.”
To stop the killing, the killing has to go on.
What is more, Kushner was struck by the Russian leader’s self-control. “So far Putin has shown restraint and he has agreed not to use nuclear weapons and he has reassured us that is his intention.”
Kushner denied Trump had put any pressure on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, defying his interviewer to provide evidence – at which point Döpfner recited a list of examples, including only last month when the US president suggested that Ukraine should get a new leader.
Trump was “a strong counter-puncher”, argued Kushner, implying that Zelenskyy had thrown the first punch in a conflict that began with a Russian invasion. Relations with Ukraine were cooperative, he said before pointedly saying Kyiv needed things from the US, without which “Ukraine will not be safe in the future”.
After noting that “the territorial issue is now a little bit of a deadlock”, his strategic insight was that if a future security architecture for Europe could be agreed, the answer to the land question in Donbas would eventually follow.
In essence, he proposed a revival of the Russia-Nato council, one of the bodies eviscerated by Putin’s war.
He also envisioned Ukraine inside the European Union with security guarantees akin to those offered by Nato’s article five. Though it was impossible at this stage to give “more specificity” about these guarantees in the detailed way Ukraine sought, he admitted.
So far, neither Moscow nor Kyiv have bought this plan, let alone a wary Europe.
Kushner tried to be polite about Europe, insisting it had to be at the negotiating table, but he could not stop himself characterising European military assistance to Ukraine as a “proxy war” against Russia.
As an analysis of why the Ukraine war had not ended inside the 24 hours Trump had promised when he took office again, Kushner showed an alarming belief that the answer lay in granting more concessions to Putin, and that the misunderstandings and misperceptions would then evaporate.

https://taz.de/Chancen-haengen-stark-von.title: Forscherinnen über Klassismus: „Soziale Herkunft wurde im Journalismus vernachlässigt“
https://taz.de/Chancen-haengen-stark-von.author: Marco Fründt
https://taz.de/Chancen-haengen-stark-von.text:
Forscherinnen über Klassismus: „Soziale Herkunft wurde im Journalismus vernachlässigt“
Im Journalismus zeigt sich: Soziale Herkunft behindert stärker als Migrationshintergrund. Zwei Forscherinnen fordern Konsequenzen zum Ausgleich.
taz: Frau Köhler und Frau Lönnendonker, Sie haben die soziale Herkunft des journalistischen Nachwuchses untersucht. Wer wird heute Journalist:in?
Tanja Köhler: Unsere Untersuchung zeigt, dass Menschen aus nichtakademischen Elternhäusern im journalistischen Nachwuchs deutlich unterrepräsentiert sind. Wir haben soziale Herkunft dabei anhand der Bildungsabschlüsse der Eltern erfasst. Bei den Volontär:innen stammen knapp 48 Prozent der Befragten aus einem nichtakademischen Elternhaus, bei den Journalistenschüler:innen sind es nur knapp 35 Prozent. Zum Vergleich: In Deutschland stammen rund 72 Prozent der 18- bis 25-Jährigen aus einem nichtakademischen Elternhaus. Die soziale Zusammensetzung unserer Gesellschaft spiegelt sich im journalistischen Nachwuchs also nicht wider.
taz: Weshalb wird Klasse in der Forschung so wenig beachtet? Sind Klassenunterschiede weniger relevant geworden?
Förderberaterin im Referat Forschungsförderung der TU Dortmund. Zuvor hat sie an der Deutschen Welle Akademie, der Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) und am Institut für Journalistik der TU Dortmund Kommunikationswissenschaften mit Fokus auf Journalistik gelehrt und geforscht. Ihre Forschungsschwerpunkte liegen in der international vergleichenden Journalistik, der EU- und Auslandsberichterstattung wie europäischer Öffentlichkeit und Identität.
Köhler: Soziale Herkunft war nicht immer ein blinder Fleck in der Journalismusforschung. Gerade in den 70er- und 80er-Jahren wurde untersucht, aus welchen sozialen Schichten Journalist:innen kommen. Die Studien zeigten schon damals, dass Journalist:innen überwiegend aus der Mittel- und Oberschicht stammten, während Menschen aus Arbeiterfamilien deutlich unterrepräsentiert waren. Danach ließ das Forschungsinteresse allerdings spürbar nach. Offenbar ging man davon aus, dass sich diese soziale Schieflage durch die Bildungsexpansion und zunehmende soziale Mobilität mit der Zeit von selbst verringern würde.
Professorin für Digitalen Journalismus an der Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg und Co-Direktorin des Instituts für Medienentwicklung und -analyse (Imea). Sie leitet aktuell Forschungsprojekte zu sozialen Ungleichheitsstrukturen im Journalismus.
Julia Lönnendonker: In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten sind dann andere Diversitätsdimensionen stärker in den Fokus geraten, etwa Geschlecht oder Migrationshintergrund. Die soziale Herkunft wurde dagegen lange vernachlässigt.
taz: Heute wird in Ausschreibungen zumindest formal viel Wert auf Diversität gelegt. Haben es Menschen mit Arbeiter:innenhintergrund dadurch einfacher als jene ohne?
Lönnendonker: Nein. Wir wissen aus vielen Studien, dass die Bildungschancen in Deutschland sehr stark von der sozialen Herkunft abhängen. Von 100 Akademikerkindern nehmen 78 ein Studium auf, bei Familien, in denen kein Elternteil einen Hochschulabschluss hat, sind es nur 25. Und in Familien, in denen kein Elternteil eine Berufsausbildung hat, sind es sogar nur 8.
taz: Wer sind die Menschen, die heute ein Volontariat oder einen Platz an einer Journalistenschule bekommen?
Köhler: Die Volontär:innen und Journalistenschüler:innen unserer Studie sind überwiegend weiblich, akademisch ausgebildet und stammen mehrheitlich aus Elternhäusern, in denen mindestens ein Elternteil einen Hochschulabschluss hat. Auffällig ist vor allem das hohe formale Bildungsniveau. Menschen mit einem Realschulabschluss sind unter unseren Befragten nur in Einzelfällen vertreten. Einen Hauptschulabschluss hat niemand.
Lönnendonker: 97 Prozent hatten Abitur und 86 einen Hochschulabschluss. Das heißt, es hat schon vorher eine Bildungsselektion stattgefunden.
Köhler: Vergleichsweise hoch ist auch der Frauenanteil. Auch der Anteil der Befragten mit Migrationshintergrund liegt nur noch leicht unter dem Bevölkerungsdurchschnitt. Zumindest bei diesen Diversitätsmerkmalen scheinen die Medienhäuser und Journalistenschulen bei der Auswahl ihres Nachwuchses auf einem guten Weg zu sein.
taz: Wie erklären Sie sich, dass Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund stärker vertreten sind als jene aus einem Arbeiter:innenhaushalt?Köhler: Die Merkmale schließen sich zunächst einmal ja nicht gegenseitig aus. Wir wissen aber aus der Forschung, dass soziale Herkunft sich stärker auf Bildungschancen auswirkt als ein Migrationshintergrund. Möglicherweise, weil das eine leichter erkennbar sein kann, etwa durch Namen, während das andere unsichtbar bleibt. Soziale Herkunft – das wissen wir aus der Forschung – ist außerdem sehr schambehaftet.
taz: Personen aus akademischen Elternhäusern sind im Journalismus also überrepräsentiert. Macht das einen Unterschied, wenn Journalist:innen doch eh die Wahrheit abbilden müssen?
Köhler: Soziale Herkunft prägt unseren Blick auf die Gesellschaft und kann beeinflussen, welche Themen und Perspektiven Redaktionen wichtig finden. Natürlich gelten journalistische Standards. Aber wenn Redaktionen sozial sehr homogen zusammengesetzt sind, dann besteht die Gefahr, dass bestimmte Lebenswelten und Perspektiven aus dem Blick geraten.
taz: Unterscheiden sich Journalist:innen anhand ihrer sozialen Herkunft?
Köhler: In unserer Untersuchung zeigen sich Unterschiede im journalistischen Rollenverständnis. Befragte aus akademischen Elternhäusern messen der Aufgabe, die Mächtigen zu kontrollieren, eine höhere Bedeutung bei als Befragte aus nichtakademischen. Befragten aus nichtakademischen Elternhäusern ist es dagegen wichtiger, Randgruppen und Minderheiten eine Stimme zu geben und Menschen zur politischen Teilhabe zu motivieren.
taz: Welche Rolle spielt der Klassenhintergrund in der Berichterstattung über die Gen-Z-Proteste, Miete oder die neue Grundsicherung?
Köhler: Gerade bei Themen wie steigende Mieten, Armut oder sozialpolitische Reformen kann soziale Herkunft eine Rolle spielen. Wer selbst Erfahrungen mit finanzieller Unsicherheit gemacht hat, bringt möglicherweise andere Fragen und Perspektiven in die Berichterstattung ein. Fehlen solche Perspektiven, besteht die Gefahr, dass bestimmte Lebensrealitäten in der Berichterstattung kaum vorkommen oder Menschen aus weniger privilegierten Verhältnissen stereotyp dargestellt werden.
taz: Wie wirkt sich das auf die Wahrnehmung von Journalismus aus?
Köhler: Menschen mit niedrigerem Bildungsniveau haben Studien zufolge tendenziell weniger Vertrauen in die Medien. Wenn sie ihre Lebensrealität in der Berichterstattung nicht wiederfinden, kann das ihr Vertrauen beeinträchtigen. Deshalb ist Perspektivenvielfalt im Journalismus wichtig.
taz: Und jetzt?
Köhler: Zunächst müssen Medienhäuser und Journalistenschulen soziale Herkunft überhaupt berücksichtigen. Dazu gehört, die eigenen Auswahlverfahren kritisch zu überprüfen. Außerdem sollte nicht nur an Gymnasien, sondern gezielt auch an Real- und Gesamtschulen für den Beruf geworben werden. Und wir brauchen Förderprogramme, die Menschen aus weniger privilegierten Verhältnissen den Zugang zur journalistischen Ausbildung erleichtern. Es sollte zudem Quoten für Menschen aus weniger privilegierten sozialen Verhältnissen geben. Denn strukturelle Benachteiligung verschwindet nicht alleine dadurch, dass man sich zu Diversität bekennt.
Lönnendonker: Ganz wichtig sind auch die finanziellen Hürden beim Berufseinstieg. Wer es sich nicht leisten kann, schlecht oder gar nicht bezahlt zu arbeiten, hat von vornherein schlechtere Chancen im Journalismus.
Tanja Köhler, Julia Lönnendonker: „Klassismus im Journalismus“, Herbert von Halem Verlag, 28 Euro

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
Voters will decide whether to scrap the country’s ‘nuclear-free homeland’ policy on Saturday.
Voters in Taiwan are set to decide whether to bring back nuclear power – 18 months after its last operational reactor was shut down.
A referendum on the issue is being held alongside local elections on Saturday. It is the island’s fourth vote on nuclear power in just eight years.
It comes as demand for electricity to fuel the country’s burgeoning computer chip industry soars and concern grows about how Taiwan would keep its lights on if China, which claims the island as its own territory, cut it off amid escalating tensions.
Here is what we know.
What is the referendum about?
Voters are being asked whether the government should return to using nuclear power to boost the economy. That would mean abolishing the country’s longstanding “nuclear-free homeland” policy.
The opposition Kuomintang (KMT) proposed the referendum and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is also backing it. The legislature approved the referendum in August and the Central Election Commission signed it off on August 28.
To pass, ‘yes’ votes must outnumber ‘no’ votes and exceed a quarter of all eligible voters.
The ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which has long had a policy of no nuclear power in its mandate, is urging ‘no’. DPP legislator Chen Pei-yu called the referendum unnecessary, saying lawmakers could change the policy by amending existing laws instead.
Why did Taiwan give up nuclear power?
Taiwan once relied heavily on nuclear power. In 1985, its three plants produced 52 percent of the nation’s electricity.
Nuclear power then became one of the most partisan issues in Taiwanese politics. Lev Nachman, an assistant professor at the Graduate Institute of National Development at National Taiwan University, said the divide goes back to the DPP’s founding.
“There was a major group of environmentalists that were part of the party that were very anti-nuclear,” Nachman told Al Jazeera. The nuclear industry, by contrast, was built and run under the KMT.
Polarisation turned that into “a very green-versus-blue issue”, Nachman said, referring to the colours of the DPP and the KMT.
Safety fears run deep. Nachman said Taiwan watched the 2011 Fukushima nuclear plant meltdown in neighbouring Japan very closely.
“There is this sort of fear of any sort of nuclear reaction that would ever happen in Taiwan would just devastate the entire island,” he said. Active geological fault lines run across Taiwan and the question of how to dispose of nuclear waste remains unresolved.
The DPP has governed since 2016, partly on a pledge to phase out nuclear power. In May last year, Taiwan shut down its last reactor at Maanshan in Pingtung County.
Why is nuclear power back on the agenda?
Public opinion has been mixed in three previous referendums. In 2018, voters opted to scrap a legal deadline for phasing out nuclear power. But in 2021, they rejected restarting construction on an unfinished fourth nuclear plant. In August last year, a majority vote to restart the Maanshan plant was voided due to low turnout.
Now, nuclear power is back on the agenda because surging electricity demand from Taiwan’s semiconductor and AI industries, along with growing fears about energy security and over-reliance on imported fuel, have renewed the debate over how the island keeps the lights on in an emergency.
According to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan imports more than 97 percent of its energy. Natural gas generates about 43 percent of its electricity and coal about 35 percent. Both arrive by ship.
Taiwan only has about 11 days of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in reserve. Japan and South Korea hold between 14 and 20 days.
“There’s two sides to it,” Nachman said. The first is energy security: “If China actually blockades Taiwan and cuts off access to the outside world, then Taiwan only has so much energy it can rely on.”
The second is the chip industry, which requires huge amounts of power and “that’s only going to increase over time”, he said.
The war with Iran this year has added to the pressure by disrupting LNG shipments from the Middle East.
Will the ruling party change its stance?
The DPP has already started to shift. In March, President William Lai Ching-te said the government would begin the process of restarting the Maanshan and Kuosheng plants. He cited AI-driven demand and conflicts abroad causing disruption to energy supplies.
On September 24, the Nuclear Safety Commission approved state-owned Taipower’s restart plan for Maanshan. Further safety assessments are still needed before it can operate again.
Nachman said Lai has tried to push his party to rethink its “very dogmatic anti-nuclear stance”. The question is whether DPP voters have come around.
Nuclear power is not Taiwan’s first choice for filling the gap, however. “Investment in LNG – that’s still Taiwan’s kind of number one goal,” Nachman said.
How important is Taiwan’s microchip industry?
Taiwan is the most important link in the global AI supply chain.
It makes more than 90 percent of the world’s most advanced semiconductors, nearly all of them at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). TSMC has more than 60 percent of the global contract chipmaking market.
Its customers include Nvidia – the world’s most valuable semiconductor company – AMD and Apple. TSMC makes Nvidia’s Blackwell and Rubin AI processors, and Taiwanese firms such as Foxconn and Quanta build most of the world’s AI servers.
That uses huge amounts of electricity and water. In September, Taiwan’s semiconductor industry used more than 4.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity for the first time. That was up 11.55 percent from a year earlier, driven by AI demand.
S&P Global estimated that TSMC alone used about 8 percent of Taiwan’s electricity in 2023. That share could rise to almost 24 percent by 2030, it added.
Nachman cautioned against seeing the referendum only through the demand for microchips and semiconductors. “In today’s media, Taiwan has become a single issue, just about semiconductors,” he said. “For a lot of people in Taiwan, the semiconductors aren’t even the priority. It really is the security side.”
Will China object to Taiwan having nuclear power?
Probably not. Beijing does not appear to have commented on the referendum itself.
“The nuclear issue is a completely separate issue from anything related to China,” Nachman said. “It’s much more a matter of domestic politics.”
China has, however, used Taiwan’s energy weakness in its messaging. In March, Chen Binhua, a spokesman for China’s Taiwan Affairs Office, said closer integration with China could help solve Taiwan’s energy problems. He pointed to the island’s reliance on oil and gas from the Middle East.
Taipei rejects unification with Beijing. Analysts writing in The Diplomat called the offer an exercise in optics.
However, it remains a top priority for China. During a speech in Beijing on November 12, President Xi Jinping once again stated that Taiwan and China must be reunified.
The referendum is about civilian power reactors, not weapons. Asked whether Taiwan might seek a nuclear weapon, Nachman said: “No, of course not. This is just about nuclear power.”
Taiwan did secretly pursue nuclear weapons in the 1970s and 1980s. The programme was shut down in 1988 under US pressure, after a senior nuclear scientist, Chang Hsien-yi, defected to the United States.
Since then, Taiwan’s leaders have consistently stated that they will not seek nuclear weapons. Its nuclear facilities are inspected under an arrangement between Taiwan, the US and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
The bigger worry is a blockade by China if it seeks to press reunification in the future. Nachman said large military drills and naval patrols China has held around Taiwan since US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s visit in 2022 have all rehearsed one.
Will the referendum pass and what happens next?
Nachman said he is sceptical. “We keep doing it over and over again and it still doesn’t usually pass,” he said. “So my expectations are actually fairly low.”
The outcome will depend on DPP supporters. “It’s really more a matter of whether or not green voters have come around to it,” Nachman said.
If the referendum does pass, he said Lai and the DPP “would probably be largely okay with it”.
The restart process is already under way either way. Supporters say reactors could be running again within 18 months to three years. Opponents say a restart could take five to 10 years and cost several hundred billion New Taiwan dollars.
Results are expected on Saturday night.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Mudar a fotografia do poder é possível? Avanços e lacunas nas eleições de 2026
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Dani Portela
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Foram 146.123 votos os que me consagraram como a deputada estadual mais votada de Pernambuco e a mulher negra com maior proporção de votos em todo o país com 2,78% dos 5.248.293 votos válidos do estado. Passado o susto da expressividade de uma votação que surpreendeu adversários e aliados, algumas reflexões são necessárias sobre o significado deste resultado e dessas eleições.
Na noite do dia 4 de outubro um filme passou em minha cabeça e fui imediatamente levada à minha primeira candidatura, em 2018, ano que disputei o Governo do estado de Pernambuco. Naquele ano recebi 188.087 votos, ficando na 3ª colocação e alcançando a maior votação nominal para uma mulher ao cargo de governadora na história de Pernambuco até então.
Na minha 2ª eleição, em 2020, fui a vereadora mais votada da cidade do Recife, com mais de 14 mil votos. Ali eu compreendi o que a minha candidatura representava para um grupo que sempre esteve à margem dos espaços de decisão: mulheres negras, trabalhadoras, nordestinas, que ao longo da história foram ensinadas que as cadeiras do parlamento e do legislativo não poderiam ser ocupadas por elas.
No meu primeiro dia na casa, fui abordada por uma mulher negra, funcionária terceirizada do setor de serviços gerais que relatou ter sofrido racismo ao escutar de um outro parlamentar que uma “pariceira” dela estava vindo para aquela Casa, desta vez não para limpar o chão, mas para ser parlamentar igual a ele. Segundo o parlamentar, aquele mundo “estava perdido mesmo”.
Ali eu entendi o que meu corpo e minha mandata representavam naquele espaço. Quando subo à tribuna pela primeira vez, trago em meu discurso que a minha eleição sinaliza o desejo de pessoas negras, mulheres, periféricas, LGBTs, de ocuparem e serem representadas neste espaço. Como disse no dia 1º de janeiro de 2021, aquele não era um discurso de posse, mas de reintegração de posse.
Desde então, venho afirmando que ser a primeira ou a única não é suficiente. Movimentos sociais negros e feministas têm me ensinado que para mudar a fotografia do poder é necessário estratégia, incidência política e, sobretudo, construção coletiva. Não basta abrir a porta e ocupar a cadeira: é preciso garantir que outras mulheres negras possam entrar, permanecer e exercer seus mandatos com condições reais.
Cada voto recebido por uma mulher negra representa o desejo de muitas que vieram antes de nós de que haja o compromisso com o fortalecimento de candidaturas negras, feministas, LGBTs e periféricas; de que nossa atuação dispute o orçamento, que coloque essas pessoas como prioridade e que suas demandas sejam levadas e defendidas no parlamento.
Assim, aprendi que representatividade significa, além de ocupar espaços de poder, imprimir a nossa história de resistência em ações concretas, como leis aprovadas, fiscalizações, incidências no orçamento público, na defesa por políticas públicas, entre outras ações.
Ao longo desses anos, iniciativas como o “Quilombo nos parlamentos”, da Coalizão Negra por Direitos; e a campanha “Eu Voto em Negra”, da Rede de Mulheres Negras de Pernambuco; têm nos mostrado que o movimento de mudança da fotografia do poder só se faz de forma coletiva. Essas iniciativas existem porque os números ainda nos desafiam. Se o meu resultado surpreende e anima, o retrato nacional revela o quanto falta para que deixemos de ser minoria no ambiente da política.
Na Câmara Federal, as mulheres negras foram 18,2% das candidaturas, mas foram apenas 6,6% das eleitas. Já os homens brancos, que foram 33,7% das candidaturas, ocuparão 58,7% das cadeiras. A diferença aparece também na taxa de êxito: 3% das candidatas negras a deputada federal se elegeram, contra 7% das candidatas brancas. No Senado, das 12 mulheres eleitas — seguimos sem nenhuma negra.
Os números mostram que a bancada feminina, a maior da história recente, com 21,2% das cadeiras, está longe de nos representar. Das 109 deputadas federais eleitas em 2026, apenas 47 são de esquerda ou centro-esquerda. Olhar para estes dados nos lembra os desafios que ainda temos para mudar esse quadro, considerando que ainda seguimos com um congresso majoritariamente branco, masculino e de direita.
Porém, é preciso fazer uma ressalva: queremos, sim, mais mulheres negras ocupando essas cadeiras, mas mulheres que estejam comprometidas com as pautas das populações que historicamente não são representadas por aqueles que ocupam as Casas Legislativas deste país. Por isso, é importante lembrar que a representatividade precisa vir acompanhada de um projeto político coletivo, pensado por negras e negros, trabalhadoras e trabalhadores, pessoas perifériacas e LGBTs que vivem na pele as desigualdades que o parlamento tem o dever de enfrentar.
Tivemos, nestas eleições, uma conquista simbólica importante: Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) tornou-se a mulher mais votada da história da Câmara dos Deputados. Por outro lado, Benedita da Silva (PT-RJ), uma das principais referências das mulheres negras na política, não se elegeu ao Senado.
Por isso, a pergunta “mudar a fotografia do poder é possível?” tem uma resposta que depende de nós: é possível, mas só se cada voto recebido por uma mulher negra for respondido com compromisso, estratégia e construção coletiva. Essa construção coletiva passa por reconhecer o que ainda impede que mais mulheres, sobretudo negras, cheguem ao poder e permaneçam nele.
Não se trata apenas de aumentar o número de candidaturas, mas de enfrentar as barreiras que se repetem a cada eleição. O avanço de mais mulheres na política depende de enfrentar problemas estruturais: o combate às candidaturas laranjas, a distribuição desigual dos recursos, a falta de suporte às candidatas, a desigualdade nas relações de poder dentro dos partidos e a violência política de gênero e raça. Sem isso, falta às mulheres eleitas a condição de exercer seus mandatos e permanecer na política.
São os nossos corpos que sofrem e atuam cotidianamente contra a violência política de gênero e raça e estão ali para, além de mudar a fotografia do poder, trazer uma nova forma de fazer política. Os números de 2026 mostram que tivemos conquistas, mas também que o cenário ainda é muito desigual. Enquanto as mulheres negras forem sub-representadas, a democracia brasileira seguirá incompleta.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: The best US Black Friday deals on 23 of our absolute favorite holiday gifts
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Filter editors
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
- Visit our ultimate guide to Black Friday for more deals on cozy winter clothing and buy-it-for-life products – carefully vetted by Filter US editors
Black Friday is usually the time to upgrade your cordless vacuum and stock up on toilet paper for less. It’s also an opportunity to knock out your holiday shopping in one fell swoop - preferably before December sneaks up on you (it somehow always does).
We spent months testing and handpicking 145 presents for our ultimate holiday gift guide, from cozy knits to shiny kitchen gadgets to delightful little stocking stuffers.
Now, we’ve rounded up our favorites on sale, so you can check off everyone on your list without paying full price.
More of our Black Friday coverage
- Non-toxic cookware deals
- Winter apparel deals
- Women’s fashion deals
- Household essentials deals
- Streaming service deals
Viktor Jurgen neck and shoulder massager
When my husband bought this Viktor Jurgen neck and shoulder massager, I figured it would end up collecting dust in the back of a closet. But the pressure – delivered via 16 heated orbs that rotate in two directions at three speeds – is deep-tissue level, earning it a permanent place near the couch. Juno DeMelo
Material Kitchen Trio of Knives
The chef’s knife, serrated knife and paring knife cover the needs of most home cooks – and after more than a year of near-daily use, the Japanese steel blades on all three are still sharp. It’s a great starter set or starting-over set, and it’s available with a magnetic knife stand or without. Emily Farris
Fly By Jing Mini Hot Pot
This starter set comes with chili crisp samplers to make your own hotpot base, though you can also buy Fly By Jing’s premade base, which produces a savory, tongue-tingling broth with a satisfying kick of Sichuan peppercorn. Give it to a homebody who loves to cook, then wait for the hotpot dinner invite. Everyone wins! Karen Yuan
Cozy Earth Men’s Stretch Knit Long Sleeve Pajamas
People spend more time in pyjamas than most clothes, so a decent set is an investment in the care and comfort of those you love. These Cozy Earth bamboo stretch-knit pajamas are wonderfully cozy, with a flexible fit and a wonderful feeling of smooth luxury. The breathable bamboo fabric also keeps things cool on a warm night. Richard Baguley
Jacobsen sea salt
Juno DeMelo, a Filter contributor, does not leave home without one of these tiny tins of Jacobsen sea salt from Oregon. “I keep one in our camping bin and another in my purse so I can dial in the salt level of whatever I’m eating no matter where in the world I am,” she wrote. Karen Yuan
Beats Solo 4
“That seems to be popular. I think everyone, mostly friends at school, wants to listen to music, and they are just the popular brand,” said Ollie, a 17-year-old. Lauren Gould
Mzoo Sleep Mask
In testing, the Mzoo sleep mask beat out 31 competitors to become our overall favorite, then went on to become one of our most popular recommendations of all time (our readers are a sleepy bunch). It gives total blackout coverage and stays comfortable enough to wear all night or a whole plane flight. Karen Yuan
Kitsch Satin Pillowcase
$20 $26 at Amazon, $21 $45 at Kitsch
Satin pillowcases help keep your skin smooth and your hair undamaged. This one from Kitsch is available in a Galactic Empire or Rebel Alliance theme, depending on your political orientation to the Force. Richard Baguley
Parachute Plush Organic Bath Towel
If you know someone who desperately needs a spa day but can never find the time, bring the spa to them. The Parachute organic super plush towels are some of the best bath towels we have ever tested. Made of thick, squishy organic Turkish cotton, Parachute’s towels are soft from edge to edge, giving you a sense of coziness that other towel brands struggle to match. Jon Chan
Shark NeverChange Air Purifier
Between wildfire smoke and pollution, air quality is a rising concern. If you are interested in giving the gift of clean air to a loved one, this Shark NeverChange air purifier is one of the best air purifiers I have tested, with a Hepa and carbon filter that can last up to five years. Jon Chan
Necoichi Wide Ceramic Pet Food Bowl
$18 $26 at Chewy, Amazon
I switched to this elevated dish after Tux kept managing to push his lightweight bowl under a nearby bar cart. This sturdier bowl stays put more easily and means less crouching for a more comfortable mealtime. Tracy Allison
Apple AirTag
Apple’s AirTags are button-sized pucks that wirelessly connect to Apple devices within Bluetooth range to report their approximate location. Put one in your bag, and you will always know where it is. If you have a forgetful friend or someone whose checked bags tend to disappear, they make a great gift. Tim Stevens
Stio Fleece Pants
Made from super-soft microfleece and available in men’s and women’s sizing, Stio’s Turpin joggers provide the exact right amount of warmth for light hiking in cool weather, aprés-ski and camping. Juno DeMelo
SkinThin Yoga Paws
Long hours on cramped airplanes do a number on your back. Yoga is a huge part of how I keep things limber, but yoga without a mat is a real challenge. SkinThin’s YogaPaws are gloves and booties that are like tiny yoga mats you can wear, surprisingly functional yet small enough to be easily packable. I was skeptical at first, but I bring these on every trip. Any yoga fan in your life will too. Tim Stevens
Kitsch Towel Hair Scrunchies
When I want to air-dry my hair without dripping water on to my shoulders, I pop on one of these. These Kitsch Quick-Dry towel scrunchies are made from a microfiber material that supposedly speeds drying time and looks nice enough for the beach or poolside. Maria Ricapito
Pilcro Alani 100% cashmere mock neck sweater
Any Anthropologie employee knows about the Alani sweater – and anyone who receives this as a gift will be happy to – whether it be your stylish mom, in-law or friend who hates spending money on themselves. Even after testing far pricier sweaters, I still have not found something softer than this one. While I have a crewneck version that’s not currently sold, the mockneck design is an equally great gift. It’s also not too heavy, which makes it a wonderful transition piece come spring. Lauren Gould
Amazon 16 GB Kindle
Even Amazon’s most basic Kindle is a phenomenal e-reader that the bookworm in your life will welcome with open arms. And they are not stuck buying books from Amazon. Pairing it with the Libby app makes it easy to borrow ebooks from your local library in seconds, totally free. Adam Doud
Dyson Nural Hair Dryer
$349 $599 at Sephora, Ulta Beauty
I have had my Dyson blowdryer for several years with no signs of needing to replace it. But as time and tech have moved on, the brand’s latest versions have new features such as “pause detect mode”, “attachment learning” and “scalp protect mode”. This model, the Dyson Supersonic Nural hairdryer, comes with the aforementioned bells and whistles as well as five magnetic attachments for different styling needs (to smooth flyaways, pouf up curls, concentrate air flow and detangle). Give this to someone whose janky old drugstore hairdryer is on the fritz – it’s worth it. Maria Ricapito
Kari Traa Base Layer
Kari Traa is perhaps the best-known name in women’s base layers and for good reason. The fun patterns and colors give women a chance to show off their style. The Smekker is one of my favorite layers to wear during my 50-plus ski days each season in Aspen because I can take it from the chairlift to the après and still look good. Heather Balogh Rochfort
Mountain Hardwear Coat
$262 $350 at Mountain Hardwear (men’s), (women’s)
Mountain Hardwear’s hooded jacket is like yoga pants for your arms. You get the warmth of a down jacket, but it is super stretchy thanks to flexible fabric and welded (instead of stitched) seams. I have broader shoulders and it makes the jacket far more comfortable when I am hiking. Heather Balogh Rochfort
Nothing Ear (3a) earbuds
The Nothing Ear (3a) earbuds are a really good value, with a fun, transparent design, excellent sound and very decent active noise-cancellation. If your teenager’s AirPods are always dying or your spouse spends hours on the train every day, give them the gift of reliability – you also get a solid eight-hour work day on a single charge with a couple more charges in the case. Adam Doud
Olipop Prebiotic Pomegranate Soda
Olipop’s new pomegranate prebiotic soda tastes tart and refreshing, like a cross between pomegranate juice and cider. If your giftee has a big sweet tooth, I am thrilled to share it is available in chocolate form too. Karen Yuan
Touchland Hand Sanitizer
$7 $10 at Sephora, Ulta Beauty
Touchland’s tween-endorsed bestseller from last year’s gift guide is still popular in 2026. When I recently gave my nine-year-old cousin one from Amazon’s beauty Advent calendar, it caused far more excitement than you would think for a hand sanitizer. Lauren Gould

How we choose the deals in this guide
We work for our readers, rather than the brands we write about. Every item we recommend is something a Filter editor or contributor has personally tested and can vouch for unless stated otherwise. On occasion, we may present a close substitute from the same brand and explain any differences from the original.
We scour competing retailers for the lowest prices on any item, and we use price-tracking tools such as Camelcamelcamel to check price history and ensure the discounts are truly good value, rather than a faux markdown. (So while we love sharing good deals, we also aren’t afraid to call out the unimpressive ones.)
Our mission at the Filter US
Our mission is to help you filter out junk products and buy fewer, better things.
At the Filter US, we test the products we recommend ourselves and never take your trust for granted. We also consider possible impacts on your health or the environment in our coverage and companies cannot purchase a spot in our product rankings because we are here to serve you, not corporations.

https://taz.de/Autobranche/!6233547/.title: Autobranche: Passgenaue Drohung
https://taz.de/Autobranche/!6233547/.author: Simon Poelchau
https://taz.de/Autobranche/!6233547/.text:
Autobranche : Passgenaue Drohung
Die Autobauer zeichnen ein düsteres Bild der Branche. Klar, denn damit wollen sie in der laufenden Tarifrunde Druck aufbauen.
C ui Bono?“ „Wem nützt es?“ Diese Frage kann eigentlich bei jeder Studie gestellt werden, die eine Lobbyorganisation herausbringt. Bei der jüngsten Publikation des Autobauerverbandes VDA geht es dabei nicht nur um den Inhalt, auch der Zeitpunkt der Veröffentlichung ist aufschlussreich. Schließlich veröffentlichte der Verband sie, just als Gewerkschaften und Arbeitgebervertreter mitten in der vierten, entscheidenden Runde der Metall-Tarifverhandlungen steckten.
Die Message der Studie ist schnell erzählt: Die Lage der für das Land wichtigen Autobranche ist schlecht. So schlecht, dass zwei von drei Unternehmen in der Zulieferbranche sowie bei den mittelständisch geprägten Herstellern von Anhängern, Aufbauten und Bussen geplante Investitionen verschieben, verlagern oder streichen wollen; mehr als jedes zweite würde sogar Stellenabbau betreiben und jedes dritte Investitionen ins billigere Ausland verlagern.
Die Studie zeichnet das bekannte Bild der drohenden Deindustrialisierung. Und damit ist sie selbst eine Drohung: Wenn nicht umgesetzt wird, was der Verband will, gehen in den Werkshallen bald die Lichter aus. Das heißt: eine weitere Verwässerung der CO₂-Flottenwerte, „weniger Bürokratie“, billigere Energie und – ganz wichtig – Richtung Gewerkschaften: niedrigere Arbeitskosten. Letzteres verbunden mit einer weiteren, in ein Studienergebnis gegossenen Drohung: Der Fachkräftemangel ist angeblich kein Problem mehr für die Branche.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Der VDA will der Gewerkschaft sagen: Eure Verhandlungsposition ist schlecht, also nehmt, was wir euch bieten. Und das in Tarifgesprächen, die härter und langwieriger sind als sonst. Denn die Branche befindet sich in einer Krise, die man nicht leugnen kann. Gleichzeitig spüren die Beschäftigten die Inflation. Sie fordern ein Lohnplus von 5 Prozent statt Mehrarbeit. Kein Wunder also, dass die Lobbyisten da mit einer passenden Studie kontern.
Der Druck, der auch mit solchen Veröffentlichungen auf die Gewerkschaft ausgeübt wurde, hat dann auch gewirkt. Sie ließen sich auf einen Tarifabschluss ein, der für die nächsten zwei Jahre Reallohnverluste bedeutet, da die vereinbarten Entgeltsteigerungen vermutlich unter der Inflationsrate liegen werden. Vor allem ließen sie sich auf eine Öffnungsklausel für weniger profitable Unternehmen ein, mit der die Beschäftigten zu Lohnverzicht und unbezahlter Mehrarbeit verpflichtet werden können.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths
Paul Mackenzie, already serving 200 years, is the founder and pastor of the Good News International Church.
A Kenyan court has found cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 of his followers, the latest conviction for Mackenzie, the founder and pastor of the Good News International Church.
Mackenzie was convicted on Friday in the coastal city of Mombasa, along with 29 followers, including his wife, Rhoda Mumbua.
Magistrate Alex Ithuku said Mackenzie “gave the directions to fast to death”, Reuters reported. Mackenzie pleaded not guilty, and one of his lawyers said he would appeal after sentencing.
Earlier convictions
On November 6, Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 191 people, 190 of them children. He had denied forcing the victims to starve, but the court rejected his defence.
He was also convicted this week of child cruelty, assault, radicalisation and “terrorism-related offences”, according to Reuters. He is due to be sentenced on the child cruelty and radicalisation charges in December, The Associated Press reported.
The Shakahola deaths
Mackenzie led the Good News International Church in the Shakahola Forest, near Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast.
He told followers to starve themselves and their children to death to meet Jesus before the end of the world.
Police arrested him in 2023 after a tip-off, and authorities began uncovering more than 400 bodies. People familiar with the cult told Reuters that Mackenzie planned the starvation in three phases: children first, then women and young men, and finally, the remaining men.
Mackenzie had been arrested twice before, in connection with the deaths of children, and released.
Calls for oversight
The killings have shocked Kenya and led to calls for tighter oversight of religious groups.
President William Ruto said in 2023 that he took responsibility as head of state for the government’s failure to prevent the deaths.
Other mass killings linked to cults include one in Uganda in 2000, when a doomsday group killed more than 700 people, and the 1978 massacre in Guyana, where an American cult leader ordered more than 900 followers to drink poison, Reuters said.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.title: Conceição Evaristo: ‘O povo negro tem pulsão de vida, se não estaríamos ainda nos negreiros’
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.author: Conversa Bem Viver
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.text:
Às vésperas de completar 80 anos, a escritora Conceição Evaristo está sendo homenageada com a ópera “Conceição Evaristo: Uma Ópera Escrevivência”, em cartaz no Theatro São Pedro, na capital paulista. Ao mesmo tempo, ela debuta como atriz protagonista do filme “Se Eu Fosse Vivo… Vivia”, dirigido por André Novais Oliveira. O longa-metragem abriu o 20ª Mostra Internacional de Cinema de Belo Horizonte (CineBH), na qual a escritora recebeu o Troféu Horizonte.
Em entrevista ao programa Conversa Bem Viver, a futura octogenária aponta que a vida é uma eterna descoberta e vê com bons olhos sua arte literária percorrer outras linguagens artísticas.
“Descobrir o meu texto literário numa modalidade que inspira a criação de uma ópera; me aventurar e debutar em um filme; além de ver esse meu texto literário ser apropriado por uma escola de samba… Acho que é tudo que a gente quer: estar produzindo uma arte que se democratize em suas formas de apresentação, que varie o mais possível para justamente também seduzir um público mais diverso. Uma experimentação mais democrática da arte, tanto em termos de feitura quanto de recepção”, relatou Conceição.
Conceição também relata que sua obra é uma escrita muito devedora dos processos de oralidade, e que ela foi forjada e inspirada a partir das experiências familiares de contação de história oral. “O meu contato com as histórias orais, com a contação de história da minha família, principalmente da minha mãe e da minha tia, me preparou, me forjou nesse encanto pela palavra, nesse exercício de escuta, de criação, de pensar o significado da palavra, mas também o significado que você, um outro, pode dar à palavra. Você tem que prestar atenção no gestual, no olhar, na palavra que não é dita.”
Ao comentar a vitalidade que tem, beirando os 80 anos de vida, Evaristo reflete sobre o conceito de acumular juventude e da velhice em ascensão.
“Antonio Pitanga está dizendo que nós temos juventudes acumuladas. Eu acho a história da Benedita da Silva, a história do Pitanga, a minha história, do próprio presidente Lula… Quando você teve uma juventude aguerrida, você segura a vida desde a juventude, muitas vezes desde a infância; isso se transforma numa característica sua. O tempo vai passando, você vai acumulando juventudes, mas você também vai crendo no direito à vida, e essa velhice em ascensão. Muitas vezes a velhice significa o declínio; para nós, a velhice tem significado de conquista, comprometimento, resultado de muitos desejos.”
No contexto das resistências, ela destaca que mulheres negras como ela acumulam anos de vida e se relacionam com uma pulsão de vida da população negra de forma coletiva, uma pulsão ancestral, mas também da contemporaneidade. “O povo negro tem uma pulsão pela vida, porque, se a gente não tivesse essa pulsão pela vida, todo mundo ficava nos negreiros e talvez não existisse essa diáspora africana, e a gente pode sair do Brasil. Você vê a luta dos negros nos Estados Unidos, a luta das pessoas descendentes de africanos na América Latina, no mundo inteiro, e nada foi colocado a nosso favor. O que era colocado a nosso favor foi justamente a morte. E ainda hoje você vê a luta dos grupos periféricos, a luta pela própria sobrevivência”.
Durante a conversa, a escritora disse não saber se a Academia Brasileira de Letras (ABL) quer uma candidatura sua para ocupar uma cadeira como imortal, mas celebrou a nomeação de Ana Maria Gonçalves, que se tornou a primeira mulher negra a integrar a instituição.
“Eu fiquei feliz também e estive presente na posse de Ana Maria Gonçalves na ABL. E tenho dito também que o importante não é ser a primeira, é você abrir perspectiva. E eu não tenho nenhuma dificuldade para dizer que, após a minha candidatura, a ABL se renovou, independentemente de eu estar lá dentro ou não. Eu acho que a Academia começou a buscar uma representatividade maior.”
Ela ainda recordou quando seu livro “Olhos D’água” foi laureado com o Prêmio Jabuti, em 2015, na categoria de contos e crônicas. Conceição relata que esse foi um momento de solidão, por não ter, na mesma premiação, outras pessoas negras sendo homenageadas.
“Outras escritoras e escritores começaram também a ser agraciados com o prêmio Jabuti; de certa forma, isso me contempla. Porque eu tenho certeza de que o meu posicionamento, o meu questionamento e a minha audácia ajudaram a fertilizar esse campo.”
Conversa Bem Viver
A sintonia da Rádio Brasil de Fato é 98,9 FM na Grande São Paulo.
Assim como os demais programas da Rádio Brasil de Fato, você pode ter acesso a esse conteúdo com antecedência para reproduzir gratuitamente na sua rádio. Acesse este formulário e faça sua inscrição.

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.title: Hackers reportedly breach US air force’s flagship cloud computing platform
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.author: Edward Helmore
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text:
Hackers are reported to have breached the US air force’s flagship cloud computing platform, a break-in that comes days after reports that a CIA database was accessed.
Reuters reported on Friday that the intrusion into the USAF’s Cloud One platform could jeopardize the security of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
The outlet said the breach was discovered within the past month or so during a systems upgrade, citing two sources, and that it had led to disruption across the platform. But Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the extent of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.
The air force said it “does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department [of the Air Force] information, systems and mission capabilities”.
Cloud One was designed to serve as a hub for the air force’s IT needs, including personnel data, pay, logistics and maintenance, using the services of four cloud managers – Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet.
But the system is also used for command and control and theater-integrated combat munitions system, or TICMS, that tracks and manages munitions inventories across more than 200 locations worldwide.
“A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources told Reuters.
One source said that intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control system and could in theory leverage that to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts.
The reported breach comes after reports of electronic break-ins at ‌the FBI,  Department of Homeland Security personnel information, the treasury department and two spy agencies.
In a breach at the Pentagon, hackers were able to access a system known as defense manpower datacenter, affecting 2.76 million living people and 294,000 deceased individuals, a US defense official told Military.com.
Exposed information included social security numbers and, depending on the individual, names, birthdates, contact information and military occupational specialties, the outlet said.
Earlier this week, it was reported that hackers breached a system used by the CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence system to reach unclassified information.
According to the New York Times, the affected system is an intelligence analysis tool that scans open-source and unclassified material for insights and information.
The CIA has declined to comment, but the ODNI representative said in an emailed statement to Bloomberg that “there have been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems”.

https://taz.de/Versorgungssicherheit-und.title: Versorgungssicherheit und Nachhaltigkeit: Wirtschaftliche Resilienzen
https://taz.de/Versorgungssicherheit-und.author: Heike Holdinghausen
https://taz.de/Versorgungssicherheit-und.text:
Versorgungssicherheit und Nachhaltigkeit : Wirtschaftliche Resilienzen
Billiger Strom für die Industrie stärkt Deutschlands Abwehrkräfte gegen Krisen keineswegs. Was es braucht, ist sorgsamer Umgang mit Ressourcen.
W as bedeutet das für ein gesellschaftliches Subsystem wie „die Wirtschaft“, wenn ihre Akteure keine eigene Sprache für ihre Anliegen entwickeln können, sondern beständig Begriffe aus anderen Subsystemen entwenden, sie umdeuten und schließlich, entleert, zurücklassen? Diese Frage wirft der große „Resilienzkongress“ des Bundesverbands der deutschen Industrie (BDI) auf, zu dem er hochrangige Referenten nach Berlin geladen hat.
Eine „resiliente Wirtschaft“ sei notwendig für eine Versorgungssicherheit in Gegenwart und Zukunft, heißt es in der Einladung. Konkurrenten und Gegenspieler der europäischen Industrie „erkennen die fundamentale Bedeutung von Rohstoffen und Energie, wandeln sie gezielt in einseitige Abhängigkeiten um und setzen sie als strategisches Druckmittel ein“. Ob Erdgas, Öl oder Seltene Erden, die Angriffe zielten und zielen auf die Grundlage „unserer wirtschaftlichen Wettbewerbs- und Handlungsfähigkeit“.
Dafür gewappnet zu sein, erfordere eben diese Resilienz – die Fähigkeit, sich flexibel an Krisen anzupassen und externe Schocks abzufedern. Der Industrieverband will sie mit weniger Bürokratie und schnelleren Verfahren erreichen, mit einer verlässlichen Energieversorgung zu wettbewerbsfähigen Preisen, staatlichen Analysen strategischer Abhängigkeiten mit Frühwarn- und Krisenwarnsystemen sowie einem geordneten Informationsfluss zwischen Behörden und Unternehmen.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Resilienz ist ein Begriff aus der Psychologie, der die Eigenschaft bezeichnet, mit Krisen umzugehen, ohne psychisch zu erkranken. In der Ökologie meint er etwas Ähnliches, nämlich die Fähigkeit von Ökosystemen, auf Störungen zu reagieren und ihre Funktionen im Grundsatz zu erhalten. So konnten sich Korallenriffe nach heftigen Störungen wie Hurrikans und Hitzeperioden trotz steigender Temperaturen und zunehmenden Kohlendioxidgehalts im Ozean dank strenger Schutzmaßnahmen regenerieren und wieder einen Lebensraum bieten.
Verbrauch innerhalb der planetaren Grenzen
Die Umweltbewegung hat den Resilienzbegriff dankbar aufgenommen und damit eine Gesellschaft beschrieben, die innerhalb der planetaren Grenzen konsumiert und wirtschaftet; die nicht mehr auf Wirtschaftswachstum angewiesen ist, sondern der es gelingt, ohne immer mehr Verbrauch natürlicher Ressourcen ein gutes Leben zu bieten; die Ernährung, Mobilität, Wohnen und Konsum so umgestaltet, dass sie Klimawandel, Artensterben und Verschmutzungskrise stoppt und möglichst wenig unter ihren Konsequenzen leidet.
Eine Gesellschaft, der ein umfangreiches, preisgünstiges ÖPNV-Angebot samt Fahrradinfrastruktur zur Verfügung steht, leidet weniger unter Ölpreisschocks als eine, die auf Autos mit Verbrennungsmotoren angewiesen ist. Es heißt, dass der Bevölkerung in Europa unter den neuen Bedingungen von Hitzestress und Dürreperioden auch in Zukunft Nahrung (im Überfluss) zur Verfügung steht, wenn Förster:innen, Landwirt:innen und Planungsbehörden dafür sorgen, dass die Landschaft Wasser hält und die Böden fruchtbar bleiben.
Die Übersetzung ins Praktische gelingt aber nur, wenn der Begriff tatsächlich etwas meint. Was sonst passiert, zeigt der Begriff der „Nachhaltigkeit“. Sie beschrieb einst die Idee, dass die Ansprüche der heutigen Generationen befriedigt werden sollten, ohne die der kommenden zu gefährden. Zwar hatte das Wort in seiner ursprünglichen Bedeutung in der Forstwissenschaft zunächst die sichere Versorgung mit Holz im Blick und nicht den Erhalt der Artenvielfalt. Doch ohne Biodiversität und stabiles Klima auf Dauer kein Forst – und kein Holz.
Wirtschaftslobbyisten überbetonten den ökonomischen Aspekt der Nachhaltigkeit jahrelang so erfolgreich, bis die ökologischen und sozialen Aspekte in dem Konzept kaum noch eine Rolle spielten. Heute ließe sich getrost die Drohung von Mercedes-Benz oder Audi als nachhaltig bezeichnen, Werke in Deutschland zu schließen und Verbrenner in den USA zu produzieren, weil damit ihre Wettbewerbsfähigkeit erhalten bleibt. Heute steht das Streben nach Nachhaltigkeit auf jeder Website, zahnlos und belanglos.
Ohne Erneuerbare geht es nicht
Dem Begriff der Resilienz droht dasselbe Schicksal. Der BDI beschreibt sie als Fähigkeit von Unternehmen, unter widrigen Bedingungen so weiterzumachen, wie sie es in den vergangenen Jahrzehnten getan haben. Jeden Ansatz von Wandel und Transformation hin zu neuen, klimafreundlichen Technologien oder Verhaltensweisen wehren sie ab. Diskussionen darüber, wie große Unternehmen sich selbst wandeln, wie sie demokratischer, transparenter, offener werden könnten – Stichwort Open Source oder Commons – finden nicht statt.
Im Gegenteil: Die Autoindustrie lobbyiert so lange für eine Abkehr vom Verbrenner-Aus, bis Berlin und Brüssel einknicken; seit Jahren verzichten die allermeisten Industrieunternehmen zugunsten ihrer jeweils nächsten Bilanz auf langfristige Lieferverträge oder eine sichere Versorgung mit kritischen Rohstoffen, auf die sie dringend angewiesen sind. In einer Art neuem Schweinezyklus geraten sie jedes Mal in Panik, wenn China ihnen den Hahn für günstige Seltene Erden, Wolfram und anderes abdreht.
Staatliche Einflussnahmen – wie ein Lieferkettengesetz oder eine Entwaldungsrichtlinie – bekämpfen sie, staatliche Unterstützung im Krisenfall fordern sie. Ändern müssen sich immer die anderen – der Staat, der schneller und weniger Regeln erlässt und preisgünstiger Energie zur Verfügung stellt, egal welche; die Beschäftigten, die mehr und zu niedrigeren Kosten arbeiten sollen. Diese Forderungen enden nicht in einem resilienteren System, sondern in besseren Quartalszahlen im nächsten Halbjahr.
Die Zukunft der Industriestaaten wird von erneuerbaren Energien, von gemeinschaftlichen Lösungen, von intelligenten Ressourcenkreisläufen geprägt sein. Die „deutsche Wirtschaft“ aber deutet alle Begriffe, die den Weg in diese Zukunft beschreiben könnten, so lange um, bis sie nur noch ihren eigenen Status quo wiedergeben. Am Ende hat sie nicht einmal mehr Worte, mit denen sie ihren notwendigen Aufbruch beschreiben könnte.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.
The US military says it has fired on a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman and claims it was trying to breach an American blockade on Iranian ports.
Military aircraft fired “precision munitions” at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the “ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed”, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement.
US officials say the Pacific Archer left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before it attempted to run the blockade. Ship tracking websites list the vessel’s destination as Singapore. It is at least the 15th vessel the US military has publicly acknowledged disabling since the blockade began in April, and the sixth since it resumed it in July. The previous vessel was disabled on November 7.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Friday that two tankers attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an “unauthorised” route, claiming that one of them struck a naval mine while the other was forced to turn back.
The claims could not be independently verified.
The commander of the Iranian navy, Shahram Irani, said on Friday on state television that Iran will carry out operations “that will not only break the naval blockade but also drive the enemy out of the region’s waters”.
American blockade action
The US military has maintained a sizeable naval force in the region, including a constant presence of two aircraft carriers and a host of other ships.
American ships have been blockading Iranian ports since April, although the blockade was temporarily lifted during talks with Tehran and resumed in July. Since then, the US military says it has redirected 158 merchant ships and disabled those that refuse to comply.
CENTCOM, which has its headquarters in Florida, has consistently said that American forces issue multiple warnings before firing on the merchant ships.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: 28ª Feira Estadual de Economia Solidária reúne 85 expositores no centro de Porto Alegre
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Começa na segunda-feira (30) e vai até 5 de dezembro, a 28ª Feira Estadual de Economia Solidária, com 85 estandes no Largo Glênio Peres, em frente ao Mercado Público de Porto Alegre, valorizando a produção artesanal. A feira funcionará das 8h30 às 19h.
A cerimônia oficial de abertura está marcada para segunda-feira, às 16h, com apresentação cultural e homenagem ao ex-governador Olívio Dutra, em reconhecimento à sua trajetória de apoio à economia solidária.
Os visitantes terão a oportunidade de adquirir produtos diretamente de seus produtores, experimentar sabores e conhecer iniciativas de diferentes regiões do Rio Grande do Sul, contribuindo para a geração de renda de centenas de famílias.
Ao longo dos seis dias de programação, de segunda-feira a sábado, a feira contará com atividades que vão além do comércio justo e do consumo consciente. Estão previstas apresentações de moda e acessórios, ações formativas, rodas de conversa, exposições sobre bancos comunitários e moedas sociais, lançamentos de livros e diversas manifestações culturais. A organização também orienta os visitantes a levarem suas próprias sacolas, como forma de diminuir o impacto ambiental causado pelo uso de embalagens.
“Esperamos encantar o público, pois cada produto carrega um pouco do sonho de quem o produz”, afirma Nelsa Nespolo, coordenadora da Feira e presidenta da Central de Cooperativas e Empreendimentos Solidários do RS (Unisol-RS). Segundo ela, optar pela compra direta de quem produz representa uma escolha política que valoriza a economia local, o trabalho coletivo e a sustentabilidade.
Oficinas, clube de trocas e desfile
A programação gratuita inclui oficinas voltadas ao cuidado ambiental e ao artesanato. Na terça-feira (1º), às 14h, será realizada uma atividade sobre reciclagem e separação de resíduos, seguida, às 17h, de uma oficina de feltragem de lã de ovelha. Já na quarta-feira (2), às 14h, ocorre o Clube de Trocas entre expositores da Feira, e, às 17h, uma roda de conversa sobre saúde mental, ambas abertas à comunidade.
A coleção da Setorial de Artesanato da Unisol-RS será exibida nos dias 3 e 5 de dezembro, às 14h, permitindo ao público conhecer a diversidade criativa do segmento. Na quinta-feira (3), às 16h, também haverá uma roda de conversa sobre bancos comunitários e moedas sociais, iniciativas desenvolvidas na Capital que contribuem para o fortalecimento da economia comunitária.
Na sexta-feira (4), às 15h, o público poderá acompanhar uma apresentação cultural e o lançamento de livros e publicações voltados ao terceiro setor. Mais tarde, às 17h, um tapete vermelho de 20 metros será palco do desfile de roupas e acessórios produzidos pelos empreendimentos, apresentando as criações e a identidade dos trabalhadores do setor.
Encontro Estadual de Economia Solidária
Na segunda-feira (30), às 8h30, representantes de diferentes regiões do Rio Grande do Sul participam do Encontro Estadual de Economia Solidária, no auditório do Hotel Plaza São Rafael. O espaço será dedicado ao debate sobre as condições de comercialização, os princípios que norteiam a produção e os desafios enfrentados pelos empreendimentos.
Entre os participantes convidados estão o presidente da Fundação Banco do Brasil, André Machado, e o secretário nacional de Economia Solidária (Senaes), Fernando Zamban.
Outros dois seminários realizados durante a feira abordam experiências de comercialização e perspectivas para a economia solidária.
- 3 de dezembro | Estratégias para transformação: o seminário contará com a participação do economista e presidente do IBGE, Márcio Pochmann, da socióloga Helena Singer e de representantes do Conselho Estadual de Economia Solidária.
- 5 de dezembro | Desafios do cenário nacional e internacional: o debate terá como convidados a deputada Maria do Rosário e um representante da experiência cooperativa de Mondragón, na Espanha.
Casas de economia solidária abertas o ano inteiro
Os produtos comercializados na Feira também podem ser encontrados durante todo o ano nas Casas de Economia Solidária, que funcionam em Porto Alegre (Rua Vigário José Inácio, 307), Santana do Livramento (Rua Rivadávia Corrêa, 60) e São Leopoldo (Av. Henrique Bier, 942).
Além dessas unidades, estão em processo de implantação novas casas em Passo Fundo, Caxias do Sul e Pelotas. “São espaços de formação, exposição e comércio com a produção dos coletivos formados em sua maioria por mulheres”, destaca Ana Inês Castro, coordenadora da Casa de Santana do Livramento. Integrante da organização desse segmento, ela celebra o crescimento de uma economia que atua de forma articulada para oferecer produtos de qualidade, promover o comércio justo e contribuir para o bem-viver.
Serviço
O quê: 28ª Feira Estadual de Economia Solidária do Rio Grande do Sul
Quando: de 30 de novembro a 5 de dezembro de 2026, das 8h30 às 19h
Onde: Largo Glênio Peres, em frente ao Mercado Público, Centro Histórico de Porto Alegre
Abertura oficial: 30 de novembro, às 16h, no Largo Glênio Peres
Encontro Estadual de Economia Solidária: 30 de novembro, às 8h30, no auditório do Hotel Plaza São Rafael
Organização: Unisol-RS, Fórum Estadual da Economia Solidária e Federação dos Trabalhadores/as na Agricultura Familiar (Fetraf).
Apoios: Fundação Banco do Brasil; Governo Federal, por meio do Ministério do Desenvolvimento Agrário e da Senaes; e Governo do Estado, por meio da Secretaria do Trabalho/FGTAS e da Secretaria de Estado da Cultura.
